Following the metriplectic (equivalently, GENERIC) approach, we add to the Hamiltonian vector field a dissipative term generated by a symmetric bracket, here constructed from a Riemannian metric. The resulting flow conserves the energy, and optionally further invariants, while driving a chosen generalised entropy monotonically, which makes the dynamics irreversible; when the entropy is bounded on energy level sets in the direction in which it is driven, it acts as a Lyapunov functional. We apply this construction to ideal fluids on compact Riemannian manifolds, choosing Casimirs of the Lie-Poisson bracket as entropies. In two dimensions, dissipating enstrophy yields the already-known energy-constrained Navier-Stokes equations, which include a nonlocal term restoring energy balance. In three dimensions, where enstrophy is no longer a Casimir, we derive new irreversible models. For incompressible and compressible fluids carrying an advected scalar, dissipating potential enstrophy or higher potential-vorticity moments gives a nonlinear, anisotropic diffusion that acts to align the gradients of the scalar and of the potential vorticity. For a purely incompressible fluid, taking helicity as the entropy gives a first-order, non-smoothing dissipative term whose stationary states are Beltrami fields.
Integer Decomposition Property of Edge Polytopes of Weighted Oriented Graphs
Jennifer Biermann; Kuei-Nuan Lin; Augustine O'Keefe

We classify the lattice polytopes arising from vertex-weighted oriented graphs that have the integer decomposition property (IDP). Allowing vertex weights and edge orientations introduces non-vertex lattice points in the polytope which need to be accounted for when studying the IDP. We can then identify forbidden induced subgraphs in the sense that their presence obstructs the IDP for the supergraph. We establish positive results for several families of graphs under suitable orientation and coprimality conditions, including weighted oriented paths and cycles, and show that any weighted oriented tree with a unique sink has the IDP.
Hinge comparison and excess estimates via modified Hessian bounds on manifolds with density

We study geometric consequences of modified Hessian estimates on Riemannian manifolds with density. For general radial functions, we derive tensorial, spectral, and trace identities for the modified Hessian in the original metric. We also establish a comparison identity relating the modified Hessians of two radial functions and characterize when they are proportional. We then prove a hinge comparison theorem under an upper bound on the modified Hessian, yielding a weighted law of cosines and lower bounds for the excess function. Finally, under nonnegative weighted sectional curvature and suitable density control assumptions, we obtain an Abresch-Gromoll-type upper excess estimate.
Accelerated Transformed Primal Dual Methods for Smooth Convex Optimization Problems with Affine Equality Constraints

Accelerated transformed primal--dual (ATPD) methods are proposed for smooth convex optimization problems with affine equality constraints. The methods combine primal--dual dynamics with a transformation designed to accelerate convergence. In the strongly convex case, ATPD achieves an accelerated linear convergence rate and matches the known lower bounds on first-order oracle complexity in terms of gradient evaluations and matrix--vector products. The analysis distinguishes these two types of computational work when assessing the complexity of the method. For general convex objectives, a homotopy perturbation strategy is introduced, and an accelerated sublinear rate for the modified Lyapunov energy is proved under a uniform boundedness condition on the primal iterates at all homotopy stages. The acceleration mechanism is based on an exponentially stable ATPD flow and a modified discrete Lyapunov function. This continuous-time perspective guides the construction and analysis of the discrete methods. Numerical experiments on policy evaluation and constrained signal reconstruction problems support the theory and illustrate the efficiency of the proposed methods.
Spin-Boson Hamiltonians as Generators of Spin-Dressed Bogoliubov Dynamics

Following Bach, Lieb and Solovej, quadratic Hamiltonians can be defined as generators of unitary groups implementing one-parameter groups of Bogoliubov transformations. We develop an analogous dynamical definition of generalized spin--boson Hamiltonians. For a single spin level, we review results of Guichardet and Dereziński: the van Hove Hamiltonians, including the renormalized ones, are exactly the generators of affine Bogoliubov dynamics that do not mix creation and annihilation operators. For several spin levels, there is no analogue of this group, and we introduce spin-dressed implementations, that is to say the free flow of the fields is implemented up to bounded operator-valued displacements, which vanish at a rate measured by a so-called regularity scale and have a spin observable, the coupling map, as derivative at time zero. The one-particle Hamiltonian $Υ$ and the coupling map are determined by the Hamiltonian, and the field obeys a quantum Langevin equation. Spin-dressed implementations in Fock space, at the finest scale and for form factors in $D(Υ^{-1/2})$, are exactly the generalized spin--boson Hamiltonians, unique up to the spin Hamiltonian. At the roughest scale, the renormalized spin--boson Hamiltonian of a two-level system with ultraviolet-singular form factor and arbitrary tunnelling is a spin-dressed implementation, and the definition alone yields asymptotic Weyl operators on the test functions along which the coupling map is integrable, a dense set under standard assumptions.

Given a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, the reconfiguration graph $\mathcal{R}_{k}(G)$ has the proper $k$-colourings of $G$ for vertices, two of which are adjacent if and only if they differ on precisely one vertex of $G$. In $2022$, Cambie, Cranston and the author proved that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{Δ+2}(G)$ is at most $n+2μ$, and put forth a collection of conjectures that in its strongest and most beautiful form would imply that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{Δ+2}(G)$ is precisely equal to $n + μ$, for every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, matching number $μ$ and maximum degree $Δ$. Here we disprove most of those conjectures. Our constructions have reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{3}{2}μ-2$. We also provide counterexamples that are $Δ$-regular, we show that every graph has reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{1}{2} μ$, and we advertise an extension to hypergraphs. It is now much more mysterious how the diameter behaves, so we propose a number of open problems.
Continuum space hierarchical Cannings process: II. Genealogies and ancestral web

The present paper is the second in a series of three papers in which we consider a \emph{spatial multi-type population model} arising as the many-individuals-per-site limit of individual-based models. The evolution mechanisms in this model are: migration, Fleming-Viot resampling, $Λ_0$-Cannings resampling, and $(Λ_k)_{k \in \N}$-Cannings block-resampling. This evolution leads to a collection of \emph{measure-valued} processes indexed by a continuum geographic space $Ω_N^\infty$, called the \emph{continuum hierarchical group}, obtained as the limit of a discrete hierarchical group $Ω_N^L$ as $L\to\infty$, where $Ω_N^L = \oplus_{k \geq -L} Z_N$ with $Z_N$ the cyclical group of order $N$. On this geographic space, each component is a probability measure on a type space $\K$.
 In the first paper \cite{gh1}, we \emph{constructed} the measure-valued process on $Ω_N^\infty$ describing the type frequencies in the population and identified its main properties. We found a \emph{dichotomy} between this process being \emph{stochastic} (= locally monotype) or \emph{deterministic} (= locally multitype). In the present paper we turn to the \emph{genealogies} of the population on $Ω_N^\infty$.
Control Variates to reduce the variance of the empirical Moment Generating Function: an extreme value perspective
Louison Bocquet-Nouaille; Jérôme Morio; Benjamin Bobbia; Philippe Naveau

Accurate estimation of Moment Generating Functions is fundamental in many applications, but empirical estimators have high variances. Within a control variate setup, Extreme Value Theory is leveraged to identify how extreme values affect the variance reduction method's optimality.
Poincaré polynomials of nilmanifolds associated with path graphs
Marco Aldi; Samuel Bevins; Eleftherios Chatzitheodoridis; Sergio Da Silva; Quincy Frias; Tomás Mejía Gómez

We give explicit and recursive formulas for the Poincaré polynomials of Dani--Mainkar nilmanifolds associated with path graphs. We also prove that these polynomials are unimodal, and we calculate a range of Betti numbers asymptotically. As an application, we derive a sharp lower bound for the dimension of the total de Rham cohomology of a Dani--Mainkar nilmanifold.

We obtain infinite spin representations of the super-Poincaré algebra from a higher-derivative superparticle action on a super-Minkowski background in 3, 4, 6 and 10 dimensions. Super-twistor transforms are performed, and used to deduce first-quantised spectra.
Real log canonical tresholds and real log canonical tresholds with signs

In this paper, we study the properties of the real log canonical threshold $\text{rlct}(X,Y)$ associated with a pair $(X,Y)$ and the real log canonical thresholds with signs $\text{rlct}^{\pm}(f)$ associated with a polynomial function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$. In particular, we relate these invariants to other invariants arising from the theory of motivic integration. We also show how to compute these invariants in several particular cases, including the Newton non-degenerate case and the case of analytically irreducible plane curve germs.
Hausdorff measures of planar Brownian level sets

For any Hausdorff gauge \(h\), we prove that all level sets of planar Brownian motion have zero \(h\)-measure almost surely if and only if \(\liminf_{r\to0^+}h(r)\log(1/r)=0\). This resolves Taylor's question for arbitrary Hausdorff gauges. The proof yields \(0<\HH^{h_0}(L_x)<\infty\) for some \(x\) almost surely, where \(h_0(r)=1/\log(1/r)\). The Hausdorff dimensions of the spatial mass superlevel sets form a deterministic, strictly decreasing bi-Lipschitz spectrum. For each fixed positive mass below the supremum, the exact-mass set almost surely has the same dimension as the corresponding superlevel set.
Macroscopic $L^\infty$ bounds for the homogeneous Landau--Coulomb equation

We establish an instantaneous global $L^\infty(\R^3)$ bound at positive times for smooth, rapidly decaying solutions to the three-dimensional spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, where the upper bound depends solely on the initial mass, momentum, energy, and entropy. This resolves an open problem posed by Golding, Gualdani, and Loher \cite{GGL} without requiring any initial higher velocity moments, Fisher information, or Lebesgue integrability. The proof builds on two main analytical ingredients. First, we establish the instantaneous generation of the negatively weighted Fisher information with weight $\la{v}^{-1}$. On the lifted two-particle phase space, we compare the separable weight matrix against a collision-invariant pair weight and control the rotational commutator near the diagonal via the quadratic local mass decay supplied by the conserved energy, closing a Riccati differential inequality at the second-moment threshold. Second, to overcome the $\la{v}^{-3}$ radial degeneracy of the diffusion matrix at large velocities, we prove a truncated anisotropic mixed Nash inequality on upper level sets of the density that recovers longitudinal regularity from two transverse Fisher directions and the nonlinear high-density part of the Coulomb entropy dissipation. Localizing this functional inequality to radially aligned velocity cells with the critical weight $\la{v}^{3/2}$ and coupling it with a weighted truncated entropy identity across nested exterior domains yields a superlinear De Giorgi recurrence that bounds the velocity tail uniformly in $\R^3$.
The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
Bonan Chen; Xiang Fang; Feng Guo

We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture.
 The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity.
 We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar.
 In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.
Entire sig-jump-diffusions, their expected signature and applications to score-based generative modeling
Christa Cuchiero; Francesca Primavera; Sara Svaluto-Ferro

We develop score-based generative models for time series and standard finite-dimensional data, building on the analytical computation of the expected signature of a new class of jump-diffusions, called entire sig-jump-diffusions. These are semimartingales whose characteristics are given by linear combinations of potentially infinitely many components of their own signature. We show that their expected signature can be computed by solving linear ODEs in the extended tensor algebra, providing a tractable foundation for learning procedures. Specifically, the learning of a generalized score function for jump diffusions, a key ingredient of our generative modeling framework, can be reduced to solving linear ODEs and a deterministic optimization problem.
 We further prove that polynomial jump-diffusions can be embedded into this framework, and that their expected signature reduces to a finite-dimensional system of linear ODEs. Building on this result, we develop an alternative approach for finite-dimensional data, based on inverse signature matching, a method that learns the score by matching the expected signature of the reverse process with that of the inverse forward signature.
How to arrange four points in the plane

Arranging points in the plane appears to be an elementary geometric problem, yet it is deeply rooted in statistical physics. As a toy model, we consider the configuration of four points. We completely classify the minimal configurations of four points interaction energy in $\R^2$ under the general Lennard-Jones potentials $V(r)=r^{-p}-br^{-q}$, where $p>q>0$ and $b\in\R$. We find that there is a threshold curve \[
 D_{p,q}=2^{-(p-q)/2}\Bigl(1+\frac{p-q}{q+2}\bigl(1+2^{-(q+2)/2}\bigr)\Bigr) \] to determine the minimal shapes. The main results can be stated concisely as follows: consider $\min\sum_{1\le i<j\le4}\bigl(|x_i-x_j|^{-p}-b|x_i-x_j|^{-q}\bigr)$. For $b\le0$, the minimizer does not exist. For $b>0$, the minimizer is unique up to rotation and translation. Furthermore, the minimizer is \[
 \begin{cases}
 \text{a square},&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}\ge1,
 \text{a rhombus with angle }θ\in(π/3,π/2),&\hbox{if}\;\; D_{p,q}<1.
 \end{cases} \]
A lift of Baxter's cyclic summation identity with applications to quantum topology

While studying the chiral Potts model Baxter discovered a cyclic analogue of Ramanujan's ${}_1ψ_{1}$ summation identity. This identity was subsequently interpreted by Faddeev and Kashaev as a pentagon relation for the quantum dilogarithm function, a key ingredient in cyclic quantizations of Teichmüller theory. Existing forms of the identity involve multivalued functions so one must either accept overall phase ambiguities or keep track of branches on a complicated covering space. In this paper we show how to remove the phase ambiguities with a much simpler choice of covering space. As an application we compute the Fourier transform of the holonomy $R$-matrices of the author and Reshetikhin. A corollary is a simpler proof that Kashaev's $R$-matrix is a specialization of the colored Jones $R$-matrix, which was first shown by Murakami and Murakami.
Direct Search meets Frank-Wolfe: Inexact Derivative-Free Bilevel Optimization over Polytopes
Matteo Pernini; Francesco Rinaldi; Gabriele Sanguin; Marco Viola

In this work we propose BLDS-SIMPLEX, a derivative-free direct search method for the solution of bilevel optimization with polytope constraints at the upper level. The proposed method reformulates the feasible set using barycentric coordinates and explores it using Frank-Wolfe-type directions, relying on a fixed-accuracy black-box oracle for the upper-level objective function. We analyze its convergence properties and complexity in the case of smooth reduced objective; additionally, we analyze a variant for the case of nonsmooth objectives and show its convergence to a specific kind of stationary point that we introduce as a natural generalization to the classic stationarity notions in this setting. Numerical tests on modified instances from BOLIB support the viability of our new approach.
Certified Hierarchical Planning and Tracking: A Learning-Based Approach
Weijian Li; Vince Kurtz; Panos J. Antsaklis; Hai Lin

In this paper, we develop a hierarchical control framework for nonlinear dynamical systems with safety constraints. Specifically, a low-fidelity model is introduced for trajectory planning, while a tracking controller is designed for the high-fidelity system. We first characterize the tracking error bound (TEB) using a storage function. Then, we formulate the synthesis of the tracking controller, the storage function, and the TEB as an optimization problem. Following that, we develop an offline learning approach to approximately solve the optimization problem, by incorporating behavior cloning and satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solver. We further integrate the learned controller and the TEB into online tracking of the high-fidelity system. This framework enables the control of high-dimensional nonlinear systems with safety guarantees, while maintaining computational efficiency for real-time implementation. Finally, experiments are provided for illustration.
Off-diagonal decay of capacitance matrices via Brownian motion

We establish upper and lower bounds for the off-diagonal entries of the capacitance matrix of infinite systems of spherical resonators in chain, screen and crystal geometries. Let $d$ denote the distance between two resonator centres. For chains contained in a cylinder of bounded radius and with bounded axial gaps, the decay is of order $d^{-1}\log^{-2}(2+d)$. For screens contained in a slab and relatively dense in the tangential directions, it is of order $d^{-3}$. For relatively dense three-dimensional configurations, we obtain exponential upper and lower bounds. No periodicity is assumed. Our proofs are based on the classical connection between the Dirichlet problem and Brownian motion, which enables us to relate the decay estimates to hitting probabilities of Brownian motion.
Non self-similar solutions to the Ricci flow coming out of metric cones
Alix Deruelle; Tristan Ozuch; Felix Schulze

Given an asymptotically conical unstable expanding gradient Ricci soliton, we provide the existence of a family of Ricci flows starting at the same metric cone up to isometry. Moreover, the family of solutions we construct is shown to be parametrized by positive modes of the weighted Lichnerowicz operator associated to the background expanding gradient Ricci soliton. Each solution of this family is shown not to be induced by an expanding gradient Ricci soliton. If the background expander has no non-trivial infinitesimal deformations, we show furthermore that the solutions we provide are not self-similar. We finally prove that solutions are distinct up to isometries preserving the potential function of the background expanding gradient Ricci soliton.
A binomial-adjusted $θ$-trapezoidal tau-leaping method for chemical kinetic systems
Maximilian Scott; Sam McCallum; James Foster

In Hu, Li and Min (2011), the authors propose a weak second order accurate $θ$-trapezoidal method as an improvement to the classical tau-leaping method. However, for complex chemical kinetic systems their model's underlying analytical assumptions can fail to hold in practice, leading to a significant reduction in its computational effectiveness. Here we introduce a modification to the method which allows it to regain desirable convergence characteristics, both given the original and a relaxed version of the underlying assumptions. We confirm this improvement through a local error analysis and present numerical examples showing it consistently performs either better or comparable to the $θ$-trapezoidal method.
Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
Tattwamasi Amrutam; Diptesh Saha; Xumin Wang

We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.
Rainbow matchings in non-uniform hypergraph systems

Let $s\geq 1$, $r_1, r_2,\dots, r_{s+1}$ be given positive integers and $r=\max\{r_1, r_2,\ldots, r_{s+1}\}$. We prove that if $\mathcal{F} = \{\mathcal{F}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{F}_{s+1}\}$ is a family of hypergraphs on a ground set of $n$ vertices, $n\geq 4r^2(s+1)$, such that $\mathcal{F}_i\subseteq \binom{n}{r_i}$ and $|\mathcal{F}_i|>\binom{n}{r_i}-\binom{n-s}{r_i}-\binom{n-s-r}{r_i-1}+1$, for all $i \in [s+1]$, then $\mathcal{F}$ admits a rainbow matching of size $s+1$ or there exists $W \in \binom{[n]}{s}$ such that $W$ is a vertex cover of $\mathcal{F}_i$, for all $i \in [s+1]$. This improves upon the previously known range $n>2r^3s$ to $n>4r^2(s+1)$. Moreover, for a given family $\mathcal{F} = \{\mathcal{F}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{F}_{s+1}\}$ of hypergraphs $\mathcal{F}_i\subseteq \binom{n}{r_i}$, we give a best possible Ore-degree condition for $\mathcal{F}_{i}$'s that guarantees the existence of a rainbow matching of size $s+1$ for $\mathcal{F}$.
Characterizations of Pettis Integrable Multifunctions in Locally Convex Spaces

In this paper, we present characterizations of Pettis integrability in $bcc(X)$ and $cwk(X)$ of a multifunction $Γ: Ω\to cc(X)$, where $(Ω, Σ, μ)$ is a complete finite measure space and $cc(X)$ $(bcc(X), cwk(X))$ is the family of all nonempty convex closed (bounded convex closed, convex weakly compact) subsets of a Hausdorff locally convex topological vector space $X$. Incidentally, a convergence theorem for scalarly integrable multifunctions is proved. As an application, we are going to prove full characterizations of Pettis integrability for fuzzy maps defined on $Ω$ and taking values in the generalized fuzzy number hyperspace $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$.
Asymptotic Dimension of Persistence Modules of Bounded Presentation
Sushovan Majhi; Atish Mitra; Žiga Virk

We compute the asymptotic dimension of spaces of multiparameter persistence modules of bounded presentation under the interleaving distance. The $d$-parameter modules with at most $n$ generators and $m$ relations have asymptotic dimension, and Assouad-Nagata dimension, exactly $d(n+m)$, the number of coordinates of their generator and relation grades, over every field; for two parameters this is $2(n+m)$. The space has continuous moduli, already for two parameters and $n,m\ge2$: over an infinite field it contains, at every scale, infinite uniformly separated families of pairwise non-isomorphic modules with one fibered barcode, so it is not doubling even at a fixed fibered barcode; already for $m\ge1$ it is not coarsely equivalent to a proper metric space. The proof is an induction on the number of distinct grade coordinates: an interleaving small compared with the gaps between these coordinates moves each of them by at most twice its size and preserves the induced grid representation, so the continuous moduli are invisible at large scale. Each class of modules at finite distance therefore embeds coarsely into Hilbert space; for $n,m\ge2$ over an uncountable field, the classes that contain these families admit no such embedding into a separable Hilbert space. Under the two-parameter matching distance $2(n+m)$ is a lower bound, attained for one generator and for two generators with at most one relation; on a finite net of $S$ slices the asymptotic dimension is at most $2nS$.
A completely decomposable modular Jacobian of dimension $1777$

We exhibit a congruence subgroup $Γ\subset\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ of level $120$ and index $23040$ whose modular curve $X_Γ$ has genus $1777$ and whose Jacobian is isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ to a product of elliptic curves. This surpasses the previous record of a completely decomposable complex Jacobian of dimension $1297$ found by Ekedahl and Serre in $1993$.

Crossing a domain wall can permute anyons, and intersecting strings can create a particle. These couplings between defects of various dimensions are specified by higher groups. We develop a lattice framework defining higher-group statistics as Berry phases of closed sequences of hopping operators, invariant under local modifications of the operators. Our central example is a closed Majorana chain, a 1-dimensional topological superconductor, embedded in 3 dimensions. We construct a loop-flip process with phase $+i$, refining the usual $\pm 1$ loop-flip invariant through intermediate transfer of fermion parity between the chain and physical fermions. In two dimensions, charge-wall statistics distinguish two $\mathbb Z_4$ toric codes enriched by $\mathbb Z_2$ charge-conjugation symmetry, with identical anyon statistics but distinct gauged theories: the quantum doubles of the dihedral group $D_4$ and the quaternion group $Q_8$. We provide two complementary constructions of statistical processes. The first extends the Smith normal form algorithm in [Phys. Rev. X $\textbf{16}$, 011010 (2026), arXiv:2412.01886] to higher groups, generating processes from lattice geometry and prescribed local moves. For a finite higher group $\mathbb G$, we prove that statistical processes on a $d$-sphere are classified by $H_{d+2}(B\mathbb G,\mathbb Z)$. The second constructs processes directly from homology classes without examining exponentially many defect configurations, enabling us to study statistics for complex higher-group structures where the previous method is computationally prohibitive. These processes detect boundary anomalies of higher-group symmetry-protected topological phases. For example, we distinguish 2-group anomalies in 1, 2, and 3 dimensions. Higher-group statistics provide new invariants for characterizing coupled defects in quantum many-body systems.
Non-existence of closed embedded magnetic geodesics
We give a counterexample to S. Novikov's 1982 conjecture that every Riemannian $2$-sphere contains a closed embedded curve of curvature $c$ for every $c>0$.
An algorithm for solving the Burgers equation based on rational approximations and the collocation method
I. A. Bugoets; B. V. Semisalov

We propose a numerical method for solving initial-boundary value problems for the Burgers equation that takes into account the presence of singularities of the analytic continuation of the solution into the complex plane. The algorithm uses rational approximations, a collocation method and a new scheme for time discretization combined with the relaxation method. An adaptive strategy is developed to account for the location of the singular point of the solution. Solutions to the well-known benchmark problem with a sine-shaped initial condition are obtained for the values of the viscosity as low as nu = 10^-8. Verification of the numerical results in such an extreme parameter regime makes it necessary to modify a classical formula for the exact solution so as to avoid floating-point overflow during its computation. The developed method is compared with an algorithm employing the Runge-Kutta scheme, and the conditions under which each approach yields superior results are outlined. An important feature of the proposed method is its capability to track the singular point of the solution. To verify this, we consider a problem whose solution has a simple analytical form and demonstrate that the exact and approximate coordinates of the singular point of the solution agree with high accuracy, even when the singularity comes extremely close to the domain of the problem. Taking the location of the singular point into account yields significant gains in both accuracy and run time relative to other methods.
Ramsey numbers of loose triangles versus cliques
Ayush Basu; Abhishek Dhawan; Abhishek Methuku

An $r$-uniform loose triangle $C_3$ consists of three edges that intersect pairwise in exactly one vertex and have no vertex common to all three. For graphs, this is the usual triangle, and the Ramsey number $R(C_3,K_t)$ has order of magnitude $t^2/\log t$ by celebrated results of Ajtai, Komlós, and Szemerédi and of Kim.
 Kostochka, Mubayi, and Verstraëte proved that $R(C_3,K_t^{(r)})=O_r(t^{3/2})$ for every fixed $r\ge3$ and showed that this bound is sharp up to a logarithmic factor. Motivated by the logarithmic saving in the graph case, they conjectured in 2013 that the upper bound could be improved to $o(t^{3/2})$.This conjecture has since received significant attention and has been reiterated in several papers. We prove the conjecture by showing that, for every fixed $r\ge3$, \[
 R(C_3,K_t^{(r)})
 =O_r\left(\frac{t^{3/2}}{\sqrt{\log\log t}}\right). \]
On real-analytic non-degeneracy of left-symmetric algebras in dimension 3

In this paper, we show that any three-dimensional differentially non-degenerate left-symmetric algebra over $\mathbb R$ is non-degenerate both in the formal and real-analytic categories via the correspondence with Nijenhuis operators.
Stability Conditions on Twisted Derived Categories I: Existence and Full Numerical Support

We prove that for every nonempty smooth projective variety $X$ over an arbitrary field and every Brauer class $α$, the twisted derived category $D^b(X,α)$ admits a Bridgeland stability condition with full numerical support. Based on Chunyi Li's construction and its extension to arbitrary fields, we establish uniform phase control under tensoring by an Azumaya algebra and calibrate the resulting slicing to the induced central charge. We further show that the constructed stability condition is geometric and satisfies a mass--Hom bound, which persists throughout its connected component.
Gradient stability for the Sobolev inequality with optimal dimensional dependence

Figalli and Zhang [29] established gradient stability for the sharp Sobolev inequality with the optimal exponent $r_p=\max\{2,p\}$. We prove that, for every fixed $p>1$, the corresponding optimal stability constant $\mathsf C_{n,p}$ admits effective upper and lower bounds of order $n^{-1}$ for all integers $n>p$. In particular, the dimensional dependence $n^{-1}$ is optimal. Our result extends the optimal dimensional dependence established for $p=2$ by Dolbeault, Esteban, Figalli, Frank, and Loss [18] to every $p>1$.
On the packing-dimension analogue of Bourgain's constant

For every $n\geq 2$, we construct a domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose harmonic measure has packing dimension $n$. That is, the packing analogue of Bourgain's constant is zero, in contrast with Bourgain's constant, which is positive. Moreover, the elliptic measure of the same domain also has packing dimension $n$ for every uniformly elliptic matrix.
Permutation polynomials of given index up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence

Let $q$ be a prime power and let $\ell$ be a divisor of $q-1$. We classify the permutation polynomials of $\mathbb F_q$ of polynomial index exactly $\ell$ up to quasi-multiplicative equivalence $G(X)\equiv uF(vX^d)\pmod{X^q-X}$, where $u,v\in\mathbb F_q^*$ and $\gcd(d,q-1)=1$, and we count the classes. For polynomials vanishing at $0$, the classes are the orbits of an explicit finite group on vectors of values at the $\ell$-th roots of unity. Through the permutation it induces on the roots of unity, each orbit lies over a double coset of the symmetric group $S_\ell$ with respect to its translation subgroup and an explicit affine group, and the stabilizers are explicit. For polynomials with nonzero constant term the action is free. Burnside's lemma, Möbius inversion over the coefficient support and congruences along the cycles of affine permutations give an exact formula for the number of classes. For fixed $\ell\geqslant2$ these numbers are quasi-polynomials in $s=(q-1)/\ell$ of degree at most $\ell-1$, with period dividing $\ell$ for odd $\ell$ and $2\ell$ for even $\ell$; for polynomials vanishing at $0$ the degree is exactly $\ell-1$, and we determine the leading coefficient. For odd prime $\ell$ and for $\ell=4$ the counts are given in closed form. For index four we also count the binomials and trinomials at each admissible coefficient support. The sums of two binomial counts that occur are expressed through quartic Jacobi sums and Frobenius traces of elliptic curves and of a curve of genus two; one of the elliptic curves is the reduction of the curve $Y^2=X^3+8X^2+32X$, which has no complex multiplication over $\mathbb Q$. The trinomial counts are expressed through quartic cyclotomic numbers and these sums. All these terms cancel when the counts with a fixed residue of the vanishing order modulo $s$ are added.
GFF for 3D Ising interfaces in three moves of Tetris

We show that at sufficiently large inverse-temperature $β>0$, the 3D Ising model on the torus, under boundary conditions that have a positive slope $θ_1,θ_2>0$, has a GFF scaling limit for its interface. The proof goes through three steps of a Tetris map, which lets cubes drop according to gravity in each of the three axes, yielding Solid-On-Solid (SOS), Half-Monotone SOS (HMSOS) and monotone surfaces (dimers). Rohrbach's conjecture holds for finite groups. To the best of our knowledge, the only prior fully discrete strong convergence analysis of explicit stabilized integrators for SPDEs is due to [A. Abdulle et al. IMA J. Numer. We prove tightness of the joint renormalized lattice gauge-Higgs laws, after continuum extension, as the lattice spacing tends to zero and the volume tends to infinity. For the gauge field, we establish high-frequency estimates for the effective force and combine them with quantitative diamagnetic control in the infrared.

We study Chern characteristic classes of normal vector bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ in complex generalized flag manifolds $G_n/P_n$. This procedure can be regarded as the relative version of Schubert calculus for the pair $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ and $G_n/P_n$. The CW structure and additive structure of the cohomology of $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$ allows inductive calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$. The combination of representation theory and algebraic geometry allows to derive analogous properties for the isotropic Grassmannians $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$ via their embeddings in $\mathrm{Gr}(m, k)$. Then the induced CW structure yields the additive structure on the cohomology of $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$, and consequently leads to the calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$.

For any fixed integers $q\ge2$ and $t\ge1$, we construct explicit $q$-ary codes of length $n$ that correct any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions, and substitutions, with redundancy at most $2t\log_q n+O_{q,t}(\log\log n)$ $q$-ary symbols. This matches the leading redundancy term of Levenshtein's classical existential bound. Building on the standard graph-coloring approach, we use a prime-based multicoloring of the edit-confusion graph to assign multiple colors to each $q$-ary word of length $m<n$. Appending a short, edit-protected representation of an assigned color to the length-$m$ word yields a length-$n$ codeword. The choice among the assigned colors carries additional message information, thereby reducing the redundancy. The construction admits deterministic encoding and decoding in $\widetilde O_{q,t}(n^{6t+2})$ and $\widetilde O_{q,t}(n^{7t+2})$ time, respectively.
Congruences involving the products of three binomial coefficients II
Estimates of short exponential sums with primes in major arcs

When solving a number of additive problems with almost equal summands, along with estimating short trigonometric sums with primes of the form $$ S_k(α;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}Λ(n)e(αn^k), $$ on the minor arcs, estimates of these sums on the major arcs are also needed, except in a small neighborhood of their centers, as well as an asymptotic formula in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs.
 In this paper, using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line, for $S_k(α;x,y)$ on the major arcs $\mathfrak{M}(\mathscr{L}^b)$, $τ=y^5x^{-2}\mathscr{L}^{-b_1}$, $\mathscr{L} =\ln xq$, except in a small neighborhood of their centers $|α-\frac{a}{q}|>\left(2πk^2x^{k-2}y^2\right)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{1}{2k-1+η_k}}\mathscr{L}^{c_k}$, $$ η_k=\frac{2}{4k-5+2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}}, \qquad c_k=
 \frac{2A+22+\left(\frac{2\sqrt{2k-3}}{\sqrt{2k-2}}-1\right)b_1}{2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}-(2k-3)}, $$ a nontrivial estimate of the form $$ S_k(α;x,y)\ll y\mathscr{L}^{-A}, $$ is obtained, where $A$, $b_1$, $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive numbers, and an asymptotic formula is proved in a small neighborhood of the centers of the major arcs.
A new proof of nonamenability for free Burnside groups of odd exponent
Anna Cascioli; Sam Shepherd; Katrin Tent

We prove that the free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is nonamenable for every $m\ge 2$ and every odd exponent $n\ge 557$. This improves Adian's bound $n\ge 665$ and matches the infiniteness bound of Atkarskaya, Rips and Tent. Our proof combines their canonical form construction with a counting argument to obtain an explicit isoperimetric inequality.
Finite cyclic monodromy in BMS3 gravity

We investigate inducing data for three dimensional asymptotically flat BMS gravity on hyperbolic Virasoro orbits with winding, which contain no constant supermomentum, and the restriction of formal smooth equivariant sections to global Lorentz orbits. Using the developing map of the associated Hill operator we rederive their stabilizer and show that, in the spin double cover, it is the direct product of a line with a cyclic group of even order. The character of the cyclic factor is therefore a discrete inducing label independent of the continuous one, unlike for the massive BMS particles, where it is fixed by the spin. At points with the corresponding finite rotational symmetry, restriction of formal smooth equivariant sections to a global Lorentz orbit yields the finite cyclic equivariance condition, while an independently defined unitary global branch realizes the associated finite difference equation. At points with timelike projected momentum we derive the resulting ladder of Poincare helicities, show that the projected rest energy is not an orbit invariant, construct locally flat winding BMS geometries with hyperbolic Lorentz holonomy, prove that the smooth real periodic near horizon current model excludes these winding orbits, and obtain selection rules and closed form expressions for finite monodromy resolved orbital functionals. A unitary realization on the full infinite dimensional orbit is not constructed, and the interpretation of the cyclic sectors in quantum gravity remains conjectural.
Finiteness of strongly reflective modular forms

Let $Γ\subset\mathrm{O}^+(n,2)$ be a rational arithmetic group with $n\geq 3$. A non-constant modular form for $Γ$ is called strongly reflective if its zero divisor is a reduced union of mirrors of reflections in $Γ$. We show that, up to conjugation and multiplication by a nonzero scalar, there are only finitely many strongly reflective modular forms. As a consequence, we establish the finiteness of holomorphic automorphic products of singular weight. These results answer a question posed by Borcherds in 1995 and settle a conjecture of Gritsenko--Nikulin from 1998. As an application, up to conjugation, we prove the finiteness of $Γ$ whose corresponding algebra of modular forms is freely generated. The key ingredient is a uniform upper bound on the covolume of $Γ$, obtained by adapting the higher-rank lattice convergence theorem of Abért et al. to the study of the degrees of reflective branch divisors.
Automatic Threshold Selection Leaves Finite-Degree Bias in Network Power-Law Fits

Minimum-distance fitting selects a degree threshold and a power-law exponent from the same network. We study the procedure that fits a continuous Pareto law with the Hill estimator and minimizes the Kolmogorov--Smirnov distance over retained ranks. For homogeneous linear preferential attachment and Norros--Reittu graphs with Pareto weights, we derive the joint limiting law of the selected rank, retained fraction of the threshold tie, and exponent error. The selector retains of order $n^{2/(α+2)}$ of $n$ vertices, where $α$ is the survival exponent. At this rank, integer spacing and finite-degree departures from a Pareto tail have the same order as sampling fluctuations. The exponent estimate is consistent and retains a shift on the scale used for confidence intervals. For integer degree laws whose tail sums have a first-order inverse-degree expansion, adding the retained tie fraction divided by the threshold to the Hill statistic removes the leading contribution of the tie. Under homogeneous preferential attachment with a fixed known number of edges per new vertex, removing the remaining model-specific term and calibrating for selection gives confidence intervals with asymptotically exact coverage. Observed networks show sensitivity of the fitted exponent and the classification of degree variance to threshold ties. Simulations assess interval coverage and show improved pooled connectivity predictions after correction under both specified graph laws. Changes to the Norros--Reittu weight distribution can reverse the prediction gain.
Morse index, nullity and Jacobi fields of homogeneous minimal two-spheres in complex hyperquadrics
Qing Chen; Shuping Huang; Shoulan Yi

We determine the Morse index and normal nullity of all linearly full homogeneous minimal two-spheres in complex hyperquadrics. These invariants satisfy a common relation involving only the ambient dimension and the induced Gauss curvature. We also prove that every normal Jacobi field is integrable through minimal immersions.
Uniqueness of addition in Schrödinger algebras

We obtain a criterion for the uniqueness of addition in Schrödinger Lie algebras, applicable to both bijections and injections. This allows us to construct the first example of a Lie algebra with unique addition and a non-trivial center over a field of characteristic zero. Furthermore, a necessary and sufficient condition is established for the Schrödinger algebras to have bracket width one.
Observability from Measurable Sets for Heat Equations with Bounded Space-Time Potentials

We establish final-state observability for heat equations with real-valued bounded space--time potentials on bounded $C^2$ domains, from arbitrary measurable space--time sets of positive measure. On $\mathbb R^n$, we prove observability from time-dependent sets whose spatial slices are uniformly thick on a set of times of positive measure. A counterexample for the free heat equation on $\mathbb R$ shows that integral thickness alone is insufficient for observability.
Classification and Geometry of Loxodromic Curves on Surfaces of Revolution in Three-Dimensional Euclidean Space

This paper investigates the global geometry of loxodromes and loxodromic curves on surfaces of revolution in $\mathbb{R}^3$. A loxodrome is a regular curve avoiding the poles and making a constant directed angle with the meridians. To allow curves to reach or pass through poles, we introduce loxodromic curves, whose pole-free interior portions are loxodromes. The directed azimuths of these portions agree modulo $π$.
 We classify surfaces of revolution into four types based on the number of poles and whether the profile curve is closed: cylinder-like, torus-like, paraboloid-like, and sphere-like. For cylinder-like surfaces, every maximal loxodromic curve other than a parallel is non-self-intersecting. For torus-like surfaces, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves are closed or dense according to the rationality of their rotation numbers. For paraboloid-like and sphere-like surfaces, only maximal meridians can pass smoothly through poles, while nonmeridional, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves have poles as endpoints.
 We derive the differential equations for arc-length-parametrized loxodromes and introduce coordinates in which they are represented by straight lines. We solve the direct and inverse problems for loxodromic segments on all four surface types and give criteria for maximal loxodromic curves to be geodesics. We show that diffeomorphisms preserving maximal loxodromic curves preserve surface type and that their inverses preserve such curves. These maps preserve maximal meridians and parallels on surfaces with poles, but need not do so on pole-free surfaces. We characterize azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms and, for cylinder-like surfaces, establish criteria for conformality and isometry. In particular, azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms are conformal when both surfaces have poles.
Concentration of Quasimodes at Spherical Interface between 3D-Topological Insulators

In this work, we study the edge states localized at a spherical interface between two $3\mathrm{D}$-topological insulators from a continuous model of the semiclassical Dirac equation. Using the dynamical and spectral properties of the semiclassical Dirac operator tangent to the interface and the Landau level stratification of the energy in the transverse variable, we describe several concentration and invariance properties of the semiclassical measures associated with quasimodes of the system localized at the interface. Moreover, we construct explicit quasimodes which fulfill some of these properties and concentrate on some particular single periodic geodesics of the sphere.
Nevanlinna theory for generalized tropical meromorphic functions and applications to ultra-discrete equations
Tingbin Cao; Risto Korhonen; Yuting Wang

The main purpose of this paper is to establish the tropical Nevanlinna theory to piecewise linear real functions with arbitrary first-kind discontinuities (called generalized tropical meromorphic functions). The key point is that we introduce the directional jump counting functions $J^+(r,f)$ and $J^-(r,f)$ for the case of arbitrary first-kind discontinuities to refine the single function $J(r,f)$ in the previous theory. We first obtain the new tropical version of the Poisson-Jensen formula, the first main theorem. Under the assumption that $f$ is slope-admissible, we show that $T(r,f)$ is nondecreasing and establish a logarithmic derivative lemma. These results unify the classical continuous case due to Halburd and Southall and the one-sided continuous case due to Halonen, Korhonen and Filipuk.
 As applications, we study several first-order and second-order ultra-discrete equations, showing that certain equations admit infinitely many generalized tropical meromorphic solutions, and that under suitable conditions infinite-order solutions also exist. Finally, using the logarithmic derivative lemma obtained above, we establish a tropical Clunie lemma.
Finite Bodies on Norton's Dome: Escape-Time Divergence and a Center-of-Mass Barrier Theorem

Norton's dome illustrates how a Newtonian initial-value problem can admit both rest and delayed departure from the same initial state. We examine how this nonuniqueness changes when the point particle is replaced by a rigid sphere of positive radius. For a generalized family of Norton's domes, we show that any fixed positive sphere radius prevents spontaneous departure from rest at the apex. We then extend the analysis to more general bodies and establish two sufficient conditions: a geometric constraint on the distance between the center of mass and the apex, and an interior tangent ball condition for rigid bodies whose center of mass is vertically aligned with the initial contact point. Both arguments combine geometric estimates with an energy inequality and Grönwall's inequality. The first condition also applies to passive deformable bodies without releasable internal energy. These results identify explicit conditions under which finite-body geometry excludes the spontaneous motion allowed by Norton's point-particle model.
Parameter estimation in models with explosive drift and Gaussian noise
Yuliya Mishura; Kostiantyn Ralchenko; Mykyta Yakovliev

We study drift parameter estimation for a positive stochastic process with singular mean-reverting drift driven by Gaussian noise. For Riemann-Liouville fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter $H>1/2$, an observable fractional transformation reduces the model to a semimartingale with drift linear in the unknown parameters. Using the quasi-likelihood approach, we derive explicit estimators of both drift coefficients. For a broader class of Gaussian driving processes, we construct a strongly consistent estimator of the ratio $a/b$, which has a natural mean-reversion interpretation, and verify the required assumptions for several Gaussian models. The theoretical results are complemented by a simulation study investigating the effects of the observation horizon and the discretization step on the finite-sample accuracy of the proposed estimators.
Intrinsic reduction data and the loci related to indeterminacy of iterate maps for rational functions

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of not necessarily characteristic $0$, and $d,n$ be integers $\ge 2$. We first formulate the dynamical moduli spaces of rational functions defined over $k$ in terms of the intrinsic reduction data of non-archimedean rational functions. As an application, we show that the locus $C_{d,n}$ of semistable intrinsic reduction data in degree $d$ whose $n$th iteration is defined and unstable is of codimension $d$ in the intrinsic reduction data space of degree $d$, settling a conjecture of Kiwi and Nie, and show that the image of $C_{d,n}$ in the compactified dynamical moduli $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{d,k}$ is of dimension $\le d-2$ and the equality holds precisely either if $d$ is even or if $d\ge 5$ is odd and $(4/d)^n<1/(d-3)$ and determine the dimensions even for all the five exceptional pairs $(d,n)$, in addition describing the images of $C_{3,n}$ themselves. We also determine the indeterminacy of iterate maps either on the intrinsic reduction data spaces or on the compactified dynamical moduli spaces.
Boundary Actuation of a Chain Fountain - Physically Admissible Tracking, Stochastic Limits and Zero-Gravity Circulation

This paper was inspired by a post on Twitter and by the eight months the author spent at the AASS Centre at Orebro University in 2007. This phenomenon is interesting not only to a physicist, but also to someone like me working in control theory, because of its potential relevance to stabilizing drones and similar flying machines subject to random velocity fluctuations while hovering. A chain fountain can settle without an engineered controller, yet its natural height is selected by transport and boundary forces. We ask how an ideal boundary traction force can sustain a prescribed height or motion. Within an established three-state model, we connect feedback design to force and energy balances and derive sufficient conditions for nominal tracking that preserve the model's mechanical constraints. We also bound the deviations caused by bounded pickup uncertainty. The resulting framework explains how feedback can shape a naturally regulated process and identifies physical limits on the motions it can sustain: stabilizing a mathematical trajectory is useful only if the corresponding motion remains mechanically admissible. This is a preliminary step towards stabilization of the chain in three dimensions.
Data-Driven Robust Inventory Planning and Advertising under Product Return
Hongyan Zhang; Yugang Yu; Qinshen Tang; Ye Shi; Li Chen

Online advertising is a central marketing lever for e-commerce retailers, yet it complicates operational planning by simultaneously stimulating product demand and increasing product returns. Motivated by the practice of a fashion retailer on Amazon, we study a retailer's joint inventory and advertising problem across multiple products over a single season, in which advertising has both direct and cross-product spillover effects on demand and returns. Using linear net-demand and return models that capture both effects, we formulate a contextual stochastic optimization model that jointly determines inventory levels and advertising decisions before the selling season. Because ad clicks are realized only after the advertising decision, the predictive covariates are partially observable and decision-dependent, and their joint distribution with the demand and return errors is unknown. We therefore develop an estimate-then-robustify (ETR) approach grounded in a data-driven robust satisficing framework. We establish a finite-sample guarantee on the out-of-sample profit of the ETR solution that holds for any parameter estimator, show that the solution is asymptotically optimal when the estimator is consistent and the profit target approaches the empirical optimal profit, and derive a mixed-integer conic approximation via affine recourse adaptation that is exact for a single product. On the retailer's data, ETR improves out-of-sample profit over conventional estimate-then-optimize by 6.39\% and earns the higher profit in 74.5% of instances, with the largest gains when training data are scarce; the gain falls to 1.02% when the decision model omits cross-product spillovers.
Three Lipschitz functions on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with no common point of Fréchet differentiability

We prove that on every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(H\), there exist three real-valued Lipschitz functions with no common point of Fréchet differentiability. This gives a negative answer to a longstanding question of Lindenstrauss, Preiss, and Tišer. The proof is constructive and relies on elementary calculus and finite-dimensional linear algebra. Since every Lipschitz map from a Hilbert space into $\mathbb R^2$ has a point of Fréchet differentiability, the target dimension three is optimal.
Key Relay and Secure Network Coding: One-Shot Equivalence and Separation on Undirected Networks
Yuji Ando; Edmund Chen; Go Kato; Toyohiro Tsurumaru; Derek Zhang; Donald Zvada

Motivated by quantum key distribution networks, we compare key relay protocols with secure network coding on the same undirected graph. In this comparison, we fix the finite field, terminal set, and wiretap family. Each edge supplies one independent uniform symbol to its endpoints for key relay, or carries one symbol once for network coding. The network code may choose its source terminal, edge orientations, and causal transmission order before execution. In this setting, the standard one-time-pad simulation readily converts every secure network code to key relay. We investigate the reverse conversion to linear network coding. For two terminals and a one-symbol key, arbitrary key relay is equivalent to scalar linear acyclic network coding over the prescribed field. The proof uses connectivity and flow conservation, related to the binary $st$-flow protocol. However, this equivalence fails in general when several terminals seek one common key. A doubled triangle separates key relay from acyclic coding but admits causal coding on a cyclic orientation. On the four-terminal complete graph, a linear key relay protocol over the ternary field withstands the three perfect-matching wiretap sets, whereas no linear causal network code distributes a source symbol of the same size, even with private randomness at every vertex and its use in decoding. We also establish a linear key relay normal form that removes interaction and private randomness and bounds public communication. All results concern one-shot feasibility with exact agreement and perfect secrecy.
Novel upper bounds for Borsuk numbers from contact points and spherical partitions

Let $b(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every bounded set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ of positive diameter can be partitioned into $m$ sets of smaller diameter. We prove that \[
 b(4)\le6,\qquad b(5)\le12,\qquad b(6)\le31,\qquad b(7)\le45,\qquad b(8)\le89, \] and that \[
 b(n)\le1+2^{n-1}\left(\tfrac{39}{64}\right)^{\lfloor(n-1)/8\rfloor}
 \qquad\text{for every } n\ge9 ; \] for instance, $b(9)\le157$ and $b(17)\le24337$. Further constructions give, for example, $b(10)\le289$ and $b(13)\le2313$. These bounds improve Lassak's bound $b(n)\le2^{n-1}+1$ of 1982 in every dimension $n\ge4$. In dimension four they also improve the recent bounds $b(4)\le8$ (Tolmachev and Voronov, May 2026) and $b(4)\le7$ (Arman, Bondarenko, Prymak and Radchenko, October 2026); the bound $b(4)\le6$ was announced independently by Chalmers in November 2026.
 The bounds for $n\ge7$ have analytic proofs: a quantitative form of Lassak's reduction to coverings of the sphere is combined with normal partitions of weighted vector configurations, for which the smallest inner product within a region is estimated explicitly. The bound for $n=6$ uses a covering of $S^4$ by thirty sets, checked in rational arithmetic. For $n=4,5$ three contact points of the circumscribed ball reduce the problem to a four-parameter family of bodies, which is split by finitely many power diagrams; that all parts have diameter less than one is verified by a computer program with rigorous error control.
On the randomized lattice-point count problem

Counting (integer) lattice points in a convex body $K$ has a rich history, beginning with the famous circle problem imposed by Gauss in 1834. Clearly, the number of covered lattice points depends on the position, orientation, size, and shape of $K$ in a delicate way. In 1947, Kendall was the first to consider a randomized version of this problem by allowing random translations of $K$. In this survey, we aim to provide an overview of the current state of research on the \emph{randomized lattice-point count problem}, i.e.\ on the distribution of the lattice-point count under random rotations and translations of $K$. As it turns out, even the variance is far from being well-understood, leaving multiple open questions for future research. The motivation for the present work grew out of the author's research interest in a related combinatorial problem, dealing with the convex hull of all covered lattice points.
Integrals over Hilbert schemes and multiple $q$-zeta values

We establish a version of Okounkov's conjecture on multiple $q$-zeta values arising from integrals over Hilbert schemes of points on smooth projective surfaces. We prove that normalized generating series of integrals involving products of Chern characters of tautological bundles belong to the algebra $\mathcal Z_q$ of multiple $q$-zeta values, without restrictions on the canonical class of the surface. The proof combines vertex-operator methods with a reduction to graph sums, whose arithmetic structure is governed by the cohomology of the surface. We also derive a closed universal formula for the Chern character operators acting on the cohomology of Hilbert schemes by solving a system of differential equations arising from Lehn's commutator relations.
Composition loci, invariant Bezoutians, and finite-orbit correspondences

We compute projective degrees of composition loci for polynomial and rational maps of the projective line. For normalized polynomials of degree $rs$ with a right composition factor of degree $s$, a projective-bundle construction gives the degree $S(r+s-2,r)$. We extend this calculation to composition chains, and obtain $S(r+s-1,r)$ in the uncentered normalization used for decomposable interpolation. For rational maps, a Grassmann-bundle model gives a Plücker degree formula and an interpretation by prescribed critical points. We relate these loci to factorization of the Bezoutian in the ring of symmetric polynomials, where factors correspond to monodromy orbits on unordered pairs. Fried's polynomial criterion then determines the invariant reducibility locus. For rational maps we determine its composition components when a marked pole fiber has exactly one ramified point and at least one unramified point. The qualitative equivalence between finite full orbits and a first integral is already known. We give a direct proof from forward stabilization, with an explicit test using bounded forward orbits and with quotient fibers identified at every point. We also determine when absolute and invariant irreducibility differ and give a growth formula for a class of translation correspondences.
Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration

The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with Hölder-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the Hölder topology.
Eventual Collisional Relaxation After Large Echo-Driven Amplification in a Weakly Collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System

We study the weakly collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system near a Maxwellian equilibrium and construct global classical solutions exhibiting large transient growth before eventual collisional relaxation. The main mechanism is a nonlinear plasma-echo cascade which remains effective up to the enhanced-dissipation time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$, producing norm inflation of size larger than $ν^{-1}$ from arbitrarily small $ν$-dependent perturbations. At the same time, the nonzero spatial modes decay at the enhanced-dissipation scale $e^{-rν^{\frac13}t}$, while the zero mode relaxes at the thermal scale $e^{-νt}$. The estimates also reveal a sharp contrast in the smoothing effects before and after the collisional time scale $t\sim ν^{-1}$. As a consequence, our construction gives explicit upper bounds on the Sobolev and Gevrey stability thresholds: perturbations of the corresponding $ν$-dependent sizes can still trigger severe echo-driven amplification before collisional dissipation becomes dominant at the critical time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$.
Propositional Dynamic Logic without tests does not have Craig Interpolation

It was shown recently by Borzechowski et al. (2026) that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has Craig Interpolation. Whether test-free PDL, i.e. PDL without the `?' operator, has interpolation remained open. Here we answer this question in the negative with a counterexample: a test-free PDL validity for which no test-free interpolant exists. The validity only uses one atomic program and the Kleene star, so it implies that the basic modal logic K extended with the reflexive transitive closure does not have interpolation, as previously shown by Studer (2009).
 The example was originally obtained using LLMs and Lean. We describe our methodology and provide links to all prompts, LLM output summaries as well as the Lean proof.
A risk-aware individualized blood pressure target to avoid hypotension in surgery
Simon Bur{é}; Jona Joachim; Florent Di Meglio

We propose an online method for choosing both a blood pressure target and a norepinephrine dose for an individual surgical patient. From a short record of mean arterial pressure (MAP) and norepinephrine delivery, the method fits a reduced pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model and uses a local Gaussian approximation to propagate uncertainty to future MAP readings. It searches for the lowest target for which a bolus and constant infusion keep the predicted probability of at least one MAP reading below 65 mmHg after the rise phase within a prescribed limit. If no such target is found, the decision returns to the clinician. We assess calibration of the predicted minimum MAP on retrospective surgical records under the doses actually administered. In a cohort of 4,096 virtual patients, the method recommended a dose for 74 % of patients at a nominal risk of 5 %. Among the patients receiving a recommendation, 6.9 % had a reading below 65 mmHg. A fixed target of 70 mmHg yielded a rate of 25 % when applied to the full virtual cohort.
Existence, Nonexistence, and Regularity Results for Supercritical Quasilinear Elliptic Problems with Hardy Potential
Boumediene Abdellaoui; Susana Merchán; Luigi Montoro

In this paper, we investigate the existence of solutions to the following supercritical elliptic problem involving the $p$-Laplace operator and the Hardy-Leray potential \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{array}{rcll}
 -Δ_p u +u^β|\nabla u|^p &= & {\vartheta} \dfrac{u^q }{|x|^p}+ f\;\; &\hbox{in } Ω
 u &\geq & 0\;\; &\hbox{in } Ω
 u &= & 0\;\;&\hbox{on } \partialΩ, \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} where $0\inΩ$. We analyze the effect of the perturbation term $u^β|\nabla u|^p$, with $β\geq 0$, and the role of the exponent $q$ on the existence of solutions. We also analyze nonexistence of solutions when $f$ is a singular measure. Finally, we focus on the regularity and asymptotic properties of these solutions.
Strong Completeness of Provability Logic for Languages of size at most continuum

We investigate the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ for an infinite set of propositional variables $\mathbb P$ over ordinal spaces equipped with the interval topology $\mathcal{I}_1$. For every infinite cardinal $κ$, we consider the set \[ Γ_κ= \{\Diamond p_ξ:ξ<κ\} \cup \{\Box(p_ξ\to\Diamond p_η):ξ<η<κ\}, \] and prove that $Γ_κ$ has a model on an ordinal space with $\mathcal{I}_1$ if and only if $κ\nrightarrow_{\mathrm{ipath}}(ω)^2_{ω,<ω}$. We also prove that if $|\mathbb P|<\mathfrak p$, then $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ is strongly complete with respect to $(ω^ω+1,\mathcal I_1)$. Finally, we establish the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ with respect to the same space whenever $|\mathbb P|=\aleph_1$.
Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements

Machine learning coupled with device simulation is widely used to optimize thin-film solar cells, but almost exclusively in the forward direction, from device parameters to predicted performance. The inverse problem encountered after fabrication, namely identifying the mechanism that limits a given device, is still addressed by manual inspection of characterization data. In this work, both directions are examined for lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells using approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations. Replacing the Spiro-OMeTAD hole transport layer with CuI increases the simulated power conversion efficiency from 19.6\% to 21.6\%, almost entirely through the fill factor. Surrogate models trained and tested on a factorial parameter grid substantially overstate their predictive accuracy. An XGBoost regressor attains $R^2 = 0.9997$ on held-out grid points but only 0.58 on independently sampled devices, whereas training on a Latin hypercube design of comparable size restores $R^2 = 0.995$. For the inverse problem, a multi-label classifier identifies which of six degradation mechanisms are present from simulated temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit-voltage measurements. It achieves a macro $F_1$ score of 0.938, compared to 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline. The classifier does not, however, generalize to combinations of mechanisms absent from the training set.
Topological Entropy of Group Cellular Automata is Effectively Computable
Niccolò Castronuovo; Alberto Dennunzio; Jarkko Kari; Luciano Margara

Topological entropy is a fundamental invariant of dynamical systems, quantifying their complexity. For cellular automata, however, determining topological entropy is generally algorithmically intractable. We study group cellular automata, namely cellular automata over a finite group alphabet whose global map is a group endomorphism.
 In dimension one, we decompose topological entropy into two one-sided components describing information propagating from the left and from the right in space--time. We introduce finite families of left and right traces and prove that the entropy is the sum of their growth rates. Hence, the entropy is completely determined by the growth rate of a fixed-width family of space--time patterns. This reduction from arbitrarily large windows to uniformly bounded width yields an effective procedure for computing the entropy. In particular, the entropy of every one-dimensional group cellular automaton is the logarithm of a positive integer.
 Using Pontryagin duality and the Bridge Theorem between topological and algebraic entropy, we also derive an explicit formula for linear cellular automata over $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n$ in terms of their characteristic polynomial. Moreover, in every dimension $D\geq 2$, a group cellular automaton is either equicontinuous with zero entropy or sensitive to initial conditions with infinite entropy. Combined with decidability of equicontinuity, this implies that topological entropy is effectively computable from the local rule in every dimension.
 Thus, group cellular automata form a natural nontrivial class in which algebraic structure restores computability of topological entropy.
Fluctuations of sample eigenvalues in a spiked covariance model with Haar-rotated spikes: a transition at $p^2 \asymp n$

We study the outlying eigenvalues of a sample covariance matrix whose population covariance is itself random. The population covariance is $Σ_p=A_p+O_pB_pO_p^*+σ^2I_p$, where $A_p$ and $B_p$ are deterministic positive semidefinite matrices of fixed ranks $r$ and $s$, and where $O_p$ is Haar distributed on the orthogonal group in the real case, and on the unitary group in the complex case. Conditionally on $O_p$, we observe $n$ independent centered Gaussian vectors with covariance $Σ_p$, and we build the sample covariance matrix $\widehatΣ_p$ from these vectors. The fluctuations of the spike eigenvalues of $\widehatΣ_p$ come from two different sources: the Haar matrix $O_p$, which displaces the population spikes at the scale $1/p$, and the sampling, which acts at the scale $n^{-1/2}$. Comparing these two scales amounts to comparing $p^2$ with $n$, so the ratio which governs the fluctuations is $p^2/n$, while in the classical spiked model it is the aspect ratio $p/n$. We give the limiting law of each spike in four regimes where $n,p\to \infty$. When $p/n\to c>0$, and when $p/n\to0$ with $p^2/n\to\infty$, the sampling term dominates, the limit does not depend on $O_p$ and is Gaussian, as in the classical spiked model. When $p^2/n\to0$, the Haar randomness dominates, and the limit is a weighted sum of independent $χ^2_1$ variables in the real case, and of independent exponential variables in the complex case. When $p^2/n\toτ\in(0,\infty)$, the two terms are of the same order, and the limit is the convolution of Gaussian and $χ^2_1$ or Exponential variables. We then apply these results to a linear mixed model with a continuous batch effect, in which the Haar assumption is what makes the separation of the signal and of the batch possible, and we build a test for the value of a single spike.
Invariant subspaces for integration and differentiation on convex domains

For a conformal map $g$ of the unit disc $U$ onto any bounded convex domain $Ω$ we determine the invariant subspaces for the integration operator $T_gf = \int_0^zfg'$ on the Hardy space $H^p$, by means of a Fock space model. Under some additional regularity assumptions on $\partialΩ$ we also treat integration from a boundary point of $U$, and we determine the residual subspaces (those invariant subspaces on which the operator has empty spectrum) for the left inverse $D_gf = f'/g'$ of $T_g$ on the smooth disc algebra $A^\infty$. The latter result is new even for $Ω= U$.
Exterior-Row Replacement for Grid-Based Multinode Shepard Collocation on Implicit Planar Domains
Anouar El Harrak; Amal Bergam; Hatim Tayeq

Grid-based multinode Shepard collocation combines tensor-product Lagrange interpolants on overlapping Cartesian subgrids. On an implicitly defined domain, retained subgrids may cross the boundary and contain exterior source nodes. Removing or moving these nodes changes the local interpolants. We introduce exterior-row replacement (ERR) to preserve the source nodes and coefficients of every retained subgrid. We assemble PDE rows at strictly interior sources and supply the remaining equations through boundary evaluations. We consider two square completion methods based on projection and redistribution, an oversampled weighted least-squares one (ERR-OS), and a completion method that selects boundary rows through the interior PDE nullspace (ERR-QR). Full column rank is characterized by the boundary action on this nullspace. We also give completion conditions for prescribed fitted rows and an error estimate in terms of the residual. Global-full (GF) support uses all retained subgrids, whereas nearest-active (NA) support uses only those containing the active source nearest to the evaluation point. NA keeps off-source boundary rows sparse. The numerical study covers a disk, an annulus, a smooth star-shaped domain, a square hole with fitted and implicit boundary components, and a fitted L-shaped domain. With degree-$4$ local tensor polynomials, ERR-OS and ERR-QR recover the expected fifth-order accuracy in the reported refinement study. Further experiments examine the effects of boundary oversampling and trimming on algebraic admissibility and boundary observability.
Asymptotic stability of self-similar blow-up for the two-dimensional Zakharov system
Tej-eddine Ghoul; Jie Liu; Nader Masmoudi

We prove asymptotic stability of the small-parameter Glangetas-Merle self-similar blow-up solutions of the two-dimensional Zakharov system under nonradial perturbations in the energy space. The proof establishes dissipation on the wave time scale by canceling the fast density coupling. We impose nonlinear orthogonality to the ground state of the density-dependent Schrödinger operator for modulation and use successive energy corrections after subtracting the instantaneous density response from the Schrödinger error. The resulting dissipation yields power-law decay of the rescaled errors in the Schrödinger gradient, weighted local mass, and wave energy norms.
Continuous Grassmannian Brascamp--Lieb inequalities and their equality cases

In this paper, we establish the forward and reverse geometric Brascamp--Lieb inequalities for isotropic measures on a Grassmann manifold, and characterize their equality conditions. The proofs use transportation and the Grassmannian Ball--Barthe inequality of Li, Xi, and Zhang. The functions form a jointly continuous family whose fiber integrals are positive and continuous. The equality conditions are described by an orthogonal decomposition determined by the supporting projections. On the common eigenspaces, the forward inequality permits arbitrary independent factors, whereas the reverse inequality requires log-concavity for factors shared by a nontrivial parameter distribution. On the orthogonal complement, the extremizers have Gaussian factors. Their centers are compatible projections in the forward inequality and may vary continuously between fibers in the reverse inequality. Gaussian convolution preserves extremizers, and the original factors are recovered at a fixed positive time using characteristic functions. As applications, we obtain Gaussian rigidity results and volume bounds for bodies defined by projection integrals and barycentric infima. These bounds recover the reverse isoperimetric inequalities of Li, Xi, and Zhang for bodies associated with Grassmannian cosine transforms, together with their equality conditions away from the endpoint cases. We also establish a forward extension under weaker mass assumptions and give a mass-escape example for the reverse inequality.

How well a superposition of nonorthogonal states, such as an optical cat state, serves as a resource depends on how its components interfere. Here we determine the optimal probability of converting one such superposition into another by superposition-free operations. These operations cannot make the components of a superposition interfere more destructively with certainty while keeping all of them, and this principle fixes the optimal probability for every source that is symmetric under permutations of its components. When the reference states are coherent states, as in a cat state, every operation that maps each of them to a coherent state, such as photon loss or photon subtraction, is superposition-free. For two reference states we solve the problem completely. Superpositions with coefficients of equal modulus, the counterparts of the maximally coherent states of coherence theory, are therefore inequivalent resources: an odd cat state becomes even with certainty by a normalized photon subtraction, whereas an even one becomes odd only with a probability that vanishes for small amplitudes, and the even and the Yurke$-$Stoler cat states cannot be converted into each other with certainty in either direction. Collective operations on several copies can do better than converting them one at a time, except in the distillation of coherence, which gains nothing from them.
