For three or more reference states with equal positive overlaps, no state reaches every other state with certainty; the equal-modulus superpositions that interfere most destructively still yield a maximally coherent state with certainty and reach every superposition of all reference states at least as well as such a state does, but in the worst case no better.
Higher moments of twisted Kloosterman sums and the arithmetic of algebraic varieties

For an odd prime $p,$ consider the affine varieties $X_k: \sum\limits_{i=1}^{k}(x_i+x_i^{-1})=0$ over the finite field $\F_p.$ In this paper, a key feature of our work is arithmetic interpretation between the higher power moments of Kloosterman sums, modular forms and arithmetic geometry of the varieties $X_5$ and $X_6$ through their rational point counts. Our main results provide two distinct explicit formulas for the point count $\#X_5(\F_p).$ In the first formula, we express $\#X_5(\F_p)$ in terms of Fourier coefficients of modular forms and a certain weighted average of fourth power twisted Kloosterman moments, where the average is taken over multiplicative characters. We further establish an identity expressing this weighted average of fourth power moment of twisted Kloosterman sums in terms of fifth power quadratic twisted Kloosterman moment, together with Fourier coefficients of modular forms. Moreover, we derive an independent expression for the same average with different weight directly in terms of Fourier coefficients of modular forms. In the second identity for $\#X_5(\F_p)$, we express this purely in terms of Fourier coefficients of two modular forms. Moreover, we express $\#X_6(\F_p),$ in terms of Fourier coefficients of three modular forms. For these two expressions of $\#X_5(\F_p)$ and $\#X_6(\F_p),$ our approach is based on an identity that relates the point counts of $X_k$ to the $k$-th power moments of Kloosterman sum and its quadratic twist.
Complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional: examples and rigidity
Giovanni Catino; Paolo Mastrolia; Dario Daniele Monticelli

We study complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional \[ g\mapsto\int_M S_g^2\,\dv_g, \] with criticality understood under compactly supported variations, focusing on rigidity phenomena and nontrivial examples. In dimension three, we prove that every complete critical metric is scalar-flat, without any additional assumption. In dimension four, we construct complete non-Einstein critical metrics with bounded, nonconstant negative scalar curvature. In every dimension $n\geq5$, we show that either $S_g\equiv 0$ or $S_g<0$ everywhere, and a new argument proves scalar-flatness whenever $S_g \in L^p$ for some $0<p\leq P_n$, where $P_n>2$ is an explicit threshold. Moreover, we construct complete critical metrics with bounded, negative scalar curvature, decaying to zero at infinity. These examples establish the optimality of our rigidity threshold $P_n$ in dimension six and in every dimension $n\geq10$. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first complete critical metrics for this functional that are neither scalar-flat nor Einstein.
Thermodynamically Consistent Quantum-Classical Hybrid Dynamics: A Metriplectic Approach to Generalized Lindblad and Bloch-Torrey Equations
Azeddine Zaidni; Ayoub Arraji; Philip J. Morrison

We develop a metriplectic framework for quantum--classical hybrid dynamics that ensures thermodynamic consistency through conservation of energy and non-negative entropy production. The approach combines a hybrid Poisson bracket with a metriplectic $4$-bracket, with coupling between quantum and classical subsystems arising solely through dissipative processes. Within this hybrid formulation, we produce thermodynamically consistent generalizations of the Lindblad master equations and the Bloch--Torrey equations for open quantum systems. This provides a unified description of quantum relaxation and classical diffusion, together with a clear interpretation of entropy production.
Data-Driven Discovery and Rigorous Certification of Periodic Solutions in Infinite-Dimensional Dynamical Systems
Aaron Loh; J. D. Mireles James

In this work, we consider a standard regression technique for time series analysis which fits a low-dimensional proxy system to a higher (even infinite) dimensional target model. We then propose a novel diagnostic that exploits a-posteriori computer-assisted proofs, and try to certify the existence of a true periodic solution of the target, nearby. When successful, this certification procedure provides mathematically rigorous information about how well an invariant structure in the proxy approximates a corresponding invariant structure in the target model.
 To illustrate the utility of the procedure, we develop surrogates using time series data from the Mackey--Glass delay differential equation, and for the Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) partial differential equation, using periodic boundary conditions for forecasting and Neumann boundary conditions for certification. In both test cases we extract invariant dynamics from low-dimensional proxies and use this to validate the existence of corresponding structures in the targets.

We prove that a boundary point $p$ of a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\ge2$, is strictly pseudoconvex if the boundary is locally $C^{2,α}$ near $p$, $0<α\le1$, and the squeezing function tends to one along the inward normal. Neither finite type nor convexity is assumed. Under local $C^2$ regularity alone, the same limit gives the normal logarithmic Bergman-kernel growth exponent $n+1$. The proof uses normalized Bergman-kernel profiles and holomorphic translation semigroups on the ball.
History, mathematics and physics: two cases of the inverse square law

How did mathematicians of the past relate to history? What can we learn from their experience? It is a truism to say that all people are embedded in history. It impacts on them in ways that they may or may not realise. At the two extremes, some may be completely oblivious; others may deliberately set out to change the historical narrative and the course of history.
 In this chapter, I explore these questions through two case studies. Both are of eminent British mathematicians/physicists in the late 1800s and their handling of an inverse square law of force. Both case studies show ways in which these men were blind to the history of their subject, conscious of it but limited by it, or deliberately trying to use it.
 First, I look at William Thomson's and James Clerk Maxwell's attempts to establish the inverse square law of electrostatics in the 1850s to 1870s. I ask the question, why did Maxwell devote the last years of his life to editing the 100-year-old electrical researches of Henry Cavendish and repeating Cavendish's experimental verification of the inverse square law of electrostatic repulsion?
 Second, I discuss John Henry Poynting and Newton's law of gravitation in the 1880s and 1890s, asking why Poynting preferred to describe his experiments as measurements of the mean density of the Earth rather than of the gravitational constant.
The q-Jack Lemma and Its Applications

In this paper, we establish a Jackson $q$-difference analogue of Jack's lemma and its higher-order extension by Miller and Mocanu, which serve as cornerstone tools in geometric function theory and differential subordination. Applying this foundation, we establish $q$-counterparts of Nunokawa's boundary theorem and the Miller-Mocanu subordination lemma, and deduce applications to circular enclosure bounds. All obtained results naturally recover their classical counterparts in the limiting case as $q \to 1^-$.
Free Gödel algebras over Gödel hoops

We give an explicit description of the left adjoint $F$ of the forgetful functor $U\colon\mathsf{GAlg}\to\mathsf{GHoops}$ from Gödel algebras to Gödel hoops. If $H$ is a Gödel hoop with a least element $m$, then $F(H)$ is the direct product of the Gödel algebra obtained by adjoining a new bottom element to $H$ and of $H$ itself, regarded as a Gödel algebra with bottom element $m$. For an arbitrary Gödel hoop $H$, we glue these products along the principal filters of $H$, and we describe the operations of $F(H)$, the action of $F$ on homomorphisms and the unit of the adjunction. As an application, we show that the unit of the adjunction $F\dashv U$ is not cartesian, and that the same holds for BL-algebras and basic hoops. Moreover, the semi-abelian categories of Gödel hoops and of basic hoops are not equivalent to the slice categories of Gödel algebras and of BL-algebras over their initial object. Thus, in contrast with the cases of Wajsberg hoops and of product hoops, the free-forgetful adjunctions between Gödel algebras and Gödel hoops, and between BL-algebras and basic hoops, do not give rise to ideally exact contexts.
Hilbert's 17th problem for symmetric functions: undecidability and a counterexample

We study inequalities between symmetric functions that hold in every number of variables. First, we prove that it is undecidable whether a symmetric function with rational coefficients is nonnegative in all dimensions, answering a question posed by Acevedo, Blekherman, Debus and Riener. As a consequence, the validity of dimension-free moment criteria for entanglement in quantum information is undecidable. Second, we present a homogeneous symmetric function of degree 8 which is positive definite in every dimension but admits no sum of squares multiplier that is uniform in the number of variables. Consequently, Artin's solution of Hilbert's 17th problem and the Krivine-Stengle Positivstellensatz have no any-dimensional analog and any-dimensional Positivstellensätze asked for by Levin and Chandrasekaran cannot hold in general.
An Analytic Toroidal MHD Equilibrium with Trivial Euclidean Symmetry Group

We provide a method to construct a real-analytic ideal MHD equilibrium $(B,p)$ in a solid toroidal domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{3}$, with $B$ tangential to the boundary $\partialΩ$. The regular pressure level sets foliate $Ω\setminusΓ$ by nested tori surrounding a magnetic axis $Γ$, with $\nabla p\neq0$ away from the axis. We construct an example where the magnetic field is nonvanishing on $Ω$, and the rotational transform equals 2 on every regular pressure surface. The equilibrium has a trivial Euclidean symmetry group. It is non-isolated in the sense that it belongs to a real-analytic one-parameter family connecting it to an axisymmetric equilibrium. The toroidal domain, magnetic field and pressure vary smoothly along this family. Under the MHD--Euler correspondence, the construction also yields a real-analytic steady incompressible Euler flow with a nonconstant Bernoulli function. This constructively disproves one formulation of Grad's conjecture by exhibiting a smooth toroidal MHD equilibrium with nested pressure surfaces whose Euclidean symmetry group is trivial.
Fluctuations of Local Patterns in Non-Periodic Uniquely Ergodic Systems

We study various families of non-periodic configurations of symbols assigned to vertices of regular graphs. We restrict ourselves to such systems where considered configurations support a uniquely ergodic measure. Symbols can be interpreted as particles and we are concerned with configurations which minimize the interaction energy of particles, the so-called ground-state configurations. One of the main questions then is whether ground-state configurations are stable with respect to small perturbations of interactions. Such stability may be interpreted as a sort of rigidity of non-periodic structures such as tilings, substitution systems, Sturmian systems, and other uniquely ergodic non-periodic systems. We introduce a property of bounded fluctuations of finite patterns of non-periodic configurations, the so-called Strict Boundary Property. We discuss how relevant this property is for stability of non-periodic structures. Examples of Robinson's tilings, Thue-Morse, and Sturmian systems are presented. Some open problems are formulated.
The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies
Linus Behn; Roberto Colombo; Xavier Fernández-Real; Florian Grube; Harsh Prasad; Xavier Ros-Oton

The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies asks whether uniform ellipticity implies $H^s$-coercivity for symmetric nonlocal kernels of order $2s$, with $0<s<1$. We show that the conjecture fails whenever $n>2s$ for every $s \in (0,1)$ and $n \geq 1$, even for smooth compactly supported test functions; for $n=1$ and $s>1/2$, we show that it holds. The construction also gives bounded discontinuous weak solutions in $H^s_{\rm loc}$ to nonlocal equations in divergence form with kernels in this class. Despite the failure, we show that the conjecture holds for several important classes of kernels. We establish a general local coercivity criterion based on annular cancellation, which applies in particular to kernels satisfying both divergence- and nondivergence-form symmetry. The criterion also allows us to treat kernels comparable to stable kernels with bounded measurable coefficients, as well as non-cutoff Boltzmann kernels under a geometric nonconcentration assumption. As an application, we obtain a short and self-contained proof of the Gressman--Strain anisotropic coercivity estimate. Furthermore, by combining our new criterion with existing regularity results, we obtain Hölder estimates under ellipticity and cancellation assumptions.
Immaculate complexes and Strong Generation by Injectives

We study the category of bounded complexes of finite sums of indecomposable injectives over a locally Noetherian scheme, which we call the immaculate complexes. We show that regularity and finiteness of dimension can be detected from this category using strong generation. Our methods involve studying when the unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck category is strongly generated by injectives. As applications we prove a conjecture of Hartshorne and recover a result of Keller and Krause. To any specialisation closed subset we associate a semi-orthogonal decomposition of the immaculates and use this to compute additive finitary invariants in terms of the completions of the local rings. The immaculates are equivalent to the perfect derived category of a left coherent preadditive category i.e. a ring with many objects and we compute this category for one-dimensional integral or Gorenstein schemes.

In this paper, we introduce a time-changed compound Poisson process (TCCPP) obtained by subordinating the classical compound Poisson process (CPP) with a subordinator and an inverse subordinator, which are defined via distinct Bernstein functions. We study the governing equations and distributional properties of a TCCPP including its moments, dependence structure and limiting behaviour. We derive distributions of the integrated CPP and a linear combination of TCCPPs. We also obtain the law of iterated logarithm, the central limit theorem and weighted sum representation for a TCCPP. Finally, we provide some characterizations of a TCCPP in terms of martingales, a univariate multinomial process, a triangular array process and waiting time distribution. The proposed framework generalizes several existing fractional stochastic processes and offers greater flexibility for modelling complex count data.
Infectious Disease Horizon in Emerging Infectious Diseases
Miaomiao Lv; Juan Zhang; Zhen Jin

Emerging infectious diseases often spread freely before an outbreak is detected, yet the duration of this free-transmission period and the infection size accumulated during this period are difficult to quantify. These quantities directly affect forecasts of subsequent transmission dynamics, estimates of infection size, and decisions regarding prevention and control measures. In this study, we propose and compute the infectious disease horizon (IDH)-the time span from when an infectious disease begins spreading to when it is first detected-and examine its antecedents and consequences. First, based on the SEAIR free-transmission model, we derive transmission characteristics, including the generation interval, the serial interval, the basic reproduction number, and the effective reproduction number, and describe the incidence using a renewal equation. Second, by considering two detection routes, we further obtain the distribution and mean of the IDH under different detection settings and quantify the infection size at the time of outbreak detection. Third, intervention measures are incorporated to derive a post-detection transmission model with generally distributed stage durations, followed by the derivation of the corresponding model under exponentially distributed stage durations and the determination of the final infection size. Finally, under the exponential-distribution assumption, the model is applied to the COVID-19 outbreak in Xi'an. The unified framework developed in this study provides a theoretical basis for evaluating early surveillance capacity for emerging infectious diseases, optimizing testing strategies, and determining the intensity of prevention and control measures after outbreak detection.
The External Path Length and Terminal Wiener Index in Random Trees

We consider two distance-based concepts in rooted trees and compare them to their leaf-restricted counterparts. The path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the vertices of the tree, while the external path length is the sum of all distances from the root to the leaves of the tree. Upon dividing by the number of vertices and leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance to the root. The Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of vertices, and the terminal Wiener index is the sum of all distances between pairs of leaves. Dividing by the number of pairs of vertices and pairs of leaves respectively, we obtain the average distance between vertices and average distance between leaves. For two important classes of random trees, we show that the average distance of the root to a random leaf is almost the same as the average distance to a random vertex and that the average distance between vertices is almost the same as the average distance between leaves. For Bienaymé--Galton--Watson trees, each of these differences is bounded in probability. For three varieties of increasing trees (recursive trees, $d$-ary increasing trees, generalised plane-oriented recursive trees), on the other hand, the differences converge to constants in probability. This allows the transfer of convergence results for the path length to the external path length, and results for the Wiener index to be transferred to the terminal Wiener index.
Strict $\mathcal{C}^\infty$-triangulation of subanalytic sets in low dimensions
Jos{é} F. Fernando; Riccardo Ghiloni; Wiesław Pawłucki

Let $R$ be a real closed field expanded by an o-minimal structure, let $A$ be a definable, closed and bounded subset of $R^n$ and let $p$ be a positive integer. It was recently shown in \cite{pa2} that $A$ admits a strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation $({\mathcal T},h)$, i.e., there exist a finite simplicial complex ${\mathcal T}$ in $R^n$ and a homeomorphism $h:|{\mathcal T}|\to A$ that is definable and of class ${\mathcal C}^p$.
 The aim of this article is to analyze a generalization of the notion of strict ${\mathcal C}^p$-triangulation of subanalytic sets to the case $p=\infty$. Examples in dimension $n=3$ show that such a generalization is not always possible within subanalytic geometry, where the class ${\mathcal C}^\infty$ is equivalent to the class ${\mathcal C}^ω$. We formulate the conjecture that strict ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-triangulations of subanalytic sets always exist in the wider o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{{\rm an},\exp}$, generated by subanalytic sets and the exponential function. We check the conjecture for all subanalytic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n\leq 3$, and prepare tools to address the conjecture for arbitrary $n$.
 We also apply the obtained strict ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-triangulation results to approximate subanalytic continuous mappings $f:X\to Y$ between subanalytic sets $X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^m$ by ${\mathcal C}^\infty$-mappings $g:X\to Y$ definable in the o-minimal structure $\mathbb{R}_{{\rm an},\exp}$, with respect to the strong Whitney ${\mathcal C}^0$ topology. If the continuous mapping $f:X\to Y$ is not necessarily subanalytic, we can still approximate it by ${\mathcal C}^\infty$ mappings $g:X\to Y$.
Exact Fourier Coupling Relations for the Method of Auxiliary Sources on Elliptic Cylinders
Prisca Le Dily; Arnaud Coatanhay; Marie Kintzinger; Yves-Marie Scolan

The Method of Auxiliary Sources has been extensively studied in the case of cylindrical geometries. In this article, the authors provide analysis elements for the elliptical geometry case. Based on a Mathieu functions expansion, the impedance matrix is projected into a reduced diagonal matrix. At the same time, the matrix is studied in the Fourier domain. A checkerboard structure is found and a relation between the different elements of the matrix is proven. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical results. We additionally identify an exact finite-grid parity rule, an aliasing identity connecting the discrete and continuous Fourier representations, and controlled near-circular Fourier-band localization. These results are mostly independent of a small-$q$ truncation of radial Mathieu functions.
Refined critical flux bounds for Leray's problem in a pipe with the Navier-slip boundary

We study uniqueness for stationary incompressible Navier--Stokes flows in infinite pipes with the Navier-slip boundary. For a cylindrical pipe of unit radius and a positive friction ratio, uniqueness holds when $|Φ|\leq 2π\sqrt{40/7}\approx 15$. This significantly improves upon the result of the first author, Liu and Zhou (J. Differential Equations 461:114108, 2026) where the uniqueness requires $|Φ|\leq π/16\approx 0.2$. For small positive friction ratio $α$, this flux condition can be improved to $|Φ|\leq 4\sqrt{2}\,π^2/α$. For an infinite pipe with a bounded, smooth, simply connected cross-section $Σ$, we prove uniqueness for every $0<α<\infty$ provided that $|Φ|\leq c_Σ(1+α)/α$, where $c_Σ>0$ depends only on $Σ$.
Proof of the Quasi Riemann Hypothesis using $\mathbb Q[i]$

Using quartic Gauss sums in place of the cubic Gauss sums in OpenAI's original proof, we prove that the Dedekind $ζ$-function $ζ_{\mathbb Q(i)}(s)$ of $\mathbb Q(i)$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Re s>599/600$, thereby obtaining the same zero-free half-plane for the Riemann $ζ$-function.We obtain the upper bound for the smoothed sum by applying Poisson summation twice and using the functional equation of the quartic Kubota series of angular weight $1$.In the Mellin representation, a zero-density bound for the family of quartic characters controls the terms from nonprincipal characters,and a residue and a lattice average over fourth powers give the main term.
Information Spectrum Methods for MUltiple-Access Channels--Part III : The Strong Converse in the $K$-User Gaussian Case

This paper, Part III of a series, treats $K$-user multiple-access channels (MACs). Its starting point is a pair of fundamental lemmas, a random-coding lemma of Feinstein type and a converse lemma of Verdú--Han type, which are the $K$-user extensions of the two lemmas underlying Han's information spectrum approach to the general two-user MAC. From them we derive the capacity region of the general $K$-user MAC with cost constraint and show that it contains the polymatroid capacity region of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC. We then prove, by an elementary information spectrum calculation that adapts a diffuse--exceptional subspace decomposition used in recent second-order converses for the Gaussian MAC, that for every subset $\cS$ of users and every independent input satisfying the power constraints, the conditional information spectral-sup rate of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC does not exceed $\frac12\log(1+P_\cS/N)$, where $P_\cS$ is the total power of the users in $\cS$, with a probability bound that does not depend on the input. Consequently, the strong converse for the $K$-user Gaussian MAC, in the sense that the error probability tends to one for every rate tuple outside the capacity region, follows directly from the converse lemma, without the wringing technique and without hypothesis-testing meta-converses. This strong converse was first established by Fong and Tan, whose per-blocklength bounds yield it, through wringing and quantization. It is the key ingredient in the converse parts of the coding theorems for mixed Gaussian MACs in Part I, where the $\varepsilon$-strong converse would not suffice.
A Derivative-Free Bellman Equation for Dynamic Time-to-Collision: Two-Sided Certificates and Explicit ReLU Approximation

Dynamic time-to-collision (TTC) is the first contact time of a prediction flow and defines a feedback map implicitly. We study its capped value function $\VV$ for Carathéodory dynamics with bounded, measurable forcing. A self-contained argument establishes local Lipschitz continuity on the transversal collision domain. A derivative-free stopped-step Bellman equation then characterizes $\VV$ uniquely: it advances the prediction for a fixed duration or until contact and adds the elapsed time. A two-sided error bound uses only the candidate's residual along complete stopped trajectories and its error at their endpoints. Exact continuum iteration recovers $\VV$ after finitely many sweeps, including one additional sweep for initializations that violate the boundary condition. We also characterize an optional-duration infimum operator: its fixed points are the dynamic-programming subsolutions, so its residual alone does not identify $\VV$. Finally, on compact subsets of the transversal domain, an optimization-free ReLU construction has explicit size, controlled local residual, and robustness to errors in its nodal TTC values. The optimal velocity model provides the running application.
On the size of the defect set of an analytic matrix field

In this note, we study the defect set of a symmetric analytic matrix field $M$ defined on an open set $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\ge2$. A defect point $x \in Ω$ of $M$ is defined as a point for which no eigenframe can be chosen continuously in any neighborhood of $x$. We show that the defect set $S(M)$ is contained in a locally finite union of analytic submanifolds of codimension at least $2$. The proof follows fairly directly from results by Parusinski and Rond (Trans. Am. Math. Soc., 2020) and by Kurdyka and Paunescu (Duke Math. J., 2008). This result can be applied in the context of the Landau-de Gennes Theory to estimate the physical defects of a nematic liquid crystal.
Complete enumeration of maximal T-curves in degrees eight and nine
Zoe Geiselmann; Michael Joswig; Lars Kastner; Marcel Wack

We use a highly parallelized backtracking algorithm implemented in CUDA to enumerate every compatible collection of Harnack splits in degrees eight and nine. By a theorem of Haas (1997) this yields every maximal T-curve. In this way, we find that exactly 38 real schemes of real plane algebraic curves of degree eight with 22 real components and 225 of degree nine with 29 real components are realized by combinatorial patchworking.
Exact Turán densities of even zycles

We determine the exact Turán density of the $3$-uniform zycle $Z_\ell$ for every even integer $\ell\ge 4$ with $3\nmid\ell$, showing that $π(Z_\ell)=5/9$. More generally, we prove that $π(Z_\ell)\le 5/9$ for all even $\ell\ge 4$. In the range of equality, we also establish a stability theorem, showing that every almost extremal $Z_\ell$-free $3$-graph is close in edit distance to the classical Turán construction.
Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels --Part II : $\varepsilon$-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Finite-Alphabet Case

In a nonergodic channel such as a slowly fading link, the channel law is drawn once and held fixed for the whole codeword, and the relevant performance measure is the $\varepsilon$-capacity. We study the $\varepsilon$-capacity regions of two-user mixed multiple-access channels (MACs) with finite alphabets, additive cost constraints and an arbitrary mixing measure. The direct parts are derived from a single information spectrum formula; the converse parts use, in addition, Fano's inequality and Ahlswede's strong converse applied to each component. Without knowledge of the realized component, we prove a single-letter inner bound for every $0\le\varepsilon<1$, in which one input serves all components; for $\varepsilon=0$ it is tight, and the capacity region is given by the essential infima of the component mutual informations. We prove a single-letter outer bound, the outage region, in which each component may use its own input; it holds with or without channel state information (CSI) at either terminal, and it is the $\varepsilon$-capacity region when the encoders know the component and the parameter space is countable. Both bounds coincide, in all four CSI scenarios, for well-ordered mixed MACs, which include degradedly ordered families and mixtures with a common optimal input, such as mixed additive MACs. Without CSI the outer bound can be strictly loose, and the no-CSI $\varepsilon$-capacity region for $0<\varepsilon<1$ remains open in general. Finally, we extend Ahlswede's strong converse to $K$ users with cost constraints and show that most of these results extend to $K$-user mixed MACs.
Matrix Waring Problem in finite fields with coefficients from $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$
Sutirtha Datta; Sourav Ghosh; Aniruddha Maji; Antara Manik

Let $k$ be a fixed positive integer and $p$ be an odd prime such that $\gcd(p-1,k)=1$. For sufficiently large primes $p$, we show that the equation $AX^k+BY^k=C$ has solutions $X,Y \in \mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, where $A$ and $B$ are fixed matrices in $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, and $C$ is a fixed matrix in $\mathrm{M}(2,\mathbb{F}_p).$ Our proof relies on Fourier analysis over $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p).$
On 2-Homogeneous Colourings of Cubic Bipartite Graphs
Rong-Xia Hao; Jianbing Liu; Federico Romaniello

A proper vertex colouring is 2-homogeneous if every open neighbourhood contains exactly two colours. We show that every cubic bipartite graph admits a 2-homogeneous colouring with at most four colours, proving a conjecture of Janicová, Madaras, Soták and Lužar. For 3-connected det-extremal cubic bipartite graphs, we establish the stronger bound $χ_h^{(2)}(G) = 3$, showing that every such graph admits a fall 3-colouring.
Optimized Mirabbasi-Martin Pulse Shaping Filter for Higher-Order Modulation in Zak-OTFS

The performance of Zak-OTFS modulation depends critically on the delay-Doppler (DD) domain pulse shaping filter, which must support both accurate channel estimation and reliable data detection. Filters reported in the Zak-OTFS literature fall short in bit error rate (BER) performance for higher-order modulation due to sensitivity to model-free channel estimation errors and pilot-data interference. Motivated by this, in this paper, we introduce a separable two-dimensional Mirabbasi-Martin (MM) filter for Zak-OTFS and propose a filter coefficient optimization framework that minimizes the aggregate sidelobe energy while preserving the compact structure of the MM prototype. By trading exact Nyquist nulls for high localization, the optimized MM filter exhibits no sidelobes with the narrowest $-40$ dB DD domain pulsewidth compared to sinc, Gaussian, and GS pulses. This compactness of the optimized filter tightly confines the pilot energy within the pilot region of the embedded frame, ensuring that the full response is captured for model-free channel estimation while significantly reducing pilot-data interference. This yields both an improved estimation performance and a significantly improved BER performance for higher-order QAM. For the proposed filter, we derive closed-form expressions for the effective DD domain channel and the covariance of the receive-filtered noise, which drastically reduce simulation run times. Our simulation results demonstrate that the optimized MM filter achieves significantly better uncoded/coded BER performance for higher-order QAM compared to that of sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters. For example, for 64-QAM with M=32, N=48, rate-1/2 convolutional code, and TDL-A channel model with fractional DDs, the optimized MM filter achieves a coded BER of 3x10^{-4} at an E_b/N_0 of 40 dB, while the sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters exhibit error floors above 10^{-2}.
Variational approximation by complex Gaussians for the nonlinear logarithmic equation

We consider the semiclassical logarithmic Schr{ö}dinger equation, with an at most quadratic potential and with Gaussian initial states. For a critical nonlinear term in the semiclassical regime, we analyze an approximation based on the variational evolution of Gaussian wave packets. We also prove a nonlinear superposition principle for solutions issued from the sum of two Gaussian wave packets initially localized at distinct points in phase space. For both a single Gaussian wave packet and a superposition of two Gaussian wave packets, we compare the variational approximation with the standard coherent-state approximation and highlight their respective features. The required assumptions are weakened in this setting without becoming technically involved.
The Query Complexity of Unknown Sparse Gradient Residuals

We study optimization of an average of \(n\) functions when gradient predictions are exact except for at most \(k\) unknown components. An initial scan may miss these exceptions.
 For a class of smooth problems, we prove that the optimal worst-case expected number of component-gradient evaluations needed to find an approximate stationary point is \[ Θ\!\left(\min\left\{nk+\mathcal R,\frac nk\mathcal R\right\}\right), \] where \(\mathcal R\) represents the optimal cost when the exceptional components are known. Prediction evaluations are free.
 This bound shows that discovering even a few exceptions can cost more than one full scan and can account for most of the gradient evaluations.
Bloch groups of local rings with residue field $\mathbb{F}_2$
We give a generic presentation of the pre-Bloch group of a local ring with residue field $\mathbb{F}_{2}$. We apply this to the calculation of pre-Bloch groups and Bloch groups of some local rings.
On compact homogeneous Locally conformal symplectic manifolds

A locally conformally symplectic (LCS) structure on a manifold $M$ is a pair $(η,ω)$ consisting of a closed $1$-form $η$ called Lee form and a nondegenerate $2$-form $ω$ satisfying
 \[
 dω=η\wedgeω.
 \]
 We classify compact connected homogeneous LCS manifolds with nonzero Lee form. To this end, we construct three explicit families of pairs $(G,K)$, where $G$ is a connected simply connected Lie group and $K$ is a closed subgroup such that $G/K$ is compact, the $G$-action is almost effective, and $G/K$ admits a $G$-invariant LCS structure. We show that every compact connected homogeneous LCS manifold with nonzero Lee form arises from one of these families.
 Moreover, each such manifold is LCS-isomorphic to a product $(S/H_d)\times S^1$, where $S$ is a compact connected simply connected semisimple Lie group and $S/H_d$ carries an $S$-invariant contact form $α$. Under this identification, the LCS structure is given by
 \[
 η=π_2^*ξ,\qquad
 ω=d(π_1^*α)+π_1^*α\wedgeη,
 \]
 where $π_1$ and $π_2$ are the projections onto the two factors and $ξ$ is a nowhere-vanishing $1$-form on $S^1$. This description also yields topological consequences for compact homogeneous LCS manifolds. In particular,
 none of these compact
 homogeneous LCS manifolds admits a symplectic
 structure, even without any invariance assumption.
 As a consequence, we show that in dimension four the underlying manifolds are precisely $L(d,1)\times S^1$, where $L(d,1)$ is a three-dimensional lens space. In dimension eight, we obtain families arising from seven-dimensional lens spaces and Aloff--Wallach spaces, including infinitely many distinct topological types.
A Weighted Second-Order Nonlocal Total Variation Regularizer for Image Restoration
Francesc Alcover; Joan Duran; Catalina Sbert

Despite the remarkable progress of deep learning in image processing, variational methods remain a fundamental and actively developing framework, offering interpretability, mathematical rigor, and well-founded guarantees. In this work, we introduce a weighted second-order nonlocal total variation regularizer for image restoration, which is based on measuring gradient differences across the image domain and allows for weights that are neither smooth nor symmetric and may vanish outside a search window. We first provide a rigorous definition of the regularizer and prove that it enjoys several desirable properties under realistic assumptions on the underlying weight function. We then consider a nonlocal variant of the variational image restoration model of Chambolle and Lions, and prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the associated minimization problem. On the computational side, we develop a discrete formulation of the model and derive the corresponding Chambolle-Pock primal-dual algorithm. Finally, we conduct an extensive experimental evaluation, comparing the proposed regularizer with a range of local and nonlocal, first- and second-order regularizers across several image restoration tasks. The results demonstrate its strong noise-suppression and texture-preservation capabilities, as well as its robustness to nonlocal weights computed under non-ideal conditions.
Optimal One Health control of antimicrobial resistance: a household mean-field model with community feedback and parameters from Burkina Faso
Mifiamba Soma; Pingawindé Sawadogo; Yisso Fidèle Bacye; Evariste Bako; Mariétou Sissao; Maurice Sarigda; Adama Kiemde

We study how to combine three One Health interventions against antimicrobial resistance: prescription-only dispensing of antibiotics to people, access to veterinary care for animals, and treatment of household sludge and manure. Each household is a Markov chain on the carriage states of its people, animals and soil, and households are linked through the community, whose prevalence feeds the acquisition rates. We prove that, as the number of households grows, the distribution of household states converges to the solution of a nonlinear mean-field equation. This system is monotone for the stochastic order, so that no intervention increases carriage anywhere, and for every constant intervention it has exactly one equilibrium, which attracts all solutions and is given by a scalar equation. For the optimal control problem we prove existence, necessary conditions, positivity of all controls under a quadratic cost, uniqueness for short horizons, and a turnpike property under an explicit dissipativity condition, which we verify for our parameters by a computer-assisted numerical certification. With parameters from Tenkodogo, Burkina Faso, the optimal combined strategy averts about 17% of human carriage over three years in the baseline scenario, and 11% to 28% over the plausible scenarios for the parameters that the survey cannot identify; these figures are projections conditional on the model. The strategy itself is robust: the value of perfect information on the unmeasured parameters is about 2% of the achievable benefit. A compartmental model with the same transmission rates but without households underestimates the benefit, and targeting the interventions by zone of the town increases it.
Quantitative Accumulation of Invariant Circles Near a Non-splitting Separatrix

For a smooth area-preserving cylinder map with a non-splitting separatrix and an exact symplectic linearization at its saddle, we prove accumulation by smooth essential invariant circles when the boundary transition is sufficiently $C^4$-close to a translation. As an application, we give an answer to Herman's open problem in 1983.
Optimal control for an anisotropic Stokes-Nernst-Planck-Poisson system

We study an optimal control problem aimed at enhancing mixing in anisotropic electrolytes described by an instationary Stokes-Nernst-Planck-Poisson system in three space dimensions, where the anisotropy is encoded by a given director field in the diffusion and permittivity matrices. The control is the external electric potential entering through the Robin boundary condition of the Poisson equation. The cost functional combines tracking-type terms for the charge concentrations and an $L^2$-regularization of the control with a negative vorticity term that favors rotational flow. Assuming that the diffusion and permittivity matrices coincide, we first prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions with nonnegative, essentially bounded concentrations, together with Lipschitz continuous dependence on the control. Since, through the negative vorticity term, the cost functional is no longer weakly lower semicontinuous, existence of an optimal control relies on strong convergence of the velocity gradients. Finally, we prove Fréchet differentiability of the control-to-state operator, introduce the adjoint system, and derive first-order necessary optimality conditions in the form of a variational inequality.
Nonsense nonlinear correlations between independent random walks

Sample distance correlation can remain large between independent random walks. For centred walks with independent, identically distributed increments of finite, positive variance, we prove convergence in distribution to the distance correlation of the joint occupation measure of two independent Brownian paths. This universal limit lies strictly between zero and one almost surely and has full support on the unit interval. We calculate the expected squared distance covariance of the limiting measure and show that ordinary permutation calibration rejects independence with probability tending to one at every fixed nominal level. Gaussian simulations illustrate the persistent dispersion of random-walk correlations and the failure of permutation calibration.
Quantitative flocking of Cucker-Smale flocks under time-delay and noise
Seung-Yeal Ha; Xinyu Wang; Chen Wu; Fanqin Zeng

We study the asymptotic flocking dynamics of the delayed stochastic Cucker-Smale (in short, DSCS) model driven by agent-wise independent, component-wise multiplicative Brownian noise. The simultaneous interplay of stochastic perturbations and time delay yields fundamental challenges to asymptotic stochastic flocking analysis, as the communication weight may lose a uniform positive lower bound, while the velocity moment is no longer monotone. To overcome these difficulties, we present a sufficient framework and an analytical tool combining the method of time-varying effective region and Lyapunov functional approach with time-delay corrections. This approach avoids any reliance on uniformly positive communication weights or monotone velocity moments. The proposed approach recovers sufficiently strong effective velocity alignment despite stochastic fluctuations and delay effects. As a consequence, we establish the mean-square stochastic flocking with an explicit polynomial convergence rate. The admissible decay exponent is determined by the communication kernel exponent and the orders of the spatial and velocity history moments. These results establish a quantitative theory for long-time stochastic flocking under simultaneous delay and multiplicative noise, and we provide a positive answer to an open problem raised by~[R. Erban, J. Haskovec, Y. Sun, SIAM J. Appl. Math., 76, 1535--1557 (2016)]. We also develop robust analytical tools applicable to delayed stochastic collective dynamics with degenerate communications.
Access to the quasi-geostrophic model from within the BK19 compressible flow solver

We extend BK19 the semi-implicit finite-volume solver, to provide access to the quasi-geostrophic (QG) regime within the same compressible framework that already admits soundproof and hydrostatic limits. In order to achieve this goal, we incorporate the asymptotic framework from the continuous theory into the numerical scheme. Adopting the usual asymptotic setting for the quasi-geostrophic regime and using it directly in the numerical model, we perform a scale analysis of the compressible Euler equations in the synoptic length and time scales in the limit of small Rossby number. In this limit, the discrete implicit step recovers geostrophic balance, together with the pseudo-incompressible divergence constraint. We construct a staggered-grid curl operator consistent with the discrete derivatives and use it to define the vorticity in the numerical framework. An asymptotic analysis of the fully discrete scheme then yields a Poisson-type equation for the leading-order Exner-pressure perturbation that coincides with the QG pressure Poisson equation in the continuous theory. As a result of this analysis, we introduce two additional blending switches that (i) convert the elliptic pressure problem from the full Helmholtz to its QG Poisson-type equation and (ii) control whether the horizontal momenta are updated prognostically or diagnosed from geostrophic balance. In combination with the existing soundproof and hydrostatic switches, the resulting algorithm can be operated in fully compressible, pseudo-incompressible, hydrostatic, and QG modes without changing the underlying discretization. The functionality of the numerical scheme in the QG regime is then tested by two idealized vortex test cases to show how stable the vortices remain in the QG run and that, as the Rossby number is reduced, the full compressible scheme converges to slow, balanced QG dynamics.
Coarse geometry of stable mixed commutator length II: coarse kernels for nilpotent quotients
Morimichi Kawasaki; Mitsuaki Kimura; Shuhei Maruyama; Takahiro Matsushita; Masato Mimura

This paper studies the global difference between the stable commutator length ${\rm scl}_G$ and the stable mixed commutator length ${\rm scl}_{G,N}$ from the perspective of coarse geometry, as well as the space ${\rm W}(G,N)$ of non-extendable quasimorphisms modulo invariant homomorphisms. Our main theorem concerns a finitely generated group $G$ and its normal subgroup $N$ such that the quotient group $ Γ= G/N$ is nilpotent. In this setting, we prove that the natural inclusion map of coarse groups from $[G,N]$ to $[G,G]$, equipped with the metrics induced by ${\rm scl}_{G,N}$ and ${\rm scl}_G$, respectively, is coarsely surjective. Moreover, this map has a splitting coarse kernel that is coarsely isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}^n, \| \cdot \|_1)$, where $n$ is the dimension of ${\rm W}(G,N)$. As a consequence, $[G,N]$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}^n \times [G,G]$ as a coarse group.
The dynamical Seppäläinen-Johansson model and the Brownian web landscape
Julian Ransford; Bálint Vető; Bálint Virág

The dynamical Seppäläinen-Johansson first passage percolation defines a random directed metric on $\mathbb Z^2$ where the environment is updated according to a Poisson process. We show that its finite dimensional distributions converge after $0:1:2$ scaling to those of the Brownian web landscape defined on the finite dimensional marginals of the dynamical Brownian web. We prove non-uniqueness of geodesics in the Brownian web landscape and we relate it to exact formulas on one-sided reflected Brownian motions. We prove a locally uniform law of large numbers and uniform deviation bounds, and identify Poisson increment-stationary laws for the associated height evolution.

We present a new axiomatic theory of disquotational truth based on the theory of positive disquotation PUTB. Formulated in classical logic, PUTB restricts the T-schema to positive sentences and satisfies key epistemic desiderata (semantic conservativity and trustworthiness). However, it fares poorly in proof-theoretic strength compared to reflective truth frameworks. To address this, we propose a new theory of positive disquotation aimed at axiomatizing its least fixed-point model. Without requiring additional resources, we achieve this by incorporating ill-founded reasoning under suitable soundness restrictions, applying the tools of cyclic proof theory to axiomatic theories of truth. The resulting theory, CPUTB, is sound relative to the minimal fixed-point model and proves the same arithmetical theorems as the impredicative theory ID1.
Recovering Small Perturbations of a Known Inclusion from One Mixed Steklov Eigenpair with Local Boundary Data

We study the recovery of small normal displacements of a known inclusion from a single mixed Steklov eigenpair. The data consist of the eigenvalue and the eigenfunction trace on any nonempty open subset of the fixed outer boundary, with the eigenfunction normalized using only that subset. For an inner Dirichlet condition, we prove that the linearized measurement map is injective at every simple eigenvalue. A compatible adjoint identity yields a reconstruction method with a conditional stability estimate on any fixed finite-dimensional space of smooth displacements. For the principal Dirichlet eigenpair, the same local data also determine the inclusion uniquely among sufficiently small normal graphs. In a three-dimensional concentric shell, the eigenvalue determines the mean displacement at first order, while spherical harmonics diagonalize the remaining full-boundary trace map. The singular values decay exponentially with harmonic degree, yielding logarithmic conditional stability under a Sobolev prior. Numerical experiments using the perturbed geometry illustrate the quadratic linearization error and the deterioration of conditioning as the observed patch shrinks. For an inner Neumann condition, we prove linearized injectivity at every positive simple eigenvalue.
A locally complete family of Kummer type hyperkähler fourfolds
Franco Giovenzana; Andrés Rojas; Jieao Song

We construct a 4-dimensional family of projective hyperkähler fourfolds of Kummer type. A general member of this family can be described as an irreducible component of a complete intersection of Heisenberg-invariant cubics in an 8-dimensional projective space. Several properties of the corresponding moduli space are also obtained. Our arguments rely on specializing to the case of generalized Kummer fourfolds of genus-two Jacobians, and make use of classical results dating back to Burkhardt and Coble.
Scaling limits of Chebyshev polynomials at a hard edge

Let $\mathsf{E}\subset\mathbb{R}$ be compact. We derive local scaling limits of the Chebyshev polynomials associated to $\mathsf{E}$ at a gap edge. We describe the scaling limits by a one parameter family of functions explicitly given by elliptic integrals. We show that for the union of two generic intervals all functions in this family are in fact attained as limits. As a consequence, we describe the local scaling behavior of the zeros of the Chebyshev polynomials at the gap edge.
Critical mass for infinite-time blow-up in a Keller-Segel system with indirect signal production on closed Riemannian surfaces

We study a parabolic-elliptic-ODE chemotaxis system with indirect signal production on closed connected Riemannian surfaces. For all sufficiently regular nonnegative initial data, the system admits a unique global classical solution. We show that the solution remains globally bounded if the total mass $M<8π$. For each $M>8π$, we find initial data of mass $M$ that yield infinite-time blow-up solutions. We then adapt the argument to the corresponding Neumann problem in a smooth bounded planar domain and obtain infinite-time blow-up solutions for any mass $M>4π$. At the critical mass $M=8π$, we show that the solutions are globally bounded on spheres equipped with the canonical spherical metric, and we construct a solution blowing up in infinite time on the Riemann sphere equipped with a special metric.
Kobayashi distance to submanifolds in a Riemannian manifold

We prove that totally geodesic hypersurfaces are at infinite Kobayashi distance in a Kobayashi hyperbolic Riemannian manifold. To do this, we prove a Schwarz lemma on minimal maps with a uniform control on their Laplacians. Finally we give a full characterisation of submanifolds at infinite distance on spaces of constant sectional curvature in dimension at least 4.
On graceful labeling of Jahangir graphs

For a graph with q edges, a graceful labeling assigns distinct integers from {0,...,q} its vertices so that the absolute differences across the edges are exactly 1,...,q. A Jahangir graph J_{n,m}, with n >= 2 and m >= 3, consists of an outer cycle on nm vertices and a hub joined to m equally spaced vertices of that cycle, with q = (n+1)m edges. This family of graphs is known to be graceful. In this paper we strengthen the gracefulness property of such graphs by assigning labels to their vertices through a parametric formula. These labeled graphs have a mono tonicity property: deleting an edge from the outer cycle leaves a path whose edge differences, in the negative orientation, are strictly increasing for even n and strictly decreasing for odd n. The starting observation is that large differences admit few endpoint pairs and require adjacencies between high and low labels. This suggests a construction based on alternating two separated label sets along the outer cycle. The formula has two parity branches, each with two cases modulo 4. Applications are given for every case.

A $BCK(p)$-term is a closed lambda-term in which each abstraction binds at most $p$ variables; for $p=1$ these terms are related to the axiom system BCK of combinatory logic. We determine the number of $BCK(p)$-terms of size $n$, up to a constant multiplicative factor, for every $p\ge2$. For $p=2$ the result is fully explicit: \[ f\_n\sim A\,n^{2n/5}2^{n/5}e^{-2n/5}n^{-3/5}e^{P(n^{1/5})}, \] where $P$ is an explicit polynomial of degree $4$. In general the asymptotic formula involves $n^{pn/(2p+1)}$ and an exponential of a polynomial in $n^{1/(2p+1)}$. The proof combines a linearization of the defining functional equation, the analysis of the Borel transform of the linearized generating function, which satisfies a linear differential equation with an irregular singularity at infinity, the saddle point method for Hayman-admissible functions, and positivity arguments comparing the original and the linearized sequences. For $p=1$ this comparison fails: the quadratic term then also changes the polynomial factor.
Central limit theorems for Frobenius, Hecke and Kloosterman angles
Shreyas Pai; Kaneenika Sinha; Naman Thakkar

The Frobenius angles of non-CM elliptic curves and the Hecke angles of non-CM newforms are equidistributed with respect to the Sato--Tate measure, while for Kloosterman angles, this is known on average over natural families. We study the fluctuations around these laws in large families, for smooth test functions. We prove an unconditional central limit theorem for Frobenius angles of elliptic curves for a much larger class of test functions than previously considered; earlier results assumed the Riemann hypothesis for $L$-functions of Hecke eigenforms of full level. This result follows from a general framework, developed here, which yields Gaussian moments for statistics of sequences in $[0,1]$ varying over families. In this framework, independence is replaced by two quantitative conditions: approximate independence at distinct indices, and convergence of the family averages to the Weyl limits at a suitable rate. As further applications, we extend central limit theorems for Kloosterman angles and for Hecke angles of newforms to larger classes of test functions, the latter with the weight and the level varying simultaneously. We also treat the dilated angles $αθ$ for integers $α\geq2$, whose limiting distribution is uniform. Finally, we discuss sharp statistics, obtaining a central limit theorem for Hecke angles and explaining the obstruction for the other two families.
Polynomial eigenfunctions and recurrences of fixed length

This paper solves the fixed-length recurrence problem posed by Horozov, Shapiro and Tater. For the rational Darboux transformations specified here, it also resolves the order and classification questions raised by their two conjectures. It classifies monic polynomial sequences whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients and for which multiplication by the variable involves a fixed number of consecutive polynomials. Orthogonality is not assumed, and only sufficiently large degrees need be prescribed. If the lowest recurrence index is $n-m+1$, with $m\ge3$, the differential order equals $m$ times the degree of the eigenvalue as a polynomial in $n$. After translating the variable, every such sequence is a finite rational Darboux transform of an explicit family with differential order $m$ and eigenvalue $n$. Necessary and sufficient conditions on the factors determine all polynomial differential eigenoperators of the resulting family. For families that cannot be obtained by these transformations from families of smaller minimum differential order, the minimum differential and recurrence orders coincide. All such families are classified in minimum differential orders at least three, including additional families in composite orders.
To Race or Not to Race? Exploiting Performance Variability in Mixed-Integer Programming via Root-Gated Resource Allocation
Mourchid Adegbindin; Brenda Dietrich; Jamol Pender

Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solver runtimes vary substantially across random seeds. Parallel replication exploits this variability but can waste computational resources when applied indiscriminately. We investigate whether information from an ordinary solve can guide this allocation decision.

Using 101,615 seeded SCIP runs, we examine the association between root-LP dual degeneracy and replication value. We then introduce a non-invasive root-gated policy that preserves the original solver trajectory and launches three additional seeded processes when a root dual-degeneracy indicator reaches a fixed threshold.

These findings demonstrate the promise of selective parallel resource allocation without solver-source modifications.
A Finite Markov Chain Analysis of the Simplified Swarm Optimisation Update Rule

Simplified swarm optimisation (SSO) updates each variable by one draw that copies the global or personal best, keeps the current value or redraws uniformly, with probabilities $c_g$, $c_p$, $c_w$ and $c_r$. As a finite Markov chain under frozen memory, its coordinate kernel $c_w I + (1 - c_w)Π$ has an explicit stationary law and exact convergence rate $c_w^t$. The elitist chain has a geometric hitting-time bound, from a non-optimal start a fixed $c_r$ needs at least $\exp(nc_r/2)$ expected evaluations to reach a unique optimum, and a coupling under changing memories gives $O(n\log n)$ and $O(n^2)$ expected generations on OneMax and LeadingOnes for every population size with redraw share of order $1/n$ and no inertia, and within a $\log n$ factor for fixed inertia. With a frozen memory, inertia cannot speed up first entry into any set from stationary positions, though it can from others. Where the three reference values agree, only $c_r$ acts; where they disagree, copy branches recombine the memories, forcing a redraw only where no active branch holds the target value. Branch logging and checkpoint replay show inertia slowed the tested OneMax and LeadingOnes runs and suggest memory-mediated gains on wider gaps. On Jump functions SSO needed 3.8--8.9 times fewer evaluations than the (1+1) evolutionary algorithm with rate $1/n$, but no consistent advantage over rate-adjusted mutation or a $(μ+1)$ genetic algorithm with uniform crossover was established. The analytical redraw rule improved six of eight benchmark--setting pairs and redundancy allocation, but was slower than $c_r = 0.1$ on Jump$_2$.
