Asymptotically Optimal Bounds for Counting Near-Minimum Circuits in Regular Matroids

For a regular matroid on $m$ elements with positive weights and weighted girth $g_w$, we prove that the number of circuits of weight at most $αg_w$ is bounded by $(Km)^{2α}$, for every real $α\ge1$ and an absolute constant $K$. This improves the previous $m^{O(α^2)}$ bound of Gurjar and Vishnoi and matches classic graph cut and cycle counting bounds of Karger and Subramanian. We also show this is asymptotically optimal for all real $α\geq 1$ under the Erdős girth conjecture, while unconditional optimality holds for half-integer $α$ by prior results. As consequences, we resolve a recent conjecture by Khanna, Putterman, and Song implying the existence of a parallel basis search algorithm for regular matroids terminating in logarithmically many rounds of independence queries, and obtain improved bounds on the number of near-minimum weight codewords in regular codes and near-shortest vectors in totally unimodular lattices under $\ell_p$-norms.
Shift-Symmetric Configurations in $d$-Dimensional Cellular Automata: Enumeration, Bounds, Irreversibility, and Detection
Peter Banda; John Caughman; Tobi Lehman

A configuration of a cellular automaton on the $d$-dimensional torus $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ is shift-symmetric if it is fixed by some nonzero translation. Banda, Caughman, Cenek, and Teuscher (Chaos 29, 063120, 2019) enumerated these configurations in two dimensions and drew dynamical and algorithmic consequences. We extend their results to every dimension. We give an explicit closed-form enumeration for all $n$, $d$, and alphabet sizes $σ$, in which the two-dimensional coefficients $1$, $p+1$, and $p$ become $r_d(p,v)=p^{\binom{v}{2}}\binom{d}{v}_p$, with $\binom{d}{v}_p$ the Gaussian binomial; it extends to configurations with a prescribed number of active cells and to all finite abelian groups. The case of prime $n$ recovers, in complement form, a result of Castillo-Ramirez and Gadouleau; the multi-prime closed form and the dynamical consequences beyond the stabilizer inclusion are new. We prove a lower bound attained exactly when $n$ is prime, and upper bounds, among them $(2^d-1+2\log_2 n)\,σ^{n^d/2}$. As $d$ grows, the symmetry probability decays as $σ^{-c\,n^d}$ with $c\to1-1/p_1(n)$, set solely by the smallest prime factor of $n$, and the symmetry advantage of the side $p+1$ over a prime side $p$ inverts within an explicit window around $d_c(p)\approx p\ln 2$. Under the necessary hypothesis of translation-equivariant neighborhoods, shift-symmetry is irreversible, the per-prime symmetry ranks never decrease, and non-symmetric tasks are unsolvable from symmetric inputs. We give a detection algorithm with worst-case cost $O(n^d\sum_{p\mid n}\frac{p^d-1}{p-1})$ and an average-case analysis, exact for each subgroup test. The mathematical content of every numbered statement is formally verified in Lean 4, and the correspondence between each theorem, lemma, proposition, and corollary and its formal statement was audited by hand.
Minimizing Monotone Norms in Fractional Load Balancing
Daniel Blankenburg; Antonia Ellerbrock; Thomas Kesselheim; Jens Vygen

We devise a fully polynomial time approximation scheme for minimizing a monotone norm $\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert$ over a convex set $X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$. We study the multi-customer setting, where $X=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$ and the solution set $X_i\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$ is given by a linear minimization oracle for each customer $i$. Our algorithm computes, for any given $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate solution. With high probability, it uses $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \varepsilon^{-2}(n+d) \right)$ single-customer linear minimization oracle calls and the same number of generalized KL projections to the dual space $Y=\{y\in \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}: \left\lVert y \right\rVert^* \le 1\}$. We assume no prior knowledge on $X$, and our running time depends only on $n$, $d$, and $\varepsilon$. Our result is robust in the sense that it allows for approximate linear minimization oracles and approximate KL projections. We show that the (approximate) KL projection can be performed efficiently for large classes of monotone norms, demonstrating the applicability of our approach.
 While such a result (with exact projection) is well-known for the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm via multiplicative weight updates and was recently obtained for ordered norms via a smooth norm approximation and a novel randomization, existing techniques do not extend to general monotone norms. In particular, a key feature used in previous proofs was dual price stability, which was derived from a global contraction property of the KL projection to the dual space $Y$. We show that this property does not extend to general monotone norms. Therefore, we use a different price mechanism, based on the well-known mirror descent paradigm, for which a local contraction property holds and guarantees stability.
Quadratic Convexification with Two Switching Variables via Extreme Rays
Yipeng Zhang; Yuyuan Ouyang; Boshi Yang

We consider the convex hull of the quadratic lift $(x,xx^\top,y)$ of the set $\{(x,y) \mid 0 \le x \le y,\ y \in \{0,1\}^n \}$. Descriptions of this convex hull provide convex relaxations for quadratic optimization with switching variables, including problems with indefinite quadratic objectives and constraints. For $n=2$, we completely characterize the extreme rays of the corresponding cone of nonnegative quadratic functions, which consists of two switching rays, six boundary-product rays, discounted affine-square rays, and a parameterized family of discounted rank-two rays. These families generate the cone, so their linearizations give a complete valid-inequality description of the convex hull in the lifted space. The discounted rank-two rays also show that rank-one liftings cannot generate all valid inequalities. Using this classification, we prove a conjecture of Anstreicher and Burer on an exact semidefinite representation of this convex hull.
Dennis Hall; Simon Pfeil; Jesse Taylor

Matroid theory and skew zero forcing (SZF) in graphs are both topics of mathematical interest, but very little is known about their overlap. When a matroid arises from a graph in the traditional way, the edges of the graph correspond with the elements of the matroid. However, the SZF color change rule for graphs can be viewed as a closure operator on the vertices of a graph. As such, when a matroid arises from a graph via SZF, the vertices of the graph correspond with the elements of the matroid. We call such a matroid SZF-realizable. Notably, unlike the traditional method of obtaining a matroid from a graph, skew zero forcing in a graph does not always give rise to a matroid. This paper establishes fundamental results in graph and matroid theory with respect to (1) which matroids are SZF-realizable, and (2) what kinds of graphs do and do not give rise to SZF matroids. The main result of the paper focuses on cycle matroids of outerplanar graphs.
Exceptional parameters in the Erdős similarity problem

The Erd\H os similarity conjecture says that for every infinite set $A \subset \mathbb{R}$, there exists a set $E$ of positive Lebesgue measure which does not contain any affine copy of $x + tA$ of $A$ (with $t \neq 0$). Kolountzakis proved that for every infinite $A$, there exists $E$ of positive Lebesgue measure so that the exceptional sets $D_E(A)$ of scales $t$, and $\mathcal E_E(A)$ of affine maps $(x,t)$, for which $x+tA\subseteq E$, are both Lebesgue null. We show that these exceptional parameter sets are small in two finer senses. First, given any countable family of Fourier decay rates, a single $E$ can be constructed so that $D_E(A)$ is null with respect to every measure whose Fourier transform decays at one of these rates. Consequently, there are compact sets $K$ of measure arbitrarily close to $1$ for which $D_K(A)$ and $\mathcal E_K(A)$ have modified Fourier dimension zero. Second, we give a criterion, depending both on the growth of a gauge function $h$ and on the gaps between elements of lacunary sequences in $A$, which guarantees that $\mathcal H^h(D_E(A))=0$ for gauges with $h(u)/u\to\infty$, as well as a similar result for $\mathcal E_K(A)$. For sets such as $A = \{1/n!\}$ and $A = \{e^{-n^q}\}$, this yields explicit gauges of the form $h(u) = u\exp((\log 1/u)^θ)$ with $0 < θ< 1$.
The Fourier dimension conjecture for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos on the circle

Bonnefont, Rajamäki and Vargas conjectured that, for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos built from a single real Gaussian field, the Fourier dimension at $α+iβ$ equals the dimension of the real chaos at $α$ minus $β^2$. We prove the conjecture on the circle throughout their stated parameter range. For the canonical holomorphic family, the identity holds on one event of probability one for all $γ=α+iβ$ in the union of the open unit disk and the region $1/\sqrt2<|α|<\sqrt2$, $|α|+|β|<\sqrt2$. For each fixed parameter on the conjecture's sloping boundary, where $1<|α|<\sqrt2$ and $|α|+|β|=\sqrt2$, the Fourier coefficients decay at a logarithmic rate almost surely and the Fourier dimension is zero. For nonzero interior parameters with $|α|\ne1/\sqrt2$, the critical Sobolev index is half the Fourier dimension minus $1/2$. The chaos fails to belong to the corresponding space when $|α|<1/\sqrt2$ and belongs to it when $|α|>1/\sqrt2$. For $1/\sqrt2<|α|<\sqrt2$ and $|β|\le\sqrt2-|α|$, we bound the Fourier coefficients at the decay power predicted by the dimension formula, up to logarithmic factors. For $0<|γ|<1$ and $α^2<1/2$, the measures obtained by multiplying the squared modulus of the smoothed chaos by $ε^{|γ|^2}$ converge weakly almost surely along $ε=e^{-m}$, uniformly on compact parameter sets, to explicit multiples of the real chaos at $2α$.
Subwavelength registration of skull-compensating acoustic holograms via nonlinear parametric array feedback
Pradosh Pritam Dash; Costas D. Arvanitis

Realizing the potential of optimized acoustic holograms for applications like transcranial ultrasound requires sub-wavelength alignment accuracy (less than 1.5 mm at 1 MHz), which is difficult to achieve with current non-MRI optical neuro-navigation methods. To address the critical challenge of alignment, we leverage the parametric array (PA) signal as an alignment surrogate, a highly penetrative, low-frequency difference wave generated by the nonlinear mixing of two primary high-frequency beams. Simulations show that a misaligned skull-compensating lens increases the primary acoustic energy within the skull bone (volumetric energy trapping), which strengthens the nonlinear source of the PA signal. We also tested whether shear-mode conversion in bone contributes: 2D elastic simulations showed only a small (3-5%) increase in shear-type motion with misalignment, and the transmitted ex vivo bursts did not lengthen as a shear path would require. Pseudo-sound and microbubble artifacts were examined and found unlikely to explain the signal, consistent with the PA signal arising from the intrinsic nonlinearity of the bone. Minimizing this PA signal yields a noninvasive real-time feedback mechanism that achieves sub-wavelength alignment accuracy, outperforming standard neuronavigation. Our findings present a robust framework that supports the design of simple, economical, and high-performance transcranial ultrasound systems for high-precision neuro-interventions.
Intersections, Equations, and Singularities of Lissajous Varieties

Lissajous varieties are affine algebraic varieties parametrized by sine and cosine functions. They generalize algebraic Lissajous curves in the plane to higher dimensions by applying a component-wise trigonometric map to a rational affine subspace and are motivated by applications in dynamical systems (Kuramoto model) and semidefinite optimization (graph elliptopes). We establish several algebraic and geometric properties of Lissajous varieties. In particular, we show that intersections of Lissajous varieties are finite unions of such varieties and describe them explicitly. We investigate algebraic properties of the defining polynomials of Lissajous hypersurfaces and describe the singular locus of Lissajous varieties.
Shuffles of permutations in cycle form
Ron M. Adin; Sergi Elizalde; Ira M. Gessel; Yuval Roichman

We study a variation of the shuffle operation on permutations, which acts on their cycle structure instead of their one-line notation. Given two permutations $σ\in S_k$ and $τ\in S_{n-k}$, the $\textit{shuffle-by-cycle}$ $σ\mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c τ$ is the set of all permutations in $S_n$ whose set of cycles can be separated into two disjoint subsets: one whose standardization is $σ$, and one whose standardization is $τ$. One can think of the sets $σ\mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c τ$ as refinements of conjugacy classes.
 We show that if $σ$ and $τ$ have no order-isomorphic cycles, then the descent set has the same distribution, over the set $σ\mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c τ$ of shuffles-by-cycle, as over the set $σ\mathbin{\sqcup\!\sqcup} τ$ of standard shuffles; our proof is bijective. This result no longer holds when $σ$ and $τ$ have order-isomorphic cycles. For an arbitrary shuffle-by-cycle, we provide a description of the distribution of the descent set in terms of plethysm of quasisymmetric functions. For the set $σ\mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c σ\subset S_{2n}$, where $σ$ is an $n$-cycle, we deduce explicit generating functions for the bivariate distribution of descent number and major index.
Reliable Near-Field Source Enumeration and Positioning Informed by Two-Stage MUSIC
Jiaying Li; Haifeng Wen; Changsheng You; Yuanwei Liu; Hong Xing

Accurate and reliable near-field multi-source localization is essential for location-aware processing in future wireless systems. However, coherent multipath propagation complicates the direct recovery of line-of-sight (LoS) source positions, while existing estimation methods generally lack explicit control of the risk of source underestimation and positioning uncertainty. In this paper, we investigate reliable source enumeration and positioning in near-field coherent multipath environments. Specifically, we develop a conformal risk control (CRC) based source enumeration scheme that calibrates the penalty coefficient of an eigenvalue-based criterion to control the expected miss-detection ratio at a prescribed level. We further propose MUSIC-Net, a model-based deep learning framework informed by two-stage MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC), which learns the LoS-related subspace and surrogate distances through subspace-distance-based training, thereby enabling direct source positioning without estimating non-line-of-sight (NLoS) path parameters or performing subsequent path association. To quantify the uncertainty of the estimated positions, we develop a split conformal prediction (SCP) based calibration method that constructs angle-range predicted regions with finite-sample simultaneous coverage guarantees. Numerical results show that the proposed framework effectively controls the risk of source underestimation, while providing improved positioning accuracy with tighter predicted regions than benchmarks given the same target coverage levels.
Dynamic Prandtl-Reuss Thermoplasticity with Degenerating Yield Constraints

We study a three-dimensional dynamic thermoplastic system with a temperature-dependent convex yield set whose deviatoric section may collapse completely at a finite temperature. The underlying constitutive model is rate-independent Prandtl-Reuss perfect plasticity, without Kelvin-Voigt viscosity, hardening, or a safe-load condition. We construct global approximation-generated relaxed entropy-energy states by a one-parameter Temam-Norton-Hoff-Galerkin scheme with an undiscretized heat equation and untruncated plastic heat production. The logarithmic temperature is strongly compact in $L^2(0,T;L^q(Ω))$ for every $q<6$ and in $L^p((0,T)\timesΩ)$ for every $p<8/3$. An entropy-weighted work estimate yields convergence of the overstress at rate $O(\sqrt{\log n/n})$ in every fixed finite Lebesgue space and identifies stress admissibility. The constitutive limit comprises a distributional plastic balance, finite support-weighted measures, and compact-fibre lifts carrying exact normality and maximum plastic work. A locally finite lift on the positive-radius fibres unifies the level-restricted limits at every continuity level. At the macroscopic level, however, the available compactness does not identify a canonical stress-plastic-flow pairing. Moreover, an explicit smooth state satisfying the intrinsic relaxed balance conditions shows that these conditions do not imply macroscopic Prandtl-Reuss normality. In the fully collapsed regime, an energy-entropy rigidity argument determines the evolution and yields approximation-generated examples in which the plastic flow need not be a finite measure or the displacement need not retain its full boundary trace. Thermal concentration and plastic entropy production remain explicit throughout.
Trust-region high-index saddle dynamics for ill-conditioned saddle-point computation
Guanghua Ji; Longjing Li; Zhen Xu; Jianyuan Yin

We propose a trust-region high-index saddle dynamics (TRHiSD) framework for computing high-index saddle points in ill-conditioned problems. To address the deterioration of high-index saddle dynamics caused by inappropriate step sizes and search directions, we exploit its intrinsic local min--max structure and construct separate trust-region subproblems on the maximization and minimization subspaces to adapt the two trust-region radii to different local curvature scales. Under suitable assumptions and with exact spectral subspaces, we prove local linear convergence of the Cauchy-point variant and local quadratic convergence of the Newton-step variant. Numerical experiments on modified Rosenbrock functions are consistent with the predicted convergence rates. For the Landau--de Gennes model, a TRHiSD variant using a truncated conjugate-gradient step for the minimization subproblem substantially reduces the outer-iteration count and the wall-clock time in the tested cases.
Ideal polyhedral surfaces with prescribed cusped hyperbolic metric and their degeneration
Wai Yeung Lam; Carl O. R. Lutz

Rivin showed that every cusped hyperbolic metric on a punctured sphere is uniquely realized by a convex ideal polyhedron in hyperbolic space with possible degeneration. We consider the analogous problem for cusped hyperbolic metrics on a punctured surface of positive genus: locally convex ideal polyhedral surfaces in hyperbolic space. Each such surface determines a complex projective structure on the underlying closed surface. With a cusped hyperbolic metric $h$ prescribed, we investigate the space $\mathcal{P}(h)$ of such ideal polyhedral realizations and their possible degeneration. Particularly in the case of tori, we show that the space $\mathcal{P}(h)$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^2$, and that the induced map to Teichmüller space of the closed torus is a $C^1$-embedding. This map extends to a bijection from the closure of $\mathcal{P}(h)$ onto the whole Teichmüller space, where the added points are degenerate surfaces. This is dual to the Kojima-Mizushima-Tan conjecture about circle patterns on closed surfaces with complex projective structures.
Quantifying the Cost of Restoring AC Feasibility for Approximate Optimal Power Flow Solutions

Power system operations rely on approximate solutions of the AC optimal power flow problem, most notably the DC optimal power flow used in security-constrained unit commitment and economic dispatch, while convex relaxations, machine learning surrogates, and other approximations are studied extensively in the academic literature. Because these approximations neglect or relax parts of the AC power flow equations, their solutions must be adjusted before dispatch; for example, the DC optimal power flow, which neglects transmission losses, reactive power, and voltage magnitude variations, is known to produce solutions that are always infeasible. The cost of this adjustment is not adequately understood. This paper proposes a method that quantifies, for any approximate solution, the minimum cost of the adjustments that restore AC feasibility, which is a lower bound on the cost of the heuristic adjustments used in practice. We apply it to the DC optimal power flow, the second-order cone and quadratic convex relaxations, and the AC optimal power flow solved to a loose relative tolerance of $10^{-4}$ instead of $10^{-8}$. Relative to the AC optimal power flow solution obtained from a local nonlinear optimization solver, and even with the minimum adjustment, the DC optimal power flow requires adjusting, on average, generators that account for 15.6% of total generation capacity and incurs a 1.10% cost increase; the convex relaxations require more adjustment (17.2% and 16.9%) but smaller cost increases (0.68% and 0.78%); and the loose-tolerance AC optimal power flow requires 6.1% and incurs 0.42%. These results indicate significant value in operating markets directly on the AC optimal power flow, which avoids the distortion of the dispatch and prices caused by heuristic feasibility restoration.
Energy rigidity and weak--strong uniqueness for the anisotropic Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^2_+$

In this paper, we study the two-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with only horizontal dissipation in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{R}^2_+$. The combination of the missing directional regularity and the influence of the boundary presents an essential difficulty for the pressure estimates. We circumvent this difficulty by establishing an extension theorem for the weak formulation, based on the divergence-free condition and the homogeneous impermeability boundary condition. A key feature of this extension principle is that no boundary condition is required for the tangential velocity component. Consequently, every weak solution in the natural energy class on $\mathbb{R}^2_+$ admits a reflection extension that is a weak solution of the corresponding whole-space problem on $\mathbb{R}^2$. This extension allows us to transfer the energy rigidity and weak--strong uniqueness properties established by Demmel and Wiedemann \cite{E-W} to the half-plane setting. In particular, we prove the energy equality for weak solutions in the natural energy class and establish weak--strong uniqueness under the corresponding additional regularity assumptions.
Christian Böhning; Hans-Christian Graf von Bothmer; Alena Pirutka; Zhijia Zhang

We prove that a very general quartic hypersurface of any positive dimension over an uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2 does not admit an integral decomposition of the diagonal, and in particular it is not stably rational.
A posteriori error estimates for the bulk--surface Cahn--Hilliard system with dynamic boundary conditions

This paper develops reliable residual-based a posteriori error estimators for the full discretization of a bulk--surface Cahn--Hilliard system with a two-parameter family of dynamic boundary conditions on a curved domain. The main novelty are theoretically justified computable temporal, coarsening and geometric error estimators. The numerical method combines a linear bulk--surface finite element method in space and a linearly implicit backward Euler method in time. Based on the derived error indicators, a space--time adaptive algorithm is proposed and numerical experiments illustrate and complement the theoretical result.

We consider a construction of hyper-Hermitian structures on total spaces of circle bundles over 3-quasi-Sasakian manifolds. We study the HKT-Einstein equation in this setting, proving that a large family of non-homogeneous hyper-complex manifolds admit compatible HKT-Einstein metrics with positive Einstein factor. We also show that the hyper-Hermitian structures on such circle bundles are quaternionic balanced or quaternionic Gauduchon if and only if they are HKT. Finally, the HKT-Einstein condition is investigated under the twist construction.
Critical L-values and genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants

We establish a period comparison for a two-dimensional rational Hodge summand of type $(3,0)+(0,3)$ in a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb Q$ with $h^{3,0}=1$. Given an algebraic projector onto the summand and a correspondence whose action on the motive of a rational weight-four newform is nonzero after projection to the summand, restriction to the holomorphic de Rham lines identifies motivic morphisms with maps between these lines. Fixing rational generators of the holomorphic de Rham lines determines a unique isomorphism of homological motives. Its Betti realization then yields an exact relation between geometric periods and two critical modular $L$-values. For the Fermat sextic, we construct the correspondence over $\mathbb Q$ and compute its Betti and de Rham actions, determining the scale from algebraic traces and cup-product pairings. Critical-value evaluations and, under mirror comparison and explicit continuation hypotheses, a continued genus-zero Gromov--Witten partition identity follow as corollaries.
Optimization of Finite Alphabet Message Passing Decoding on Fully Node-Parallel Architectures for 5G LDPC Codes
Alexander von Bank; Oliver Griebel; Eike-Manuel Edelmann; Norbert Wehn; Laurent Schmalen

In this paper, we propose a novel design method for the lookup tables (LUTs) of the minimum reconstruction, computation, and quantization (min-RCQ) LDPC code decoding algorithm. The proposed design method uses Bayesian optimization and samples from a subspace of the design space. The novel design method does not require knowledge about the channel or the modulation format and uses the frame error rate (FER) as loss function. The design method is applicable to irregular low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes with puncturing and shortening. Furthermore, the design method creates a set of iteration-agnostic LUTs that can be used over all iterations, which makes this approach suitable for fully node-parallel decoder architectures. We show that our proposed approach achieves a 38.6 % better energy efficiency than a state-of-the-art normalized min-sum (NMS) decoder without loss in error correction performance.
A posteriori space error estimates for the finite element approximation of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations based on the variational multiscale framework
Javad Sekhavati; Ignacio Martínez-Suárez; Sheraz Ahmed Khan; Joan Baiges; Guillermo Hauke; Ramon Codina

This study introduces a novel a posteriori space error estimator derived within the variational multiscale (VMS) framework for the stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In this framework, the continuous problem is decomposed into coarse and fine scales. The fine scale, often referred to as the sub-grid scale (SGS), is modeled as proportional to the component of the residual orthogonal to the finite element (FE) space. This modeled SGS then serves as a reliable error estimator. Specifically, the approach employs a scaled norm of the SGSs as an a posteriori error estimate, evaluated within the stabilized norm associated with the problem. This methodology was previously applied to the stationary convection-diffusion-reaction equation (Codina et al., 2025) and is now extended to the stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. The accuracy and robustness of the proposed space error estimator are assessed through a series of numerical experiments on both manufactured and benchmark incompressible flow problems. Additionally, its performance is compared in selected cases with the space error estimator proposed by Irisarri and Hauke (2021).
Algebraic coarsening of hierarchical splines with guaranteed error control
Marcelo Actis; Silvano Figueroa; Eduardo M. Garau

We present a purely algebraic coarsening operator for hierarchical spline spaces, obtained by inverting locally the refinement matrix that relates the coarsened basis to the current one. Only the B-splines that interact with the coarsened region are involved, so that a coarsening step reduces to one small least-squares problem followed by explicit corrections of the surviving coefficients, without mass matrices or numerical quadrature. The operator is a left inverse of the refinement matrix, hence exact whenever the fine spline belongs to the coarse space, and leaves the spline unchanged away from the coarsened region. The residual of the least-squares problem bounds the $L^\infty$-error with no unknown constants and is available before the mesh is modified, which yields an adaptive multi-level algorithm that guarantees a prescribed tolerance. The construction carries over to truncated hierarchical B-splines, where the corrections disappear. In numerical experiments, the bound is sharp within an order of magnitude, the local transfer is nearly as accurate as a global $L^2$-projection, and much of the refinement left behind a moving front is removed without degrading the solution.
Density of periodic measures on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ with prescribed arithmetic information
Lifan Guan; Chengyang Wu; Weisheng Wu

Let $F$ be the diagonal flow on the modular space $X_2$, and let $\mathcal{S}_f$ be the set of positive square-free numbers, which is identified with the set of all real quadratic fields via the natural map $d\mapsto \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt d)$. In this paper, we prove that, for any finite subset $A\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f$, there exists a density-zero set $B\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f\setminus A$ such that the set of all $F$-periodic measures with associated quadratic fields from $B$ is dense in the set of all $F$-invariant measures on $X_2$.
Critical excited states in quantum metrology

We investigate criticality-enhanced sensing near ground- and excited-state quantum phase transitions in a strongly coupled qubit-boson system. Accounting for finite-size effects, we design driving protocols that exploit diverging susceptibilities to enhance signal-to-noise ratios in parameter estimation using experimentally relevant generators. We show that the excited-state criticality provides a metrological advantage through single-mode bosonic squeezing in regimes that circumvent the 'death of adiabaticity', limiting conventional critical quantum metrology with ground-state criticality.
Artin-style characterizations of the multiple gamma and sine functions

We extend Artin's characterizations of the gamma function to the multiple setting by means of the Kubert identity. We obtain uniqueness theorems for positive continuous solutions of a difference equation $G(z + 1) = α(z)G(z)$ that also satisfy an Artin-type multiplication formula, remaining within the class of continuous functions under a modest initial condition. The results apply in particular to the Barnes multiple gamma functions and the Kurokawa multiple sine functions.
Newton's Method and Policy Iterations for Viscous Hamilton--Jacobi Equations
Diogo A. Gomes; Xiaoqin Guo; Yeoneung Kim; Hung V. Tran; Yuming P. Zhang

We study Newton's method for the Cauchy problem for viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equations with Hamiltonians that need not be convex. Each Newton step solves a linear parabolic equation obtained by linearizing the equation at the current iterate. We prove that the iterates converge geometrically in \(L^\infty\) from any initial guess satisfying the initial condition, and quadratically in the parabolic Hölder space \(C^{2+α,1+α/2}\) from initial guesses close to the solution. When the Hamiltonian admits a control representation, the Newton iterates coincide with those of classical policy iteration, which therefore inherits both convergence rates. We extend the local quadratic convergence to uniformly parabolic fully nonlinear equations. For small viscosity, we introduce a Nash--Moser variant that smooths the iterate and the residual in space, and we give a convergence criterion with constants independent of the viscosity. Finally, we show how computable residuals certify the error of inexact Newton corrections computed with physics-informed neural networks.
Meridional ranks of iterated Whitehead doubles
Honghao Gao; Shijie Gu; Zhenkun Li; Jian Wang

We prove that every iterated untwisted Whitehead double of a nontrivial two-bridge knot satisfies the meridional rank conjecture. More precisely, for such a knot $K$ and every $N\geq0$, the augmentation rank, meridional rank, and bridge number of $\operatorname{Wh}^N(K)$ are all $2^{N+1}$. We use microlocal sheaf theory and a doubling construction to produce a lower bound for the meridional rank of the Whitehead double, assuming the peripheral data satisfy suitable conditions. For two-bridge knots, the required curves arise from ideal points detecting nonzero boundary slopes. In contrast, the ordinary group rank of an $N$-fold Whitehead double is at most the rank of the companion group plus $N$. We also give a non-example when the doubling construction does not work -- the first Whitehead double of the square knot has augmentation rank at most 5, whereas its meridional rank and bridge number are 6.
Nagata dimension, separation modulus and stochastic embeddings into trees

The separation modulus of a metric space, introduced by Bartal in 1996, is related to different notions of dimensionality. Most generally, Naor and Silberman gave in 2011 an upper bound on the separation modulus in terms of Nagata dimension. We prove that this bound cannot be reversed; that is, there are metric spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension and stochastically embeddable into trees with uniform distortion, which therefore have uniformly bounded separation modulus. Similarly, we construct spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension whose spaces of probability measures endowed with the Earth Mover's Distance (equivalently, their Lipschitz-free spaces) are embeddable into $L_1$ with uniformly bounded distortion. By gluing these spaces together, we obtain infinite Nagata dimensional metric spaces whose separation modulus is finite and whose Lipschitz-free space is isomorphic to $\ell_1$, respectively. Finally, we provide relations between separation modulus and stochastic embeddability into trees, also known as random approximability by tree metrics, in particular for the case of snowflake metrics.
Autonomous Neural Adaptive Control as a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator

We study autonomous neural adaptive control, where the controller modifies the physical dynamics while the data generated by the physical dynamics itself drive subsequent parameter updates. We formulate the coupled evolution of the physical state distribution and controller parameters through a self-consistent transfer operator.
 Assuming that the physical dynamics under each fixed controller admits a unique invariant distribution, we characterize adaptive equilibria through a finite-dimensional self-consistency equation for the stationary mean learning update. We establish existence using Brouwer degree, without requiring global convexity, and reduce uniqueness to uniqueness of the corresponding zero.
 Under suitable differentiability and spectral-gap assumptions, we derive a finite-dimensional criterion for local exponential convergence of both the physical distribution and controller parameters at sufficiently small positive learning rates. The criterion involves the Jacobian of the reduced equation, computed using linear response to include the effect of controller-induced changes in the invariant distribution. The asymptotic slow relaxation time scales inversely with the learning rate.
 We rigorously verify the assumptions and apply the theory to a noisy Duffing-type system with a neural residual compensator, providing a nontrivial example of adaptive control with provable existence, uniqueness, and local stability of an adaptive equilibrium. Numerical experiments illustrate statistical feedback and the role of time-scale separation.
Asymptotic behaviors of solutions to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equations with Hardy potential
Jungang Li; Yansheng Shen; Zeming Wang

In this paper we consider positive weak solutions $u\in\mathcal{D}^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$ to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equation with Hardy potential $(-Δ_p)^s u-μ\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{ps}}=u^{p_s^{*}-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $N\geqslant 2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(1,\infty)$ satisfying $ps<N$, $p_s^{*}=\frac{Np}{N-ps}$ and $μ\in(0,\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p})$, $\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p}$ denotes the sharp constant of the fractional Hardy inequality. By means of a suitable comparison principle for weak subsolutions and supersolutions of the equations $(-Δ_p)^sf=\big(\fracμ{|x|^{ps}}+a(x)\big)f^{p-1}$ on general open set $Ω$, with nonzero exterior data and $a\in L^{\frac{N}{ps}}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$, combined with careful constructions of the weak subsolutions and supersolutions, we prove that every positive weak solution $u$ of the above problem satisfies $C^{-1}\leqslant|x|^{μ_1}(1+|x|)^{μ_2-μ_1}u(x)\leqslant C$ for a.e. $x\in\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $μ_1<μ_2$ are the two roots of the indicial equation associated with the Hardy operator and $C\in[1,\infty)$ depends on $u$. Also, we show that the constant $C$ cannot be chosen to depend only on $N$, $s$, $p$ and $μ$.
Base Change Of Local Fundamental Group Schemes

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $K/k$ a field extension, $X$ a geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$, and $x\in X(k)$. We study when the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrowπ^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. If $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated, then it is an isomorphism for every algebraic extension $K/k$. If $π^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then it is an isomorphism if $K/k$ is purely transcendental or $k$ is algebraically closed. Combining these results, if $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated and $π^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrow π^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. As an application, if $X_{\bar k}$ is smooth and rationally chain connected, then the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\longrightarrowπ^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism.
Contour-Assisted Evolutionary Computation: Estimating Peaks From the Contour Lines of Evaluated Solutions
Jun Zhang; Tong Qian; Hua Ding; Zhi-Hui Zhan; Wei-Jie Yu; Jian-Yu Li

Evolutionary algorithms (EAs) evaluate many candidate solutions but use them mainly to rank individuals. This paper treats the evaluated solutions as the spot heights of a topographic survey and draws the contour lines they imply. The contour map decomposes the evaluated region into peaks: in two dimensions a contour tree with persistence separates significant peaks from interpolation ripples, and in more dimensions hill climbing on the interpolated surface locates the peaks and ray-cast level sets describe them. A memory of the explored peaks directs the search to new ones. The data-supported contours of each peak are extrapolated to zero size by an area law, exact for quadratic peaks and second-order accurate for smooth ones, that estimates a peak's location, height and shape before it is sampled. A contour-assisted EA (CA-EA) inserts contour steps with local search and peak memory into a genetic algorithm (GA), differential evolution or particle swarm optimization. A contour-assisted surrogate-assisted EA (CA-SAEA), for expensive problems, spends each evaluation on surrogate-screened offspring or on sampling around a peak, entered at the maximum of the interpolated surface. On 2-D benchmarks, CA-EA reduces the evaluations a plain GA needs by factors of 12 to 112; controls attribute its gain over classical memetic search to restarting local search on distinct peaks. On the CEC 2015 expensive suite in 10 and 30 dimensions, CA-SAEA has the second-best average rank, behind DYCORS and ahead of lq-CMA-ES and the competition winner MVMO, although in 30 dimensions MVMO wins significantly on 9 functions and loses on 6; there the map beats sampling around the best point on 5 of 15 functions and loses on 3. Entering the peaks at their extrapolated locations brought no gain at these budgets, although, with enough samples, it improves the estimated heights on most two-dimensional functions.
Determinant Identities and Branch Selection in the Stationary Multi-Horizon Balance Problem

We study the Hennig-Neugebauer family of stationary and axisymmetric vacuum multi-horizon candidates. The regularity conditions on the symmetry axis lead to quadratic determinant relations which leave an apparent ambiguity between two sign branches. Under explicit non-degeneracy assumptions, we prove that one of these branches is impossible. This branch selection yields a system of explicit determinant equations characterizing equilibrium within the family.
Calderón-Zygmund estimates and their failure for PDE with linear growth

We investigate when Calderón-Zygmund estimates hold for PDEs of the type \[ \operatorname{div}(A(\nabla u)) = \operatorname{div}(F) \] where $A: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ is a continuous map with linear growth. We show that, under natural assumptions, $L^p$-Calderón-Zygmund estimates hold for all $p \in (1,\infty)$ if and only if $v \mapsto \lim_{t \to \infty} A(tv)/t$ is linear and non-degenerate.
An Empirical Square-Root Law for the Degree Discrepancy of Binary m-Sequences

Let $k\ge 2$, $N=2^k$, $M=N-1$ and let $Δ(r)$ be the range, over all starting offsets, of the total-variation degree discrepancy of a length-$r$ window of a primitive binary linear feedback shift register (LFSR) of period $M$. Degree-discrepancy profiles for every $k\le 28$ support the scaling $\max_r Δ(r)=Θ(\sqrt{N})=Θ(2^{k/2})$. The tabulated peaks are maxima on a discrete grid, hence lower bounds on the exhaustive maximum. The normalized peaks $d_k=\max_{r\in R_k}Δ(r)/2^{k/2}$ oscillate between values near 1/2 and values that approach, but do not exceed, 1. The data suggest $\liminf d_k=1/2$ and $\limsup d_k\le 1$. We conjecture the same square-root law for the exhaustive maximum, with those normalized envelopes. A Brownian-bridge heuristic accounts for the square-root scale. The same profiles do not place the recorded maximizer at mid-path: after folding by the complement identity $Δ(M-r)=Δ(r)$, the median of $\min(ρ^*_k,1-ρ^*_k)$ is 0.35, and several $k$ (notably 16 and 28) peak on a short window. Mid-horizon $Δ$ remains a large fraction of the peak, so the square-root scale can still come from a Brownian-bridge envelope. The same range has two readings of the starting offset: a pairing fragment in serial-knockout scheduling, and a change to the plaintext on an LFSR orbit. The location of the maximizer is not part of the conjecture. Open questions that separate the conjecture from a theorem are listed.
Sampling the Funnel: A Comprehensive Survey of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for Hierarchical Bayesian Inference

Hierarchical models are central to applied Bayesian statistics, yet the variance structures they depend on can produce posterior geometries that remain difficult to explore even with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), a designation now covering a large and increasingly heterogeneous family of algorithms. This survey uses Generalized HMC as an organizing framework to describe the many variants of HMC, their methodological and computational properties, and their empirical consequences. Varying the trajectory length, the degree of momentum refreshment, and the presence of a Metropolis correction recovers several familiar Hamiltonian and Langevin samplers as special cases. Three further, largely independent directions account for much of the remaining literature: modifying the metric, as in Riemannian HMC; modifying the Hamiltonian used by the acceptance test, as in modified or shadow HMC; and modifying the numerical integrator, as in multi-stage splitting schemes. We review these variants alongside the procedures used to tune and diagnose them, with particular attention to the effective sample size, whose standard estimators assume a reversibility that generalized and modified samplers lack, and ignore the importance weights that modified Hamiltonians introduce. We close with the open problems these methods face for hierarchical models, taking joint longitudinal and time-to-event models as the motivating example.
Metriplectic Lotka--Volterra systems with noise:interactions invisible at stationarity, visible in time
J. A. Capitán; A. Megías; C. Sardón

We show that a Lotka--Volterra system with an interior equilibrium admits a metriplectic structure, with a Volterra function $V_C$ as energy and an entropy variable for the environment, if and only if Volterra's dissipativity condition $CA+A^{\top}C\le0$ holds, and we construct it explicitly with a log-canonical Poisson bivector. Adding noise through the fluctuation--dissipation relation of stochastic GENERIC yields multiplicative environmental noise, with covariance fixed by the symmetric part of $AC^{-1}$, whose stationary law is an explicit Gibbs measure: a product of independent Gamma distributions. Unlike known Gibbs measures for stochastic Lotka--Volterra systems, this holds for nonsymmetric interactions, predator--prey included. The stationary law determines only the equilibrium and $C/k$: every interaction matrix in an open cone of dimension $n^2$, in particular any Poisson part, produces with its compatible noise the same law as uncoupled stochastic logistic equations. Gamma-distributed, uncorrelated abundance fluctuations, as observed in microbial communities, are therefore no evidence of absence of interactions. The interactions are, however, visible in time: the zero-lag derivative of the log-abundance covariance equals $A(C/k)^{-1}$, and its antisymmetric part is the Poisson part, which carries all the stationary entropy production, computed in closed form. Finally, for general noise we prove an exact Lyapunov-type identity $AK+K^\top A^\top+Q=0$ for $K=\mathrm{Cov}(x,\log x)$ at any stationary solution. It implies that the populations are independent if and only if the noise is metriplectically compatible, and gives an explicit lower bound on interspecies cross-covariances in terms of the distance of $Q$ to the compatible family. Simulations of a predator--prey model show that the bound is nearly sharp.
Chongying Dong; Siu-Hung Ng; Li Ren; Feng Xu

We investigate the orbifold theory for condensable algebras in fusion categories $\mathcal{C}$. We prove that the algebra automorphism group of a condensable algebra $A$ is finite and explicitly characterize its elements in terms of the fusion action and indecomposable $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$-bimodule decomposition of $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. We further show that a finite group action on $A$ gives rise to a group extension of the category $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$ in $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. Conversely, every such group extension arises from a finite group of algebra automorphisms of $A$. Finally, we also construct a canonical maximal group extension of $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$, thereby providing a categorical framework for the classical correspondence among finite group actions, fixed-point algebras, and twisted modules.

We study the splitting number at singular cardinals with emphasis on what we call the reduction to the cofinality problem: whether $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}$ holds for a singular cardinal $κ$. Our main tool is the transfinite logarithm function $\mathrm{log}_{2}(μ) := \min \{ λ\in \mathrm{card} \colon μ\leq 2^λ \}$ defined for every infinite cardinal $μ$. We prove that the reduction holds, and in fact $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathrm{log}_{2}(\mathrm{cf}(κ))$, whenever $\mathrm{cf}(κ)$ is uncountable and not weakly compact. When $\mathrm{cf}(κ) = \aleph_{0}$, we show that $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathfrak{s}$ provided that $\mathfrak{s} \leq \log_{2}(κ)$, while the failure of the reduction is consistent with $\mathrm{ZFC}$. When $\mathrm{cf}(κ)$ is weakly compact, we use a model constructed by Ben-Neria and Gitik to prove that, under suitable large cardinals hypothesis, $\mathfrak{s}_κ < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}$ is consistent. Furthermore, we show that the consistency strength of $\mathrm{ZFC} \, +$"$\exists κ\in \mathrm{card} [\mathrm{cf}(κ) > \aleph_{0} \wedge \mathfrak{s}_κ < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}]$'' is at least that of the negation of the singular cardinal hypothesis. Finally, we study the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}_κ$, extending several results about the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}$ to the uncountable setting. In particular, we show in $\mathrm{ZFC}$ that there are regular cardinals $κ$ such that $\mathfrak{s}_κ$ is singular, partially answering an open question posed by Fischer and Soukup.
Specializations of frozen variables for Grassmannian cluster algebra

The homogeneous coordinate ring of a Grassmannian variety $\mathrm{Gr}_{k,n}$ is equipped with a structure of a cluster algebra. The frozen variables are identified with the Plücker coordinates corresponding to length-$k$ segments of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. We study two families of algebras: the first family is obtained by specializing all the frozen variables and the second corresponds to the specialization of the nonwrapping variables. We construct flat bases in both families and study their affine spectra. The special fibers of the families are cones over projective varieties. We identify the irreducible components of these projective varieties with certain positroid varieties.
Representation Theory and the Algebraic K-Theory of Geometric Fields

We apply a derived completion construction for commutative ring spectra to give a description of the K-theory spectrum of a geometric field F (i.e. containing an algebraically closed subfield $k$) of characteristic zero purely in terms of the representation theory of its absolute Galois group $G_F$. A result that follows is that the l-adically completed Milnor K-theory of F is isomorphic to the derived completion of the representation ring of $G_F$. The main result, from which this follows, is that $K(F)$ completed at l is equivalent to the derived completion of the K-theory of the category of finite dimensional representations of $G_F$ in $k$.
Quasicentral modulus for almost normal operators
In 1984, Voiculescu conjectured that the Hilbert--Schmidt quasicentral modulus vanishes for every almost normal operator. We prove this conjecture.

We propose and provide evidence for the following conjecture: the covering number of a product of metric spaces with the sum metric is greater than or equal to the product of their covering numbers. This generalizes Vizing's conjecture in graph theory. We prove an infinitesimal version of the conjecture for Finsler manifolds of dimension at least six.
Determination of a Bi-periodic Refractive Index for the Helmholtz Equation

We investigate an inverse problem for the Helmholtz equation in a three-dimensional half-space with a biperiodic medium above a sound-soft plane. We establish the uniqueness of a real-valued, bounded, biperiodic refractive index that depends only on the horizontal variables using spectral techniques. %The frequency and quasiperiodicity parameter are fixed. An orthogonality identity is first derived from near-field measurements. By constructing suitable separated solutions, this identity is reduced to relations involving eigenfunctions of two-dimensional quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators. To recover Fourier information from these relations, we project horizontal plane waves onto suitable high-energy spectral subspaces, obtaining finite combinations of eigenfunctions that approximate the plane waves with a quantified error. Combining these approximations with the orthogonality identity, we show that all Fourier coefficients of the difference of two refractive indices vanish, thereby establishing the desired uniqueness.
Minghui Ma; Rui Shi; Jianming Yang; Shanshan Yang

Let $\mathcal M$ be a factor acting on a separable complex Hilbert space. For every operator $T$ in $\mathcal M$ with dense generalized kernel and $T^2\ne 0$, we characterize the strong reducibility of $T$ relative to $\mathcal M$ based on a $3\times 3$ asymmetric matrix representation of $T$. As applications, we obtain criteria for the strong reducibility of algebraic operators in finite factors and type $\mathrm{III}$ factors. We also prove that every Hilbert space operator with an infinite-dimensional multicyclic direct summand is similar to an irreducible operator.
Weighted minimal surfaces in H2 x R invariant under hyperbolic translations
Katianny Rosa Freitas; António Martínez; João Paulo dos Santos

In this paper, we consider weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR, namely, surfaces that arise as critical points of a weighted area functional, where the corresponding weight depends only on the height function associated with the second factor R. We refer to these surfaces as φ-minimal surfaces. For a class of increasing and concave weight potential functions φ, we focus our attention on height-weighted minimal surfaces that are invariant under isometries of H2xR that act trivially on R and act by hyperbolic translations in H2. Through a detailed analysis of the corresponding three-dimensional system of ordinary differential equations, we present families of entire graphs, graphs over half-spaces of H2 that are asymptotic to vertical planes, winglike surfaces, and surfaces whose height function has no minimum. These families show that the hyperbolic-invariant setting is considerably richer than the rotational and parabolic settings. For the class of potential functions φ we consider, they also allow us to classify all weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR that are invariant under hyperbolic translations.

High-order recombination keeps weak approximation trees of diffusions small
 by a moment-preserving reduction of the measure on each patch of nodes.
 The weighted Litterer--Lyons (WLL) test of Ninomiya and Shinozaki
 sets the patch scale using a scalar \(λ>0\) chosen
 beforehand, whose appropriate value depends on coordinate units.
 First, the anisotropically weighted Litterer--Lyons (AWLL) rule
 selects the scale during recombination within a bounded factor of
 the measured increment amplitude. On a fixed set of nodes, expanding
 coordinate units leaves the AWLL patch-count bound unchanged but raises

 systems with initial price or forward rate 100, AWLL reduces
 the terminal supports of WLL with \(λ=1\) by factors of 137 and
 1488 at comparable errors, but enlarges them at smaller Heston initial
 prices. Second, \(λ\) is extended to a positive definite matrix
 with a joint error bound for prices and sensitivities, a bound on
 the gain of its shape, and patch-count bounds. Third, the elimination stage of batched basis

 arithmetic operations for \(J\) nodes at fixed moment rank and panel width, against

Sampled resolvents of $C_0$-semigroups: aliasing and sharp rates on the Crandall-Pazy scale

For a $C_0$-semigroup $(S_t)$ with generator $B$, sampling the Laplace integral $(λ-B)^{-1}=\int_0^\infty e^{-λt}S_t\,dt$ on the grid $T\mathbb{N}$ gives $Q_T=T(I-e^{-λT}S_T)^{-1}$, the impulse-invariant discretization of the resolvent. The motivation is a dyadic series of Castillo, Costin and Costin for the resolvent of a self-adjoint operator: its partial sums are exactly $Q_{2^{-N}}$, so the series is a telescoped rectangle rule. By Poisson summation, on $D(B)$ the error of $Q_T$ is the scalar $T/2$ plus the symmetric limit of the resolvents at the alias points $λ-2πin/T$, $n\ne0$, and the dyadic levels remove these aliases according to the $2$-adic valuation of $n$. Our main result is a sharp scale of rates for the trapezoid correction $Q_T-\frac T2I$. If $(S_t)$ belongs to the Crandall--Pazy class with parameter $α\in(0,1]$, that is $\|BS_t\|=O(t^{-1/α})$ as $t\to0$, the error is $O(T^α)$ in operator norm, $O(T^{α+θ})$ on the interpolation space of order $θ$ between $X$ and $D(B)$, and $O(T^{1+α})$ on $D(B)$, the last requiring only resolvent decay of order $α$ along the line $\mathrm{Re}\, z=\mathrm{Re}\,λ$. For self-adjoint generators we give closed forms for the contribution of each dyadic level to Stone's formula, and we translate the results into an explicit error bound and step-size rule for Green functions computed from sampled autocorrelations.
