The singularities are not isolated anymore and cuspidal edges appear. In this setting, implicitization is a heavy endeavour and we need another technology, related to AI; we describe this briefly. The 2D activities have been proposed to in-service teachers learning towards an advanced degree.
Frame Measure Rigidity and Fiber Entropy for Homogeneous Self-Similar Measures

Let N >= 2, 0 < ρ< 1, and let b_0, ..., b_{N-1} be distinct vectors in \mathbb{R}^d. Let μbe the uniform homogeneous self-similar probability measure generated by the maps S_a(x) = ρx + b_a, without any separation assumption. We prove that if μadmits a frame measure, then the conditional coding measure is a Dirac mass for μ-almost every point. Equivalently, the coding map restricts to a Borel bijection between full-measure subsets of the symbolic space and the attractor. Consequently, the fiber entropy vanishes at every finite level, and μis exact dimensional with $\dim_H μ= \frac{\log N}{-\log ρ} \leq d.$ In particular, μadmits no frame measure whenever its Hausdorff dimension is strictly smaller than the similarity dimension. This excludes frame measures whenever Nρ^d > 1. As an application, we show that the uniform consecutive-digit Bernoulli convolution on the real line admits a frame measure in the range N^{-1} <= ρ< 1 if and only if ρ= N^{-1}.
Frege's election method: discrepancy, invariant polygons and Farey geometry
Jean-Pierre Conze; Svante Janson; Anders Öberg

We give a comprehensive study of Frege's modified election method as a proportional allocation rule and as a dynamical system. The method was introduced by Harrenstein, Lackner and Lackner (2022) as a modification of Frege's original proposal (1918), and it coincides with the greedy algorithm for the chairman assignment problem studied by Coppersmith et al. (2011). We consider several aspects of this method. First, we prove that the harmonic bound on the discrepancy earlier shown to be sharp for time-dependent vote proportions remains sharp for fixed vote proportions; we further quantify the restrictions on votes needed for the discrepancy to come close to this bound. Secondly, the method defines a dynamical system with a piecewise translation which, for almost every vote vector, has a unique compact attractor made up of finitely many polytopes, and every orbit is equidistributed on it, whatever choices are made at ties. Thirdly, for three parties, the dynamics is two-dimensional. We construct the invariant polygons explicitly and give a complete description of the geometry governing their bifurcations as the votes vary in the two-dimensional parameter space; this space is partitioned into a countably infinite number of ``Farey cells'' indexed by reduced fractions in $(0,\frac12]$, and each of them is further partitioned into a finite number of stability domains, separated by stability walls. In an open Farey cell indexed by a reduced fraction $u/v$, the invariant polygon has $4v+3$ vertices inside each stability domain and $4v+2$ on an internal stability wall. We construct the Farey cells explicitly and determine all stability walls and their endpoints; we also show that stability walls in different Farey cells combine to form a pattern of triangles.
Universal Approximation Theorem for Metaplectic Neural Operators

We prove universal approximation for metaplectic neural operators on nonempty bounded Lipschitz domains. The nonlocal branches are whole-space metaplectic multipliers with zero extension and restriction, associated with any fixed free symplectic matrix. Assuming a smooth, globally Lipschitz, nonpolynomial activation, we obtain compact-uniform approximation of continuous operators from $C^s$ to $C^r$ and from $H^s$ to $H^r$ in the respective output norms, for arbitrary nonnegative integers $s,r$ and finite input and output channel dimensions. In the Sobolev setting, compact input sets must additionally be uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$. One hidden operator layer with one nonlocal branch suffices. A single scalar symbol atom and finitely many positional features are prescribed by the transform and domain independently of the target operator, compact set and accuracy. The proof combines averaging neural operator theory with an exact chirp-conjugated averaging identity and derivative estimates. The result includes Fourier and fixed nondegenerate fractional Fourier multiplier constructions.

It is known that the genuine irreducible Iwahori-spherical representations of a tame $n$-fold Brylinski-Deligne cover of a $p$-adic split connected reductive group are all generic, when the degree $n$ is suitably large. This has been established by studying the the structure of the Gelfand-Graev representation as a module under the action of the Iwahori-Hecke algebra. In this paper, we present a different proof based on metaplectic Moy-Prasad theory.
Communication-Learning Co-Design for Pinching-Antenna-Assisted Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
Shuai Wang; Wenxuan Sun; Mingjie Shao; Wantao Jiang; Yanqing Xu; Lingxiang Li; Zhi Chen

Wireless federated learning (FL) suffers from two coupled bottlenecks: statistical heterogeneity across clients and communication-constrained model synchronization over unreliable wireless links. Instead of focusing on algorithmic design and/or wireless resource optimization, this paper provides a systematic study of pinching antenna (PA)-empowered FL for heterogeneous wireless networks and develops a unified communication-and-learning framework. Specifically, we integrate a segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (SWAN) architecture with a heterogeneity-robust FL algorithm based on client variance reduction and dual quantization, so as to jointly mitigate communication bottlenecks and client drift. On this basis, we further develop a two-stage SWAN-assisted downlink protocol and formulate fairness-oriented uplink optimization problems for PA positioning, bandwidth allocation, and quantization design. Efficient solution frameworks are then derived for the resulting downlink and uplink optimization problems. Experimental results show the superiority of the proposed design in convergence speed and final accuracy under non-independent and identically distributed data and communication bottlenecks.
Distributionally Robust Indirect-Feedback Stochastic MPC with Gelbrich Ambiguity Sets
Jiaxun Sun; Riccardo Cescon; Marcell Bartos; Melanie N. Zeilinger

Stochastic model predictive control uses disturbance statistics to set safety margins. Errors in these statistics can invalidate the safety guarantees. This paper therefore describes the uncertainty in the disturbance mean and covariance by a prescribed Gelbrich ambiguity set. This contains distributions of any shape whose moments are close in the Gelbrich distance to the nominal values, including distributions with unbounded support. For linear time-invariant systems with additive disturbances, we build on the indirect feedback paradigm, propagate this moment uncertainty along the error dynamics, and obtain a closed-form constraint tightening that is computed offline. Robustness enters as a single additive term that grows with the size of the ambiguity set, so the online problem remains a quadratic program. Recursive feasibility and closed-loop satisfaction of conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraints hold for every disturbance distribution in the set. We illustrate the method on a linearized planar quadrotor.
Optimization-Based Path Planning for Industrial Manipulators: Experimental Validation in Additive Manufacturing
Shiva Ganesh Murali; Valentin Bhend; Deepak Ingole; Gabriele Fadini; Alisa Rupenyan

Robotic additive manufacturing requires joint paths that reconcile robot feasibility with process-specific geometry. We develop an offline optimization-based path planner that combines joint-path regularity and self-collision penalties with process costs and constraints, so that a new process enters through its own reference, residuals, and tolerances. Full-path and boundary-coupled chunked optimization handle references of different lengths. Iterative Weight Tuning (IWT) determines the cost weights from the gaps between Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and their targets. In carbon-fiber winding and robotic 3D printing, the planned paths meet the geometric tolerances and all KPI targets, and both paths are executed on a UR10e, without extrusion for printing, with joint-level tracking recorded during execution.
Maximal Violation of Mermin Inequality for Commuting von Neumann Algebras and Multipartite Vacuum Entanglement in QFT
Kan He; Jinchuan Hou; Shuyuan Yang; Bingke Zheng

Summers and Werner proved that Bell inequalities are violated maximally and generically in the vacuum of a relativistic quantum field theory in [S. J. Summers and R. Werner, Commun. Math. Phys. 110 (1987), 247-259]. Their criterion concerns two-party case, that is, there are two algebras of quantum observables: one algebra and its commutant. In this case, the maximal CHSH value is converged to in every normal state exactly when the algebra is strongly stable. In the paper, we study the corresponding question for three and more mutually commuting von Neumann algebras. We focus on the multipartite Mermin inequalities instead of CHSH ones. For the tripartite Mermin functional we show that maximal violation in every normal state is equivalent to the existence of a common sequence of asymptotic GHZ stabilizers. Strong stability of each local factor is an necessary condition for maximal violation, and a joint embedding of an infinite GHZ tensor product is sufficient. Counterexamples show that strong stability and type III_1 of the individual algebras, even together with tripartite duality, do not suffice to arrive at the maximal violation. The results are also extended to n>=3 parties.
On $q$-Ary $t$-Designs from Codewords of Every Nonzero Weight in Linear Codes and Their Duals

The paper investigates when the codewords of every nonzero weight in a linear code form a $q$-ary $t$-design and how to generalize the property to its dual code. We reduce the verification of this property to a prescribed range of low weights. Specifically, for MDS codes, we show that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at every nonzero weight is equivalent to that at any fixed nonzero weight. As an application, we prove that the codewords of every nonzero weight in a $[q+1,3,q-1]_q$ MDS code and its dual hold $q$-ary $2$-designs if and only if $q$ is even. We also establish a duality principle. When $t\le\min\{d,d^{\perp}\}$, the codewords of every nonzero weight in a linear code form a $q$-ary $t$-design if and only if the same property holds for its dual code. We then investigate narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,δ,1)}$ and their duals. For $q=2^m$ and $δ=2^r$ with $1\le r<m$ and $\gcd(r,m)=1$, the codewords of every nonzero weight in these codes form $q$-ary $2$-designs. Furthermore, for $δ=4$ and $q=2^{m}$ ($m\ge4$), we establish that the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,4,1)}$ form a $q$-ary $2$-design if and only if $m$ is odd.
Two-parameter versus one-parameter quantum groups: structural differences arising from the type~$D$ phenomenon
Naihong Hu; Marc Rosso; Xiao Xu

This paper investigates several differences between two-parameter and one-parameter quantum (affine) algebras. We compare their Hopf algebra structures, algebra structures, automorphism groups of positive parts and extended Borel algebras, and module categories beyond the finite-dimensional setting. These differences are closely related to what we call \textit{``the type $D$ phenomenon''}, which widely appears in the structure of both finite and affine two-parameter quantum groups.
On the Spectral Estimation of VARMA Processes

We consider the problem of estimating the power spectral density of a Vector-valued Autoregressive Moving-Average (VARMA) process. A well-established approach to accomplishing this task consists of formulating a moment problem that selects the spectral density maximizing an entropy-like index while matching certain moments of the underlying process. However, existing methods assume that the moving-average (MA) component is either fixed or scalar, thereby reducing the class of ARMA models over which the optimal spectral density is sought. In this paper, we propose a new moment problem, based on the notion of transportation entropy, for learning the spectral density of a VARMA process without fixing the MA component or restricting it to be scalar.
Euclidean and Hermitian Self-Orthogonal Codes from Divisible Codes

Self-orthogonality and divisibility are two fundamental properties of linear codes, and the relationship between them has long been of interest. Huffman and Pless (2003) showed that every binary \(4\)-divisible code is Euclidean self-orthogonal, that a ternary code is Euclidean self-orthogonal if and only if it is \(3\)-divisible, and that a quaternary code is Hermitian self-orthogonal if and only if it is \(2\)-divisible. The general case remained open for a long time. In 2024, Li and Heng settled the odd-characteristic case, proving that every \(p\)-divisible code over \(\F_{p^m}\), with \(p\) odd, that contains the all-one vector is Euclidean self-orthogonal. In this paper we treat the even-characteristic case: we prove that every \(4\)-divisible code over \(\F_{2^m}\) containing the all-one vector is Euclidean self-orthogonal. We also prove that, for every prime \(p\), every \(p\)-divisible linear code over \(\F_{q^2}\), where \(q=p^m\), that contains the all-one vector is Hermitian self-orthogonal. In addition, we generalize the Hermitian criterion to the Galois self-orthogonal case, proving that any $p$-divisible linear code over $\gf_{q^r}$ that contains the all-one vector is $\ell$-Galois self-orthogonal for \(\ell\in\{1,\dots,r-1\}\). These criteria make the construction of self-orthogonal codes from divisible codes simple and efficient. As applications, we recover the known Euclidean and Hermitian self-orthogonality of generalized Reed--Muller codes and obtain several infinite families of new Euclidean and Hermitian self-orthogonal codes, which give rise to infinite families of quantum codes with excellent parameters.
On the minimum number of entries in a set of maximal mutually orthogonal partial Latin squares
Diane M. Donovan; Mike J. Grannell; Emine Sule Yazici

In superimposed form, a set of $k\ge2$ mutually orthogonal partial Latin squares of order $n$ is said to be maximal if no additional $k$-tuple may be inserted into any empty cell without violating orthogonality or the Latin property. For $k=2$ and $n\ge 21$ it is shown that the minimum number of filled cells in such a square is $\lceil n^2/3 \rceil$. Likewise for $k=3$ and $n\ge 44$ the minimum number of filled cells is $\lceil n^2/4 \rceil$ or $\lceil n^2/4 \rceil+1$, depending on the residue of $n$ modulo 4. In each case it is shown that the extremal systems are essentially those produced by a construction presented in the paper. A similar result is obtained for all $k\ge4$ for minimal systems that have a certain balance property, and it is conjectured that for sufficiently large $n$, even without this balance property, the extremal systems always correspond to those produced by this construction.
Triangle Factors in the Semi-Random Graph Process

The semi-random graph process is a single player game which starts with an empty graph on $n$ vertices and in each round the player is offered a random vertex and connects it to a vertex selected according to some strategy $\mathcal{S}$. The goal is, in as few rounds as possible, to arrive at a graph that satisfies some graph property $\mathcal{P}$. The main contribution of this work is to show that there is a strategy $\mathcal{S}$ which creates a $K_3$-factor in at most $2.929329 \, n$ rounds w.h.p.
Rank Reversals in Efficient Vectors for Pairwise Comparisons

Studied are the orders among alternatives given by efficient vectors for a reciprocal matrix A. The focus is upon: 1) existence of efficient vectors with a given order and 2) discrepancies between the ranking for a pair of alternatives resulting from an efficient vector and from the corresponding entry of A, called rank reversals. We use matrix intervals in which the consistent matrices built from efficient vectors lie. The existence of efficient vectors (or those from constituent convex subsets) with a rank reversal at a given position is characterized. The minimum number of rank reversals for a reciprocal matrix among all weight vectors is described and it is shown that there is an efficient vector that has this number of rank reversals. A way to construct such a vector is given. The order transitive and the uniformly ordered reciprocal matrices are shown to be, respectively, the matrices for which there is an efficient vector with no rank reversals and the matrices for which all efficient vectors have no rank reversals. The effects on rank reversals of addition and deletion of alternatives are also discussed. Using numerical experiments, the frequencies of rank reversals in certain formulaic weight vectors are given.
Automorphisms of the Reduced Finitary Power Monoid of $\N^d$

Given an additive semigroup $S$, the collection of its nonempty finite subsets can be equipped with the setwise addition \[ X + Y = \{x + y : x \in X, \; y \in Y\}, \] forming a semigroup denoted by $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin}}(S)$, which is called the finitary power semigroup of $S$. If $S$ is a monoid with identity $0$, the finite nonempty subsets containing $0$ form a submonoid $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(S)$, known as the reduced finitary power monoid, whose identity element is the singleton $\{0\}$. Let $d$ be a positive integer, $\mathbb{N}$ the set of nonnegative integers, and $\mathbb{N}^d = \{(a_1, a_2, \dots, a_d) \mid a_i \in \mathbb{N}\}$. For the one-dimensional case \(d=1\), Tringali and Yan (\textit{J. Comb. Theory, Ser. A}, \textbf{209} (2025)) established that the only nontrivial automorphism of $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(\mathbb{N})$ is the involution $X \mapsto \max X - X$. In this paper, we focus on the higher-dimensional case $d \ge 2$. We prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},0}(\mathbb{N}^d)) \cong S_d$, meaning that every automorphism is inner, induced by a permutation of the coordinate directions. This reveals a sharp contrast with the one-dimensional setting, where non-inner symmetries exist.
Geometry-Dependent Approximation and Stability Properties of Shallow ReLU$^k$ Networks on Bounded Euclidean Domains
Yuqing Liu; Tong Mao; Jinchao Xu

On bounded Euclidean domains, we study how hidden-parameter geometry affects shallow ReLU$^k$ networks through results on approximation rates, saturation-type lower bounds, Gram and stiffness matrix spectra, Bernstein and Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund inequalities, discrete least-squares recovery, and inverse approximation. Our analysis uses smooth localization and dyadic Fourier estimates. We quantify parameter geometry by the fill distance $h$ and antipodal separation distance $\underline h$. For the prescribed network space $L_n^k$, representative approximation estimates take the form \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \inf_{g_n\in L_n^k}\|f-g_n\|_{\mathcal L^2(Ω')}&\lesssim h^r\|f\|_{\mathcal H^r(Ω)},\\ \inf_{g_n\in L_n^k}\|f-g_n\|_{\mathcal L^2(Ω)}&\gtrsim \underline h^{\frac{d+2k+1}{2}}\|f\|_{\mathcal L^2(Ω')}. \end{aligned} \end{equation*} The upper bound exploits target regularity up to the critical order $\frac{d+2k+1}{2}$, while the lower bound applies asymptotically to fixed targets smoother than this order. The upper estimate holds on an interior subdomain $Ω'$, whereas the lower estimate concerns the larger domain $Ω$. We also obtain geometry-dependent spectral estimates that quantify conditioning and coefficient stability. Further results establish norm discretization and regularized recovery from function values, and infer target regularity from approximation rates under coefficient or separation conditions. Altogether, these results describe how parameter geometry governs approximation accuracy, the stability of coefficient representations, discrete recovery, and the regularity information contained in convergence rates.
Gelfand-Kirillov dimension of constants of algebraic $q$-skew derivations

Let $δ$ be an algebraic $q$-skew $σ$-derivation of an algebra $R$ over a field of arbitrary characteristic, where $σ$ is an algebraic automorphism of $R$, and let $R^δ$ be the algebra of constants of $δ$. We show that $GKdim(R) = GKdim(R^δ)$ whenever $R$ is semiprime and $R^δ$ is a PI algebra containing no infinite direct sum of nonzero ideals. The polynomial identity cannot be dropped. For every $r \geq 1$ we construct a primitive algebra $R$ with an inner derivation $d$ such that $d^{3} = 0$, $GKdim(R) \geq 2r$ and $GKdim(R^{d}) = 0$, while $R^{d}$ contains no direct sum of two nonzero ideals.
An additively idempotent semiring of least order generating a limit variety

We construct an additively idempotent semiring of order five that generates a limit variety and is not strongly nonfinitely based. The generated variety has exactly two maximal proper subvarieties, both hereditarily finitely based. We also prove that no ai-semiring of order at most four generates a limit variety. Consequently, five is the least possible order of a finite ai-semiring generating a limit variety.
On Monotonicity in Mean Field Games Induced by Discount Factor Transformations
Elisa Continelli; Nicolò De Bernardi; Hei Jie Lam; Alpár R. Mészáros

This paper is devoted to the well-posedness of a class of infinite horizon discounted Mean Field Games (MFGs) problems, where both an exponential discount and a so-called cheap control factors are present simultaneously, and scale in a possibly different way. We introduce a new class of transformations of variables, at the level of both the MFG PDE and the corresponding FBSDE systems. We then show how these transformations reveal a new mechanism that generates semiconvexity estimates for the value function and ensures the existence of mean field equilibria, as long as the parameters land in a suitable regime, that we quantitatively describe. This new mechanism demonstrates furthermore how discount factors lead to a source of strong displacement monotonicity for the Lagrangian, without any initial monotonicity assumptions on the running costs. Consequently, in such regimes of parameters uniqueness of solutions manifests. Our approach uses a Lagrangian point of view, which lets us treat general non-separable Lagrangians and both deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven models in a transparent, unified way. For a specific class of quadratic Lagrangians, using turnpike-type methods, we further obtain an exponential contractivity estimate for the mean field equilibria.
Phase transitions and sharp localisation in anomalous localised resonance

We study how detuning and absorption determine the strength and spatial extent of anomalous localised resonance in a two-dimensional quasistatic coated structure with shell permittivity $-1+c\ell^p+i\ell$, where $\ell>0$ is the loss and $c\ne0$, $p>0$ are fixed. Detuning can carry the material path through narrow resonances, producing intermittent rather than sustained power growth. For an explicit family of noncircular shells and a smooth exterior dipole source, both fixed, we classify the dissipated power under a quantitative smallness condition on the deformation. Depending on the detuning exponent and conformal source distance, the power diverges along the entire path, exhibits divergent peaks with vanishing gaps, or decays, including the threshold cases. We also identify the sharp conformal boundary beyond which the field, normalized by the square root of the dissipated power, converges locally to zero along every divergent-power sequence. For resonant sources, tangential reference crossings yield an explicit nonzero limit for the exterior gradient energy divided by the dissipated power at the critical radius.
Transforms between multivariate Laguerre and Meixner polynomials and their applications to gateways

We establish gateways in both directions between the Laguerre process and a discrete Markov process for every inverse temperature $2θ\geq 1$. Here, a gateway is an intertwining relation between Markov processes with continuous and discrete state spaces. A key ingredient is a pair of generating function identities that relate two double generating functions for multivariate Meixner polynomials to a single and a double generating function for multivariate Laguerre polynomials, respectively. These identities reveal a close relationship between the two families of polynomials and yield integral transforms that underlie the gateway relations. Gateway relations provide a means of transferring properties between continuous and discrete processes. As an application, we derive the Feller-Dynkin property and the uniqueness of the invariant distribution for the Laguerre process from the corresponding properties of the discrete process.
Lengthscale Estimation for the Gaussian Kernel and Deterministic Response Functions

The uncertainty estimates Gaussian processes output rely on the chosen covariance kernel and its hyperparameters. We study the fixed-domain asymptotics of the maximum likelihood and cross-validation estimators of the lengthscale parameter of the popular infinitely smooth Gaussian kernel when the observations are produced by a fixed univariate response function. No theoretical results for Gaussian lengthscale estimation exist in this setting. We prove lower bounds on the lengthscale estimators that depend on the regularity of the response function, as measured by the rate of decay of its Fourier transform. If the response function lives in the Hilbert space of the Gaussian kernel with lengthscale $\ell$, the lower bounds have a straightforward dependency on $\ell$. For bandlimited functions and functions whose Fourier transforms decay as $\exp(-a \lvert ω\rvert^γ)$ for $a > 0$ and $γ> 2$, we prove that the estimators blow up essentially at least as fast as $(\log n)^{(γ-2)/(2γ)}$ in the number of data points, $n$. Bandlimited functions are identified with $γ= \infty$. Unlike analogous results for finitely smooth Matérn kernels, our results make no assumptions on the geometry of the observation points. Numerical experiments illustrate the results.
Asymptotic Bayes Optimality of Sparse Multiple Testing Procedures under One-Factor Dependence

In this paper, we study sparse multiple testing under a Gaussian two-group model with known one-factor covariance and centered Gaussian signals. We derive a first-order risk expansion for the observed-data Bayes Oracle, including a finite-dimensional loading average for heterogeneous loadings and an explicit limiting constant for homogeneous loadings. Under the stated factor-estimation and signal-calibration conditions, the homogeneous one-factor Oracle has strictly smaller leading risk than its independent-coordinate counterpart; observing the latent factor yields no further first-order reduction. We establish asymptotic Bayes optimality under sparsity (ABOS) for the Maximum Residual Down (MRD) step-down procedure with Gavrilov--Benjamini--Sarkar (GBS) stagewise calibration (MRD--GBS). Uniform control of residual errors along the rejection path permits comparison with a fixed factor-known rule without requiring the rejection paths to coincide. Fixed-residual versions of GBS and Benjamini--Hochberg (BH) attain the same leading risk. We also prove ABOS for the Bayesian Step-Down (BSD) rule when supplied with the true mixture, signal variance, covariance, and loss parameters; this is an Oracle-parameterized result. When the expected signal count grows faster than the logarithm of the reciprocal signal proportion, BSD and the observed-data Oracle disagree on several coordinates negligible in probability relative to the expected signal count, explaining BSD's near-Oracle behavior in companion simulations. The results cover diverging and bounded positive expected signal counts, including every fixed polynomial sparsity rate up to the bounded-count regime, under the stated calibrations. A fixed-dimension simulation illustrates absolute-risk behavior but does not establish ABOS.
An Equivariant Coarse Green-Julg Theorem for Proper Actions

We prove an equivariant coarse Green--Julg theorem for proper isometric actions of countable discrete groups on bounded geometry metric spaces. We introduce the $(Γ, X)$-controlled proper $C^{*}$-algebra, and show that the evaluation-at-zero map between the equivariant localization and Roe algebras with such coefficients induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory.
N -phase flow simulations using X-Mesh and an explicit marker interface representation
Antoine Quiriny; Jonathan Lambrechts; Michel Henry; Nicolas Moës; Jean-François Remacle

We present a marker-based X-Mesh framework for incompressible N-phase flow simulations with sharp, explicitly tracked interfaces. The interface is represented by Lagrangian marker chains, while the computational mesh is deformed so that selected mesh edges conform to the tracked geometry without changing mesh connectivity. This combination preserves the advantages of body-fitted finite element discretizations while allowing highly distorted and nearly degenerated elements to capture fine interfacial features on relatively coarse meshes without requiring mesh refinement. The arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) finite element solver uses a pressure field that is continuous within each phase and discontinuous across the fitted interface. Surface tension is introduced through a variational membrane, so the pressure jump is resolved without prescribing a curvature-dependent correction; a Young wall energy provides the corresponding treatment of fluid-fluid-solid triple points. Topological changes are handled geometrically from the marker representation. Numerical experiments illustrate the ability of the approach to transport complex interfaces and to control topology changes through marker-based feature-size criteria.
Generalized Frobenius manifolds: symmetries and their classification in 2-dimensions
Andre Bedell; Misha Feigin; Leo Kaminski; Alessandro Proserpio; Ian A. B. Strachan

A theory of symmetries of generalized Frobenius manifolds is developed. This is used to study the solution space of all generalized Frobenius manifolds that are "above" a specific Frobenius manifold. Since all (semi-simple) Frobenius manifolds in 2-dimensions are known, by constructing all homogeneous Legendre fields associated to these manifolds we classify all 2-dimensional generalized Frobenius manifolds. With this description, the known examples of generalized Frobenius manifolds correspond to distinguished points in this solution space. For Hurwitz-Frobenius manifolds the action of a Legendre transformation on Hurwitz space data, and in particular the primary differential, is given.
Feedback Vertex Set, Max Cut, and Edge Coloring on the Strong Product of a Graph and a Path
Jan Diester; Kolja Kühn; Manuel Rapp; Samuel Schneider; Torsten Ueckerdt

We examine the computational complexity of well-known problems on subgraphs of the strong product of two paths. Namely, for Max Cut we show NP-hardness on induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ answering a question by Dvořák, Huynh, Joret, Liu, and Wood (2021). For 3-Edge Coloring we show NP-hardness on subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ and that it is equivalent to 3-Edge Coloring on planar graphs for induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$. It is a long standing open question whether 3-Edge Coloring on planar graphs is NP-hard. As a second contribution, we consider graphs of the form $G \boxtimes P$ and show that Feedback Vertex Set on these graphs is FPT in the clique-width of $G$. Furthermore, we show that it can be solved in polynomial time if $G$ is chordal or co-comparable and that the computational complexity depends on the parity of $P$ if $G$ is bipartite. Namely, it is solvable in polynomial time if $P$ has an even number of vertices but is NP-complete otherwise. For Max Cut, we show that it can be solved in polynomial time if $G$ is bipartite.
Dual-Space Preconditioning for Variational Inequalities and Root-Finding Problems
Jan Quan; Konstantinos Oikonomidis; Alexander Bodard; Panagiotis Patrinos

This paper develops a dual-space preconditioning framework for variational inequalities and root-finding problems beyond classical cocoercivity and Lipschitz continuity assumptions. To this end, we introduce both a novel cocoercivity-type condition and a relaxed Lipschitz continuity condition, and derive convergence of deterministic and stochastic methods under these generalized conditions. For isotropic preconditioners, the resulting algorithms can be interpreted as variable-stepsize variants of classical methods, extending recent analyses based on $(L_0, L_1)$-type growth conditions while allowing simpler proofs and larger stepsize ranges. We also show that the framework naturally handles variational inequalities through weak Minty-type arguments. Finally, we study the associated continuous-time dynamics and derive a variational and optimal control interpretation of the preconditioned flow. Overall, the results show that dual-space preconditioning provides a flexible mechanism for designing and analyzing operator methods beyond the standard Euclidean Lipschitz setting.
Pólya's conjecture for hyperbolic balls and Berezin--Li--Yau type inequalities

We prove the strict shifted Dirichlet Pólya inequality \[ λ_k(B_R)>\frac{(d-1)^2κ^2}{4}+4π^2\left(\frac{k}{ω_d\operatorname{Vol}_κ(B_R)}\right)^{2/d},\qquad k\ge1, \] for every geodesic ball $B_R$ in hyperbolic space of constant sectional curvature $-κ^2$, in every dimension $d\ge2$. As a consequence, we obtain the shifted Berezin--Li--Yau type inequality for hyperbolic balls, thereby providing a concrete family of domains satisfying both conjectures proposed by Laptev in 2023. For arbitrary nonempty open subsets $Ω\subset\mathbb{H}^d_κ$ of finite volume, we establish the weak Berezin--Li--Yau type inequality \[ \sum_{j=1}^{m}λ_j(Ω)\ge a_{d,κ}m+\frac{d}{d+2}\,4π^2\left(\frac{m}{ω_d\operatorname{Vol}_κ(Ω)}\right)^{2/d}m,\qquad m\ge1, \] with the optimal leading coefficient, where $a_{2,κ}=κ^2/4$ and $a_{d,κ}=d(d-1)κ^2/6$ for $d\ge3$. We also establish the global two-sided estimate for the renormalized eigenvalue sum on hyperbolic space, originally proposed by Strichartz in 1996 and valid for $d\ge3$.
The Role of Insurance in Power-System Risk Management: A Critical Review
Jing Huang; Jiale Guo; Chenjia Gu; Chengcheng Shao; Yue Xiang; Tao Qian; Alexis Pengfei Zhao; Xiuli Wang; Junyong Liu; Xifan Wang

Modern power systems are becoming more renewable-rich, digitalized, and interconnected, making risk propagation and economic consequences increasingly complex. Physical mitigation remains the primary means of risk control, but technical and economic limits leave residual risk. Insurance can complement these measures by transferring associated economic losses and influencing power-system decisions through risk-responsive terms. Despite growing interest, the literature remains fragmented across power-system engineering, actuarial science, and risk finance. This review develops an integrated physical-financial perspective for reviewing insurance in power systems. It examines how power system risks generate residual economic losses and the conditions under which these losses can be insured and transferred. It then develops an actuarial framework for insured-loss assessment and pricing. Insurance-aware decision-making is synthesized through four coupling levels describing how financial protection interacts with power-system decisions. Further progress is constrained by weak physical-financial loss validation, incomplete representation of systemic and evolving portfolio risk, and limited empirical and actuarial grounding of insurance-decision feedback. Research priorities include stronger physical-financial data linkage, forward-looking portfolio assessment, multi-timescale decision feedback, and empirical validation. Addressing these priorities would help move power-system insurance from fragmented applications toward a more coherent approach to residual-risk management in future power systems.
Connectivity and the equilibration of Boltzmann-type equations on dense graphs

We investigate the equilibration of solutions to a homogeneous Boltzmann-type equation whose collision kernel is given by a graphon encoding the connectivity structure of interacting agents. For a broad class of Lipschitz-continuous binary interaction rules, we show that, under suitable conditions relating the interaction parameters to the connectivity properties of the graphon, solutions converge exponentially fast towards those of the classical homogeneous Boltzmann-type equation without preferential connections, and hence towards its equilibrium distributions. We then consider in detail compromise-diffusion interaction rules and establish a quasi-invariant limit leading to a Fokker-Planck-type equation parametrised by the graphon connectivity. This limiting equation allows us to characterise explicitly both connectivity-independent and connectivity-dependent equilibrium distributions.
An Accelerated Dynamic Stochastic Primal-Dual Method for Multi-stage Stochastic Optimization
Bin Zhou; Zhiyun Guo; Hailin Sun; Qi Deng

We consider multi-stage stochastic optimization problems with smooth convex stage costs and linear linking constraints. Dynamic stochastic approximation (DSA), a stochastic first-order method, uses a recursive structure whose memory requirement grows only linearly with the number of stages. Its implementation, however, requires an exact solution of the proximal subproblem associated with the stage cost, and this subproblem often admits no closed-form solution. To resolve this issue, we develop an accelerated dynamic stochastic primal-dual (A-DSPD) framework that retains the recursive value-function structure and only requires the gradient of the stage cost. Within this framework, each stagewise saddle-point subproblem is solved by an inexact accelerated stochastic primal-dual method (iASPD), which applies Nesterov acceleration to the smooth stage cost and uses recursively generated stochastic $ε$-subgradients for the nonsmooth downstream value function. For the stochastic composite saddle-point problem, after $N$ primal-dual updates, iASPD yields optimality and feasibility bounds in which the contribution of the smooth stage cost decays at a faster rate $O(1/N^2)$, while the terms associated with stochastic $ε$-subgradients of the nonsmooth value function decay as $O(1/\sqrt{N})$, up to the prescribed oracle inexactness. We also develop bounds for the stochastic $ε$-subgradient estimators and the dual iterates, which yield complexity guarantees for A-DSPD. Specifically, A-DSPD computes an $ε$-solution using $O(1/ε^4)$ sampled scenarios and $O(1/ε^5)$ primal-dual updates for three-stage problems. We further extend the method and its convergence analysis to problems with an arbitrary finite number of stages. Numerical experiments on three-stage stochastic portfolio models illustrate the empirical advantage of the proposed method.
Thermodynamic Formalism for Non-Invariant Probabilities: Entropy, Divergence, Channels
Artur O. Lopes; Elismar R. Oliveira

Let $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}_σ$ denote, respectively, the sets of Borel and $σ$-invariant probabilities on the uncountable set $Ω=\{1,2,...,d\}^\mathbb{N}$. Given a Hölder Jacobian $J$, the dual Ruelle operator $μ\in \mathcal{M} \mapsto \mathcal{L}_{J}^* (μ)$ will play the role of a dynamical channel; generalizes the action of a stochastic matrix on probability vectors. Since $\mathcal{L}_{J}^*$ generally breaks $σ$-invariance, we introduce the \emph{ni-entropy} $h_{ni}(μ)$ for non-invariant measures, employing the concept of the expected value function on cylinders of size one. $h_{ni}(μ)$ differs from Shannon entropy but extends the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy from $\mathcal{M}_σ$ to $\mathcal{M}$; $h_{ni}$ is concave and u.s.c. This leads us to the concept of ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}(A)$ of a potential $A:Ω\to \mathbb{R}$. $μ\in \mathcal{M}$ is not a density with respect to a dominating measure. We define an {\it ni-Kullback-Leibler divergence} $D_{ni}(ρ|| ν)$ not assuming absolute continuity. We investigate concepts of Information Theory such as Minimal Output Entropy, Donsker-Varadhan variational principle, a variational formula for $h_{ni}$, bounds for divergence, information projections, and their connections to the ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}$.
Switching reconstruction of signed graphs: net-degree and balance
Matteo Cavaleri; Alfredo Donno; Stefano Spessato

The switching reconstruction problem for $2$-edge-colored graphs, introduced by Bondy and Mercier, asks whether such a graph is determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of the graphs obtained by exchanging the colors of the edges at each vertex; for complete underlying graphs it is the vertex-switching reconstruction problem of Stanley. We study this problem in the language of signed graphs, where the net-degree of a vertex and the notion of balance come naturally into play. We prove that a signed graph on $n\neq4$ vertices is reconstructible when its net-degrees are all positive, all negative or all zero, which generalizes the reconstructibility of regular graphs in Stanley's problem. For connected balanced signed graphs, whose switching reconstruction problem we show to be equivalent to that of connected graphs with a distinguished bipartition of the vertex set, we prove reconstructibility when the two parts of the bipartition differ in size by more than two, and when all net-degrees are non-negative.
On the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence for the quantum semisimple groups

The Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence, when it holds for an algebra, characterizes its primitive ideals ( that is, the annihilators of irreducible representations) both algebraically and topologically within the prime spectrum. A stronger form, known as the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence, was introduced by Bell, Launois, and Nolan in their work on 'A strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence for quantum Schubert cells'. In this paper, we prove that the generic quantized coordinate rings of connected, simply connected semisimple complex algebraic groups satisfy the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence.
Face lattices of polytopes and bipolar polytopes

We show that the face lattice of every convex polytope $Q$ is, on the combinatorial level, the vertex set of a polytope one dimension higher: the faces of $Q$ are the vertices of a \emph{bipolar polytope} $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$, and the intervals of the face lattice are its faces. Here a bipolar polytope is a polytope with two distinguished vertices, the poles, such that every facet contains exactly one of them and an intersection property holds. The vertices of every bipolar polytope carry a lattice order whose intervals are the faces, and this lattice is the face lattice of the vertex figure at either pole; conversely, every atomistic and coatomistic lattice that is an abstract polytope arises in this way. Geometrically, the polar of the Cayley polytope of $Q$ and $Q^\circ$ is a convex realization of $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$ whenever the normal fan and the face fan of $Q$ satisfy a certain interval condition; this holds for cubes and cross-polytopes and for suitable realizations of all polytopes of dimension at most three. Finally, every combinatorial type of $3$-polytope has a realization that decomposes into convex bipolar polytopes, one for each vertex.
Grzegorz Bobiński; Carolin Hartung; Jan Schröer

We introduce generalized Jacobian algebras and show that a finite-dimensional algebra is E-symmetric if and only if it is generalized Jacobian. We also characterize E-symmetric algebras in terms of its simple modules. We show that Enomoto's counterexample to the Periodicity Conjecture is a generalized Jacobian algebra, which is not Jacobian in the classical sense.
Bartłomiej Pawelski; Andrzej Szepietowski; Błażej Szepietowski

We study congruence properties of Dedekind numbers $d_n$. Our approach relies on actions of $p$-subgroups of symmetric groups on posets of monotone functions and leads to the congruences $d_{10}\equiv 106\pmod{210}$, $d_{11}\equiv 117\pmod{210}$, and $d_{12}\equiv 12\pmod{30}$. In particular, $d_{11}$ is odd, confirming a claim stated by Yamamoto without a proof.
Weak Quasi-Convexity: First- and Second-Order Conditions, Monotonicity, and Quadratic Functions

In this paper we introduce weakly quasi-convex functions, which are a generalization of weakly convex functions. We study the behavior of weakly quasi-convex functions in Euclidean spaces. We provide several illustrative examples that demonstrate the scope and distinctive features of this new class of generalized convex functions. We derive a necessary condition for weak quasi-convexity under certain assumptions and provide an example showing that its converse is not true for discontinuous functions. Under the continuity assumption on the function involved, a sufficient condition is provided with an adjusted weak quasi-convexity modulus. Also, we bring out various kinds of monotonicity in connection with weakly quasi-convex functions through the gradient mapping. We provide several illustrative examples that interpret and emphasize the newly introduced notions. We establish a first-order necessary condition for the class of differentiable weakly quasi-convex functions. Conversely, we show that a differentiable function satisfying this first-order condition is weakly quasi-convex with an adjusted modulus. We provide a second-order necessary condition under appropriate assumptions using second-order Dini derivatives. As a consequence, we derive a Hessian-based necessary condition for the class of twice continuously differentiable weakly quasi-convex functions. We provide an example to show that the converse of the second-order characterization does not hold. Furthermore, we establish various kinds of necessary conditions concerning general quadratic functions and provide many counterexamples for the failure of their sufficiency. Finally, we derive several consequences of weak quasi-convexity for optimization problems.

In the first half of these notes, we survey some aspects of the stack-theoretic perspective on $p$-adic Hodge theory, with an emphasis on the non-abelian aspects. In the second half, we report ongoing joint work on ``quantizing'' non-abelian $p$-adic Hodge theory.
Alexander Tyurin; QuocViet Pham; Valentin Khrulkov; Ivan Oseledets

We introduce LongTails, a framework for discovering and improving oracle-complexity bounds with formal verification in Lean 4. Using LongTails, we have already obtained more than 100 new results across a broad range of optimization problems, including generalized smoothness, heavy-tailed noise, finite-sum and composite optimization, and higher-order and zeroth-order methods. Our goal is to scale discovery and continually develop new methods with non-trivial and valuable theoretical guarantees using modern agentic systems. The framework is specialized for optimization, where we separate a Setup, specifying the problem class, assumptions, available information, and success criterion, from a Complexity, specifying a sufficient oracle-call budget. Once a Setup is fixed (e.g., $L$-smooth convex optimization with the goal of finding $x_{\mathrm{out}}$ such that $f(x_{\mathrm{out}}) - f(x^\star) \leq \varepsilon$), agents search for better Complexities (e.g., $O(\sqrt{L R^2 / \varepsilon})$, where $R \geq \|x_0 - x^\star\|$) by designing algorithms and proving their convergence. The framework then checks the proofs and guarantees that every accepted Complexity can indeed be attained under the given Setup. This turns the search for new methods into an ongoing effort to improve their theoretical guarantees. To the best of our knowledge, LongTails is the first framework to scale automated research in optimization across such a broad range of problems with formally verified theoretical guarantees.

Cosmological particle production, the excitation of field quanta by a dynamical spacetime, underlies the primordial perturbations observed in the cosmic microwave background and has been realized in analog quantum simulators with ultra-cold atoms. We ask the inverse question: given the excitation spectrum, can the cosmological history that produced it be reconstructed, and is that reconstruction unique? We approach this problem through a mapping of particle production to one-dimensional quantum scattering, in which the expansion history plays the role of a scattering landscape and the produced spectrum the role of reflected and transmitted waves. This mapping reveals a rich interplay between scattering theory and cosmology. The scale factor enters as a zero-energy resonance, an exceptional case of scattering theory, while cosmic singularities correspond to bound states, so that regular cosmologies are governed entirely by the scattering continuum. We find an interesting isospectrality: histories related by an inversion of the scale factor (expansion <-> contraction) yield identical particle numbers, differing only by a pi-shift in phase. Given both the particle number (or alternatively the amplitude) and phase of the cosmological power spectrum, the reconstruction is unique for regular, asymptotically static cosmologies. We demonstrate the reconstruction both analytically, for exactly solvable scattering landscapes, and numerically, recovering common logistic expansion histories to better than 0.02%. We further quantify its robustness to the momentum-space resolution and measurement uncertainties characteristic of analog quantum simulation. This work establishes a direct link between the observable power spectrum and the cosmological history that produced it, offering a new perspective on the classification of early-universe scenarios and the construction of alternatives to inflation.
Victor Bailey; Eva A. Gallardo-Gutiérrez; Jonathan R. Partington

A central question in dynamical frame theory asks when the orbit $\{Λ^n f\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+}$ of a vector $f$ under a bounded operator $Λ$ on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$ is a frame. Christensen, Hasannasab and Philipp answered it, showing in particular that such an operator must be similar to the compression of the unilateral shift on $H^2(\mathbb{T})$ to a coinvariant subspace. We prove a continuous analogue: if a $C_0$-semigroup $\{T(t)\}_{t\ge0}\subset B(H)$ generates a continuous frame $\{T(t)φ\}_{t\ge0}$, then the operators $T(t)$ are simultaneously similar to the compressions of the shift semigroup to a fixed coinvariant subspace. Moreover, $\{T(t)φ\}_{t\ge0}$ is a continuous frame if and only if $\{C^n(I-A)^{-1}φ\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_+}$ is a frame, where $A$ is the infinitesimal generator and $C=(I+A)(I-A)^{-1}$ the cogenerator; the frame bounds of the two systems differ by a factor $2$. We also derive necessary conditions for the existence of frame vectors and discuss several examples. Finally, we show that the compressed shift on a model space $K_θ$ is the cogenerator of a $C_0$-semigroup admitting frame vectors if and only if the inner function $θ$ has a finite angular derivative at $1$; in that case we describe all frame vectors, and the boundary reproducing kernel at $1$ generates a tight continuous frame.
From Complex Regularization to Polynomial Flow: Capture and Escape in Rocking Dynamics
Francisco Prieto-Castrillo; Set Pérez-González; Jesús S. Pérez del Río

We develop a planar polynomial system based on a complex regularization of free rocking and analyze the equilibrium states and phase portraits via an effective radial potential. The conflict between the centrifugal effect, which is introduced by means of regularization, and gravity yields a potential well and an escape barrier for 0 < beta < 27/256; both vanish at a saddle-node bifurcation point. The exact energy conservation law allows us to separate dissipative relaxation, conservative periodic motions along the radial direction, and energy creating trajectories. The node-focus boundary of finite equilibria is different from the degeneracy condition for compactification at infinity. As the last step of analysis, we reconstruct the complex phase portrait and discover that a stable radial equilibrium corresponds to a relative equilibrium in the regularized dynamics, whereas the reconstruction of an impact dynamics requires taking a singular limit.
A Second Order Extended Zarankiewicz Number for Biquadratic SOS Rank

We introduce the \emph{second order extended Zarankiewicz number} $z_{2M}(m,n)$, obtained from the second order Zarankiewicz number $z_2(m,n)$ of Löfberg and Qi by relaxing the simplicity condition $(S)$ for the \emph{secondary halves} of 2-edges, while keeping the limited condition $|E_1|=z(m,n)$. We prove the hierarchy $$ BSR(m,n)\ge z_{2M}(m,n)\ge z_2(m,n)\ge z_{SL}(m,n)\ge z_{RL}(m,n)\ge z_{wL}(m,n)\ge z(m,n), $$ and show that $z_{2M}$ is not capped by the universal cell bound. We prove the counting bound $z_{2M}(m,n)\le mn-1$, and a sharper linear-in-$m$ bound for fixed $n$ obtained from orthogonality of coefficient vectors. We analyse how the recursive criterion $(RW3^{+})$ of Löfberg and Qi must be modified under $(S_M)$, prove soundness of the resulting $(RW3^{+}_M)$ for multiplicity-one sharing, and show that a signed sharing closure $(SC)$ can supplement but not replace it. We prove $$ z_{2M}(21,4)\ge 56>55=z_2(21,4). $$ The witness is an explicit $56$-edge $(S_M)$-admissible configuration, and its irreducibility is certified by a full-rank system of $2255$ linear equations in the $1540$ off-diagonal inner products. This reaches Marin's lower bound $BSR(21,4)\ge 56$.
C*-embeddings of spaces of probability measures, nonnegative measures and unit balls
E. A. Reznichenko; Yu. V. Sadovnichiy

For a Tychonoff space $X$ and $p\in\{d,β,R,τ,σ,a\}$ let $M_p(X)$ be the space of discrete, compactly supported, Radon, $τ$-additive, $σ$-additive or finitely additive signed measures on $X$, regarded as a subspace of $M(βX)=C(βX)^*$ with the weak$^*$ topology, and let $M^+_p(X)$, $U_p(X)$ and $P_p(X)$ be its subsets of nonnegative measures, measures of norm at most one, and probability measures. In the companion paper it was shown that $M_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $M_q(X)$ iff it is $C^*$-embedded iff it is $G_δ$-dense. We show that $G_δ$-density of $Q_p(X)$ in $Q_q(X)$ is the same condition for all $Q\in\{M,M^+,U,P\}$, and that $C^*$-embedding of $Q_p(X)$ in $Q_q(X)$ implies $G_δ$-density, while the converse fails for $Q\in\{M^+,U,P\}$. We prove that $M^+_p(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $M^+(βX)$ iff $P_p(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $P(βX)$, that pseudocompactness of $P_p(X)$ implies pseudocompactness of all its powers, and that the unit ball $U_R(X)$ is $C^*$-embedded in $U(βX)$ iff $P_R(X)$ is pseudocompact. If $βX$ is $κ$-metrizable (e.g., a product of metrizable compact spaces or a compact group), then pseudocompactness of $P_p(X)$ and the $C^*$-embeddings of $P_p(X)$, $U_p(X)$ and $M^+_p(X)$ in $P(βX)$, $U(βX)$ and $M^+(βX)$ are equivalent to the $C$-embedding of $M_p(X)$ in $M(βX)$. Consequently, $P_τ(X)$ is pseudocompact for every pseudocompact dense subspace $X$ of a Tychonoff cube. This gives a space $X$ for which $P_τ(X)$ is pseudocompact while the space $P_R(X)$ of Radon probability measures is not, and answers a question of the first author.
Morse index and bifurcation of Clifford hypersurfaces under Hopf squashing

Clifford hypersurfaces are products of two spheres embedded in a round sphere. We call them balanced when their radii are chosen so that the product is minimal in the round metric. We study how their Morse index and nullity change when the ambient metric is deformed along the fibers of a Hopf fibration. This deformation, called \emph{Hopf squashing}, rescales the fiber metric by a parameter $t>0$ while leaving the horizontal metric unchanged. For the complex, quaternionic, and octonionic Hopf fibrations, we determine the index and nullity of balanced Clifford hypersurfaces throughout the fiber-shortening range and show that their Jacobi potential is independent of $t$. In the octonionic case we also determine the first positive Jacobi eigenvalue and its multiplicity. In the octonionic case, at $t=27$, a branch of nonhomogeneous minimal hypersurfaces bifurcates from the balanced Clifford hypersurface; its members have Morse index $1432$ and nullity $15$.
Existence and Splitting of Dirac Points in Honeycomb Gyromagnetic Photonic Crystals

We establish the existence of Dirac cones and magnetically induced local band gaps for the transverse magnetic Maxwell system in a two-dimensional honeycomb array of circular yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cylinders. For fixed positive material parameters with nonzero permeability contrast, we prove that sufficiently small cylinders support a Dirac point in the nonmagnetic case $κ_g=0$: two Bloch dispersion surfaces meet at a double eigenfrequency and form a nondegenerate cone. For each fixed sufficiently small nonzero gyrotropic bias $κ_g$, we show that this degeneracy splits and a local band gap opens near the original Dirac point. Our approach combines a quasi-periodic layer-potential formulation with honeycomb symmetry and rigorously controlled finite-dimensional reductions. The central contribution is a unified derivation of the conical crossing and magnetic gap opening directly from the full Maxwell transmission problem, without assuming an effective discrete model. This establishes the transition from Dirac dispersion to a locally gapped spectrum in a small-inclusion regime with fixed material contrast.
A Moment Proof of the Hollman-Xiang Conjectures on Kloosterman Polynomials

Let $F=\F_{2^n}$ and let \[ \mathcal T_1=\{t\in F:\Tr_{F/\F_2}(t)=1\}. \] For an integer $u=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_i2^i$ of even binary weight, put \[ L_u(X)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}u_iX^{2^i}, \qquad L_{1,u}(t)=t+L_u(t^{-1}). \] Hollmann and Xiang conjectured that $L_{1,u}$ permutes $\mathcal T_1$ if and only if $u\in\{0,3,6,10\}$. We prove the necessity by a moment method; the sufficiency is their Theorem~4.1. The quadratic moment yields a cyclic autocorrelation identity, while the cubic moment gives a two-variable group-algebra identity. An elimination argument reduces the coefficient word to a monomial or a complementary monomial, and explicit cubic and quartic moments complete the classification. We also prove Hollmann and Xiang's Conjecture~4.5. Namely, if $n>3$ and \[ L_{c,d}(x)=L_c(x)+L_d(x^{-1}) \] is a Kloosterman polynomial on $\F_{2^n}$, then its positive linearized part $L_c$ is injective on both trace fibers. This second result follows from relative quadratic and cubic moment identities and a spectral-zero rigidity argument. Consequently every Kloosterman polynomial is obtained by composing one of $L_{1,0},L_{1,3},L_{1,6},L_{1,10}$ with a linearized map that is injective on both trace fibers.

A non-edge of a $K_4$-free graph is $K_4$-saturating if adding it creates a copy of $K_4$, and $f(G)$ counts these non-edges. Erdős and Tuza showed that the minimum of $f$ over $n$-vertex $K_4$-free graphs jumps from zero to a quadratic quantity once the number of edges exceeds $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$. Balogh and Liu [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 109 (2014)] determined the asymptotic size of this jump. In this paper, we study the jump phenomenon at Nosal's spectral threshold $λ(G)>\sqrt m$, where $λ(G)$ is the spectral radius and $m$ is the number of edges. This spectral threshold does not involve the order, and its boundary contains unbalanced graphs far below the Mantel threshold. We prove that every $K_4$-free graph $G$ with $λ(G)>\sqrt m$ satisfies $f(G)+ \frac{1}{2}q(G)> \frac{1}{9} λ(G)^2$, where $q(G)$ counts the vertices in triangles. The constant $\frac{1}{9}$ is best possible, and the triangle-free case of this inequality reduces to Nosal's theorem. Consequently, the minimum of $f$ over $K_4$-free graphs with $m$ edges jumps from $0$ to $\frac19m+O(\sqrt m\,)$ at the Nosal threshold, and the error order $\sqrt m$ is best possible. For large $λ(G)$, we also prove $f(G)>\frac19λ(G)^2-\frac13λ(G)$, and graphs on the boundary $λ(G)^2=m$ attain this value. In the extremal graphs, the three edges of every triangle have booksizes in the ratio $4:1:1$, so these graphs are different from those of Balogh and Liu. We also show that the spectral Mantel condition $λ(G)>λ(T_{n,2})$ forces asymptotically fewer $K_4$-saturating non-edges than the condition $e(G)>\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$. Our proof transfers the Balogh-Liu theorem through a weighted blow-up and replaces the choice of an extremal edge by a zero-sum comparison over all edges of a neighborhood.
Optimal Last-Iterate Bounds for Nonexpansive Stochastic Approximation
Ramanan Tamizholi; Siddharth Chandak; Rahul Singh

We establish last-iterate mean-square residual bounds for nonexpansive stochastic approximation (SA), or stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann (KM) iterations. In particular, we consider fixed-point mappings that are nonexpansive with respect to the Euclidean norm, and focus on polynomially decaying stepsizes. We study three conditions on the conditional second moment of the noise, and obtain bounds that are optimal up to logarithmic factors in each case. When it scales linearly with the squared residual, the best rate is $O(1/k^{1-ε})$ for any $ε>0$. In this case, for all considered stepsizes, our bounds match those of the noiseless KM iteration. When it is bounded by a constant, the best rate is $O(\log^2 k/\sqrt{k})$. When it scales affinely with the squared norm of the iterate, the best rate is $O(1/k^{1/2-ε})$, and the mean-square residual can diverge if the stepsizes are not square-summable. Thus, unlike for contractive SA, square-summable stepsizes are necessary for nonexpansive SA. We demonstrate how various algorithms with cocoercive maps, such as stochastic gradient descent, linear SA, and learning in cocoercive games, fit into our framework, and how the different noise conditions arise in each of them.
Nonzero-Sum Stochastic Exit Games with Singular Belief Dynamics

We study a two-player nonzero-sum stochastic exit game with asymmetric information. Each firm chooses the time to exit a duopoly and, conditional on remaining active, when to exit a monopoly. The asymmetry stems from privately observed exit values, while profit flows are driven by a general one-dimensional diffusion. Allowing for exit from monopoly induces singular dynamics of the associated belief process, so we construct it as a limit of regular approximations. The underlying dynamics are not described by a system of SDEs, which requires a new mathematical approach. We construct a symmetric Nash equilibrium in which the duopoly exit is a hitting time of the belief process while the monopoly exit is described through the underlying diffusion. Our equilibrium exhibits novel phenomena: the market may be abandoned by both firms in finite time (market collapse), and firms with heterogeneous exit values may optimally exit simultaneously (clustering). These features are absent when monopoly is always preferred to exit.
Towards funnel control on Riemannian manifolds

Funnel control for time-invariant control-affine systems with relative degree one is transferred to the case of dynamical systems evolving on a Riemannian manifold. It is shown that, under some regularity assumptions, the classical proofs carry over. The regularity assumptions reflect the particularities of the nonlinear theory and degenerate in the classical Euclidean case.
On funnel control with star-shaped funnels

Funnel control for the trivial control-affine prototype is extended to the case of star-shaped funnels, both in the special case that the dynamical system is formulated in an Euclidean space and the general case of a Riemannian manifold.
Rank Additivity and Comon's Conjecture for Real Hankel Tensors

Let $\mathscr{H}_m(n)$ denote the set of real Hankel tensors of order $m$ and dimension $n$, and let $\textbf{H}\in\mathscr{H}_m(n)$, where $m\ge3$ and $n\ge1$. Set $M=(m-1)(n-1)+1$. First, we prove that the CP rank $r(\textbf{H})\le M$ and that CP rank is additive under direct sums of $\textbf{H}$ with any real tensor $\textbf{T}$ of the same order. Second, we prove that partially symmetric rank $p_j(\textbf{H})=r(\textbf{H})$ for $1\le j\le m-1$ and that, if $r(\textbf{H})\le M-1$, these ranks also equal its symmetric rank $s(\textbf{H})$. Third, we construct a fourth-order Hankel tensor $\textbf{H}_*\in\mathscr{H}_4(4)$ that attains this CP rank bound and satisfies $r(\textbf{H}_*)=10$ and $s(\textbf{H}_*)=11$. Moreover, for the direct sum $\textbf{H}_*^{(k)}=\bigoplus_{a=1}^k\textbf{H}_*$, we further prove that $r(\textbf{H}_*^{(k)})=10k$ and $s(\textbf{H}_*^{(k)})=11k$. This provides a low-dimensional counterexample to Comon's conjecture over the real numbers and further shows that the Comon rank gap is unbounded among real symmetric tensors of order four.
Lu Cui; Wenming Wu; Wei Yuan

We study the structure of general $\mathbb{R}$-linear unitary preservers between unital C$^*$-algebras. Representing any unital $\mathbb{R}$-linear unitary preserver in terms of three $\mathbb{R}$-linear maps on the self-adjoint part of the domain yields a canonical decomposition into a Jordan-type summand and a purely non-Jordan summand. When the domain is abelian, we completely classify the purely non-Jordan summand via type $\mathrm{I}_2$ JW-algebras. For unital C$^*$-algebras with no two-dimensional irreducible representations, we characterize a natural class of purely non-Jordan unitary preservers governed by pairs of Jordan $*$-homomorphisms.
C-embeddings of spaces of signed measures
E. A. Reznichenko; Yu. V. Sadovnichiy

For a Tychonoff space $X$ let $M_a(X)\supset M_σ(X)\supset M_τ(X)\supset M_R(X)$ be the spaces of finitely additive, $σ$-additive (Baire), $τ$-additive and Radon signed measures on $X$, and let $M_β(X)$ and $M_d(X)$ be the spaces of compactly supported and discrete measures; all of them are regarded as subspaces of $M(βX)=C(βX)^*$ with the weak$^*$ topology. We study when $M_p(X)$ is $C$-embedded ($C^*$-embedded) in $M_q(X)$. We prove that $C$-embeddedness, $C^*$-embeddedness and $G_δ$-density of $M_p(X)$ in $M_q(X)$ are equivalent, and that they are equivalent to a lifting property: for every continuous map $f$ of $X$ into a metrizable compact space, the image of every probability measure in $M_q(X)$ is the image of a probability measure in $M_p(X)$. The main tool is a general theorem, proved in a separate paper, asserting that $C$-embeddedness, $C^*$-embeddedness and $G_δ$-density are equivalent for dense subspaces of locally convex spaces in the weak topology, and, more generally, of products of first-countable spaces. We characterize the spaces $X$ for which $M_σ(X)$, $M_β(X)$, $M_d(X)$ and $M_R(X)$ are $C$-embedded in $M_a(X)$ (pseudocompactness, pseudo-$ω$-boundedness, scatteredness of $βX$, and a lifting property of Radon measures, respectively). We give an example of a pseudocompact locally compact space $X$ for which $M_τ(X)$ is not $C^*$-embedded in $M_σ(X)$, and we show that $M_τ(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $M(βX)$ for every $G_δ$-dense subspace $X$ of a product of metrizable compact spaces. Using a set of universal measure zero, we construct a pseudocompact space $X$ for which $M_R(X)$ is $C$-embedded in $M(βX)$, although the restriction to $X$ of a coordinate projection onto $[0,1]$ maps no $σ$-compact subset of $X$ onto $[0,1]$.
Optimal radio labelings for the Cartesian product of a path and the Heawood graph
Payal Vasoya; Miral Doshi; Devsi Bantva

For a simple graph $G$, let $d(u,v)$ denote the distance between two vertices $u$ and $v$ in $G$, and let $diam(G)$ denote the diameter of $G$. A radio labeling of $G$ is a mapping $f : V(G) \rightarrow \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$ such that $|f(u)-f(v)|\geq diam(G) + 1 - d(u,v)$ holds for every pair of distinct vertices $u, v \in G$. The span of $f$ is the difference between the largest and smallest integers assigned by $f$, and the radio number $rn(G)$ is the minimum span taking over all radio labelings of $G$. Let $P_n$ denote the path on $n$ vertices and let $H$ denote the Heawood graph (see Figure-1). In this paper we determine the radio number for the Cartesian product of a path and the Heawood graph, and characterize all optimal radio labelings of $P_n \Box H$. Moreover, we show that the radio number of $P_n \Box H$ exceed the lower bound given for $rn(G)$ in [6], where $G$ is any graph, and that this gap is arbitrarily large.
Combinatorial curvature flows for spherical vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces

We study the combinatorial Yamabe and Calabi flows for spherical vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces. Under the assumptions of uniformly bounded vertex degree and an $ε$-uniformly nondegenerate initial metric, we establish the short-time existence of smooth solutions to both combinatorial curvature flows. We also establish short-time uniqueness for the combinatorial Yamabe flow. For the combinatorial Calabi flow, we establish short-time uniqueness among solutions that are continuous in time with respect to the $L^\infty(V)$ norm.
Uniqueness of generalized conformal restriction measures

In this note, we give a new proof of the uniqueness of generalized chordal and radial conformal restriction measures for $c\le 1$, where the $c<-2$ case is unproved before. Our approach (called the SLE arc test) is inspired by the completely conformally invariant (CCI) measure introduced by Lawler and Werner (2000), and also by Cai's recent Green's function test for the Brownian loop catcher (2026).
Elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals for orthogonal groups and Seiberg duality on the lens space

We derive new transformation formulas for elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals associated with the orthogonal groups $\mathrm{SO}(N)$. The sum/integrals are written in terms of the lens elliptic gamma function, which depends on an integer $r\geq 1$ in addition to the usual complex variables, and they reduce to the elliptic hypergeometric integrals of Spiridonov and Vartanov for $r=1$. The derivation uses the $BC_n\leftrightarrow BC_{\tilde n}$ transformation formula proven in our previous paper, together with a duplication formula for the lens elliptic gamma function proven here. The duplication formula takes a different form depending on whether $r$ is even or odd. Physically, the new transformations show that the supersymmetric lens indices on $S^1\times S^3/\mathbb{Z}_r$ of the 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ $\mathrm{SO}(N)$ and $\mathrm{SO}(N_f-N+4)$ gauge theories related by Seiberg duality are equal for odd $r$. For even $r$, where the lens index depends on the global form of the gauge group, they show the equality of the contributions from flat connections whose holonomies lie in a common maximal torus. The $BC_n$ formula itself gives the corresponding statement for the symplectic groups.
Learning the Brownian Motion in Machine Learning for Parametric Parabolic PDEs: A Backward Quadrature Approach
Qiang Han; Shaolin Ji; Yanan Qi

We propose a backward quadrature learning (BQL) method for solving high dimensional parametric semilinear parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs). To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to extend the applicability of BSDE-based stochastic numerical methods to this class of PDEs. Specifically, inspired by the approach of learning the random variables (LRV)~\cite{BeckerJentzenMullerWurstemberger2024}, BQL incorporates learnable quadrature for Brownian increments at each time level into the backward recursion of BSDEs, enabling more efficient layerwise approximation of local conditional expectations. Furthermore, BQL introduces a continuation surrogate to facilitate the transfer of value-function information from subsequent to preceding time levels, avoiding nested quadrature while controlling the propagation of local approximation errors. Our main theoretical contribution is the derivation of a global error bound that explicitly characterizes the decomposition of the total error, together with a proof of first-order mean-square convergence under suitable approximation and integrability assumptions. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate that BQL achieves competitive solution accuracy while substantially reducing the amortized computational cost per query. For the HJB benchmark across the tested dimensions, with $Q=7$ parameter queries, BQL achieves computational cost reductions of approximately 40-fold and 4-fold compared with P$^2$INN~[2] and FBSNN~[3], respectively.
A congruence-group counterexample to Kourovka Problem 21.7

For every prime $p>24$, let $H$ be the kernel of $\SL_2(\Z/p^9\Z)\to\SL_2(\F_p)$. We prove that $H$ is not IYB, whereas $H\times C_{p^8}$ is IYB. The proof excludes a pre-Lie multiplication on the rank-three Lie ring with bracket $p[x,y]$ over $\Z/p^8\Z$ using three trace identities. It follows that the supersoluble group $H\times(C_{p^8}\rtimes C_2)$, with the involution acting by inversion, has IYB Sylow subgroups and is not IYB. Its nilpotent residual is cyclic and its Sylow $p$-subgroup has nilpotency class eight. For $p=31$, an action of order three gives a supersoluble counterexample of odd order $3\cdot31^{32}$. The same construction gives an IYB $p$-group with a specified central cyclic direct factor such that the quotient of the whole group by the unique subgroup of order $p$ in that factor is non-IYB.
On the proof of Falconer distance conjecture
Kotaro Inami; Jianbin Li; Yudong Liang; Bochen Liu; Francisco Romero Acosta

We are able to catch the main idea from OpenAI's recent release and present a proof of Falconer distance conjecture in our own words. Arguments are judiciously simplified and carefully designed for graduate-level readers.
Limit theorems for dispersing billiards with infinite cusps
Marco Lenci; Françoise Pène; Hong-Kun Zhang

Extending Lenci's work in CMP (2002), Chaos (2003), we present new insights into semi-dispersing billiards with infinite cusps. We investigate the Convergence to Stable Processes (CSP) and Functional Central Limit Theorems (FCLT) both for the collision map and for the billiard flow. Whereas the billiard map always preserves an infinite measure equivalent to Lebesgue, the billiard flow preserves the Lebesgue measure, which is either finite or infinite depending on the finiteness of the area of the billiard table. When the reference measure is infinite, the usual LLN fails, but we are able to prove the CSP and FCLT. We also prove classical FCLT for the flow when the area of the billiard table is finite. These results are obtained through a precise study of the properties of the billiard map, combined with a general approach based on induction and on coupling involving point processes.
Besicovitch-like Pseudo Almost Automorphic Stochastic Processes: Theory and Applications to Semilinear SDEs

This paper introduces, for the first time, the concept of Besicovitch-like pseudo almost automorphic stochastic processes. As a meaningful application, we investigate a class of semilinear stochastic equations driven by Brownian motion in a separable Hilbert space. By combining the Banach fixed point theorem with refined inequality techniques, we establish sufficient conditions guaranteeing the existence, uniqueness, and global exponential stability of Besicovitch-like pseudo almost automorphic solutions in distribution for the considered equations. An example is provided to show the validity of the obtained results.
The Grothendieck property of noncommutative Marcinkiewicz spaces
Yi Gao; Jinghao Huang; Ran Xu

We study sufficient and necessary conditions of a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space to have the Grothendieck property. In particular, we show that every noncommutative weak $L_p$-space, $1<p<\infty$, is Grothendieck. This answers questions due to several open problems in the literature.
Unified Far-field and Near-field Codebook Design for XL-array Systems
Chao Zhou; Changsheng You; Liujia Yao

While extremely large-scale antenna arrays (XL-arrays) hold immense promise for next-generation wireless networks, the paradigm shift encompassing new near-field communications renders conventional discrete Fourier transform (DFT)-based Type-I codebooks inefficient. Meanwhile, existing near-field alternatives usually impose prohibitively high storage and/or feedback burdens. To tackle these challenges, we propose in this letter a unified codebook applicable to both far-field and near-field XL-array systems. Our key idea is to express the near-field channel steering vector in an equivalent form, which is a Hadamard product of an angular vector and a curvature-related vector. This new representation allows direct reuse of the legacy Type-I codebook for angle quantization, while only a lightweight auxiliary codebook is newly added for additional curvature quantization. Subsequently, we optimize the auxiliary curvature codebook by maximizing the average beamforming gain given the information of user distribution. By leveraging the local monotonicity of the beamforming gain with respect to curvature mismatch, the optimization problem is further reduced to a quantization-error minimization problem, for which suboptimal curvature codewords are obtained. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed unified codebook achieves near-optimal beamforming performance that approaches its upper bound based on perfect channel state information (CSI), while significantly reducing the required feedback overhead as compared to various benchmark schemes.
Diophantine approximation with prime denominators in short intervals

For any real number $x$, let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer, and let $α$ be any irrational number. We prove that, for $Y=X^γ$ with $7/12<γ\le 1$ and $0<θ<\min \{(12γ-7)/24, 1/9\}$, there exist infinitely many $X$ for which there are primes $p$ satisfying $$ \|αp\|<p^{-θ},\quad X-Y<p<X. $$ Moreover, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of such primes. Our result extends the admissible range of short intervals in the corresponding result of Baier and Roy from $2/3<γ\le 1$ to $7/12<γ\le 1$, reaching Huxley's classical range for primes in short intervals and also improves the exponent $θ$ in $2/3\le γ\le 3/4.$
Finite Numerical Joyce Transport and Derived Hall Scattering Groupoid

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category over a finite field $k$ satisftying certain finiteness conditions. Let $Σ$ be a connected component of the space of numerical stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}$ with one element $σ\inΣ$ satisfying the support property and the finite counting condition. We prove that each of the Joyce elements with respect to $σ_1\inΣ$ is a finite rational Lie polynomial in those of any other $σ_0\inΣ$, so the generated Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{L}_σ,σ\inΣ$ in the uncompleted derived Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{D})$ is constant on $Σ$. Our proof combines completions on strict sectors with a uniform mass bound for successive local substitutions. We use the method of Hall scattering diagrams on phase categories to provide a realization of the transform of Joyce elements. For the finite-length case, we also give an alternative proof using finite-length hearts instead of phase categories.
