This article addresses the preemptive flexible job shop scheduling problem with makespan minimization (FJm | pmtn | C_max). We propose an exact constraint programming approach that completely avoids representing the processing fragments of an operation. Operations are placed in flexible time windows, where Horn's workload condition guarantees feasible preemptive scheduling, and Jackson's preemptive earliest-deadline-first rule reconstructs exact processing segments post-optimization in O(n log n) time per machine. To manage undecided machine assignments, we extend the PreemptiveNoOverlap global constraint to optional intervals within IBM ILOG CP Optimizer, performing overload checking and preemptive edge-finding in O(n log n) time while eliminating infeasible machine alternatives. The CP model is warm-started using a multi-round MILP assignment relaxation with Carlier's head-tail bounds and a window-based greedy heuristic. Extensive computational experiments on 276 pFJSSP benchmark instances and 78 pJSSP instances demonstrate that the proposed method significantly advances the state of the art. Within a 600~s time limit, it improves the upper bounds of the previously published logic-based Benders decomposition by 3.6% on average, increases the number of proven optimal pFJSSP instances from 102 to 180, and closes 74 instances for the first time (including the entire Barnes family). On the pJSSP under identical hardware conditions, it proves 67 of 78 instances optimal (compared to 51 by the baseline solver Mistral) and closes 9 of the 11 long-standing open problems.
A cyclotomic Artin-Tate formula and sphere packing for K3 surfaces

We give new necessary conditions on the Weil polynomial of a K3 surface over a finite field using techniques from the theory of sphere packing. By comparing the Artin-Tate formula over a finite extension, we derive a special values formula at roots of unity that involves the discriminant of the Frobenius coinvariant lattice. Known bounds on the minimum discriminants of even rootless lattices then imply nontrivial lower bounds on these special values. Applying these new conditions to Kedlaya and Sutherland's list of candidate Weil polynomials of K3 surfaces over the field with 2 elements rules out over 50% of the candidates.
Weak convergence orders for a fully discrete approximation of semilinear stochastic PDEs driven by multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise
Chuchu Chen; Jialin Hong; Ziyi Lei; Xu Wang

This paper investigates the weak convergence of a fully discrete approximation for a class of semilinear stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) driven by multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise. The scheme combines a spectral Galerkin discretization in space with an exponential Euler discretization in time. Compared with single-noise settings, the simultaneous presence of continuous and jump perturbations introduces additional challenges arising from discontinuous trajectories, nonlocal jump operators, and their interaction with state-dependent multiplicative coefficients. To overcome these difficulties, we establish the exponential integrability of the numerical solution processes and refined moment estimates in negative Sobolev norms for the associated first- and second-order variational processes. Combining these estimates with a discrete-time approximation argument and Wiener--Poisson Malliavin calculus, we derive regularity estimates for the solutions of the Kolmogorov equations associated with the spatial Galerkin approximations. Based on these estimates, we obtain the temporal and spatial weak convergence orders arbitrarily close to one with respect to discretization parameters $τ$ and $λ_N^{-1}$, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first weak convergence result for a fully discrete approximation of semilinear SPDEs with simultaneous multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise.
A proof of the constant-width numerical range conjecture

We prove the conjecture of Chien, Nakazato, and Meng that the numerical range of a finite complex matrix has constant width $d$ if and only if it is a closed disk of radius $d/2$, with a singleton allowed when $d=0$. For $d>0$, the characteristic polynomial of the associated Hermitian pencil and its translate by $d$ have a nonconstant common divisor over $\mathbb{C}(ζ)$. At points on the unit circle where the factorization can be evaluated, every root of the common divisor equals the smallest eigenvalue. A coefficient of the divisor thus gives a rational formula for that eigenvalue. The characteristic equation forces this rational function to be a Laurent polynomial with exponents in $\{-1,0,1\}$. Antipodal symmetry then makes the midpoint of the extreme eigenvalues a first harmonic, giving the support function of a disk. We also obtain the corresponding quadratic factor of the Kippenhahn polynomial.
Sufficient Dimension Reduction with Multimodal Predictor Objects

We study the regression of a scalar response $Y$ on a Euclidean predictor $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^p$ and a random predictor object $\mathcal{Z}$ in a general metric space under arbitrary structural dependence. We introduce a joint sufficient dimension reduction $(\mathbf{B}^\top\mathbf{X}, \mathcal{G}_Z)$ constructed via a sequential conditional independence framework, which differs fundamentally from the ordinary central subspace of $Y \mid \mathbf{X}$. Methodologically, $\mathcal{Z}$ is embedded into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and a regularized kernel-response envelope model extracts a finite-dimensional reduction of the feature map. Partial adaptive estimation then recovers the Euclidean reduction conditional on the first-stage coordinates. We establish root-$n$ consistency rates for the first-stage envelope subspace under a shrinking regularizer, alongside large-sample consistency for the second-stage Euclidean subspace estimator. Simulations and two real-data applications illustrate the utility and flexibility of the proposed method.
Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function

The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-δ_k+o(1)})$ where $δ_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.
Surface subgroups with prescribed finite quotients
Jean-François Lafont; Zhenghao Rao; Hongbin Sun

We prove that every finite quotient of a finite covolume Kleinian group $G$ can be realized by a surface subgroup. More precisely, given an epimorphism from $G$ onto a finite group $F$, there exists a surface subgroup that maps surjectively onto $F$. As a consequence, the union of the surface subgroups is dense in $G$ with respect to the profinite topology. We also apply this result to obtain more examples of atoroidal surface bundles with signature zero in the construction of Kent--Leininger.
Divisibility graphs of semigroups as weighted poset blow-ups
Xuang Yang; Yong Shao; Lingli Zeng

We develop a structural theory of divisibility graphs of arbitrary semigroups. For a semigroup $S$, let $S/{\mathcal J}$ be the poset of Green's ${\mathcal J}$-classes ordered by inclusion of principal ideals,and equip each $\mathcal {J}$-class $J$ with the weight $|J|$. We prove that the divisibility graph ${\operatorname{Div}}(S)$ is obtained from the comparability directed graph $Comp(S/{\mathcal J})$ by replacing each $\mathcal J$-class with a complete symmetric graph of order $|J|$ and by replacing each directed edge $J_u$ to $J_v$ in $Comp(S/{\mathcal J})$ with all directed edges from every element of $J_u$ to every element of $J_v$. Consequently, ${\operatorname{Div}}(S)$ is determined, up to isomorphism, by the weighted poset $(S/\mathcal {J},\{ J \}_{J\in S/{\mathcal J}})$. This yields structural descriptions of its strongly connected components, maximal unilaterally connected subgraphs. The main contribution is the reduction of divisibility graph problems to weighted quotient-poset problems. As applications, we obtain reconstruction and isomorphism criteria and prove an inheritance theorem for divisibility $D$-saturated subsemigroups.
Complete Decentralization of Wave Equation Control on a Compact Domain

A feedback control policy is completely decentralized if the actuation signal at each location in space can be computed based only on state information from that location. For systems equipped with large numbers of spatially distributed sensors and actuators, completely decentralized controllers are desirable since they can be implemented in a communication and computation efficient manner, but generally perform worse than centralized counterparts. However, through a case study of Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) design for wave dynamics on a compact spatial domain, we show that careful design of system parameters to satisfy certain conditions causes a decentralized control policy to perform as well as any centralized policy. We then propose a spatially filtered $H_2$ norm to show that satisfying these conditions does not inherently degrade achievable closed-loop system performance, enabling simultaneous realization of both desirable performance and communication/computation efficiency via system-control co-design. Additional robustness analysis characterizes a range of system parameters such that the system interconnected with a decentralized controller maintains stability and near-optimal performance. Although our framework is derived for spatially continuous dynamics, we demonstrate that this theory can be leveraged to derive results for decentralization in finite-dimensional settings through a damped mass-spring example.

We give a geometric formulation of the $q$DE/ODE/IM correspondence for families of differential operators associated with simple Lie algebras of ADE type. Under analytic hypotheses, the $q$-connection associated with shifted monodromy defines a twisted $(G,q)$-oper and has Steinberg form in the frame of solutions normalized by prescribed asymptotics in a sector at infinity. We identify the central connection between the normalized solution frames at zero and infinity with a universal meromorphic $(G,q)$-Wronskian. Its generalized minors give $Q$-functions satisfying the ADE $QQ$-relations. When $q$ is not a root of unity, we parametrize shifted monodromy by quantum-affine $q$-characters evaluated on shifted $Q$-ratios, using the same character formulas that describe normalized transfer-matrix eigenvalues. We verify the analytic hypotheses for generic untwisted Feigin--Frenkel--Hernandez affine opers, thereby relating these affine opers to twisted $(G,q)$-opers.

In this paper, we first provide necessary and sufficient conditions for a Krull-Schmidt triangulated category with Auslander-Reiten triangles to have square-zero radical. One of these conditions is that the middle term of every Auslander-Reiten triangle is either zero or indecomposable. We then call an artin algebra {\it G-radical-square-zero} if the stable category of Gorenstein-projective modules has square-zero radical. We characterize when a G-radical-square-zero algebra is CM-finite and, in this case, give an additive generator of the stable category. For certain Iwanaga-Gorenstein G-radical-square-zero algebras, we further show that the stable category admits an additive generator consisting of higher syzygies of simple modules.
Regularity Estimates for a Nonhomogeneous Free Boundary Interface Problem
Romildo Lima; Mayra Soares; Leandro Tavares

In this work, we establish regularity properties for minimizers of a novel nonhomogeneous interface problem with a free boundary, formulated in Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. The nonlinear terms fulfill Lieberman-type structural assumptions with subcritical growth. The principal difficulties stem from the nonhomogeneous framework and the lack of suitable representation formulas. Our findings extend recent contributions in the field and provide new insights even in the particular case of the Laplacian. Keywords: Free Boundary Problems; Orlicz-Spaces; Nonhomogeneous Operator; Transmission Problem; Regularity.
Joshua Evan Greene; Shiyu Liang; John Luecke

We classify the simple knots in lens spaces with planar rational Seifert surfaces. As a consequence, we classify the homology classes of all knots in lens spaces that admit planar rational Seifert surfaces.

A graph $G$ is called a \emph{brick} if it is $3$-connected and $G-\{u,v\}$ has a perfect matching for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v\in V(G)$. A brick is \emph{minimal} if deleting any edge results in a graph that is no longer a brick. A graph is \emph{claw-free} if it contains no induced $K_{1,3}$. Plummer proved that every $3$-connected claw-free graph of even order is a brick. In this paper, we completely characterize all claw-free minimal bricks. Apart from $K_4$ and the six-vertex wheel $W_5$, they are precisely the line graphs of graphs obtained from loopless $3$-edge-connected cubic multigraphs by subdividing every edge outside a matching of even size exactly once. Consequently, every claw-free minimal brick of order $n$ contains at least $4n/5$ cubic vertices and at least $4n/5$ edges joining cubic vertices. Both bounds are sharp. This establishes the conjectures of Norine and Thomas and of Lovász for claw-free minimal bricks in sharp quantitative forms. We also show that, for a claw-free minimal brick of order at least $8$, deleting an edge leaves a matching covered graph if and only if the edge lies in a triangle.
A uniqueness theorem for Allen--Cahn global minimizers asymptotic to the Simons cone

For every integer $m\ge4$, we prove that the saddle-shaped solution of the Allen--Cahn equation in $\R^{2m}$ constructed by Cabré and Terra \cite{CabreTerra2009} is a global minimizer. Moreover, up to sign, it is the unique global minimizer whose nodal set at infinity is a normal graph over the Simons cone with a height that decays faster than that of the Hardt--Simon leaves.
Minimum Synthesis Time for Single-Deletion Correcting Codes of Prescribed Size
Yuling Li; Wenjun Yu; Gennian Ge

DNA is a promising medium for data storage, but the high cost of DNA synthesis remains a major obstacle to its widespread deployment. In the reference-based synthesis model, synthesis time is measured by the length of the reference sequence. Previous studies have analyzed code sizes under synthesis-time constraints and constructed cost-constrained codes, including codes that correct deletions. In this paper, we study the minimum synthesis time for codes of prescribed size, considering both unrestricted codes and single-deletion correcting codes. We establish finite-length lower bounds valid for arbitrary reference sequences and upper bounds using existing $q$-ary differential VT codes. For fixed $q\geq3$, $A>0$, and $R\in(0,1)$, we determine the minimum synthesis time up to an $O(1)$ term when the code size is $M_n=\lfloor Aq^{Rn}\rfloor$. The corresponding redundancy is $(1-R)n\log_2q-\log_2A+o(1)$ bits. In particular, for these code sizes, the minimum synthesis time for single-deletion correcting codes exceeds that for unrestricted codes by a term proportional to $\ln n$, and we determine its coefficient. We also derive upper and lower bounds for code sizes $\lfloor q^n/(nq^{s_n})\rfloor$, where $s_n\to\infty$ and $s_n=o(n)$. These sizes correspond to redundancy $\log_2 n+s_n\log_2q+o(1)$ bits. For code sizes $\lfloor q^n/(nq^c)\rfloor$ with fixed constant $c$, the redundancy is $\log_2 n+c\log_2q+o(1)$ bits. We give conditions under which single-deletion correcting codes exist or do not exist for all sufficiently large $n$, together with bounds on the minimum synthesis time. These results show how code size and the single-deletion correcting constraint affect synthesis time and provide theoretical guidance for the construction of cost-constrained codes.
Regression Modeling for the Bloc Basu Bivariate Exponential Distribution: Marginal and Conditional Means
Osama Idais; Eric Nyarko; Ola Alkhuffash

The bivariate absolutely continuous exponential distribution introduced by \citet{block1974continuous} provides a model for dependent lifetimes in reliability and survival analysis. Its marginal means depend jointly and nonlinearly on the rate parameters, which complicates regression modeling and the interpretation of covariate effects on these means. In this paper, we develop two regression approaches based on a region-wise multivariate exponential-family representation. In the full-distribution approach, link functions relate the cumulant derivatives in a fixed reference region to linear predictors. These derivatives do not directly equal the marginal means, which are instead probability-weighted combinations of the regional derivatives. This relationship allows covariate effects on the marginal means to be examined. Likelihood derivatives are obtained through the chain rule, and the regression coefficients are estimated by maximum likelihood. The rate parameter estimates are then recovered through the inverse link functions and an explicit inverse mapping, with the admissible solution selected to ensure positive rates. As an alternative, we propose regression models based on the normalized conditional distribution within each region. In this setting, the cumulant derivatives coincide with the conditional means, allowing covariates to be linked directly to these means. Both approaches are evaluated through a simulation study.
Bi-parameter local linearization and parameter estimation for the damped stochastic Klein--Gordon equation with spatially colored noise

Consider the one-dimensional nonlinear damped stochastic Klein--Gordon equation driven by Gaussian noise that is white in time and fractional in space, with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/2,1)$. For a globally Lipschitz diffusion coefficient, we approximate characteristic mixed increments by those of the additive equation, multiplied by the coefficient frozen at the base point. A critical-kernel reduction and localized Riesz covariance estimates control the additional kernel terms and spatial correlations. We also establish $L^p$ error bounds for normalized quadratic variations and, under a nondegeneracy condition, construct jointly strongly consistent estimators of the Hurst parameter and a positive diffusion parameter.
Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements

With single-copy measurements, every mixed fermionic Gaussian state on $m$ modes, pure modes included, is learned to trace distance $ε$ from $Θ(m^3/ε^2)$ copies, with no logarithmic factor, against the known $Θ(m^2/ε^2)$ for collective measurements. We prove the upper bound, resolving Conjecture 10.1 of arXiv:2609.23189 (lower bound for $ε\le1/3600$), and fill most open entries of the sample-complexity table of fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states, for single-copy, $k$-copy and collective measurements. The single-copy measurement's noise is matched to the metric at every occupation scale. With blocks of $k$ copies, the covariant highest-weight measurement of arXiv:2611.07271, read out through the Weyl-shift estimator, is exactly unbiased for every state; it gives $Θ(\max\{m^3/k,m^2\}/ε^2)$ in Frobenius norm on all states and in trace distance on every class at a fixed distance from the pure boundary. The gain $1/k$ ($k\le m$) away from the pure boundary, against $1/\sqrt k$ on cold number-conserving states, is therefore attained. For bosonic Gaussian states with bounded covariance, any displacement and squeezing, and occupations $n_1\le\dots\le n_m$, $O((m^2+r^3+\sum_{i,j>r}1/(n_i+n_j))/ε^2)$ single-copy measurements suffice, $r$ the largest index with $r\,n_r\le2$; this is the minimax rate on dyadic-interval classes, with no spectral gap or cold-mode count assumed, and holds with no covariance bound for displaced passive states. With no bound on energy or squeezing, non-Gaussian measurements learn centred one-mode states, mixed included, from $O(ε^{-2})$ and centred pure $m$-mode states from $O(m^2/ε^2)$ single copies, free of the $\log\log E$ term of Gaussian measurements, and $m$-mode states from $O(m^3/ε^2)$ copies, entangled only in a first round on blocks of $4m+6$.
Ostrik's Theorem for Operator Algebras in a Unitary Tensor Category

We define Hilbert modules for $\mathrm{C^*}$ and $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebra objects in the ind-completion of a unitary tensor category. We then prove an operator algebraic Ostrik's theorem in an ind-category: the 2-category of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebras objects, their modules, and adjointable intertwiners is $\dagger$-equivalent to the 2-categories of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ module categories.
Gromov-Witten Nonvanishing and Symplectic Deformations of Toric Varieties

Let $A$ be nonzero in the cohomology ring of a smooth projective toric variety $X$. In this note, we observe the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A, A, \ldots\rangle_{0, n,β}^X$ as a consequence of Iritani's work on the big quantum cohomology ring of $X$. This implies Kollár's conjecture on the symplectic deformation invariance of rational connectedness in the case where $X$ is toric. If $X$ is moreover Fano and $B$ is also nonzero in the cohomology ring, we prove the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A,B,*\rangle_{0,3,β}^X$ using Batyrev's presentation of the small quantum cohomology ring of $X$. We conclude with a few consequences of this nonvanishing result.
Boundary-controlled irreversible port--Hamiltonian modeling and structure-preserving discretization of tubular reactors

This paper presents a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model and a structure-preserving spatial discretization for a non-isothermal tubular reactor with axial convection, variable-density momentum dynamics, chemical reaction, mass diffusion, heat conduction, and jacket heat transfer. Reaction, diffusion, and heat conduction are described by irreversible port-Hamiltonian channels, whereas convection and momentum are represented by a weighted Eulerian interconnection. The boundary ports recover the axial energy flux and the corresponding entropy flux. A partitioned finite-element method is then formulated in conservative coordinates using a power-preserving change of variables. The semi-discrete model satisfies the Hamiltonian balance and a discrete entropy balance with non-negative entropy production due to reaction, diffusion, heat conduction, and jacket heat transfer. Numerical results for an open tubular reactor are validated against independently computed continuous steady boundary-value solutions and show the transient temperature, composition, and velocity profiles in the very-low-Mach regime. The same discretization is also tested with reciprocal Soret--Dufour coupling, for which the discrete entropy production remains non-negative.
Minimal dynamics with polynomial and intermediate complexity

We study how complicated the orbits of a minimal system can be when the topological entropy vanishes, by looking at the exact order of growth of the number of distinguishable orbit segments, and not only at its exponent. For a broad class of growth rates, including all polynomial ones, we construct minimal homeomorphisms of one-dimensional continua realizing them; in particular, two such systems may have the same polynomial entropy and yet incomparable growth. We also show that passing from a minimal subshift to the maps obtained by running its suspension flow for a fixed time only rescales time in the growth law, and we characterize exactly when this rescaling has no effect. Combined with a construction of Cassaigne, this yields minimal homeomorphisms of continua whose growth lies strictly between all polynomial and all exponential rates.
Neumann Series of Bessel Functions for a Quadratic Sturm--Liouville Pencil
Vladislav V. Kravchenko; Sergii M. Torba

We construct Neumann series of Bessel functions representations for solutions and their first derivatives of the equation $-y^{\prime\prime}(x)+(q(x)+2ρp(x))y(x)=ρ^2y(x)$. The series arise from Legendre expansions of two transmutation operator kernels. The obtained series converge uniformly on horizontal strips in the complex plane of the parameter $ρ$. We develop a recursive integration procedure for computing the coefficients of these representations. The knowledge of the first coefficients allows one to recover the potentials $p$ and $q$ which is useful for solving inverse problems. For separated boundary conditions, we estimate the characteristic functions whose zeros determine the eigenvalues. Two numerical examples illustrate the practical applicability of the obtained series representations to the solution of spectral problems.
The Isomorphism Problem for Cayley Graphs on Monogenic Semigroups
Lu Li; Yong Shao; Lingli Zeng

In this paper, we investigate the structural properties of Cayley graphs of monogenic semigroups and present a complete characterization of their weakly connected components. Several essential properties of these components are rigorously proven. Building upon these structural results, we introduce the notion of labelled colour-permuting isomorphisms between Cayley graphs. Using this new isomorphism framework, we address the Cayley graph isomorphism problem for monogenic semigroups, commonly known as the CI problem. In particular, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions under which two Cayley graphs over monogenic semigroups are labelled colour-permuting isomorphic.
Local Periodic Orbit Penetration in Dynamical Systems

We introduce two complementary frameworks for studying local periodicity and recurrence in dynamical systems. In the topological setting, we consider continuous maps with nonempty periodic-point sets, restricted to the closures of their periodic points. We define the periodic penetration time of an open set as the least period of a periodic point it contains. Using dynamically refined finite generating covers, we construct asymptotic mean and variance invariants that describe local periodic penetration relative to the logarithms of minimum subcover cardinalities. We establish their invariance under topological conjugacy and investigate their behavior for finite periodic systems, full shifts, shifts of finite type, and zero-entropy systems with dense periodic points. We also extend the construction to invertible systems using symmetric dynamical refinements. In the measure theoretic setting, we define local return times through positive measure intersections of measurable sets with their iterated preimages. Using dynamically refined finite generating partitions, we construct corresponding asymptotic mean and variance invariants and establish their invariance under measure-theoretic isomorphism. We derive explicit formulas for finite probability-preserving systems and study finite periodic approximations of uniform Bernoulli shifts on $q\geq 2$ symbols, proving that their system-level mean and variance invariants converge to $1/\log q$ and $0$, respectively. Our results demonstrate that local periodic penetration and return-time statistics provide information about dynamical systems beyond that captured by classical entropy.
Hamilton cycles in vertex-transitive graphs of prime-power order
Farzad Maghsoudi; Dragan Marušič; Bobby Miraftab

A graph is vertex-transitive if, for any two vertices, there is an automorphism mapping one to the other. We prove that every connected vertex-transitive graph of order $p^n$, where $p$ is a prime and $p^n\geq 3$, has a hamiltonian cycle. Our main tool extends Witte's theorem [JCTB (1986)] on Cayley digraphs of $p$-groups.
Product Asymptotics for Rows of the Walsh Table on Regular Compact Sets

Let $E$ be a regular compact set with connected complement, and let $f$ be holomorphic in a neighborhood of $E$. We establish Hadamard-type asymptotic formulas for products of errors of best uniform rational approximation of $f$ on $E$, formed from the first $m+1$ rows of the Walsh table. When the corresponding meromorphy radii are finite, we also show that the extremal exponential rates of the approximation errors along these rows are attained along a common subsequence. We also prove a sharp asymptotic comparison theorem for ratios of best rational approximation errors along fixed rows of the Walsh table on $E$ and its closed Green sublevel sets, and derive corresponding sharp asymptotic estimates for ratios of their products. These results extend earlier product theorems from continua with connected complement and Jordan boundary to the more general setting of regular compact sets with connected complement.
Pre-Model Structures on the Category of $C_p$-Sets

It is a folk theorem of Goodwillie that there are exactly 9 model structures on the category of sets, coming from 18 pre-model structures. We investigate model structures and pre-model structures on the category of $G$-sets for a finite group $G$. We outline a strategy for finding all model structures in this category, and partially execute this strategy for the case of $C_p$-sets, where $C_p$ denotes a cyclic group of prime order $p$. In particular, there are exactly 1777 pre-model structures on the category of $C_p$-sets.
The Optimal Constant for One-Shot Channel Simulation and Strong Functional Representation Lemma

We prove a tight bound for one-shot channel simulation via a stronger version of the strong functional representation lemma: for any random variables $X,Y$, there exists a random variable $Z$ with $I(Z;X)=H(Y|X,Z)=0$ and $H(Y|Z)\le I+\log I+(1-γ)\log e-\log\log e+O(I^{-1}\log I)$, where $I=I(X;Y)$ and $γ$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant. A more convenient bound is $H(Y|Z)<I+\log(I+2)+1$. The first bound is notable in the sense that the constant term $(1-γ)\log e-\log\log e$ is optimal, and cannot be improved for any bound stated only in terms of $I$. Hence, this is the tightest form of the strong functional representation lemma up to the third order. We also prove that the Poisson functional representation is almost optimal up to a constant gap, and provide a simple finite-blocklength achievability bound that implies the $(1/2)\log n$ redundancy of the simulation of memoryless non-singular channel. These are proved via a generalization of the functional information, in particular, the exponential functional information, which closely approximates the cost of one-shot channel simulation.
Edge-coloring spectra of odd-fold graph covers and counterexamples to a conjecture

For a loopless multigraph $G$ and an odd integer $\ell\ge3$, let $Δ(G)$ be the maximum degree of $G$, let $s_\ell(G)$ be the minimum chromatic index of a cyclic $\ell$-fold cover of $G$, and let \begin{align*} L_\ell(G):=\max\left\{ Δ(G),\ \max_{\substack{S\subseteq V(G)\\ |S|\ge3\text{ odd}}} \left\lceil\frac{2\ell|E(G[S])|}{\ell|S|-1}\right\rceil \right\}. \end{align*} In this paper, we prove the sharp upper bound \begin{align*} s_\ell(G)\le\max\{Δ(G)+1,L_\ell(G)\}. \end{align*} For every nonempty bridgeless cubic graph $H$, we construct two $3\ell$-regular graphs, one a multigraph and the other a simple graph. In each case, the minimum chromatic indices over cyclic and over all $\ell$-fold covers both equal the chromatic index of the multigraph obtained by replacing each edge of $H$ with $\ell$ parallel edges. Taking $H$ to be the Petersen graph gives both multigraph and simple graph counterexamples to a conjecture of Chen, van der Holst, Luo, and Ma, which asserts that $s_\ell(G)=L_\ell(G)$ always holds. When $G$ is connected and $L_\ell(G)>Δ(G)$, we determine the common spectrum of its connected cyclic and arbitrary $\ell$-fold covers. We give polynomial-time algorithms to compute $L_\ell(G)$ and the spectrum endpoints. For fixed $\ell$, we also construct in polynomial time a connected cyclic cover with any prescribed chromatic index in the spectrum.
The unavoidable minor in graphs of uncountable edge-connectivity
Max Pitz; Lucas Real; Roman Schaut

For any given uncountable cardinal $κ$, we show that every $κ$-edge-connected graph admits a minor embedding of the graph $T_κ\star1$ (the $κ$-regular tree with a new apex vertex adjacent to all its nodes), which is itself $κ$-edge-connected. This extends a previous result of Kurkofka regarding unavoidable minors of $\aleph_0$-edge-connected graphs to all uncountable cardinalities $κ$.
Cluster-theoretic Newton--Okounkov polytopes of flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$
Shin Hong; Jeongsoo Kim; Eunjeong Lee

Newton--Okounkov bodies have been used for studying toric degenerations of flag varieties. We classify the Newton--Okounkov polytopes associated with cluster valuations and the anticanonical line bundle on full flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$. In type $A_4$, the $672$ seeds of cluster type $D_6$ yield $162$ affine unimodular equivalence classes, which coincide with the combinatorial equivalence classes. We determine the subgroup of exchange-graph automorphisms preserving every polytope class. It is a Klein four group of index six in the automorphism group of the exchange graph of cluster type $D_6$. In type $B_2$, we give defining inequalities for all six seeds. At the anticanonical weight, the two combinatorial equivalence classes split into three affine unimodular equivalence classes. Their respective class-preserving automorphism groups have orders four and two.
Settling the Burn-in Gap: Sharp Risk Bounds for Tail-Averaged SGD in Linear Regression
Qingyue Zhao; Xuheng Li; Quanquan Gu

We study the excess risk of constant-stepsize online stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with tail-averaging for high-dimensional linear regression. Building on the instance-dependent spectral framework of Zou et al. (2021), we establish matching initialization-explicit upper and lower bounds on the total excess risk of tail-averaged SGD in terms of the population covariance spectrum $\mathbf{H}$ and initialization $\mathbf{w}_0-\mathbf{w}^*$ whenever a trajectory spectral feedback condition holds. Existing analyses exhibit a fundamental gap in the effective variance: the upper bound of Zou et al. (2021) retains an undamped contribution from the initial error in the head eigenspace $\mathbf{I}_{0:k^\dagger}$, whereas their lower bound omits the variance induced by the head initialization altogether. We show that both the existing upper and lower bounds are loose: the single-hop fast-mode variance contribution from the head initialization is exponentially damped during the burn-in phase, whereas fourth-moment energy scattered from the head initialization into slow spectral modes during the early burn-in steps survives undamped into the averaging window. We prove that our spectral feedback condition is satisfied in two concrete constant-stepsize regimes: (i) for arbitrary covariance spectra $\mathbf{H}$ and any finite horizon, under an explicit horizon-dependent stepsize chosen prior to execution; and (ii) for polynomially decaying spectra $λ_i\asymp i^{-a}$ ($a>1$), under a single horizon-independent positive stepsize. Finally, we complement these positive results with explicit one- and two-dimensional separation constructions proving an exponential-versus-polynomial gap in the lower bound of Zou et al. (2021) and showing why fourth-moment assumptions alone cannot determine the asymptotic exponential decay rate without additional structural conditions.
Quantitative Gaussian limits of periodic O(N) models at and below the critical temperature
Weiqi Jiang; Pengcheng Hou; Zhiyi Li

We prove a volume-uniform Gaussian approximation for local spin coordinates in the zero-field nearest-neighbour $O(N)$ model on periodic boxes of side $M$ in $d\ge3$, at and below the critical temperature of the limiting spherical model. On a fixed spatial window, for sufficiently large $M,N$, the unnormalized $1$-Wasserstein error for the first $p\le N$ coordinates is at most $C\sqrt p (N^{-1/2}+s_M)$, where $s_M\to0$ is the spectral shift of the finite-volume mean spherical model. The estimate is uniform on compact ranges of positive directional couplings and inverse temperatures. The target has independent coordinate fields, each a scaled anisotropic Gaussian free field with an independent spatially constant Gaussian term below criticality. On a window containing a nearest-neighbour star (a site and its $d$ positive-direction neighbours), the error tends to zero as $M,N\to\infty$ exactly when $p=o(N)$ and $\sqrt p s_M\to0$. For any choice of periodic infinite-volume accumulation states, the error on any nonempty fixed window tends to zero as $N\to\infty$ exactly when $p=o(N)$. In $d\ge5$, when the inverse temperature exceeds its critical value by at least a fixed positive amount, the bound improves to $C(p/N+\sqrt p M^{-d})$. For fixed $p$, the sharp order is $N^{-1}+M^{-d}$ on star-containing windows and $N^{-1}$ on every nonempty fixed window in periodic accumulation states.
Divergent Trajectories in the $3x+1$ Problem and a ${\em S}$- Units Equation

In this note we assume the existence of divergent trajectories (if any) under the Collatz map and investigate the consequences of this assumption, even though the Conjecture of Collatz seems to be true. In a trajectory we show that the Diophantine exponential equation $x + y = w 2^n$ in the integers $x, y, w, n$ plays an important role. In this context the recent strong finiteness theorem of Bennett and Billerey on ${\it S}-Units has consequences on the set of prime numbers generated by a collection of local minima, called wave-minima (defined ad hoc for simplicity's sake) in a divergent trajectory. It allows to define canonically a density of a trajectory and some conjectures and open problems related to these prime numbers.
Discrete Model-Based Diffusion for Combinatorial Optimization in Multi-Robot Task Allocation
Haejoon Lee; Thomas Marshall Vielmetti; Xinyi Wang; Dimitra Panagou

Decision making in multi-robot systems often involves discrete decision variables, leading to NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems that must be solved within seconds for near real-time implementation. Denoising diffusion has emerged as a powerful tool for such problems, but existing approaches face a trade-off: Model-Based Diffusion (MBD) incorporates diffusion in sampling-based optimization (SBO) without training but only over continuous spaces, while existing diffusion-based combinatorial solvers operate over discrete spaces but require offline training. To this end, we propose Discrete Model-Based Diffusion (Discrete MBD), a training-free SBO method that directly optimizes discrete variables by approximating categorical reverse transition distributions through Monte Carlo sampling. We establish a finite-step lower bound on the probability of finding a global minimizer and show that this bound converges to one as the number of denoising steps increases. Extensive experiments on generic integer programs and heterogeneous multi-robot coalition formation and scheduling demonstrate that Discrete MBD outperforms SBO baselines in nearly all settings while achieving solution quality competitive with that of mixed-integer programming and reinforcement learning methods at a fraction of their computational cost.
$5I(K_X+Δ)$ is very ample on stable log surfaces

We prove that Bombieri's bound for canonical models of surfaces of general type extends to stable log surfaces, that is, $mI(K_X+Δ)$ is very ample for every $m\geq 5$ and every stable log surface $(X,Δ)$ over $\mathbb{C}$ with reduced boundary and global Cartier index $I$. Positive Codegree Density of Suspensions of Graphs

We determine the exact positive codegree density of suspensions of graphs $S^r(G)$ when $χ(G)=t$ and $t-2$ is prime power. The value is $γ^+(S^{r}(G)) = \frac{(t-3)(t-2)^{r-1}}{(t-2)^r-1}$. The lower bound construction is from Ellis, Ivan and Leader, while we establish the corresponding upper bound based on a weighted graph inequality.
Unimodal Singularities of Parametrized Space Curves

The aim of the article is to classify unimodal parametrized space curve singularities defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. We provide explicit normal forms of parametrizations up to $\mathcal A$-equivalence. The parametrizations are given by convergent power series over a real valued field, which includes parametrizations given by formal power series and by, for example, convergent power series over the complex numbers or the field of Puisieux series. The list of normal forms is surprisingly simple.

Cone-constrained eigenvalues of a matrix are defined through a complementarity problem constrained by a closed convex cone. The discrete dual Minkowski problem asks for the necessary and sufficient conditions on a finite discrete measure $μ$ on $S^{n-1}$ such that $μ$ is given by the $q^{th}$ dual curvature measure of a convex polytope in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In this paper, using topological degree theory, a novel framework is developed to prove existence of solutions. We characterise additive and multiplicative commutators in free skew fields in terms of traces and determinants of matrix evaluations. Namely, a noncommutative rational function is a sum of additive commutators if and only if all its matrix evaluations have trace zero, and it is a product of multiplicative commutators if and only if all its matrix evaluations have determinant one. Finally, using valuations and free Poisson fields, we show that the identity and the generators of a free skew field cannot be expressed as a nonempty product of additive commutators, answering a question of Gardella and Thiel in the negative.

Let $P$ denote a finite poset in which no two incomparable elements have an upper bound. The coalition lattice Coal$(P)$ of $P$ consists of all subsets of $P$, ordered as follows: $X$ is less than or equal to $Y$ if and only if there exists an injective map from $X$ to $Y$ that sends each element to an element greater than or equal to itself. Czédli, Gy. Pollák, and B. Larose about three decades ago. As the main application of the coordinatization, the paper proves that if $K$ is a finite simple lattice with at least three elements, then Coal$(P)$ has no sublattice isomorphic to $K$. In this paper, we establish enumerative formulas and derive geometric inequalities for flags of holomorphic distributions on complex manifolds. First, given a codimension-one holomorphic distribution $\mathcal{G}$ on a complex manifold $M$, we establish an upper bound for the number of independent holomorphic $p$-distributions tangent to $\mathcal{G}$ with a prescribed associated twisting line bundle $\mathcal{L}$. We extend the efficient classical simulation of Ising quantum computers from braidings to measurements. In case the circuit generator can see the entire input, we give a detailed proof that efficient simulation of classical computation would imply the separation of complexity classes $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{PSPACE}$. If the circuit generator sees only the input length, we prove that Clifford quantum computers decide what we call affine languages.

This article is based on a lecture given at Westlake University. We begin with the Eulerian framework of ramified optimal transportation, including discrete transport paths, their basic properties, numerical approximation, and the passage to general transport paths represented by rectifiable currents. Finally, we review landscape functions associated with transport paths and explain how two existing approaches can be unified within a broader family of rectifiable $1$-currents. We compute the VC-dimension of metric ball classifiers in the model spaces of Riemannian geometry (Euclidean, spherical, hyperbolic) and present upper and lower bounds on the VC-dimension of metric balls in several other situations, including general normed vector spaces (potentially infinite VC-dimension), vector spaces with $\ell^p$-norms (VC-dimension grows at least linearly in the dimension, faster than Euclidean for $p=1$), flat tori, and general Riemannian manifolds (arbitrarily large VC-dimension after a conformal change). FP64 Performance and the Limits of Ozaki Emulation on HPC Systems
Katarzyna; Swirydowicz; Nicholas Malaya; Noah Wolfe; Paul Bauman; Pieter Ghysels; Jonathan Belof

A growing industry narrative holds that native double precision can be deprioritized in HPC accelerators, on the hypothesis that low-precision tensor cores can emulate FP64 on demand, and that most HPC workloads are bandwidth-bound. This paper evaluates some of those claims and explores the importance of FP64 in scientific computing. We also consider FP64 emulation via the Ozaki method to ascertain some of the possibilities and limitations of these approaches. Furthermore, even in this favorable regime, standalone GEMM speedup is not enough to accelerate (or avoid performance regression) for the application: numerical behavior, workspace requirements, matrix shape, and integration overhead determine whether the benefit survives at application scale. Furthermore, we show that dense GEMM accounts for only a small fraction of FP64 computation across HPC workloads, leaving most application-level FP64 work beyond the reach of GEMM-based emulation.
ARIA: An AI-Powered Radio-Channel Inference and Analysis Pipeline

Statistical channel models play a key role in the design and standardization of next-generation wireless systems. Future wireless systems will operate in global spectrum allocations from 1 to 150 GHz. Species sampling priors through exact augmentation

Discrete random probability measures are central to Bayesian nonparametric mixture modeling and clustering. We show that every proper species sampling process (SSP) admits an exact two-stage finite representation of its sampling law. An almost surely finite index selects an initial set of atoms, and a draw is then made with explicitly reweighted probabilities. Axisymmetric solutions of the classical wave equation in three spatial dimensions are shown to be in one-to-one correspondence to functions which annihilate the two-electron kinetic energy operator expressed in coordinates relative to a fixed nucleus.

We propose a discrete-time dynamical model in which two players, each distributed over two positions, interact only at the positions of their maximal presence, with an intensity set by an external resource. The main idea is that the evolution of the maxima closes into a self-contained two-dimensional piecewise-smooth map that can be analysed exactly. We show that a single critical level of the resource separates two outcomes: below it, the players exchange leadership forever along a stable cycle; above it, the symmetry between them breaks, and an arbitrarily small initial advantage grows into a permanent winner--loser hierarchy. The local stability of these regimes is proved, and their global attractivity is supported by numerical experiments. At the critical level itself, all dominance is erased and both players end in equal division of the resource. Mathematically, the transition is a border-collision bifurcation shaped by this symmetry.

Every hyperbolic knot admits an arc-faithful closed braid diagram, answering Conjecture 29 of McPhail-Snyder. More precisely, any braid representing the knot can be reworded in the same braid group so that the complete holonomy has distinct incoming parabolic fixed points at every crossing. The construction replaces a pinched crossing by five non-pinched crossings when a suitable third strand is adjacent. On $n$ strands it uses at most $2n-1$ letters per replaced crossing. The resulting diagram realizes the complete holonomy by nondegenerate shapes in its four-term octahedral decomposition.

In previous work \cite{WangLeeCanic2026SecondOrder}, a Robin--Robin scheme with these features was introduced, and its stability and error estimates were established under the sufficient parabolic CFL-type condition $Δt\lesssim C_*h^2$. This can be achieved with a new splitting approach by replacing the poroelastic mechanical normal Robin condition by its physical Neumann-type traction condition, which results in a Neumann--Robin splitting. For fixed coefficients satisfying the stated assumptions, we prove a fully discrete energy bound under a restriction of $Δt\lesssim C_*h$. The improvement over the parabolic restriction in the earlier Robin--Robin analysis follows from eliminating the interface residual that requires two inverse-trace estimates. We also establish an energy-norm error bound of order $h^k+Δt^2$ under explicit regularity, finite element approximation, and initialization assumptions. Numerical experiments with manufactured solutions examine spatial and temporal accuracy and compare the Neumann--Robin and Robin--Robin schemes. A 3D cylindrical pressure-pulse benchmark further investigates their numerical stability behavior. The results distinguish the less restrictive sufficient stability condition established analytically from the observed stability thresholds of the two schemes.
Handlebody-links with Euler characteristic -2 up to six crossings
Giovanni Bellettini; Giovanni Paolini; Maurizio Paolini; Yi-Sheng Wang
We enumerate all non-split handlebody-links with Euler characteristic $-2$ up to six crossings, up to ambient isotopy and mirror image.

This paper proposes a novel general Gaussian process framework for change point detection in time series. A change is defined as an alteration of the hyperparameters of the Gaussian process prior. We formulate the problem in the context of statistical hypothesis testing and demonstrate its performance over both offline and online multiple change points detection. The approach provides theoretical guaranties of its performance. An important advantage of the developed framework is that it does not need a detailed specification of the time series function before and after a change. The hyperparameter values are learned from the data. Comprehensive evaluation of the proposed framework is provided both on synthetic and real data and its efficiency is demonstrated.
Xingjian Li; Kelvin Kan; Deepanshu Verma; Krishna Kumar; Hayden Schaeffer; Samy Wu Fung

We consider the problem of approximating backward reachable and reach-avoid tubes for high-dimensional nonlinear systems whose Hamiltonians require numerical optimization over constrained controls and disturbances. Existing neural Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability methods alleviate the dimensionality bottleneck of grid-based solvers, but evaluating Hamiltonians without closed-form expressions introduces an additional computational challenge. We show that, under suitable assumptions, the gradients required for value-function training can be computed without differentiating through the inner optimization problem. Specifically, we establish an envelope-type gradient identity for the saddle point Hamiltonian, under which the optimal control and disturbance enter backpropagation as constants without gradient tracking. This enables end-to-end neural HJ reachability with numerically evaluated Hamiltonians while avoiding both solver unrolling and implicit differentiation. We demonstrate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed approach on nonlinear reachability and reach-avoid problems of different scales.

The focus of this manuscript is existence criteria for bounded point evaluations and bounded point derivations. In the single variable setting conditions for the existence of bounded point evaluations and derivations are known for many spaces of functions; however, in the several variable case far less is known. In this manuscript, we consider Campanato spaces, which contain many other function spaces as special cases, and prove sufficient conditions for the existence of bounded point evaluations in these spaces that are analogs of known results for the single variable case. We also demonstrate that for certain cases these sufficient conditions are also necessary.

We give a counterexample to a question of Borichev on polynomial approximation with monotone weights. We construct an even continuous weight $W$, strictly increasing on $[0,\infty)$, with superpolynomial growth and finite logarithmic integral, and an entire function $F$ of zero exponential type such that $F/W$ vanishes at infinity and belongs to $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$. Nevertheless, $F$ has positive distance from the polynomials in the weighted uniform norm and in every corresponding weighted $L^{p}$ norm.

Piyush P. Jirwankar; Daniel E. Ochoa; Carlos A. Montenegro G.; Ricardo G. Sanfelice

Paul Balmer; Rhea Kommerell; Emmy Van Rooy

In the absence of a theory of closed immersions in tensor-triangular geometry, we propose an alternative approach via quotients of module categories. As an application, we prove invariance of homological residue fields under completion.

Theoretical convergence analysis shows that the APM is guaranteed to recover the dominant eigen-pair of a normalized semi-definite matrix at a rate no worse than the Power Method. Prior constructions of constant query LCCs were exclusive to fields of positive characteristic and were conjectured not to exist over the reals. The construction uses low degree polynomial evaluations over an integer grid, together with a novel sampling procedure which outputs, for a given grid point $P$, a random quadratic curve through $P$ which intersects the grid in many other points (the decoding queries). We prove that a complex polynomial $f(z,\bar z)$ of degree $n$ in $z$ and degree $m<n$ in $\bar{z}$, with finitely many zeros, has at most $(4m+1)n-5m$ distinct zeros in $\mathbb{C}$. The model describes a three-hormone regulatory loop and is applicable to endocrine systems such as the reproductive, stress, and growth hormone axes. Model analysis demonstrates that a reduced hormone-pool replenishment rate produces a lower-amplitude, higher-frequency 1-cycle. The smallest $k$ for which such a coloring exists is called the \emph{chromatic number} of $L$, denoted by $χ(L)$. The Cayley table of a finite group $G$ of order $n$ is a Latin square, which we denote by $L_G$. It is known that $χ(L_G)\ne n+1$, so either $χ(L_G)=n$ or $χ(L_G)\ge n+2$. Moreover, $χ(L_G)=n$ if and only if every Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$ is trivial or non-cyclic, which completely characterizes the finite groups whose Cayley tables attain the lower bound $n$. In this paper, we consider the dihedral group $D_n$ of order $2n$, where $n$ is odd. Since $D_n$ has a cyclic Sylow $2$-subgroup, it follows that $χ(L_{D_n})\ge 2n+2$. The chromatic polynomial is a well-studied function of graphs whose coefficients, factorization, and other properties are well-known to encode structural information about the underlying graph. An analogous notion of graph colouring exists for directed graphs which is also well-studied, but little is yet known about the corresponding dichromatic polynomial. We investigate properties of the dichromatic polynomial, including its coefficient interpretations, root-dense regions, and asymptotic growth. We also show that chordal digraphs' polynomials split into linear factors in a way analogous to the undirected case, confirm a conjecture on dichromatic uniqueness posed by González-Moreno et al., and study the density of dichromatic polynomials within certain larger families of polynomials.
The Cayley-Bedregal reduction for Milnor and Hirzebruch-Milnor classes
R. Callejas-Bedregal; F. Caraballo; M. F. Z. Morgado; J. Seade

The Cayley--Bedregal reduction replaces a complete intersection $\{f_1=\dots=f_r=0\}$ by the hypersurface $\sum_iφ_if_i=0$ in the projectivized dual bundle. For an isolated complete intersection singularity of corank $c$, we express the Milnor class of this hypersurface on its singular fibre $\mathbb P^{c-1}$ in terms of the Milnor numbers of generic systems obtained by taking linear combinations of the defining equations. Its degree is the original Milnor number, and the higher components recover the Milnor numbers of the systems with fewer equations. These numbers are invariants of the analytic germ. Our second main result concerns the Hodge-theoretic refinement. For a complete intersection defined by a regular section of a rank-$r$ algebraic vector bundle, the Hirzebruch--Milnor class is determined by that of the Cayley--Bedregal hypersurface: the push-forward of the normalized Hirzebruch--Milnor class of the hypersurface, in the sense of Cappell, Maxim, Schürmann and Shaneson, is $(-y)^{r-1}$ times that of the complete intersection, with no positivity assumption on the bundle. The factor $(-y)^{r-1}$ comes from the motivic decomposition of the projective bundle, and at $y=-1$ the identity recovers Aluffi's comparison of Milnor classes. When the tautological bundle is very ample, the hypersurface formula of Maxim, Saito and Schürmann then gives the Hirzebruch--Milnor class of the complete intersection through the vanishing cycles of a single function, avoiding their induction through intermediate complete intersections and their restriction to powers of one line bundle. In integral homology we prove the analytic form of Aluffi's identity, and obtain formulas for the Milnor class in terms of local Milnor fibres and for the Chern--Schwartz--MacPherson class of any projective scheme.
Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes
Robin Croft; Gerardo García-Moreno; Paolo Pani

Understanding when gravitational collapse produces a black hole remains a central challenge in general relativity. Black-hole uniqueness results characterize the stationary endpoint under suitable assumptions, while singularity theorems establish geodesic incompleteness in the presence of trapped surfaces and appropriate energy and global conditions. Neither, however, provides a general criterion for horizon formation. The hoop conjecture offers such a criterion by relating the enclosed mass to the compactness of a matter distribution in every direction. We construct axisymmetric families of initial data describing rotating dust and test a formulation of the conjecture adapted to this setting. We explore highly prolate and oblate configurations with both constant and differential rescaled angular-velocity profiles, including configurations near the threshold for apparent-horizon formation. We find that the conjecture holds for rotating configurations, with a coefficient within 14% of unity as in the nonrotating case, provided the quasilocal mass includes the rotational energy. If the irreducible mass of the apparent horizon is used instead, the deviations grow with spin, as they do for Kerr black holes. For horizonless configurations, the conjecture likewise holds when the mass is restricted to the energy enclosed by the matter surface, whereas using the ADM mass, which also includes rotational field energy outside the matter, leads to apparent violations of up to $\approx$25%. We also discuss the possible evolution of compact configurations without apparent horizons, their relation to weak cosmic censorship, and their implications for horizonless compact objects.
Effect of car-centric social norms on traffic congestion in a compartmental model of transit mode utilization

Vehicle traffic congestion is a persistent feature of urban transportation systems around the world. Importantly, congestion is in part a consequence of human decision-making: car traffic is reduced when people choose modes of transportation such as metro trains, buses, or trams, over cars, and it is amplified when there is a persistent social bias towards driving. The underlying feedback loop in which traffic levels influence transportation mode choices, which in turn affect traffic levels themselves, is poorly understood and we study its consequences in the presented work using a compartmental modeling approach. We first consider a simplified model of only car traffic and show that it predicts a hysteresis between congested and uncongested states, which is consistent with broader literature on on traffic modeling. Next, we add buses and trains to the model as alternative transit modes, confirm the existence of hysteresis in this generalization, and derive the relative trip completion rates of each mode. Finally, to account for decision-making, we take the demand rates for the different transit modes to be dynamic, closing the feedback loop between mode choice and utilization. This redistributes demand for each mode of transportation, highlighting that traffic conditions may be a key aspect of mode choice. Furthermore, our model predicts that increasing public awareness of congestion can be an effective control strategy to increase utilization of public transit. However, car-centric social norms must be sufficiently small, or car use is instead amplified.
Global regularity of axisymmetric Navier--Stokes equations under total slip and critical smallness

We study the axisymmetric incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in a finite cylinder subject to the Navier--total--slip boundary condition, that is, the Navier slip condition with zero friction. We prove that the solution remains smooth for all time provided that the initial swirl $Γ_0 = r v_{θ,0}$ has zero mean and an explicit smallness condition on the initial data holds. The condition involves $Γ= rv_θ$ and the variables $V = v_θ/\sqrt{r}$ and $Ω= ω_θ/r$, and it is invariant under the natural scaling of the Navier--Stokes equations, hence critical. The total-slip condition produces a boundary term on the lateral wall that cannot be controlled by the dissipation alone; we overcome this with a sharp trace-type identity combined with a remainder controlled by $\|Γ\|_{L^2}$. In addition, the Robin-type boundary condition $\partial_r Γ= 2Γ$ destroys the maximum principle for $Γ$, and we replace it with a uniform $L^4$ bound. These estimates yield uniform $L^4$ bounds for the velocity, and regularity follows from the Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin criterion together with boundary regularity results for the Navier slip condition.
Expiscating the black hole singularity in holography

We argue that the leading exponential rate in the high frequency asymptotics of holographic thermal two-point functions is independent of the conformal dimension and spin (held fixed) of the operator. We analyze the leading universal WKB spectral curve governing the asymptotics at non-vanishing momentum scaling with frequency. We show that its classical action governs time domain signatures of the bouncing geodesic singularity, highly damped quasinormal modes, and the asymptotics of multi-stress tensor OPE coefficients. Beyond the leading order, we examine linear and dimension-dependent sublinear scalings of momentum with frequency. In both regimes, we derive the connection matrix between the boundary and the horizon using exact-WKB techniques. The results show a factorization of the spectral function into a perturbative part controlled by the OPE and a non-perturbative part governed by WKB transport. For linear scaling at fixed $k/ω$ in the timelike regime, the turning points controlling physical transport remain separated from the curvature singularity. Nevertheless, a singularity-anchored representative of the same transport homology class determines the leading WKB action. In the sublinear regime, the relevant turning points approach the singularity. We match an exact solution of the near-singularity scaled equation to the exterior WKB solution to determine the connection matrix and spectral function. Our results clarify how the black hole curvature singularity is encoded in dual field theory observables at leading order in the planar expansion.
Hermitian K-theory for stable $\infty$-categories IV: Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt theory
Baptiste Calmès; Emanuele Dotto; Yonatan Harpaz; Fabian Hebestreit; Markus Land; Kristian Moi; Denis Nardin; Thomas Nikolaus; Wolfgang Steimle

In analogy with the passage from connective to non-connective algebraic K-theory, Schlichting put forward the Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt spectrum as an approximation to Grothendieck-Witt theory by a functor invariant under idempotent completion. In this paper, we extend his construction to the setting of Poincaré $\infty$-categories and characterise the resulting functor by the expected universal property. Our main result places these Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt-spectra in an exact sequence involving the ultimately decorated L-spectrum and homotopy orbits of non-connective K-theory. This confirms a conjecture of Williams which had remained open even for rings in which $2$ is invertible, and allows us to deduce universal characterisations for ultimately decorated L-theory. We obtain these results by unifying the Bass-Heller-Swan and Ranicki-Shaneson splittings into a general decomposition theorem that yields, in particular, formulas for Grothendieck-Witt groups of Laurent polynomial rings. Finally, we construct multiplicative structures on both versions of our Grothendieck-Witt and L-functors and refine their universal properties to multiplicative ones. Along the way, we show that the original versions are even idempotent with respect to Day convolution.
Stabilization of the zero forcing number of generalized Petersen graphs
Young H. Kim; Youngsoo Kim; Byunghoon Lee

We show that the zero forcing number of the generalized Petersen graph $P(n,k)$ is $2k+2$ whenever $n\ge 2k^2+k+1$. We prove this by showing that the zero forcing number of the infinite generalized Petersen graph $P(\infty,k)$ is $2k+2$ and bounding the width of the closure of every set of at most $2k+1$ vertices. This bound gives a threshold on $n$ beyond which the projection of such a closure onto $P(n,k)$ does not wrap around. Combined with an exhaustive computer search for smaller $n$, we determine the zero forcing number of every $P(n,k)$ for $k\le 5$.
Local Fréchet regression with polyspherical predictors: Uniform convergence rates and factor selection

We study local Fréchet regression for responses taking values in a metric space and predictors on a product of spheres of possibly different dimensions. We propose local constant and local linear estimators with factor-specific bandwidths and establish uniform convergence rates. We select sphere factors by comparing cross-fitted prediction risks for the full and leave-one-factor-out models. The procedure consistently recovers the active factor set, and the selected local constant and local linear estimators attain the same uniform convergence rates as if the active factor set were known. For univariate Wasserstein responses supported on a common compact interval, the uniform rate holds without an entropy condition on the response space. Simulations with scalar and spherical responses and analyses of vessel speeds and drifter speed distributions illustrate the methods.
A decomposition theorem for minimal W-algebras of type A

To any simple Lie algebra, one can associate a minimal affine W-algebra. It is a vertex algebra which is obtained from the universal affine vertex algebra by a chiral Hamiltonian reduction procedure. This reduction is determined by data coming from the minimal nilpotent orbit. It is a chiral quantisation of the Slodowy slice associated to this minimal orbit. In this paper, when the simple Lie algebra is of type A, we prove that the minimal W-algebra is isomorphic to a commutant subalgebra in a localisation of the universal affine vertex algebra. Then, we establish a decomposition theorem à la Losev: the localised universal affine vertex algebra decomposes as the tensor product of the minimal affine W-algebra and another vertex subalgebra. As a direct corollary, we retrieve the celebrated result of inverse Hamiltonian reduction for the minimal W-algebra. We also prove an analogue of this result for the corresponding finite W-algebra. In both cases, our approach relies on the geometry of the associated Slodowy slice.
Block-Sparse Gauss-Newton Optimization of Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Sparse Automatic Differentiation Approach
Denis Korolev; Adrian Hill; Jeeeun Lee

In this work, we develop an efficient Gauss-Newton optimization approach for finite basis physics-informed neural networks (FBPINNs). The key ingredient is the overlapping domain decomposition architecture of FBPINNs, which localizes the influence of each subnetwork and induces block sparsity in both the residual Jacobian and the corresponding Gauss-Newton matrix. We characterize this structure and exploit it through sparse automatic differentiation, using graph coloring to partition structurally orthogonal Jacobian columns or rows. This reduces differentiation costs and memory requirements while preserving all structurally nonzero derivative information. The resulting compressed Jacobian representations allow us to assemble the Gauss-Newton system directly in block-sparse form, enabling the use of sparse direct solvers and preconditioned iterative methods. In this way, the otherwise expensive second-order optimization problem is reduced to scalable sparse linear algebra. We demonstrate the approach on multiscale PDEs, where accurate approximation requires rich neural network parametrizations and large numbers of collocation points. Numerical experiments show that our block-sparse Gauss-Newton method attains high accuracy and substantially accelerates optimization relative to first-order baselines while remaining computationally tractable for large problem sizes.
Malcolm Wolff; Elliott Zackrone; Souhaib Ben Taieb; Michael W. Mahoney; Kin G. Olivares

Multi-horizon forecasting has been dominated by discrete forecast strategies that treat model outputs as fixed-vectors or recurrently create them. In this paper, we introduce the Continuous Horizon (CH) strategy that generalizes upon recursive, direct, and multi-step strategies by redefining forecasts as a continuous operator and the forecast horizon as a query variable rather than an index. We present the theoretical foundations for the CH strategy, a Universal Operator Approximation Theorem, and a continuous-horizon bias-variance decomposition that formally proves the estimation variance improvements of CH over the discrete strategies. We validate the CH strategy empirically through a simulation study, and on 16 large-scale datasets from the M-series benchmark, showing how CH achieves competitive RMSE accuracy, while uniquely enabling parallel inference, targeted horizon querying, and interpolation and extrapolation across unseen horizons.
Unilluminable rooms: minimal examples, classifications and exceptions
J. C. F. de Winter; George W. Tokarsky

A room with mirrored walls can contain two points that are mutually invisible: no light ray from one reaches the other. Tokarsky built the first polygonal examples by tiling a room with reflected copies of a triangle and making every tile vertex of certain kinds a corner of the room. We study the smallest rooms of this kind, which we call lattice rooms. Their interior tile vertices of the remaining kind, the sources, are invisible and pairwise mutually invisible. On the tiling by isosceles right triangles, a hole-free lattice room with a source has at least 12 sides, attained only by the pinwheel. On the square tiling the least number is 16, again attained by one room. A hole-free lattice room with two sources has at least 24 sides on the first tiling and 34 on the square tiling. Up to congruence there are 12 such rooms with 24 sides, 89 with 25 sides and 14 with 34 sides. One absorbing post, one partition, or one hole that touches the outer boundary at one point lowers the least number of sides for two sources to 18, 20 and 22 (21 if sides are counted as maximal straight segments). Two and three posts give 17 and 16 sides, and a hole that does not touch the outer boundary gives 26. We list all smallest rooms. Rooms assembled from n modules have exactly 12n sides and n sources, and a hole-free lattice room with three or more sources has at least 36 sides. We also give rooms in which some tile vertices need not be corners: 15 types of 27-sided rooms on the tiling by triangles with angles 30, 60 and 90 degrees, which are smallest in their class, a nonagon with three mutually invisible corners, and a 42-sided room in which a rotation through 180 degrees takes the place of a corner. In a ring of three trapezoids a light ray returns to a corner that is invisible in one trapezoid. Several classifications rely on exhaustive computer searches made finite by the bounds proved here.
An Improved $(1+2e)$-Approximation Algorithm for Metric Data Placement

We study the metric data placement problem with site-capacity constraints and fixed installation costs, aiming to minimize the total cost of placing data (resources) and accessing their nearest copies. We develop a deterministic polynomial-time approximation algorithm based on a natural linear programming relaxation of the problem. Starting from an optimal fractional solution, we construct multiscale metric-ball partitions independently for each resource and connect overlapping balls at consecutive levels to form a flow network. The resource layers are then coupled through shared site-capacity arcs, allowing us to obtain an integral placement by minimizing a surrogate cost over a single min-cost circulation. By optimizing the choice of ball radii, we establish an approximation factor of $1+2e\approx 6.44$. To our knowledge, this is the best approximation guarantee for the metric data placement problem since its introduction by Baev and Rajaraman in 2001.
Optimality Guarantees for Minimum Variance Subset Selection via Semidefinite Programming

Given a set of data points in Euclidean space and a prescribed cardinality $k$, the minimum variance $k$-subset problem asks for $k$ points minimizing their average squared distance from their centroid. We develop a semidefinite programming (SDP) framework for exact recovery and global optimization. First, we show that the natural SDP relaxation fails Slater's condition. Identifying the proper face containing its feasible region yields an equivalent, lower-dimensional, strictly feasible formulation that enjoys strong duality. A primal--dual characterization of optimality then gives geometric necessary and sufficient conditions under which the SDP relaxation is guaranteed to be tight. These conditions reveal how tightness depends on the internal geometry of the selected subset and on its separation from the remaining points. Second, we embed the SDP relaxation in a branch-and-cut algorithm combining first-order optimization, valid inequalities and dimension-reducing branching. Extensive experiments on public data sets, with up to 1,500 points and different values of $k$, show that the method strongly outperforms general-purpose exact solvers as the number of points and cardinality increase.
Thompson indices of knots and the invertibility problem

Jones showed that Thompson's group $F$ produces all unoriented links, and introduced its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}$, which produces all oriented links; the same holds for the Brown-Thompson group $F_3$ and its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}_3$. The corresponding Thompson indices measure the complexity of a knot in these groups, much as the braid index does for braid groups. In this article we prove that the span of the Jones polynomial plus $1$ is a lower bound for the $F$- and $\vec{F}$-index, and we give lower bounds for the $\vec{F}$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index in terms of the degrees of the HOMFLY-PT polynomial. We then compute the four indices (the $F$-, $F_3$-, $\vec{F}$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index) for the prime knots with at most 13 crossings, by an exhaustive enumeration of tree diagrams (up to 13 leaves for $F$, 17 for $\vec{F}$, with the HOMFLY-PT polynomials of all the diagrams with 19 leaves, and 9 and 11 for $F_3$ and $\vec{F}_3$) completed by targeted searches; every value is rigorously certified, by exact computations and by verified computations of hyperbolic structures in interval arithmetic. The $F$-index is determined for all knots with at most 11 crossings, the $\vec{F}$-index for all knots with at most 8 crossings, and the $F_3$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index for all knots with at most 12 crossings. The main outcome of these computations is that the oriented indices are sensitive to the orientation: we find hundreds of non-invertible knots $K$ whose reverse $K^r$ has a different $\vec{F}$- or $\vec{F}_3$-index, the smallest being $8_{17}$ (with $\vec{F}_3$-index $7$ and $9$). The $\vec{F}$-index also distinguishes the Conway knot from its mutant, the Kinoshita-Terasaka knot.
Patch LegONet: Resolving Localized High-Frequency PDE Dynamics with Low-Frequency Operator Blocks
Jiahao Zhang; Junyi Wu; Yueqi Wang; Guang Lin

Localized interfaces, layers, and shocks can require high spatial resolution even when most of a partial differential equation (PDE) solution remains smooth. In global spectral methods, resolving these features requires increasing the approximation order across the entire domain. LegONet builds PDE solvers from reusable mechanism blocks, but its global coefficient representation faces the same limitation. We introduce Patch LegONet, which reuses pretrained mechanism blocks on smaller physical patches to resolve localized fine scales. The solution consists of a global background and local corrections. Mapping a fixed reference representation onto smaller patches increases local resolution without enlarging the blocks. The corrections join smoothly to the global background at patch boundaries. Differential operators are rescaled analytically to account for each patch's physical size. Nonlinear mechanisms are evaluated on the combined solution to include interactions between the background and local corrections. Patches can move, merge, or be removed during rollout while the pretrained patch blocks remain frozen. Six experiments on Allen-Cahn and viscous Burgers equations assess static, multiple, and moving patches in one to three dimensions. At comparable numbers of degrees of freedom, Patch LegONet consistently lowers the final relative solution error compared with global refinement. The reduction is approximately one order of magnitude in most tests. These results extend mechanism reuse across spatial scales and provide a practical route to local refinement in learned PDE solvers.
Robust State-Parameter Estimation in Second-Order Thévenin Batteries
Wissam Khennoune; G. Q. Bao Tran; Thach Ngoc Dinh; Jérémy Van Gorp; Mathieu Moze

We propose a scheme for estimating the full states and parameters of a second-order Thévenin battery model, using distinct features of the measured current. An identification step, run during suitable rest intervals, identifies the resistances and capacitances of the two RC branches from the voltage relaxation by linear least squares, without knowledge of the open-circuit voltage (OCV) map.
