An online estimator then runs continuously: the polarization voltages are estimated by open-loop observers; the series resistance is updated at current jumps using least squares; the state of charge (SOC) is propagated by Coulomb counting using the current capacity estimate, and both estimates are updated periodically by a sliding-window regression. We show that the identification is exact under a mild rank condition, that the series resistance is recovered at the first current jump, and that the online state and capacity estimates converge exponentially under verifiable excitation conditions. We also establish robustness of the online estimator under bounded process disturbances and measurement noise.
RALES: A Risk-Averse Augmented Lagrangian Equality-Constrained SQP Method
Harbir Antil; Drew P. Kouri; Denis Ridzal; Thomas M. Surowiec

This paper develops RALES, an augmented Lagrangian method for risk-averse optimization in function spaces with nonsmooth risk measures, nonlinear equality constraints, and convex geometric constraints. The method combines safeguarded risk and constraint multiplier updates with efficient sequential quadratic programming based on inexact subproblem solves. The analysis establishes asymptotic stationarity for nonconvex problems and gives conditions for feasibility of weak primal accumulation points. Under additional assumptions on subproblem accuracy, duality, and boundedness, it provides global primal optimality guarantees and weak convergence of the full stored and candidate multiplier sequences to a common dual maximizer. Dual convergence is strong when all penalty parameters remain bounded. Numerical experiments for a finitely sampled semilinear PDE control problem, with the Conditional Value-at-Risk and the Mean-Plus-Semideviation risk measures, illustrate the method's performance as the spatial mesh is refined and as the number of samples increases.
Vanishing Theorem of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta Invariants as Stable Sections

We develop a viewpoint of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta invariant: It can be converted to a section over a finite dimensional Pin(2)-orbit, and it takes values in ordinary stable homotopy class. This viewpoint reveals a topological limitation of the invariant: If the fiber's connectivity exceeds the dimension of the base space, then all sections are homotopic to the trivial section. We use it to recover Lin-Mukherjee vanishing theorem. Furthermore, the family Seiberg-Witten invariant can be obtained from the pullback of such sections to $S^1$-orbit. We use this fact to prove a vanishing theorem of the Pin(2)-equivariant family Bauer-Furuta invariant after two stabilizations.
Causal Learning with Invalid Instruments for High-dimensional Imaging Responses
Yiting Wang; Chunlin Li; Shan Yu; Lily Wang

Large-scale neuroimaging studies provide high-dimensional imaging phenotypes for understanding brain-related diseases and their causal relations with biological risk factors. While instrumental variable (IV) methods can address unmeasured confounding in such observational data, existing IV methods face significant limitations when applied to high-dimensional imaging data, particularly in handling large-scale data and leveraging the intrinsic spatial structure of images. To address these challenges, we propose High-dimensional Functional-imaging Instrumental Variable Estimation (Hi-FIVE), a novel framework for estimating spatially varying causal effects when a majority of the candidate instruments may be locally invalid. We first establish identifiability conditions under which the spatial continuity of the causal effect surface propagates identification from regions where valid instruments form a plurality into regions where they do not, provided that invalid-IV effects switch on non-smoothly. Motivated by this result, Hi-FIVE combines penalized multivariate splines over triangulations for the causal surface and region-wise penalties for spatially localized invalid-IV effects, under an anchor constraint that keeps at least one relevant instrument valid on every simplex. A distributed algorithm parallelizes the computation over simplices for two- and three-dimensional images. We study the asymptotic properties of Hi-FIVE, establish consistency and pointwise asymptotic normality, and construct bootstrap-calibrated simultaneous confidence regions whose finite-sample coverage is evaluated through simulations. Hi-FIVE is illustrated with an analysis of the effect of phosphorylated tau on FDG-PET imaging in the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, interpreted under the stated IV assumptions.
Smooth actions of Baumslag-Solitar groups on the interval

We study representations of the Baumslag-Solitar group $BS(m,n)=\langle a,b\mid ab^ma^{-1}=b^n\rangle$ inside the group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of the interval $[0,1]$. We prove that for integers $n,m\in \mathbb Z\setminus\{-1,0,1\}$, the group $BS(m,n)$ embeds into $\mathrm{Diff}_+^1([0,1])$ if and only if $|n|=|m|$. Furthermore, we show that for any $α\in (0,1)$, the group $BS(m,n)$ embeds inside $\mathrm{Diff}_+^{1+α}([0,1])$ if and only if $1=|m|=|n|$ or when $1=m\leq n$.
Sobolev inequalities for the Discrete de Rham complex and an application to the Navier--Stokes equations
Daniele A. Di Pietro; Jerome Droniou; Marien Hanot; Silvano Pitassi

We prove Sobolev inequalities for the discrete de Rham (DDR) method, an arbitrary-order discretisation of the de Rham complex on polyhedral meshes. We show that, for any polyhedral domain $Ω$, the DDR counterparts of the spaces $H({\bf grad},Ω)$, $\boldsymbol{H}({\bf curl},Ω)$ and $\boldsymbol{H}(\mathrm{div},Ω)$ satisfy the same Sobolev embeddings as their continuous counterparts. For the curl and divergence spaces, this establishes on quasi-uniform meshes an $L^r$-bound (with $r>2$ in general, and $r=6$ if $Ω$ is convex) on discrete vector fields that are orthogonal to discrete gradients (resp.~curls), in terms of the $L^2$-norms of the vector fields themselves and their discrete curl (resp.~divergence). These Sobolev embeddings are the first such results for a polytopal complex. Their proofs hinge on recently introduced quasi-interpolators and conforming liftings. As an application, we use these estimates to prove the convergence of a DDR scheme for the Navier--Stokes equations in the curl--curl formulation. The convergence proof uses a Maxwell compactness theorem for DDR and requires no smallness assumptions on the data.
Euclidean filling inequalities in CAT(0) spaces

We clarify and streamline OpenAI's proof of the sharp Euclidean filling inequalities in CAT(0) spaces. We extend the result to complete spaces without assuming properness or compact support, and we establish rigidity in the equality case.

We prove that the $\mathbb F_5$-gonality and the $\mathbb Q$-gonality of the modular curve $X_1(42)$ are both $12$, improving the previous lower bound of $10$. Since $J_1(42)(\mathbb Q)$ is finite, it follows that $12$ is the least degree in which $X_1(42)$ has infinitely many points. The lower bound comes from an exhaustive search over Riemann--Roch spaces, following Derickx and van Hoeij, using a new reduction by the orbits of a cyclic group of automorphisms of order $12$ on places of degree at most $5$ ($743\,231$ Riemann--Roch spaces). An earlier search with the reductions from van Hoeij's code (about $3$ million Riemann--Roch spaces, about $6$ times more CPU time) gives the same result and serves as supporting evidence. We prove the reductions and record the data needed to reproduce the computations.
Convergence of an adaptive multilevel stochastic Galerkin FEM driven by a residual-based error estimator
Alex Bespalov; Maximilian Brunner; Alexander Freiszlinger; Dirk Praetorius

In this paper we analyze a residual-based a posteriori error estimation strategy and adaptive multilevel algorithms for a class of parametric elliptic PDEs, where the diffusion coefficient depends on countably many uncertainty parameters. Under a saturation assumption on the parametric approximation space, we propose a computable residual-based error estimator. We also introduce the notion of K-compatibility of finite element meshes, which ensures that only the triangulations with comparable mesh sizes are used, and incorporate this concept into the adaptive algorithm. We prove that the estimator is reliable and satisfies K-dependent stability and reduction properties. These results underpin our convergence analysis of the adaptive multilevel algorithm: we show that the algorithm drives both the a posteriori error estimator and the true approximation error to zero. Numerical experiments illustrate and confirm the theoretical findings.
Profinite groups with finite conjugacy classes of commutators
Eloisa Detomi; Débora Senise; Pavel Shumyatsky

It was shown in a recent work by Senise and Shumyatsky that if $G$ is a finite group such that $|x^G|\leq m$ whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order, then $G''$ has $m$-bounded order. In this paper, we examine the following question: given a profinite group $G$ such that $|x^G|$ is finite whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order, does it follow that $G''$ is finite? We show that, in general, the answer to this is negative. The main result obtained in this paper is the following theorem: Let $G$ be a profinite group in which $|x^G|$ is finite whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order. Assume that $π(G)$ is finite. Then: (1) The second commutator subgroup $G''$ is finite; (2) $G$ has an open normal subgroup of nilpotency class at most $3$.
The uncertainty operator, the Weil ground state and the zeros of zeta: a numerical study and conditional positivity of the Weil quadratic form
Ronnie Andrews; Alain Connes; Antonio La Gatta

Applying the Dirichlet principle to the Weil quadratic form $QW_λ$ on $L^2([λ^{-1},λ],d^*u)$--using only the primes $p\leλ^2$ of the Euler product--yields canonical finite-dimensional Hermitian matrices whose ground state has a Mellin transform with zeros proved real in full generality when the lowest eigenvalue is simple and even. While $λ^2=13$ gave $50$ zeros of $ζ$, $λ^2=250$ ($λ\sim16$) gives the first $1000$ zeros with $>500$ correct decimals (the first with $1341$). We explain this via a correspondence between $QW_λ$ and Slepian's time-frequency uncertainty operator $U_λ=2-P_λ-\widehat P_λ$, diagonalized by prolate wave functions with eigenvalues $δ_n(λ)\sim c_nλ^{2n+1}e^{-4πλ^2}$ (Fuchs). Via $\mathcal{E}(f)(u)=u^{1/2}\sum_{n\ge1}f(nu)$ and Gevrey smoothing, $ε_λ\le Cδ_4(λ)(\logλ)^3$ is a theorem (Connes-Kastoris). Computations up to $λ^2=300$ ($ε_λ(1)\sim10^{-1618}$) show a striking logarithmic coincidence with the Fuchs ladder, confirming this simplicity and evenness. Prolate vectors reproduce all minuscule eigenvectors, and conditioning by them and the pole term removes the minuscule spectrum: $QW_λ$ is a direct sum of a finite-dimensional near-radical part (Fuchs ladder) and an infinite-dimensional positive part from the Sonin space ($U_λ=2$). Under this ladder hypothesis and $QW_λ\ge0$, we bound the ground-state distance to the target with Mellin transform $\frac14ξ(s+\frac12)$ (Hurwitz' theorem). Finally, the semilocal trace formula gives the uncertainty principle via Coburn's lemma and proves, under a hypothesis valid at $\infty$, that $QW_λ\ge c>0$ outside a finite-dimensional near-self-dual space, reducing Weil positivity to a Schur complement at the ladder's edge.
Reciprocal mirror map derivatives, euler-twisted Gromov-Witten invariants, and instanton counts via quantum Serre duality

We study mirror map derivatives as a means of relating the genus zero Gromov-Witten theories of an anticanonical Calabi-Yau hypersurface in a smooth, almost minimal Fano variety and the local Calabi-Yau formed from the total space of the Fano's canonical bundle with the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano. A precise relationship between reciprocal mirror map derivatives is obtained from the non-equivariant limit of quantum Serre duality for the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano as formulated by Iritani, Mann, & Mignon. This allows us to express the generating series of 3-point euler-twisted invariants as the derivative of the local mirror map with respect to the closed one. In low dimensions, this series is shown to be a modular form of Eisenstein type which has arisen before in this area. We prove integrality of the twisted invariants from this identification. The regularized small quantum $D$-module of the Fano is reducible, and we show it is equivalent to an inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs equation governed by this generating series. The reciprocal mirror map derivative is then shown to be a generating function of local 3-point invariants, which recovers some known results for local Calabi-Yau threefolds and proves a conjecture of the second named author and A. Malmendier in previous work on local fourfolds. Explicit calculations for $\mathbb{P}^2,\mathbb{P}^3$ and $\mathbb{P}^4$ illustrate these relationships, which includes the vanishing of positive-degree ordinary genus-zero invariants for anticanonical elliptic curves and K3 surfaces, the recovery of the quintic threefold's instanton numbers, and finally some formulas for genus-zero invariants of local projective spaces.
Microscopic derivation of the classical KMS condition for one-dimensional Bose gases
Zied Ammari; Shahnaz Farhat; Sören Petrat; Andrew Rout

The Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) condition provides an intrinsic characterization of thermal equilibrium, both in quantum and classical statistical mechanics. In this work, we establish stability of the KMS condition through the quantum-to-classical limit for one-dimensional defocusing Bose gases. More precisely, we consider scaled quantum KMS states in the (mean-field) semiclassical regime and prove that every associated Wigner measure satisfies the classical KMS condition corresponding to the nonlinear Schrödinger Hamiltonian. This result extends to an infinite-dimensional setting an earlier derivation of the classical KMS condition for finite-dimensional Bose--Hubbard systems. It also provides a complementary perspective on the derivation of nonlinear Gibbs measures from many-body quantum statistical mechanics.
Linearized contact homology and closed Reeb orbits on prequantization bundles

We study closed Reeb orbits on prequantization circle bundles $(M,ξ)\to(B,ω)$ with $c_1(ξ)|_{π_2(M)}=0$. When $ω|_{π_2(B)}\ne0$, we construct augmentations and compute contractible linearized contact homology as a direct sum of shifted copies of $H_*(B;\mathbb Q)$, under a condition on the rational Betti numbers of $B$. The construction uses Morse-Bott methods and requires neither a filling nor index-admissibility. When $c_1(TB)|_{π_2(B)}\ne0$, index recurrence and Morse inequalities yield multiplicity and non-hyperbolicity bounds for nondegenerate contact forms under additional index assumptions. If $c_1(TB)|_{π_2(B)}=0$ and either $H_{\mathrm{odd}}(B;\mathbb Q)=0$ or $ω|_{π_2(B)}=0$, every nondegenerate supporting contact form has infinitely many simple closed Reeb orbits. We also establish multiplicity and non-hyperbolicity results for smooth prequantizations of symplectic orbifolds admitting Hamiltonian circle actions with isolated fixed points.
Waldschmidt constants and invariant geometry for exceptional rank-four complex reflection groups
Krishna Hanumanthu; Jack Huizenga; Jake Kettinger; Lukasz Merta; Tomasz Szemberg; Justyna Szpond

We compute the Waldschmidt constants of the point configurations dual to the reflection arrangements of the exceptional complex reflection groups $G_{29}$, $G_{31}$ and $G_{32}$. They equal $3$ for the forty points of $G_{29}$, $36/11$ for the sixty-point Klein configuration, and $10/3$ for the forty-point Penrose configuration. Together with the known cases $W(F_4)$ and $W(H_4)$, this completes the computation for all exceptional irreducible complex reflection groups of rank four. An invariant dodecic and its sixfold orbit product give extremal surfaces for the first two configurations, and we identify the six dodecics as pullbacks of the coordinate hyperplane sections of the Segre cubic under the Igusa-Segre duality. The matching lower bounds follow from restriction to quadrics and distinguished planes, including a weighted Bézout estimate arising from two related Hesse arrangements. As a consequence, we determine the asymptotic resurgences of the three ideals.
Sharp and explicit Berry--Esseen inequalities over convex sets

We establish finite-sample Berry--Esseen bounds over all convex subsets of $\R^{d}$ for sums of independent random vectors. The upper bounds give explicit dependence on the sample size, dimension, and moments of the summands, with numerical constants. They allow arbitrary dependence among coordinates and cover every real moment order from three onward. For i.i.d. summands, we determine the optimal dependence of the worst-case error on the sample size, the dimension, and the prescribed moment bound. We obtain matching lower bounds using bounded distributions that can be chosen independently of the sample size. The results reveal a fourth-moment threshold for normal approximation over convex sets. Four is the first moment order for which uniform bounds on the corresponding coordinate moments yield a worst-case error bound linear in the dimension. Bounds on higher moments give the same worst-case rate. The proof combines convexity with the addition of independent Gaussian noise to establish a normal approximation bound for Rademacher sums on Parseval frames. Random swaps with independent copies then allow us to apply this bound conditionally to general sums of independent random vectors.
Lingrui Ge; Svetlana Jitomirskaya; Jiangong You

We solve the ten martini problem for the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum of any nonconstant real analytic one-frequency Schrödinger operator. The proof uses the intrinsic symplectic structure of the dual center of Ge--Jitomirskaya [28] and extends the Kotani--almost-reducibility strategy of Ge--Jitomirskaya--You [30] from two-dimensional centers to arbitrary finite center dimension.
Monochromatic or rainbow triangles in the triangular lattice

Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus conjectured that for each non-equilateral triangle $\operatorname{T}$, every 2-coloring of the plane contains a congruent copy of $\operatorname{T}$ with monochromatic vertex set. We confirm this conjecture for triangles with a ratio $\sqrt{7/3}$ between two side lengths. We further prove that every coloring of the plane, regardless of the number of colors used, contains congruent copies of 36 specific triangles with monochromatic or rainbow vertex sets, partially answering a question of Gehér, Sagdeev, and Tóth. Both these results were obtained by considering finite configurations on the triangular lattice.
Samuel Fiorini; J. Pascal Gollin; Tony Huynh; Simon Keil; O-joung Kwon; Sang-il Oum; Roohani Sharma; Stefan Weltge

We take a first step toward a broader study of classical combinatorial optimization problems through the maximum subdeterminants of their standard integer programming formulations, yielding new positive results for several famous (NP-hard) problems. An integer matrix is totally $Δ$-modular if every square submatrix has determinant of absolute value at most $Δ$. For every fixed $Δ$, it has been known that maximum clique, maximum stable set, and minimum vertex cover can be solved in polynomial time on instances for which the coefficient matrix of the natural formulation is totally $Δ$-modular. We extend this list by showing that the same holds for many other problems, including the weighted versions of maximum cut, the traveling salesman problem, feedback vertex set, odd cycle transversal, dominating set, max 2-sat, induced matching, and cluster vertex deletion, as well as for $k$-colorability and graph isomorphism. Our proofs reveal several new ways in which bounded subdeterminants impose combinatorial structure: they bound the size or maximum degree of the input graph, bound packings of cycles and other obstructions, or yield decompositions into tractable graph classes such as forests, chordal graphs, graphs of bounded treewidth, and graphs of bounded linear mim-width.
Mean-field BSDEs with jumps under quadratic-exponential growth
Weimin Jiang; Juan Li; Yan Shen

This paper studies the well-posedness of mean-field backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs, for short) with Poisson jumps, where the generator has quadratic growth with respect to $Z$ and exponential growth with respect to $U$, where $(Y,Z,U)$ denotes the solution of this BSDE. First, we prove the existence and the uniqueness of local solutions to mean-field backward stochastic differential equations with jumps (BSDEJs, for short) by using a fixed-point argument. Then, based on these local results, we discuss the solvability of global solutions in the following two cases: in the first one, the generator has linear growth with respect to $Y$ and the corresponding marginal distribution $μ_1$; and in the second one, the generator has subquadratic growth with respect to the marginal distribution $μ_2$ and linear growth with respect to the marginal distribution $μ_3$, corresponding to $Z$ and $U$, respectively. Finally, by employing a Girsanov transformation we establish a comparison theorem for mean-field BSDEJs under quadratic-exponential growth conditions.
Koszul duality and determinant formulas for affine hyperplane arrangements

For real affine hyperplane arrangements, we prove Lam's determinant conjecture for the inverse Varchenko matrix restricted to bounded chambers. The proof combines Lam's comparison of twisted intersection forms with the period determinant formula of Varchenko, Loeser-Sabbah and Douai-Terao. For normal crossing arrangements, we introduce the taut path algebra and the chamber intersection algebra and establish a Koszul duality between them, yielding an explicit multivariate formula for the inverse Varchenko matrix. After specializing the parameters to $q$, its restriction to bounded chambers is a scalar multiple of the $q$-intersection matrix, proving a determinant conjecture of the authors. We also discuss how the Koszul duality results generalize to affine oriented matroids.
State-constrained optimal control with the theory of functional connections: squared slacks and junction exponents

For optimal control problems with an affine state constraint, we combine the theory of functional connections (TFC), which writes every function satisfying prescribed linear conditions as an explicit expression in terms of a free function, with the squared-slack substitution $b - a^\top x(t) = s(t)^2$. Every trial trajectory then satisfies the endpoint conditions and the path constraint identically. The accuracy depends on the regularity of the slack function at the junctions with a boundary arc. Along an optimal trajectory, the constraint residual vanishes like $(t_1 - t)^m$, where the junction exponent $m$ is equal to the order $p$ of the constraint if and only if the $p$-th derivative of the constraint jumps at the junction, and thus a single polynomial slack converges algebraically. The \emph{multiple-arc TFC method} that we introduce, with unknown junction times and with residuals $(t_1 - t)^m σ(t)^2$ on the free arcs, represents the optimal trajectory exactly and converges geometrically when the arcs are analytic. In a linear-quadratic class, an exact cost identity shows that the cost of every trial trajectory is an upper bound of the optimal cost. We compare both approaches with direct collocation and indirect shooting on the Bryson-Denham problem, on a rendezvous problem with an approach corridor and on the six-dimensional atmospheric reentry of a space shuttle with three state constraints.
Cyclically covering subspaces and additive perfect codes

Let $h_q(n)$ be the largest codimension of a subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ whose cyclic shifts cover the whole space. For $r>0$, we characterize the inequality $h_q(n)\ge r$ in terms of cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes over vector alphabets with covering radius one, no nonzero word of block weight one, and a scalar dual generated by the shifts of one word. For $k,m\ge2$, let $I_q(j)$ count the monic irreducible polynomials of degree $j$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$. If $k$ is prime or $m\ge2\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}I_q(j)+2$, we prove that a cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$ linear perfect code of length $\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q^k$ exists if and only if $\gcd(m,q-1)=1$. When this condition holds, we also obtain \(h_q\!\left(\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}\right)=k(m-1).\) Restriction of scalars gives the same criterion for every $m\ge2$ when $q$ is odd, $q+1$ is a power of two, and $k=2p$ with $p$ prime. We also show that $h_q(q^k+1)=k$ exactly when $q$ is even, for every $k\ge1$.
On the Concavity of Rényi Entropy and Rényi Entropy Power along Heat Flows on Manifolds

In this paper, we establish the concavity of Rényi entropy and Rényi entropy power along heat flow on Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, for Rényi orders $α\in[1,2]$. More generally, we prove the corresponding result along the heat flow generated by the Witten Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds under a suitable curvature-dimension condition. Our argument builds on novel functional inequalities that were recently developed for the study of Tsallis entropy concavity along the heat flow. We extend both these inequalities and the resulting concavity theorem from the Euclidean setting to the Riemannian manifold setting. In addition, we establish the complete monotonicity of Tsallis entropy of order $2$ along the heat flow and derive its spectral decomposition.
Spectral-Domain Information Geometry of Stationary Covariance Models: Gaussian and Elliptical Extensions
Shu Yang; Dongying Li; Wenxian Yu

This paper develops an information-geometric framework for stationary covariance structures. We begin with the infinite-dimensional setting, where stationary covariance structures can be characterized without finite-window boundary effects. By formulating the covariance structure as a bilinear form on a suitable class of test functions, we establish its spectral representation and show how finite-dimensional Toeplitz covariance matrices arise as restrictions to nested observation subspaces. For zero-mean proper complex Gaussian wide-sense stationary (WSS) processes, we show that the normalized finite-dimensional Fisher information converges to a spectral-domain metric. In logarithmic spectral coordinates, this metric becomes the standard $L^2$ inner product, yielding an explicit Fisher--Rao distance that is also recovered as the asymptotic normalized affine-invariant Riemannian distance between Toeplitz covariance matrices. We then extend the framework to elliptical observation models by separating global covariance scale from shape. The shape Fisher information is orthogonal to radial nuisance directions and is characterized by a dimension- and radial-model-dependent coefficient. We derive a condition under which this coefficient converges to its Gaussian value as the observation dimension tends to infinity. The resulting limiting spectral-shape geometry is the centered $L^2$ geometry of log-spectra and is invariant to positive rescaling. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence results and the recovery of the Gaussian shape coefficient.
Explicit resonance and bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays

We investigate the bifurcation of symmetric periodic solutions for differential systems with multiple distributed delays. For general multiple-delay systems with a quadratic potential, we establish a Hamiltonian formulation with a \(P_{n,m}\)-boundary condition and derive explicit Maslov index and nullity formulas. For the special case of two distributed delays, we extend the analysis to general nonlinear potentials. These results yield explicit resonance criteria, bifurcation conditions, and Rabinowitz type and Fadell-Rabinowitz type alternatives for $\mathbb{R} $-distinct solutions.
Representations of the Loop mirror BMS-Kac-Moody algebra
Haibo Chen; Yongliang Wang; Ying Xu

In this paper, we construct a new family of non-weight modules $Ω(λ,ζ,α,β,γ,σ, h)$ over the loop mirror BMS-Kac-Moody algebra $\mathcal{G}$, which is a Takiff-type extension of the loop mirror Heisenberg--Virasoro algebra. We establish criteria for irreducibility, determine their isomorphism classes, and classify all $\mathcal{G}$-modules that are free of rank one. Moreover, we determine all self-extensions of these modules: for every such module $M$, $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{U(\mathcal{G})}(M,M)\cong \mathbb{C}^{6}$, and we construct explicit $1$-cocycles realizing every cohomology class. Every nonsplit self-extension of a simple module is indecomposable of composition length two. Restricting these modules to the loop mirror Heisenberg--Virasoro subalgebra $\mathcal{H}$ yields new $\mathcal{H}$-modules. Among them the $σ$-type modules $Ψ(λ,ζ,σ,α,β,γ,h)$ constitute a new family with no counterpart in the non-loop or non-Takiff case. For the degenerate case $σ=0$, we establish criteria for irreducibility and isomorphism, and describe certain maximal submodules and their simple quotients. Finally, we construct and classify a new class of tensor product $\mathcal{H}$-modules.
Counterexamples to the buckling eigenvalue-ratio conjecture in every dimension
Guowei Dai; Yingxin Sun; Yong Zhang

In 1999, Ashbaugh formulated the conjecture that the ball maximizes the ratio of the first two clamped buckling eigenvalues among bounded domains in Euclidean space. We disprove this conjecture in every dimension $d\ge2$ by constructing smooth connected domains with finitely many interior holes. The key observation is that a zero-value constraint on a concentric sphere close to the boundary of a ball increases the first two eigenvalues by the same relative amount to first order, whereas their ratio increases strictly at second order. A quantitative surface penalty and logarithmic cutoffs transfer this strict inequality to smooth perforated domains. The construction gives explicit geometric parameters depending only on the dimension \(d\).
Legendre manifolds generated by the Barenblatt equations

The paper is devoted to the construction of exact general solutions of the equations of oil filtration in a porous medium under the action of an active reagent injected into the reservoir. The choice of the reagent solution determines the control process of chemical oil flooding in hard-to-recover fields. The problem is described by a system of two first-order nonlinear partial differential equations (the Barenblatt model). Conditions are found on the Buckley--Leverett function, the adsorption function, and the distribution function of the reagent in oil under which the original system, by means of a nonlinear change of variables on a five-dimensional manifold endowed with a contact structure, is reduced to a linear wave system with constant coefficients. Six families of such functions are indicated. For them, contact transformations and Legendre surfaces corresponding to general solutions in implicit form are constructed.
FRT presentation of the $q$-Onsager comodule algebra and refined $q$-characters

We introduce a concept of counital comodule algebra $(B,δ_B,ε_B)$ over a Hopf ${\mathbb K}$-algebra $H$, where $δ_B: B\rightarrow B \otimes H$ and $ε_B: B\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ are coaction and counit homomorphisms, respectively. This structure gives a canonical (counital) comodule algebra map $ι_B: B \rightarrow H$. In this paper, we study in details the case $B=O_q$, and $H$ is the quantum loop algebra ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$ for ${\mathbb K}={\mathbb C}$. Here, $O_q$ is the $q$-Onsager algebra with four presentations: (i) the $q$-Dolan-Grady type; (ii) the alternating type; (iii) the root vectors type; (iv) the Drinfeld type. For $(O_q,δ_{O_q},ε_{O_q})$, in fact a 3-parameter family of counital comodule algebras, we establish a Faddeev-Reshetikhin-Takhtajan (FRT) type presentation, which is written in terms of a K-operator satisfying a reflection algebra relation. The coaction $δ_{O_q}$ (resp. $ι_{O_q}$) sends the K-operator to a `dressed' K-operator (resp. K-matrix) using Ding-Frenkel type L-operators of ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$; the counit $ε_{O_q}$ sends the K-operator to the most general (non-diagonal) solution of the reflection equation. The FRT presentation allows to compute the image via $δ_{O_q}$ and $ι_{O_q}$ of the generating functions of $O_q$ for each presentation (ii)-(iv). Moreover, the images of Lu-Wang's generating functions of $O_q$ in the so-called Drinfeld second realization ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$ are obtained, as well as their images via the (ordinary) coproduct of ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$, which enhance two theorems by Przeździecki. Finally, we apply our FRT presentation to the construction of new type $q$-characters for ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$, in imaginary root vectors of $O_q$, refining those of Frenkel-Reshetikhin, and we explain representation-theoretic meaning of such refining.
A complete symmetric rank-two modularity classification, obtained through a sharp uniform degree bound

We classify modular Nahm sums with a rational symmetric positive-definite two-by-two matrix and rational shifts. Up to coordinate exchange, every modular datum belongs to three explicit rational-point families, is a product of two modular rank-one sums, or is one of thirty-four exceptional triples on twelve matrices. The list consists of Zagier's rank-two examples, the Vlasenko--Zwegers additions and split products; no further data occur. The proof first bounds the joint degree of the distinguished Nahm point by four, using an initial degree bound of twenty-four and exact local exclusions at the prime 7. Explicit height and exponent bounds then give exhaustive arithmetic classifications in degrees one through four. Exact polynomial elimination determines all rational shifts, and published identities of q-series establish modularity of the survivors. The degree bound is sharp. The finite steps are accompanied by exact certificates, verification programs and independently implemented checks. Computational companion: https://github.com/johnngy44/math/releases
Coarse Embeddings Beyond Doubling: Persistence Diagrams and Multiparameter Modules
Sushovan Majhi; Atish Mitra; Žiga Virk

We study coarse embeddings into Hilbert space and the asymptotic dimension of spaces of persistence diagrams and multiparameter persistence modules. We replace doubling, the usual hypothesis for landmark embeddings, by admissible tent covers of bounded multiplicity at every scale: stacking them across dyadic scales gives an explicit $1$-Lipschitz coarse embedding, with lower gauge $c\sqrt{τt}$, or nearly linear for slowly decaying weights, and the same covers bound the asymptotic dimension by the multiplicity. The spaces of persistence diagrams are not doubling but carry such covers, and for diagrams with $n$ points our covers improve the constant of the known landmark embedding by a factor exponential in $n$. Slice by slice, the construction embeds multiparameter modules with boundedly many bars per slice under the matching distance on any finite net of slices, a class that contains the modules with at most $n$ generators. Bounding bars or persistent Betti numbers instead of generators fails: two-parameter modules with one bar on every slice have infinite asymptotic dimension, and neither they nor the modules of bounded support and bounded rank admit a coarse embedding into Hilbert space, under the matching or the interleaving distance.
Motivic Mirror Symmetry for Sink-recurrent Cluster Varieties

We prove motivic mirror symmetry for full-rank sink-recurrent cluster varieties. We allow skew-symmetrizable principal parts and invert all frozen variables. The rational geometric motive of such a variety is isomorphic to the additive orbifold motive of the mirror stack of Hu and Shende. This gives comparisons of cohomology, higher Chow groups, and algebraic $K$-theory with rational coefficients. The proof combines quantum deformation with the splitting of these motives into Tate summands. For really full-rank skew-symmetric seeds, a finite étale morphism realizes the comparison. We also study this geometric comparison in families over the projective line.
Quantitative global regularity for Navier--Stokes equations with odd viscosity on the cubic three-torus
Jinzheng Li; Yuqi Li; Hao-Yu Sun

We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equation on the cubic torus with a constant odd-viscosity operator given by the vertical derivative of the curl. Arbitrary real, mean-zero, divergence-free initial data and an independent steady force, both in the second-order Sobolev space, admit a unique global strong solution when the magnitude of one fixed odd-viscosity coefficient is at least a norm-uniform sufficient threshold. In the unforced case the solution is smooth at positive times. The qualitative argument adapts the resonant-averaging framework for rapidly rotating fluids to the different odd-viscous dispersion. Weighted lattice counts and signed corrected-energy estimates yield a sufficient bound for the odd-to-ordinary viscosity ratio that is polynomial in the normalized initial-data radius at each fixed normalized force radius, together with a separate bound in a specified force-dominated regime. No optimality is claimed for the polynomial exponents or prefactors; determining the sharp viscosity threshold for the original equation remains open. Direct kinetic and weighted enstrophy barriers also give regularity for every coefficient on explicit bounded data and force regions, including the closed unforced ball of homogeneous second-order Fourier Sobolev radius ninety-seven fortieths times the viscosity and seven closed forced rectangles. We specify how finite certificates enter the analytic argument and distinguish minimization of a sufficient formula from sharpness for the original equation. All three main theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
Eigenvector Occupation Statistics and Extremes in the Rosenzweig-Porter Model
Yan V. Fyodorov; Mariya Shcherbina; Tatyana Shcherbina

We study the occupation probabilities $p_i=|u_i|^2$ of a normalized bulk eigenvector in the GUE Rosenzweig-Porter model $A_N=B_N+τ_NG_N$, with $τ_N^2=N^{1-γ}$ and $1<γ<2$. Conditioning on an eigenvalue at a regular bulk energy $E$ through the normalized one-eigenpair Kac-Rice law, we derive an exact finite-$N$ projective density and reduce its asymptotic analysis to a Hubbard-Stratonovich integral over $2\times2$ Hermitian matrices, which we evaluate by the saddle-point method. The resulting occupation field is governed by a self-consistent Lorentzian profile with effective resonant size $K_N(E)\asymp N^{2-γ}$ and local exponential fluctuations. We prove the asymptotics of all generalized inverse participation sums and identify a transition at $q=1/2$. We also obtain a two-branch thickened amplitude-counting spectrum. At the two ends of the occupation field we prove marked Poisson point-process limits: the largest components have Gumbel fluctuations, whereas the smallest component has an exponential limit on the scale $N^{-1-γ}$. Finally, for every fixed $q>0$ the largest component contributes an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the inverse participation sum, showing that these fixed-$q$ statistics do not freeze. The statements are quenched, uniformly on a high-probability regularity event for the diagonal disorder, and hence also hold in the annealed setting.
Distributional Limits of Empirical Codegree Processes in Sampled Networks

We study fluctuations of empirical distributions of normalized codegrees under independent vertex sampling from deterministic or random weighted parent networks. We establish a quantitative multivariate normal approximation for sampled biclique counts. Under additional graph-limit and sparsity assumptions, we establish convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the empirical codegree process indexed by smooth test functions. We further establish functional convergence on Hölder balls, with a smoothness threshold depending on network sparsity and vertex sampling probabilities. We verify our assumptions for classes of graphon-generated random graphs and give counterexamples showing that the smoothness conditions cannot in general be weakened.
Adding unbounded and not bounded sets to a singular cardinal

This paper solves a problem (SP) attributed to Solovay in the 1960s, which is to add an unbounded sequence to a singular cardinal $κ$ without adding bounded subsets to $κ$, while preserving $κ^+$. The solution applies to any cofinality of the singular cardinal, with the assumption that $κ$ is a strong limit needed for the case of uncountable cofinality. Unsuccessful attempts to solve (SP), mostly for the countable cofinality, have appeared in published papers by various authors.
Discrete Configuration Spaces of Simplex Skeleta: a Middle-Dimensional Manifold Phenomenon
Emilio J. González; Jesús González; Mary Carmen Pérez-Morales

For a simple graph $Γ$ without loops and an integer $n\geq2$, Abrams showed in his Ph.D. thesis that the discrete configuration space $DConf(Γ,n)$ is homeomorphic to a closed $n$-manifold if and only if $n=2$ and $Γ$ is $K_5$ or $K_{3,3}$, the two minimal obstructions to graph planarity. We show that this manifold property persists for the infinite family of discrete configuration spaces obtained by replacing the Kuratowski graphs with the $d$-skeleton of the simplex of dimension $2d+2$, thus recovering Abrams' $K_5$ case when $d=1$. Our manifold recognition argument relies on a recursive application of Whitehead's theorem that collapsible PL manifolds are PL balls, combined with Forman's discrete Morse theory. The resulting construction produces an infinite family of combinatorial spheres that contains the Legendre polytope boundaries and is closed under taking vertex links.
On $\mathrm{HH}^1$ of blocks of finite simple group algebras
Matthew Antrobus; Lleonard Rubio y Degrassi; Can Wen

Let $G$ be a sporadic simple group, $k$ a field of positive characteristic and assume $B$ is a block of $kG$ with non-trivial defect. In this paper we prove the first Hochschild cohomology group $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is non-vanishing. Furthermore, we prove that for every wild block with abelian defect of a sporadic simple group, we have that $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is a solvable Lie algebra of derived length two, with non-zero maximal toral rank.
Delaunay Asymptotics for the Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation

In dimensions $n\geq3$, we prove that near an isolated boundary singularity a positive solution of the Escobar--Yamabe equation for a smooth metric approaches a fixed periodic Delaunay solution or the cylindrical solution if its trace lies between positive multiples of $|\overline x|^{-(n-2)/2}$, where $\overline x$ is the tangential Fermi coordinate. The relative error decays at a positive power rate, with weighted estimates through two derivatives in Fermi coordinates. The necksize is unique, and the translation parameter is unique modulo the least positive period in the periodic case. The Hamiltonian smoothly parametrizes the periodic family modulo translation. We classify Jacobi fields of polynomial growth at both ends without assuming symmetry. Translation and energy differentiation generate these fields along periodic solutions, and two oscillatory fields generate them along the cylindrical solution. We also exhibit a first-order obstruction to improving these asymptotics by boundary-preserving conformal deformations of the flat models.
Property F implies weak integrality for non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion categories
Justin Asher; Jonah Berean-Dutcher; Clay Cordova; Julio Parra-Martinez; Richard Tuddenham

We prove that every non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion category with property F is pseudo-unitary and weakly integral. In particular, every modular category with property F is weakly integral. Neither sphericality nor pseudo-unitarity is assumed. Passing to the Drinfeld centre extends the result to degenerate categories whose dimensions are positive on the intersection of the Müger centre with the adjoint subcategory; these include every braided fusion category with a pseudo-unitary Galois conjugate. Physically, the result connects the arithmetic of topological orders to the computational power of anyon braiding: non-integer squared total quantum dimension guarantees infinite braid group images, a necessary condition for universal quantum computation.
A proof of the Erdős-Herzog-Piranian lemniscate conjecture

Let $p:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n\geq 1$. In 1958, Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian conjectured that the length of the lemniscate $\{z\in\mathbb C:|p(z)|=1\}$ is maximized by $p(z)=z^n-1$. We prove this conjecture in every degree and show that equality holds precisely for $p(z)=(z-z_0)^n-e^{iθ}$, where $z_0\in\mathbb C$ and $θ\in\mathbb R$. The proof uses Möbius variations of the critical values and estimates for the inverse branches of $p$, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted estimates in a finite range of degrees.
Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity, Part II: Regular Pattern Packings and Moment Sequences
Natasha Blitvić; Mohammed Slim Kammoun; Einar Steingrímsson

We prove that broad families of regular pattern packings are enumerated by moments of probability measures on $[0,\infty)$. A packing prescribes occurrences of a consecutive permutation pattern at equally spaced positions, with successive occurrences overlapping and together covering the permutation. This regularity underlies the structure theory for the associated pattern-packing posets that we developed in Part I (arXiv:2610.29846). We obtain moment representations for all two-level shifted-grid families of Part I and all overlap-one patterns whose first and last letters differ by one or two. For families whose posets are trees with a unique minimum or maximum and overlap at most half the pattern length, positivity instead holds after finitely many initial terms of the enumerating sequence have been discarded. Our proofs develop further enumeration formulas and combine probabilistic constructions with total nonnegativity and weighted paths, yielding explicit laws or continued fractions in several cases. Although a previously conjectured universal moment property fails, our results establish positivity for all packing sequences associated with patterns of length at most four and all but one of the distinct sequences arising from patterns of length five. Extensive numerical evidence suggests that the remaining sequence is also a moment sequence. These results lead us to formulate refined conjectures for all overlap-one patterns and for the shifted-grid families of Part I with arbitrarily many levels.
Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations and Closed-Form Geodesics on Non-Naturally Reductive Orbit Spheres: The Spin(9) 15-Sphere and the Cayley Plane

By the Skew-Torsion Holonomy Theorem of Olmos and Reggiani (2012), the 15-sphere $S^{15}$ admits no non-trivial naturally reductive metric under any transitive Lie group, precluding geodesic integration via canonical Ambrose-Singer connections. Simultaneously, Nikonorov (2013) established that every $Spin(9)$-invariant metric on $S^{15}$ is a geodesic orbit (GO) space. We integrate the geodesic flow on this non-naturally reductive GO manifold via the Lie Subalgebra Closure Principle: whenever the slice generators of a multi-axial reductive decomposition close into a finite-rank reductive Lie subalgebra, the geodesic vector equations decouple into an algebraic eigenvalue problem. Using the 16-dimensional spin representation and Vol'per's decomposition $\mathfrak{spin}(9) = \mathfrak{spin}(7) \oplus \mathfrak{p}_1 \oplus \mathfrak{p}_2$, we prove that the slice generators $X_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_2$ and $Y_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_1$ close into $\mathfrak{u}(2) \cong \mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1) \subset \mathfrak{so}(16)$. The generator $M = αX_1 + βY_1$ has the four-mode spectrum $Ω\in \{ |R \pm 3α|, |R \pm α| \}$ ($R = \sqrt{α^2 + β^2}$), yielding a closed-form 4-projector decomposition and Euler-Cartan factorization for $\exp(αX_1 + βY_1)$. Under the normalized Ricci flow, we prove that the Bourguignon-Karcher squashed Einstein metric at $t = 3/11$ ($λ= 64$) is an unstable repeller separating sub-Riemannian fiber collapse from the round sphere basin. Finally, on the deformed Cayley plane $\mathbb{O}P^2 = F_4/Spin(9)$, we prove universal CROSS never-Einstein rigidity, establish the 15-dimensional three-stratum Whitney stratification of the cut locus $Cut(q_0)$ at non-polar basepoints $q_0$, and prove Blaschke and Besse rigidity for all $λ> 0$.
Stability of patterns in variational systems with continuous symmetries: a computer-assisted approach
Jan Bouwe van den Berg; Dominic Blanco

In variational models of pattern formation, periodic solutions are never isolated: since the energy does not change under translations, every shifted copy of a pattern is again a solution. This is an obstacle for computer-assisted proofs, which need isolated solutions. Imposing discrete symmetries removes the obstacle, but restricts the patterns that can be studied and only gives stability against symmetric perturbations. We develop a computer-assisted method that deals with the translations directly. We fix the position of the pattern with phase conditions and add unfolding parameters. They act as Lagrange multipliers, and translation invariance of the energy ensures that they vanish at a solution, under a condition that is verified rigorously by the computer. We then derive the stability of the pattern from the computer-assisted proof. We obtain the number of unstable directions and show that the only neutral directions are the translations. We apply the method to the Swift-Hohenberg equation in two dimensions and prove the existence of stable and unstable patterns without imposed symmetry. Since the linear algebra does not depend on the number of translation directions, the approach extends to higher dimensions.
DreamLander: A 6-DOF World Model based Reinforcement Learning Planetary Lander
George Nehma; Patrick Quinn; Madhur Tiwari; Camilo Riano-Rios

Soft powered descent landings are becoming evermore important in the field of space exploration and scientific advancement, because of their ability to deliver mission critical payloads, both highly accurately and safely. The high efficiency restriction on planetary landings due to the severely limited fuel supply results in the need for optimal guidance trajectories and control. Model based reinforcement learning is proving to be an important tool in simplifying the highly complex process of generating optimal guidance trajectories and control. In this work, we present DreamLander, a state of the art model based reinforcement learning algorithm based on DreamerV3, to generate optimal guidance and control for a realistic 6 degree of freedom entry descent landing problem. The model based approach creates a sample efficient and highly generalizable model that can be applied to a variety of scenarios whilst maintaining a high degree of accuracy, landing within 2 meters of the designated landing zone, and with velocity norm less than 0.3 meters per second. DreamLander makes use of state sensor observations, making progress toward End-to-End solutions of the Entry Descent Landing problem.
Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations of Space Forms: Curvature Pinching, Soliton Rigidity, Conjugate Loci, and Superintegrability

We study the one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics $g_λ$ induced by the Hamiltonian cotangent deformation $H_λ= H_0 + \fracλ{2}\|J\|^2$ on simply connected space forms of constant curvature $κ\in \{1, 0, -1\}$, where $J$ is the momentum map of the isotropy action fixing a base point. The master reciprocal identity $1/f_λ^2 = 1/s_κ^2 + λ$ governing the warping function controls the geometry of the family and implies that radial geodesic acceleration is independent of $λ$. From this mechanism we derive three classes of results: (1) Curvature and rigidity: closed-form sectional curvatures, the sharp positivity trichotomy, pointwise and global Brendle-Schoen $1/4$-pinching windows on $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$, never-Einstein rigidity for $λ\neq 0$, and the realization of Hamilton's steady cigar soliton on $(\mathbb{H}^2, g_1)$ as the unique gradient Ricci soliton in the family. (2) Dynamics and stability: iso-kinematic decoupling into unperturbed radial motion and uniform precession $Ω= λL$, closed-form Clairaut integration, the transcendental inward conjugate point law with Euclidean inversion $r_0 R^* = 1/λ$, and stratified $A_3$ cusp caustics. (3) Integrability and spectral theory: maximal superintegrable rational pericenter invariants on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, transverse Killing rigidity on curved space forms, Fuchsian Heun spectral reduction with modulus $τ= 1 + λ/κ$, and essential spectrum gap collapse to $[0, \infty)$ on $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$. Extensions to anisotropic sphere families and intrinsic deformations of compact rank-one symmetric spaces ($\mathbb{C}P^n, \mathbb{H}P^n, \mathbb{O}P^2$) are also established.
Global Green-Schwarz response on quaternionic sphere bundles

Local anomaly polynomials describe local variations, but a normalized Green-Schwarz phase also depends on global background data. We explain this dependence for ten-dimensional three-sphere bundles of quaternionic lines over closed spin seven-manifolds. The backgrounds retain two specified $\mathrm{Spin}(16)$ gauge bundles and an integral differential trivialization on the base, including its boundary identifications. The trivialized class is the sum of half the first Pontryagin class of the tangent bundle and the second Chern class of the quaternionic line's underlying complex bundle. For these backgrounds, the calculation combines a generally nonzero local Green-Schwarz integral with a real eta invariant evaluated by a twelve-dimensional Atiyah-Patodi-Singer filling. Together, these terms determine an integral relative characteristic number; the additive response is one third of that number, modulo integers. When the base's third and fourth rational cohomology groups vanish, the response equals eight times the Crowley-Goette invariant, without assuming that the base is simply connected. A calibration using the actual quaternionic line bundle gives additive value one third on $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$, recovering the known third-root phase. Distinct integral String data on one fixed ten-manifold give all three phase values, showing which global background information the response can detect. The physical identifications retain their prescribed fermion data, while the separate application to integral topological modular forms and vertex operator superalgebras requires compatible integral lifts. The response calculation constructs neither a microscopic realization nor an equivalence of complete theories.
A geometric Kähler--Ricci flow proof of the Calabi--Yau theorem

We give a geometric proof that every Kähler class on a compact Kähler manifold with vanishing real first Chern class contains a unique Ricci-flat metric, and that the Kähler--Ricci flow converges smoothly to this metric. The fixed Kähler class and the bounded logarithmic volume density control the mean pairwise distance. Chow's scalar-curvature decay makes available, at a fixed spatial scale and all sufficiently late times, the relative-volume comparison of Jian--Song, derived from Bamler's pointed Nash entropy estimates. This comparison upgrades the mean-distance bound to a diameter bound without an absolute lower bound for entropy. A restarted heat-gradient estimate then gives exponential decay of the Ricci potential. A parabolic Schwarz estimate and the interior estimates of Sherman--Weinkove yield smooth exponential convergence. The proof does not invoke the Calabi--Yau existence theorem or global estimates for a scalar complex Monge--Ampère equation.
Extensions from Positive and Full Unit Spheres of $C^\infty([0,1])$ with a Compatible Fréchet Metric

We study isometric extensions from positive and full unit spheres of $C^\infty([0,1],\mathbb F)$, where $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. We equip these spaces with a translation-invariant metric that induces the usual Fréchet topology, is unbounded, has convex balls, and has strictly increasing distances from zero along nonzero rays. Every surjective isometry of the pointwise positive unit sphere extends uniquely to a complex-linear surjective isometry of the complex-valued space. Restriction gives the unique real-linear isometric extension on the real-valued space. On the full unit sphere, every surjective isometry extends uniquely to a real-linear surjective isometry. The positive-sphere maps are compositions with the identity or an admissible reflection. The full-sphere maps also allow constant unimodular factors and, over the complex field, conjugation. We also classify the surjective ambient isometries. A counterexample shows that these metric properties alone do not guarantee positive-sphere extension. Under an explicit anchor condition, we classify surjective isometries of finite-order jet-positive spheres for maximum-type anchored metrics and prove that they extend uniquely to complex-linear surjective isometries. The classification allows any permutation of the anchored coordinates, combined with the identity or reflection on the highest-derivative component. The condition holds for every anchor when $m=1$ or $m=2$.

By Sylow's theorem, the number of Sylow $p$-subgroups of a finite group is congruent to $1$ modulo $p$, but not every such integer occurs. Frobenius extended the congruence to the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ for every $a\ge0$. Kulakoff and Hall showed that this number is congruent to $1$ or $1+p$ modulo $p^2$ whenever $p^{a+1}$ divides the group order. A positive integer is a Frobenius $p$-number if it is the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ of some finite group for some $a$. There are integers congruent to $1$ modulo $p^2$ which are not Frobenius $p$-numbers, and it remained open whether there are also such integers congruent to $1+p$ modulo $p^2$. We show that no finite group has exactly $106$ subgroups of order $5^a$ for any $a\ge0$.
The generic behavior of permutation entropy for continuous maps

Permutation entropy, introduced by Bandt and Pompe in 2002, measures the complexity of a dynamical system through the ordinal patterns of its trajectories. Bandt, Keller and Pompe established that for measure-preserving, piecewise monotone interval maps with finitely many monotonicity intervals, the normalized order-$n$ permutation entropy $H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)/n$ converges to the Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy. Although this result has subsequently been extended to broader classes of maps, whether normalized permutation entropy always converges has remained unknown. We show that convergence can fail, and indeed that nonconvergence is generic. More precisely, for a generic continuous Lebesgue measure-preserving map $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$, we prove that \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)}{n}=0, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)}{n\log n}=1. \] Thus, despite the generic vanishing of Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy, permutation entropy exhibits oscillations between vanishing linear growth and the maximal possible asymptotic growth. We also construct an explicit Lebesgue measure-preserving interval map with countably many monotonicity intervals for which the normalized permutation entropy has lower limit zero and upper limit infinity. This demonstrates that nonconvergence can occur even within the countably piecewise-monotone setting, beyond the scope of the convergence theorem of Gutjahr and Keller, relying on conditions concerning the lengths of the pieces.
The Minimum Canonical Volume of Threefolds of General Type
Pinxian Bie; Peien Du; Zhengjie Yu
We prove the sharp lower bound $vol(X) \geq 1/420$ for every smooth complex projective threefold $X$ of general type.
Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
Benoit Collins; Yu Kitagawa; Akihiro Miyagawa; Wangjun Yuan; Ping Zhong

For arbitrary noncommutative polynomials in independent GUE matrices, we prove that the empirical eigenvalue measure converges weakly in probability to the Brown measure of the corresponding polynomial in free semicircular variables. We also prove convergence of the entire eigenvalue set in Hausdorff distance and convergence of the spectral radius, both in probability. Equivalently, these matrix conclusions hold for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent complex Ginibre matrices. Independently, we prove that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables equals its operator spectrum. The proof of weak convergence combines a criterion based on the second moment of the Brown measure with complex Gaussian rotation and convexity. The support theorem uses linearization and rigidity of matrix Dyson equations. We also prove absolute continuity for nonconstant polynomials without adjoints in free circular variables. A matrix Dyson equation recovers Brown measures of arbitrary semicircular polynomials through regularized logarithmic potentials. For drift-corrected nondegenerate elliptic free random walks, it yields quantitative convergence of potentials in the interior of the limiting domain and weak convergence of Brown measures to that of free multiplicative Brownian motion.
Average distance and maximum induced linear forest

Let G be a connected graph of order n, let μ(G) denote its average distance, and let L(G) denote the maximum order of an induced linear forest of G, that is, of an induced subgraph whose components are chains. Hansen, Hertz, Kilani, Marcotte and Schindl conjectured that μ(G) {\le} L(G)/2, which can be written as 4W(G) {\le} L(G)n(n-1), where W(G) is the Wiener index of G. This inequality strengthens their bound μ(G) {\le} F(G)/2, where F(G) is the maximum order of an induced forest, as well as Chung's classical bound μ(G) {\le} α(G). In this paper we prove the conjecture for all connected graphs.
The dimension of multi-index assignment polytopes and Latin-square transversal polytopes, via association schemes

We determine the dimensions, and the implicit equations, of several polytopes from integer programming whose vertices are the largest stable sets of highly symmetric graphs. Our main tools are two new dimension formulae within Lee's spectral method, which reads the dimension off of an association scheme: for amorphic schemes it becomes a threshold formula, and for point sets in $GF(q)^d$ invariant under the maps $z\mapsto az+b$ it is $q-1$ times the number of hyperplane directions along which some point is not equidistributed. A single integer point, a witness, then certifies a whole eigenspace. For the multi-index assignment polytopes of Appa, Magos, and Mourtos at prime-power orders, the dimension equals that of the linear relaxation except in two infinite families, which are, to our knowledge, the first counterexamples to their expectation that the two always coincide. The missing equations are explicit clique equations that the standard integer-programming formulation omits. For every abelian group with a transversal, the Latin-square transversal polytope of its Cayley table, equivalently the polytope of rainbow perfect matchings of the corresponding edge-colored $K_{n,n}$ , has the maximal dimension ${(n-1)(n-2)}$; the witnesses come from new constructions of complete mappings. We also treat transversals of Desarguesian nets and the largest sets of symmetric $3\times3$ and $4\times4$ matrices over $GF(q)$ whose differences have rank at least $3$, of sizes $q^3$ and $q^5$.
Unified architecture for arbitrary two-qubit gates with neutral atoms
Nader Mostaan; Peter Schmelcher; Rick Mukherjee

We propose a unified architecture for two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum processors which allows the implementation of the complete set of two-qubit gates. Our approach rests on a single resource that unlocks the entire gate set: an XXZ interaction with tunable anisotropy, combined only with single-qubit operations. We introduce a Rydberg-atom realization of the tunable XXZ interaction and combine it with optimally controlled global microwave pulses to implement the B, QFT, iSWAP, and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates, as well as a continuous gate family interpolating from CZ to iSWAP via the B gate. This work allows the implementation of any two-qubit gate natively in neutral-atom platforms, enabling flexible switching between instruction sets to reduce circuit depth and compilation overhead in quantum algorithm implementation.
Concave shifts and the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property

Let $\mathcal H$ be a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on the unit disc, and assume $\mathcal H$ is invariant under the forward and backward shifts. We show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal H$ is concave, then $\mathcal H$ is a complete Nevanlinna--Pick space. This gives an affirmative answer to the concavity part of Shimorin's question \cite{Sh02} and extends his theorem on the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property of Dirichlet-type spaces with superharmonic weights.
Why the non-abelian Gyarmati--Matolcsi--Ruzsa inequality does not generally work: mechanisms and explicit examples

For finite sets in a commutative semigroup, Gyarmati, Matolcsi and Ruzsa proved \[ |A_1+\dots+A_n|^{n-1}\ \le\ \prod_{i=1}^n|A_1+\dots+A_{i-1}+A_{i+1}+\dots+A_n| . \] They asked whether in an arbitrary group \[ |A_1\cdots A_n|^{n-1}\ \le\ \prod_{i=1}^n\ \max_{a\in A_i}\,|A_1\cdots A_{i-1}\,a\,A_{i+1}\cdots A_n| , \] where each omitted set is replaced by the largest slice obtained by fixing one of its elements. Nair, Namayandeh and Zhu proved that this inequality does not hold when $n=4$ and $G=D_4^{14}$, of group order $8^{14}$. We develop its double-coset mechanism and construct counterexamples in many other groups. For $n=4$, the smallest group found has order $518\,400$, namely $A_6^2\times C_2^2$; no absolute minimality is claimed. For $n=6$ there is a witness in a group of order $1728$, for $n=10$ a class-three $3$-group of order $243$ suffices, and for $n=4$ a single class-two $2$-group of order $2^{23}$ works. We also obtain torsion-free examples. The violation ratio $R_n=|A_1\cdots A_n|^{n-1}/\prod_iN_i$ is greater than one exactly when the inequality fails; explicit four-set constructions attain $R_4\approx1.29$ in $A_8^2$, and a larger ratio of about $1.43$ is reported for $A_{10}^2$. For every $n\ge4$, the inequality holds in all direct powers of $G$ precisely when $G$ is abelian. For $n\ge2$ the optimal exponent $θ_n$ is the infimum of $\log(\prod_iN_i)/\log|A_1\cdots A_n|$ over products of size at least two. We obtain $2\leθ_n\le n-1.0768$, and an infinite family in $C_3*C_3$ shows $θ_n\le n-1-δ$ for every $δ<5-2\log_25\approx0.3561$ and all sufficiently large $n$.
Learning Rate Decay Can Exponentially Accelerate SGD for Global Optimization of Nonconvex Functions
Guneykan Ozgul; Dylan Herman; Junhyung Lyle Kim; Shree Hari Sureshbabu; Shouvanik Chakrabarti

Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is a workhorse algorithm for continuous optimization. It is a folk belief among deep learning practitioners that learning rate decay in SGD substantially improves performance. However, it has remained unclear whether learning rate decay offers an asymptotic advantage for global nonconvex optimization. We answer this question in the affirmative by demonstrating a natural class of nonconvex functions for which, we prove that SGD with learning rate decay requires exponentially fewer gradient queries for global optimization than SGD with any fixed learning rate in the small-step size regime. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first exponential advantage that has been demonstrated for learning rate decay. The class of functions we consider includes many popular benchmark nonconvex functions. Our results provide a robust explanatory theory for the empirically observed benefits of learning rate decay for global optimization. We show that annealing performs the non-logconcave sampling task associated to the optimization problem in polynomial time, via a novel application of weak Poincaré inequalities.
Adaptive Output Regulation of Linear Systems with Unknown Harmonic Exosystems and Additive Noise

This paper addresses error-feedback output regulation for known multivariable linear plants subject to an unknown exosystem and additive Gaussian process and measurement noise. The exosystem generates constant and sinusoidal signals, but its dimension, frequencies, and coupling matrices are unavailable. An output-injection transformation represents the external action through known channels. A causal observer then produces a residual independent of the applied input, whose filtered output separates into a harmonic signal, stationary colored Gaussian noise, and a decaying transient. Using this observation model, a Fourier procedure consistently identifies the number and values of the active positive frequencies in the presence of noise. The identified frequencies determine a regulator through interpolation with stable residual filters. A contractive filter realization, nonexpansive state resizing, and bounded gain updates ensure closed-loop moment bounds uniformly over the selected filter orders. If the gain bound contains the ideal interpolation gain, the adaptive plant response and tracking error converge in mean square to those of the corresponding known-frequency regulator. The limiting mean-square tracking error is a linear function of the process- and measurement-noise covariances. In the absence of both noises, the tracking error converges to zero.
Riemannian Real-Time Optimization for Robotics: Active Set SQP Parametric Pathfollowing

Robot optimal control often combines Euclidean states with configurations on Lie groups and other smooth manifolds. This paper develops a parametric Riemannian Newton pathfollowing method based on homotopy quadratic programs and parallel strict-working-set tasks. It specifies the event handling, working-set exchanges, matrix factor updates, synchronization, and residual checks used by the algorithm. Tracking guarantees are given under mildly degenerate regularity conditions and the Riemannian strong second-order sufficient condition. Drone navigation and arm manipulation are formulated as geometric optimal-control problems, including finite-force grasp acquisition, transport and supported release. Numerical examples illustrate drone navigation and arm pick-and-place through KKT-residual histories and MuJoCo simulations, together with preliminary initialization results for the full-horizon optimal-control problems.

We construct separable $\mathcal L_\infty$-spaces with Kalton's property $Q$, which, to the best of our knowledge, are the first known examples of this kind. Our technique employs the Bourgain--Pisier construction and a quantitative analysis of metric types in limits of finite-dimensional $η$-admissible embeddings. The argument rests on two complementary estimates: approximate radial centres yield asymptotic separation of tree increments, while an admissibility inequality yields asymptotic gain, leading to concentration on Kalton's interlacing graphs. This leads to an abstract criterion for property $Q$ in terms of asymptotic separation $AS_θ$ and asymptotic gain $AG_α$. We illustrate the limitations of this criterion with Johnson--Lindenstrauss spaces. Our examples exclude uniform embeddings of the unit ball of $c_0$, strengthening in a nonlinear direction the classical Bourgain--Delbaen phenomenon. As an application, every separable Banach space embeds isometrically into a separable $\mathcal L_\infty$-space whose unit ball is not a uniform retract of the unit ball of its bidual.
A Hoare Logic for Continuous-Time Stochastic Processes

Programming language researchers have developed a wide array of tools to reason about probabilistic programs, but it remains unclear how to apply these proof techniques to continuous-time stochastic processes. To bridge this gap, we propose a verification method for properties of continuous-time stochastic processes by reasoning about them as standard programs. To demonstrate our approach, we define a continuous semantics for a probabilistic imperative language $\mathrm{pWhile}^{\mathrm{dt}}$ by taking the Kuratowski limit of the standard semantics, which collects limit points of the standard program semantics as the time-step approaches zero. Then, we present a Hoare-style logic that uses loop invariants and decreasing functions to verify properties of continuous programs. To establish soundness, we identify a broad class of assertions that are preserved from the standard semantics to the continuous semantics. To demonstrate our approach, we verify properties of ten continuous-time stochastic processes modeled in $\mathrm{pWhile}^{\mathrm{dt}}$, including variants of Brownian motion and a stochastic hybrid system.
On regularity and stability results of global weak solutions to two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum

For the initial and initial-boundary value problems of the two-dimensional (2D) incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum, Lions' global weak solutions are shown to possess additional regularity, via establishing some key a priori decay-in-time rates for the approximate problem, under suitable smallness condition on the density-dependent viscosity. In addition, large-time decay rates of the pressure and gradient of velocity are obtained, which are even exponential in time for bounded domains or the periodic case. Note that these results hold without any smallness conditions on the initial data, even for initially vanishing density.
The Cheng--Yau gradient estimate for Jacobi fields

We prove a pointwise gradient estimate for positive Jacobi fields on minimal hypersurfaces of dimension two and three, inspired by the Cheng--Yau estimate for harmonic functions. The estimate also controls the second fundamental form, and so provides yet another proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in dimensions two and three.
Succinct Infinite-Horizon Lyapunov and LQR Value Problems Are BQP-Complete

Fundamental tasks in linear systems analysis and control require evaluating infinite-horizon output energies for autonomous systems and optimal value functions for controlled systems. These quantities are characterized by Lyapunov and algebraic Riccati equations, respectively. In this work, we study promise problems for their evaluation when the system matrices are sparse and represented succinctly by Boolean circuits specifying their nonzero entries, with input length polynomial in the logarithm of the system dimension. For dissipative autonomous systems with coordinate-vector initial states, we define the succinct Lyapunov value problem (SLV). Its extension to linear-quadratic optimal control is the succinct LQR value problem (SLQRV). We prove that SLV is $\BQP$-hard: every problem in bounded-error quantum polynomial time ($\BQP$) reduces to it in polynomial time. We then establish that the more general SLQRV problem admits a quantum algorithm running in time polynomial in the succinct input length. Since SLV is a special case of SLQRV, both problems are $\BQP$-complete. Consequently, unless bounded-error probabilistic polynomial time coincides with $\BQP$, no classical randomized algorithm can solve either problem on all promised instances in time polynomial in the succinct input length.
On the higher-order Titchmarsh divisor problem
Guangwei Hu; Guangshi Lü; Zhiwei Wang; Jie Wu

For every fixed integer $k\geq2$ and every fixed nonzero integer $h$, we prove that, as $x\to\infty$, \begin{equation*} \sum_{x<n\leq2x}Λ(n)τ_k(n+h) \sim C_{k,h}x(\log x)^{k-1}, \end{equation*} where $τ_k$ is the $k$-fold divisor function and $C_{k,h}>0$ is a constant depending only on $k$ and $h$.
Transport, Entropy, and the Cost of Dependence: Maximum Conditional Entropy under Transport Constraints
Andre Bertolace; Konstantinos Gatsis; Kostas Margellos

Maximum-entropy inference under Wasserstein constraints can be computationally challenging due to the underlying optimization over transport couplings. We investigate a tractable alternative based on maximizing conditional entropy under an average transport constraint. On Euclidean spaces, this formulation admits an explicit generalized-Gaussian additive-noise solution, providing a feasible approximation to the Wasserstein-constrained problem without solving an optimal transport problem. We establish quantitative bounds on the resulting optimality gap by showing that the two formulations admit a common feasible-marginal representation, with their discrepancy characterized by the mutual information retained between the nominal and perturbed variables. For discretely supported nominal distributions, we further obtain an exact decomposition of the gap into a marginal-entropy gain and a weighted Jensen-Shannon divergence.
Functorial Homological Mirror Symmetry for Acyclic Cluster Varieties

We introduce the formalism of cluster models, a class of log Calabi-Yau varieties obtained from smooth quasi-affine toric varieties by iterated affine blowups along non-toric codimension 2 centers determined by a really full rank quiver. Cluster models include the truncated cluster varieties of Gross, Hacking, and Keel with respect to really full rank quivers, all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties, and all open toric subvarieties of $\mathbb{C}^n\times(\mathbb{C}^*)^m$. We then construct mirrors to cluster models via iterated Weinstein handle attachments to toric mirrors, so that the corresponding skeleta acquire compact pieces, and we prove homological mirror symmetry for all cluster models, compatibly with freezing, deleting, and contracting vertices of the quiver. This extends toric mirror symmetry and its naturalities beyond the cotangent bundle. In particular, we obtain homological mirror symmetry for all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties. We develop this package with a view towards conjectures of Marsh, Rietsch, and Williams about mirror symmetry for Grassmannians and closed positroid varieties. Motivated by these, we also conjecture that open positroid varieties are self-mirror. Assuming a natural ansatz, we prove this for a class of positroid varieties that includes nontrivial cells in every Grassmannian and all cells in finite-type Grassmannians. Towards this end we introduce a new combinatorial input, the notion of weak $k$-booleanness for permutations and braids.
Global Asymptotics of a Toda Soliton Condensate with Random Scattering Data

We study a dense $N$-soliton condensate for the infinite Toda lattice in the limit $N \to \infty$. In contrast to previous mathematical studies of soliton gases where the norming constants are assumed to be deterministic or infinitesimal, we consider initial scattering data where both the discrete eigenvalues and the norming constants are independent random variables.
