We also disprove a 1963 result by Cohn (also reproduced in Cohn's 2006 monograph), by constructing a domain with similar elements a and b with a an atom and b not a product of atoms (resp., a product of two atoms, one of them central).
Sharp minima of higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated singularities
Chuangqiang Hu; Stephen S. -T. Yau; Lishan Yu; Huaiqing Zuo

We determine the minimum higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated complex polynomial singularities with fixed ambient dimension and multiplicity. A Fermat polynomial of multiplicity $m$, perturbed by the $(m+1)$-st power of a linear form, attains both minimum sequences at every order. These values remain the minima at each prescribed total degree $d>m$; the homogeneous case $d=m$ has a separate Tjurina formula. The proof expresses the Tjurina defect through multiplication in the filtered Milnor algebra and uses the monomial strong Lefschetz theorem to attain the resulting rank bound. We also determine the associated graded higher Tjurina algebras of this family and show that they are unchanged by terms of order at least $m+2$.
Large deviations, optimal trajectories and conservation of momenta in generalised Jackson networks

We study properties of optimal trajectories for the quasipotential that governs large deviations of queue lengths in generalised Jackson networks (GJN). The trajectories are shown to satisfy Hamilton equations. The Hamiltonian is identified. Optimal trajectories and associated costs are found for networks with two and three stations. A conservation law for adjoint variables is discovered to the effect that certain components are maintained along an optimal trajectory. A process is proposed for finding optimal trajectories and computing their costs in general GJN.
The rank of the Fano normal function via the Fermat cubic

We prove that the canonical derivative of the Fano normal function has rank ten at the Fermat cubic threefold. This yields a direct proof of its generic maximal rank, a result also implied by a general theorem of Gao--Zhang. Our approach combines Hain's equivariance principle with an explicit representation-theoretic computation and the nonvanishing of the Griffiths infinitesimal invariant established by Collino--Naranjo--Pirola.
Asymptotic spreading of Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments with time-periodic limits

In this paper, we study the rightward spreading speed of solutions for Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments. The linear growth rate has time periodic limits at the two ends of the moving frame. Each limit has a positive average and may be negative during a period. When the growth rate lies between the two limits at each time, we show that the spreading speed depends only on their averages and the asymptotic shift speed. For intermediate shift speeds, the formulas give nonlocal pulling if the right end has the larger average and speed locking if the left end has the larger average. The interior growth profile may be nonmonotone in space and aperiodic in time. We prove the formulas by constructing upper and lower solutions for a stepwise profile and then comparing with shifted stepwise problems.
Translation continuity for the local bilinear circular maximal operator

We prove a positive power translation-continuity estimate for the local bilinear circular maximal operator on the real line. More precisely, there is $η>0$ such that the operator applied to a translation difference in either input maps $L^8(\mathbb{R})\times L^8(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^4(\mathbb{R})$ with norm $O(|h|^η)$. This answers Question 6.3 in Borges's survey on bilinear spherical averages. The main step is a frequency-localized estimate for arbitrary bounded inputs. A $TT^*$ argument converts it into a linear maximal problem on the plane, associated with pairs of circles. We verify the corrected multi-parameter cinematic curvature condition of Chen, Guo, and Yang by proving an irreducibility and infinitesimal independence statement for the resulting quartic curves. Uniform algebraic sublevel estimates control the degeneracies. Interpolation also gives continuity for all finite exponents $2<p,q<\infty$, with output exponent $pq/(p+q)$.

We study the subellipticity of the analytically deformed Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and give two definitions of resonances, one based on analytic dilation and the other on analytic distortion in the $x$-variables. Due to the failure of global subellipticity of the distorted operator in dimensions $n \geq 2$, the second method can only be used in dimension one. We show that, whenever both methods are applicable, they give rise to the same set of resonances. We also prove that, when $|\na V(x)| = O(\w x^{-ρ})$ with $ρ>1$, positive resonances are embedded eigenvalues and/or scattering resonances whose resonant states belong to weighted $L^2$-spaces and satisfy an outgoing radiation condition.
Rates in the weak invariance principle for slowly mixing sequential dynamical systems

We obtain rates of convergence in the weak invariance principle for certain classes of slowly mixing sequential dynamical systems. In particular, for systems satisfying a Functional Correlation Bound with rate $n^{-γ} \ (γ>1)$, we establish an explicit bound in the Wasserstein-$r$ metric for $1\le r<γ+1$ whenever the variance grows at a sufficiently fast polynomial rate. The proof is based on Bernstein's ``big block--small block" method. Examples covered by our result include sequential heterochaos baker maps and sequential LSV maps. In particular, for random LSV maps over an ergodic base, we obtain rates in the quenched weak invariance principle.
Asymptotics of matrix orthogonal polynomials with non-scalar varying weights

We study the $2\times 2$ matrix orthogonal polynomials $\mathbf{P}_N$ on the real line with respect to the varying weights $\mathrm{e}^{-N\mathbf{Q}(z)}\mathbf{B}(z)$, where $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are real symmetric matrix polynomials that commute with a Hermite-type matrix weight, $\mathbf{Q}$ is not scalar and $\mathbf{B}$ is positive definite. We are motivated by the non-Abelian Toda deformation of the Hermite-type weight, in the sense of Deaño, Morey and Román. The weight depends on $N$ through a matrix exponential that is not scalar, so that its two eigenvalues have different exponential rates. The matrix orthogonality reduces to two scalar orthogonality problems on the real line, with a varying weight that has an essential singularity at the origin. Assuming that the associated equilibrium measure is one-cut regular, we obtain the strong asymptotics of $\mathbf{P}_N$ and of $\det\mathbf{P}_N$ by the Deift-Zhou steepest descent method. Our main result is the limiting zero distribution of the entries of $\mathbf{P}_N$. These zeros are complex in general, and they accumulate on a curve where the contributions of the two eigenvalues of the weight have the same size. When this curve crosses the real segment that attracts the zeros of $\det\mathbf{P}_N$, the zeros of the entries display a critical behavior, and a positive fraction of them accumulates on this segment.
On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
Alexandr Garbali; Cengiz Gazi; Jan de Gier; William Mead; Michael Wheeler

We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.
Real quadratic fields and finite quantum dilogarithms II: traces of quantum modular cocycles
Stavros Garoufalidis; Danylo Radchenko; Campbell Wheeler

We study traces of quantum modular cocycles at fixed points of hyperbolic elements $γ\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, formulate an algebraicity conjecture for these traces, and prove it for the cocycles associated to 1-dimensional state-integrals. In addition, we analyse a finite TQFT associated with $γ$ and conjecture that its invariants for 3-manifolds agree with the traces of their $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ quantum modular cocycles. The finite TQFTs predict a yet-to-be-defined motive with cohomology equipped with a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-degree grading and a $\mathbb{Z}$-weight grading coming from a version of the Riemann hypothesis, which suggests a similar grading should exist for an extension of the Kauffman bracket skein module, for the framed $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Floer cohomology of Abouzaid--Manolescu, and for the quantum modular cocycle. This leads to surprising additive identities among algebraic units, which we confirm for the complement of the simplest hyperbolic knot $4_1$, as well as for $S^1 \times Σ_g$ for a closed genus $g$ surface.
Certified finite-precision readout for $p$-adic kernel aggregation

In non-archimedean numerical analysis, a verified $p$-adic approximation can determine an absolute value, and hence downstream probabilistic rankings and classification decisions, with mathematical exactness long before the underlying number is fully resolved. We turn this observation into rigorous finite-precision certificates for norm-based readouts of amplitude families. For a common error radius, a nonempty resolved set already fixes every exact maximizer, ties included, at the sharp integer absolute precision $v_*+1$, and conditioning on that set yields an exact total-variation identity separating unresolved $p$-adic mass from real rounding error. For aggregates of $p$-adic exponentials, we give a centered-moment certificate with an explicit remainder bound: on rational data it runs in exact rational arithmetic without individual exponential evaluations, attains its minimal bound at an active phase, and resolves every nonzero aggregate at high order; we also obtain an aggregate perturbation bound free of summand-count factors. For multiclass $p$-adic classifiers that decode by minimizing the norm of a class discriminant, we prove a necessary and sufficient certification condition and show that the sharp common precision threshold is $v^{(2)}+1$, governed by the second-largest discriminant valuation, so the winning discriminant need not itself be resolved. We apply these certificates to discrete $p$-adic path-integral actions on uniform affine chains, deriving explicit action centers and proving exact output-independence at zero effective quadratic coupling. Pseudocode and a reproducible reference implementation accompany the theory.
Fundamental Outage and Diversity Limits of Fluid Antenna Multiple Access Under Correlated Nakagami-$m$ Fading

Existing analytical studies of fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA) are largely confined to Rayleigh fading, independent-port assumptions, or asymptotic selection metrics, leaving the fundamental outage behavior under realistic fading and spatial correlation conditions uncharacterized. This paper fills this gap by presenting the first exact and asymptotically tight outage analysis of interference-limited FAMA systems under spatially correlated Nakagami-$m$ fading. By explicitly modeling the joint statistics of the desired and interference powers across fluid-antenna ports, \textcolor{black}{we first formulate the outage probability in terms of the joint desired-signal and interference distributions and then derive an explicit integral expression under a tractable single-reference-port spatial correlation model.} Building on this result, we establish a rigorous diversity-order characterization revealing that the achievable diversity is jointly dictated by the fading severity and the spatial correlation rank imposed by the finite antenna aperture, rather than by the nominal number of ports. To enable accurate and tractable performance evaluation beyond the asymptotic regime, we further introduce a Gamma-matched outage approximation that preserves both the exact diversity order and the array-gain constant. The resulting closed-form expression provides an accurate characterization over a wide range of signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) thresholds and offers clear physical insight into the role of spatial correlation in FAMA systems. Extensive Monte Carlo (MC) simulations confirm the tightness of the exact analysis, the sharpness of the asymptotic results, and the accuracy of the proposed approximation.
Odd realisation numbers of rigid graphs
Sean Dewar; Anthony Nixon; Ben Smith

Determining the number of realisations of a rigid graph for a specific choice of edge lengths is a fundamental problem in discrete geometry. Gortler, Healy and Thurston showed that the number of real realisations of a generic framework is always even or equal to one. Despite being rare, there do exist graphs whose number of complex realisations is odd and not equal to one. In this article, we exhibit two necessary conditions for a rigid graph to have an odd realisation number other than one. We also provide an infinite family of rigid graphs with an odd realisation number other than one.
Cube tilings, partition counters, and the Calkin--Wilf and Kepler trees
Jarosław Grytczuk; Andrzej P. Kisielewicz; Krzysztof Przesławski

A tiling of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by translates of the discrete cube $K_d=\{0,1\}^d$ cuts every translate $K_d+x$ into subcubes. We study the function $\ell(x)$ counting these parts. Its sum over every translate of $K_d$ equals $3^d$, for an arbitrary translation set. For lattice tilings with a triangular basis we obtain a dimension-reduction formula, and we describe every cocyclic lattice by a single normalized congruence. Along a cyclic generator, the counter of a signed bidiagonal lattice is a row of Stern's diatomic sequence; pairs of counter values realize the Calkin--Wilf tree, and complementary binary words realize the Kepler tree. For the binary lattice, the translated counter labelings of the cube carry generating face partitions, supplied by the tiling itself, which force the levels of the Kepler tree, and every nontrivial face partition has a unique lamination direction. Using finite Fourier analysis we prove that the ordered cyclic profile determines a standard cocyclic cube tiling lattice up to coordinate reflections. For lattices tiling by discrete boxes we determine exactly when the analogous statement holds.
Multi-Target Tracking via Mean Field Feedback Control
Changming Lei; Junhao Dai; Donghua Shi

Cooperative tracking of multiple moving targets requires a swarm to continually adjust its deployment. Existing methods often rely on repeated agent-target reassignment or updates to position-dependent partitions, which can complicate coordination as swarms grow. This motivates us to seek an approach with a lighter coordination burden. Specifically, we formulate multi-target tracking as a time-varying density-tracking problem, with the targets' tracking and sensing demands encoded in a task-demand density. From an Onsager-type variational formulation, a closed-form mean-field feedback law is derived to make the swarm density track this evolving density, and the resulting closed-loop system is shown to be well posed. Under the stated assumptions, a Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence analysis establishes exponential KL convergence under ideal feedback and conditional robustness to feedback mismatch under estimated. Numerical experiments demonstrate effective tracking of multiple moving targets and show smaller density errors at comparable applied control energy compared with an existing density-tracking feedback method.
Mitigating the BICM Loss in MIMO Receivers with Correlation-Informed Logits

Bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) is widely used in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems. However, separating MIMO data detection from channel decoding and only exchanging per-bit soft information discards correlation information among the bits within each transmit vector. We show that the resulting information loss limits the performance of practical one-shot receivers. Even though iterative detection and decoding (IDD) can recover most of this loss, IDD significantly increases receiver complexity and latency. In order to reduce this loss, we propose COrrelation-Informed Logits (COIL), a soft-output format that combines per-bit soft information with pairwise coupling logits for correlated bits. We show how to incorporate these coupling logits into a conventional belief-propagation-based channel decoder, which enables correlation-aware decoding in a one-shot receiver without IDD. We evaluate COIL in a MIMO-BICM system with a conventional low-density parity-check code. For a 4x4 MIMO orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system, a one-shot linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receiver with COIL outperforms a conventional one-shot unbiased LMMSE receiver by 1.3dB and operates within 0.8dB of four-iteration IDD, while requiring only a single pass through the data detector.
Generation of semigroups for vector-valued pseudodifferential operators on the torus with space-dependent symbols
Bienvenido Barraza Martínez; Robert Denk; Jairo Hernández Monzón; Max Nendel

We consider toroidal pseudodifferential operators with spatially dependent, operator-valued symbols of positive order and finite regularity. For an arbitrary complex Banach space $E$, we prove that the negative of the closure of a parabolic operator on $C^\infty(\mathbb T^n,E)$ generates an analytic semigroup on $W_p^k(\mathbb T^n,E)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $k\in\mathbb N_0$, provided the symbol has sufficiently many spatial derivatives and discrete differences. The proof combines uniform estimates for parameter-dependent kernels with right and left parametrices. It does not require the UMD property of $E$. Real interpolation gives corresponding resolvent estimates on $B_{pq}^s(\mathbb T^n,E)$ for $0<s<k$ and $1\le q\le\infty$. The induced semigroups are strongly continuous for $q<\infty$ and on the little Besov spaces when $q=\infty$.

Heffter arrays are combinatorial structures that can be used to construct orthogonal cyclic cycle decompositions of complete graphs. A square Heffter array $H(n;k)$ is a partially filled $n \times n$ array with $k$ filled cells in each row and column. Its entries are distinct and nonzero, form a half-set of the group $\mathbb{Z}_{2nk+1}$, and sum to zero in every row and column. If the natural orderings of the rows and columns of an array are simple, the array is called globally simple. The globally simple property guarantees the orthogonal cycle decompositions constructed from the Heffter array consist of simple cycles. While existence results are known for most congruence classes of the parameters $n$ and $k$ modulo 4 for square globally simple Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$, the existence for $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$ has remained largely open. In this paper, we present a construction for globally simple integer Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$ covering all admissible values of $n$ when $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$. This settles the existence question across all congruence classes.
A criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval for a certain class of multigeometric series
Mykola Pratsiovytyi; Yaroslav Vynnyshyn; Oleh Vynnyshyn

The paper studies the topological structure of the set of subsums (incomplete sums) of multigeometric series of the form $\frac{k_1}{s} + \frac{k_2}{s} + \ldots + \frac{k_m}{s} + \frac{k_1}{s^2} + \frac{k_2}{s^2} + \ldots+ \frac{k_m}{s^2} + \frac{k_1}{s^3} + \frac{k_2}{s^3} +\ldots$, where $k_1, \ldots, k_m, s \in \mathbb{N}$. In terms of graph theory, necessary and sufficient conditions are established for the set of subsums of a given series not to be a finite union of closed intervals, as well as necessary and sufficient conditions for this set to contain an interval. As a consequence of these statements, a criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval is obtained. An example of applying the criterion to a series whose Cantorval property was previously unknown is given. A more general object of study of topological properties is the set of numbers whose representations in a numerical system with a natural base and a redundant alphabet are subject to restrictions on the use of digits. It is for this object that the above statements are proved.
Branch points and natural boundaries of Poincaré functions and of solutions of nonlinear functional differential equations

In this paper, we study the singularity structure of the analytic continuation of solutions to the equation $g(λw)=R(g(w))$, where $|λ|<1$ and $R$ is a rational function. We show that the analytic solution \(g\) near zero is branched, and that its analytic continuation yields an infinite-sheeted Riemann surface with various patterns of branch points. In one specific pattern, some branch points are delayed: they appear only when the analytic continuation reaches a particular Riemann sheet. Using this functional-equation framework, we extend the study to first-order nonlinear functional differential equations. We show that the continuation of certain special solutions near an attracting fixed point yields either single-valued or multivalued functions, with the unit circle as a natural boundary on every sheet.
On operators with many spectral components

For a complex Banach algebra $\mathscr A$ with unit and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ be the set of all elements whose spectrum has at least $n$ connected components, and let $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\sup\{n;\;\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)\neq\varnothing\}$ be the spectral depth of $\mathscr A$. We characterize nonemptiness of $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ in terms of orthogonal idempotents, compute $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ for finite-dimensional algebras, and show that every class $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ is open. For operators on an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space $X$ these classes are dense in $\mathscr B(X)$, which implies that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr B(X))$ is a dense $G_δ$-subset of $\mathscr B(X)$. By contrast, we exhibit a commutative Banach algebra whose spectral classes are all nonempty and none of which is dense. For self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space, we obtain sharper perturbation results, with positive semi-definite perturbations of prescribed rank producing spectra with exactly $n$ components. We show that a quasinilpotent weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $X$ admits a nilpotent rank-one operator $F$ such that the spectrum of $S_w+αF$ has infinitely many components for every nonzero $α$.
Geodesic connectedness of globally hyperbolic spacetimes with a causal Killing vector field

We characterize the existence of a geodesic joining two prescribed points of a globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M,g)$ admitting a complete causal Killing vector field $K$ and a complete smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface $S$. We prove that two points $p,q\in M$ are joined by a geodesic if and only if there exists an $H^1$ curve $γ$ from $p$ to $q$ such that $g(\dotγ,K)$ is constant almost everywhere. The statement is intrinsic and allows $K$ to be timelike at some points and lightlike at others. A global splitting induced by the flow of $K$ is used in the proof, but no global bounds on the metric coefficients are imposed. The proof relies on stationary perturbations of $(M,g)$, whose relevant compactness properties follow from global hyperbolicity of $g$, and on uniform estimates based on an integral admissibility condition and a Glaeser-type inequality. Two examples illustrate geodesic connectedness and the obstruction detected by the characterization.
Minimum cumulative power divergence estimation with applications to copulas

Parametric inference based on distribution functions is useful when a model is naturally specified through its cumulative distribution function or when a tractable density is unavailable. We study minimum cumulative power divergence estimation, obtained by comparing a parametric distribution function with its empirical counterpart. For a fixed positive tuning parameter and a fixed finite integration measure, we establish the existence of a consistent sequence of local solutions to the estimating equations and derive its asymptotic normality. The resulting covariance has a sandwich form whose components involve derivatives of the distribution function and the covariance kernel of the multivariate empirical process. We specialize the construction to copulas using Lebesgue measure on the unit cube, and distinguish estimation with known margins from estimation based on ranks. In the latter case, the covariance incorporates the effect of estimating the marginal distributions. The relationship with the copula divergences of Eguchi and Kato is made explicit: the power loss is closely related, whereas the integration measure determines a different estimation criterion. A simulation design for Gumbel, Clayton, and Frank copulas examines the estimation of Kendall's tau under correct specification, family misspecification, and contamination by independence. The simulations show competitive clean-data accuracy but no general robustness advantage over the empirical-copula-weighted alternatives under independence contamination.
Pascal Fong; Matilde Maccan; Ludvig Modin

We give a criterion for the contracted product $E \times^G X$ to have a singular Picard scheme, where $E$ is an elliptic curve, $G \subset E$ is a finite subgroup scheme, and $X$ is a projective $G$-normal curve, in the sense of Brion. We show that every smooth projective surface with a singular Picard scheme and a positive-dimensional automorphism group scheme arises in this way. We also illustrate the criterion by constructing two new families of surfaces with singular Picard schemes, arising from $G$-normal curves $X$ for $G = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $G = \boldsymbolα_p$, respectively. As a special case of $G = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, we recover Igusa's classical example. Finally, we compute all infinitesimal group schemes which appear as $\operatorname{Pic}^0_S/(\operatorname{Pic}^0_S)_{\mathrm{red}}$ for all (quasi)-bielliptic surfaces $S$. This completes the description of the singular Picard schemes of smooth projective surfaces of Kodaira dimension zero.
Hilton's Conjecture on Uncomplemented Incomparable Families
Yuejian Peng; Zilong Yan; Cheng Zhao

A family ${\mathcal A}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is \emph{uncomplemented} if it contains no set together with its complement. Families ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t$ are \emph{strongly incomparable} if every set in one family is incomparable with every set in another family. In 1976, Hilton conjectured that if ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ are uncomplemented and strongly incomparable, then $$\sum_{i=1}^t |{\mathcal A}_i|\le 2^{n-1}.$$ We confirm this conjecture by a matrix rank argument that encodes incomparability and uncomplementedness in the same matrix, which is quite different from the earlier methods on this problem. We also study weak incomparability, in which the same set may occur in different families. Goldwasser, Hilton and Zheng conjectured an upper bound in this setting and claimed that their conjecture is equivalent to Hilton's conjecture. We give counterexamples to their conjecture for every $t\ge3$ and identify the error in the claimed equivalence. We then propose a replacement conjecture and confirm it when $t$ is large. The upper bound $2^{n-1}$ in Hilton's conjecture can be attained if some families are allowed to by empty. It is natural to consider the maximum size of $\sum_{i=1}^t |{\mathcal A}_i|$ for uncomplemented and strongly incomparable families ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ when all families are required to be non-empty. Denote this maximum number by $M(n,t)$. We show that \[ 2^{n-1}-1\le M(n,t)\le 2^{n-1} \] for $n\ge3$ and $3\le t\le n$.
Negative normal degree and holomorphic sectional curvature pinching

We obtain an upper bound for the local holomorphic sectional curvature pinching of a Kähler manifold containing a smooth rational curve of negative total normal degree. As an application, we prove that a compact Kähler surface with positive holomorphic sectional curvature and local pinching constant at least $1/9$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$, $\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$, or the first Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_1$. For pinching strictly greater than $1/9$, only the first two possibilities occur, confirming a conjecture of Yang and Zheng. We also determine the optimal local pinching constants on $\mathbb F_1$ and $\mathbb F_2$.
Amortized Transport-Map Likelihoods for Hierarchical Inverse Problems with Application to Wetting

Hierarchical Bayesian models pool measurements, but with the forward model in the likelihood every posterior evaluation costs one forward solve per cell. To reduce this cost, we introduce a simulation-based inference framework in which a triangular transport-map likelihood, trained once per design, serves every cell. We apply it to infer wetting properties from photographs of a stable hole in a thin liquid film. The hole's radius depends, through the nonlinear Young-Laplace equation, on the contact angle and capillary length. One photograph gives rank-one information about them, so we pool many in a hierarchical model whose cells, each a substrate at one volume setting, share the apparatus geometry and the noise scale. A design fixes the number of substrates, the volume settings and the photographs per cell. The map's posteriors agree with direct sampling of the forward model in the wetting properties at a synthetic validation design, and less closely at a larger synthetic scaling design. At the validation design, simulation-based calibration detects no departure for any parameter. There, the map needs several hundred times fewer forward-model evaluations than direct sampling with a gradient-free ensemble sampler for a single posterior, and about five orders of magnitude fewer over a calibration study of 200 posteriors. On real photographs its posterior agrees with direct sampling and is consistent with the measured radii. Trained offline, the amortized map turns new photographs into a posterior with no forward solve. It is thus a major step toward measuring wetting properties in situ without disturbing the liquid.
The multiplicity bound for near-group fusion categories of type $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z+k$

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a near-group fusion category of type $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z+k$. We show $k\in\{0,3,4\}$, which then gives a complete characterization of near-group fusion categories determined by $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$.
Involution-Preserving schemes through constrained mesh motion: a novel Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian framework
Sacha Cardonna; Elena Bernardelli; Walter Boscheri

We introduce a novel structure-preserving finite volume method that exploits mesh motion to enforce differential involutions arising in hyperbolic systems of conservation laws. The key idea is to leverage the geometric degrees of freedom of an Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) framework to construct a constrained mesh motion that is intrinsically compatible with the involution constraints embedded in the governing equations. The method is developed within a cell-centered formulation on moving quadrilateral meshes, where discrete divergence and curl operators are constructed from vertex-based differential operators. Particular care is devoted to the consistent evolution of the mesh geometry and the satisfaction of the Geometric Conservation Law (GCL). The proposed framework is applied to two representative hyperbolic systems featuring distinct involution constraints: the ideal magnetohydrodynamics equations, endowed with the divergence-free condition on the magnetic field, and the hyperbolic Euler-Heat equations, subject to a curl-free constraint on the thermal impulse. Second-order accuracy in time is achieved through a Runge-Kutta discretization, with the geometric constraints consistently enforced at each stage. A comprehensive set of classical benchmark problems is presented to assess the accuracy and effectiveness of the method. The numerical results demonstrate that appropriately constrained mesh motion provides an effective mechanism for preserving differential involutions, establishing a novel connection between mesh geometry and the structure-preserving discretization of hyperbolic systems.
On Relative Smoothness in Dually Flat Geometry

We study the geometric meaning of relative smoothness on dually flat manifolds and its implications for the convergence analysis of mirror descent. Our main result yields one-sided counterparts of the classical Levi--Civita characterizations of Lipschitz Riemannian gradients, each equivalent to relative smoothness. We further investigate the stationarity of mirror descent iterates for possibly nonconvex objectives and show that relative smoothness alone does not guarantee convergence of the Riemannian gradient norm to zero. We identify a one-sided condition on the cubic tensor that ensures such convergence and yields an $O(1/N)$ stationarity bound. Examples based on the negative entropy potential illustrate the role of metric variation.
Whitney-Type Real-Analytic Approximation on Banach Spaces I: The $C^0$ and $C^1$ Cases

The classical Whitney theorem on real-analytic approximation is a fundamental result in finite-dimensional analysis and geometry. Extending this theory to general infinite-dimensional Banach spaces involves longstanding open problems. This paper is the first part of our study of Whitney-type real-analytic approximation on Banach spaces, focusing on the $C^0$ and $C^1$ cases. We prove that a real Banach space admits a separating polynomial if and only if it admits a polynomial topological embedding into a real Hilbert space. We also introduce classes of mappings that locally factor through polynomial maps into finite-dimensional spaces and develop methods of real-analytic approximation for these classes. Using these tools, we establish fine $C^0$ and $C^1$ real-analytic approximation theorems for broad classes of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones. As applications, we resolve several open problems, including those concerning Whitney-type extensions with real analyticity off closed sets, real-analytic approximation preserving Lipschitz constants, and the real-analytic equivalence of diffeomorphic open subsets of Hilbert spaces.
From Frobenius seeds to self-orthogonal modules over symmetric algebras

We construct finite-dimensional symmetric algebras admitting nonprojective self-orthogonal modules from Frobenius algebras equipped with a module satisfying explicit stable and homological conditions. The resulting modules have complexity three, and their stable endomorphism algebras are isomorphic to the algebra of dual numbers over the ground field. The construction combines a variable input with a fixed auxiliary factor carrying the required twisting, and preserves the input through specified quotient and corner constructions. The proof combines derived induction, an obstruction to perfect factorization, and a cone construction over a Gorenstein triangular matrix algebra. For a symmetric algebra and a self-orthogonal generator, we describe the derived category of the opposite endomorphism algebra through a recollement with a two-term $2$-symmetric dg algebra. For our counterexamples, it is formal and quasi-isomorphic to an explicit four-dimensional dg algebra. Applications to cyclic coverings of a quantum exterior algebra yield connected examples with explicitly determined numbers of simple modules. The construction works over every field containing an element of infinite multiplicative order.
Functions with finite energy on the Sierpinski gasket

This paper develops a systematic framework for constructing finite-energy functions on the Sierpiński gasket using Lipschitz maps and various classes of contractions. Several properties of the constructed functions are investigated, including the min--max property and bounds for their energy. Several examples of finite-energy functions, along with their graphical representations, are provided to illustrate the functions constructed using the proposed framework. It is further shown that finite energy does not necessarily imply membership in the domain of the Laplacian. The framework is then applied to a class of fractal interpolation functions on the Sierpiński gasket, for which necessary and sufficient conditions for finite energy are established under suitable contractivity assumptions.

We resolve Ge's local scalar curvature rigidity conjecture for spherical isoparametric tubes. The conjecture fails throughout its stated radius range for families with at least two distinct principal curvatures, via arbitrarily small smooth deformations supported in any regular annulus. Geodesic balls of radius less than $\fracπ{2}$ are locally rigid under $C^2$ smallness. We also prescribe sufficiently small smooth nonradial scalar-curvature increments with fixed compact interior support, under antipodal symmetry for families with 2, 4, or 6 distinct principal curvatures and without symmetry for families with 3 distinct principal curvatures.

Convergence of finite element exterior calculus for the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on closed Riemannian manifolds

We prove that the finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) approximation to the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on any closed oriented Riemannian manifold converges. Its approximate solutions, together with their exterior derivatives, converge to the continuum solutions for every source, and at the rate of the mesh size when the source and its codifferential are square integrable. We use Licht's estimate for the FEEC approximation of forms with one square-integrable derivative by finite element forms. We combine this with a new abstract error bound for approximations of Hilbert complexes. This bound uses a version of Di Pietro and Droniou's third Strang lemma. To apply these estimates, we show that every closed manifold admits a family of arbitrarily fine triangulations whose shapes stay uniformly under control.
Same Physics, Different Gradients: A State-of-the-Art Report on Differentiable Physics Simulation

Lei Shu; Zizhou Huang; Yunuo Chen; Yifei Li; Tao Du; Minchen Li; Tuur Stuyck; Miles Macklin; Kui Wu; Bo Zhu; Yin Yang; Ming C. Lin; Alberta Longhini; Rika Antonova; Leonidas Guibas; Gordon Wetzstein; Jeannette Bohg; Chenfanfu Jiang

Differentiable simulation propagates derivatives through a physics simulator, turning animation, system identification, control, and computational design into gradient-based optimization. Engines differ in the physics they model and, less visibly, in which mathematical object they differentiate. We separate two questions the literature conflates. The referent is which object the returned derivative belongs to: the finite computation that executed, the converged equation it approximates, or the continuous dynamics. The realization describes the organization of the backward pass: automatically generated differentiation, an equation-level adjoint solve, or a custom adjoint. The referent defines the target against which exactness is assessed; the implementation determines how accurately that target is approximated. Cost depends on the realization together with how the states needed by the backward pass are retained or recovered. Crossing the axes places every method and engine we classify in a cell, separates claims the literature merges, and shows that the apparent trade-off between exactness and memory follows from how methods have been built rather than from a constraint. A second, orthogonal taxonomy covers contact, where the map is non-smooth. We then ask whether a correct gradient helps. Four mechanisms by which useful gradients are lost are cataloged and measured on one testbed, where the advantage of the exact derivative over the equation-level adjoint depends on where the fitting target comes from as much as on the solver budget, and we review the evidence that zeroth-order methods can outperform simulator gradients in the regimes where those mechanisms act. The balance between feature learning and collapse in dynamical systems-based generative models

Over the past decade, a growing body of work has established that implicit biases in learning dynamics fundamentally shape the solutions found by neural networks, governing their learned features and generalisation performance. Together these findings point to a trade-off between feature learning and collapse, suggesting an operator view as a step towards a unified framework for understanding the learning dynamics of dynamical systems-based generative models.
The strong cylinder conjecture over prime fields

Let $p$ be prime and let $S\subseteq\mathbb F_p^3$ have $p^2$ points, with every affine plane meeting $S$ in a multiple of $p$ points. We give a self-contained argument that $S$ is a union of $p$ parallel lines.

Let $χ$ be a quadratic Dirichlet character and let $Λ(χ, s)$ be its associated completed $L$-function. The super-positivity property, introduced by Yun--Zhang (2017), asserts that $Λ^{(m)} \left( \frac{1}{2}, χ\right) \geq 0$ for all $m \geq 0$. We then investigate a refined form of the above property: we conjecture that the sequence $\{ Λ^{(2m)}\left(\frac{1}{2}, χ\right )\}_{ m \geq 0}$ is always eventually increasing and has at most one turning point, and we prove these assertions again when $θ(t, χ)>0$ for $t \geq 1$.

We study whether approximative controllability of the dissipative system is characterised by the same property of the larger system. The answer is negative in general, but positive for sufficiently well-structured systems - this is our main result. Building upon Krasnosel'ski\uı and co-workers, necessary conditions for the existence of a continuous stabilizing feedback have been pioneered by Brockett and Coron, providing so-called adversarial and homological conditions, respectively. We find that the design of events allows introducing new valid inequalities on the ride times. Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields

Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schrödinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.
Jacopo Borga; Valentin Féray; Peter Winkler

The compact space of permutons completes the set of permutations of all sizes under a natural topology; each permuton is not only a limit of permutations but also a generator of random permutations. Since their (relatively recent) discovery as a tool for understanding the behavior of large (possibly random) permutations, permutons have proved remarkably fruitful, with dozens of fascinating connections to combinatorics and probability. We review the fundamentals of permutons, sometimes providing new, shorter proofs, and give an account of some of their myriad applications. The survey concludes with a long list of open problems. An extensive -- but not comprehensive -- bibliography is appended.

After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities. In the final part of the paper, using different methods, we prove that every Anosov surface group representation into $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ is either Hitchin or belongs to the Barbot component. As a by-product, we obtain that some of the representations associated with the branched structures constructed above are not Anosov.
Topology, geometry and fabrication of volumetric plain weaves

While such woven fabrics are usually confined to a 2D surface, here we propose a practical approach to fabricate volumetric plain weaves, entanglements featuring three mutually orthogonal families of yarns threaded through a cubic lattice. We develop an analytic framework that converts the crossing pattern topology into continuous yarn centreline geometries, which we then leverage to fabricate volumetric weave specimens. Each crossing is encoded by a matrix that defines the offsets of the three yarns at a vertex. These are formulated to preserve the plain weave topology in every plane, where each pair of yarn families interlaces as in a planar plain weave. The framework provides a direct basis for generating weave geometries for simulation and fabrication.

Controllability allocation scores (CASs) assign weights to virtual input channels without specifying how interventions should be implemented. This paper provides an operational interpretation through randomized finite-duration interventions with prescribed, possibly candidate-dependent waveforms. Selection probabilities are fixed before a mean-output target is specified, while waveform amplitudes are optimized after the target is revealed. We derive the unique minimum expected-energy amplitude policy and formulate volumetric and weighted average-energy allocation criteria. We also establish a finite-trial mean-output error bound and show that waveform-based weighted AE-CAS minimizes an upper bound on the target-averaged mean-square error. We establish uniform convergence of normalized waveform-response Gramians and show that accumulation points of optimal allocations solve the limiting problem. With uniform timing, equal positive waveform efficiencies recover the original CAS in the short-duration limit, whereas unequal efficiencies yield waveform-weighted limits. Under the former conditions, the limiting error bound is proportional to the original weighted AE-CAS objective. For common waveforms, we further establish an exact finite-duration correspondence with the original full-state V-CAS under uniform timing.
A Computational Brainsphere Model for the Simulation of Alzheimer's Disease
Angela Kunoth; Anna Weller; Tolunay Yilmaz

Nowadays, there are different medical imaging techniques to collect data about the progression of Alzhei\-mer's disease in a patient's brain. These data describe different phenomena which are still not understood from a biological point of view. How can these data sets be combined in a mathematical model to simulate the evolution of such a neurodegenerative disease in a computer? In this snapshot, we present one possible approach to address this task with the help of graph theory and partial differential equations.
Good colorings of doubled triangles and a conjecture of Schwartz
Lakshitha Fernando; Eranda Dhananjaya; Rajitha Ranasinghe; Dinusha Priyadarshani

A good coloring of a sphere triangulation is a black-and-white coloring of its faces such that, at every vertex, the numbers of black and white faces differ by a multiple of~$3$. Good colorings correspond to proper vertex $4$-colorings. For a good coloring with fold count $\mathrm{f}$ (the number of black-white edges) on a triangulation with $F$ faces, R.~E.~Schwartz introduced the Eisenstein isoperimetric ratio $η=\mathrm{f}^2/F$. For triangulations with degree sequence $6,\dots,6,2,2,2$, he proved that $η\ge3$ and conjectured that every such triangulation has a good coloring with $η$ below a universal constant. These triangulations are indexed by the nonzero Eisenstein integers~$β$. We prove that every good coloring of $\T(n)$ has at least $3n$ folds, so $η\ge9/2$, and that this bound is attained for every~$n$. We also prove that subdividing a good coloring of $\T(β)$ gives a good coloring of $\T(nβ)$ with the same value of $η$. Consequently, Schwartz's conjecture holds in general if and only if it holds for primitive Eisenstein integers.

Let $p$ be prime. We prove that a noncollinear set of $2m+1\le p$ points in $\AG(2,p)$ determines exactly $m+2$ directions if and only if, up to an affine transformation, it consists of the origin and a coset of a multiplicative subgroup of order $m$ on each coordinate axis. Thus equality is possible precisely when $m\mid p-1$. This extends the Lovász--Schrijver classification for $2m+1=p$.

Moritz Poguntke; Eda Oktay; Yuanzhe Xi; Erin Carson; Martin Stoll

Training Gaussian processes (GPs) at large scale is computationally challenging because evaluating the log-marginal likelihood and its gradients involves large, dense kernel matrices. We develop a scalable low-rank GP training approach that combines AnchorNet landmark selection with a fully independent training conditional (FITC) correction. The resulting objective and its analytic gradients can be evaluated using low-rank factors, diagonal quantities, and small dense matrices, without forming the full kernel matrix or its derivatives. The complete training procedure is implemented in single precision and evaluated on nine large-scale regression datasets. Across these problems, the method reaches the reference predictive accuracy while substantially reducing training time, although the required approximation rank varies across datasets. We also study the numerical behavior of the full-kernel predictive solve and show that single precision can become limiting for ill-conditioned problems. Finally, we investigate further reducing selected matrix operations to fp16 or TF32. These lower-precision variants provide only modest additional speedups and can become unreliable when the reduced system is poorly conditioned.

We construct blow up solutions to the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$. More precisely, we construct the solutions $(ψ,n)$ defined for $t\in[0,T)$, blowing up at $t=T$ and taking the form \begin{align} ψ(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{T-t}P\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)e^{i(T-t)^{-1/3}}, n(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{3(T-t)^{4/3}}N\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right) \end{align} in the region $|x|\ll 1$. The fixed point argument in this procedure actually yields that these solutions are the same for $t$ sufficiently close to $T$, which combined with the persistence of high regularity gives the existence of smooth asymptotically self-similar blow up solutions.

Assuming the existence of a measurable cardinal, we produce generic extensions $V_1\subsetneq V_2$ of the universe with the same cardinals, cofinalities, and bounded subsets of $\aleph_ω$, such that $V_2$ is generated over $V_1$ by a cofinal $ω$-sequence in $\aleph_ω$, and $V_2$ is a minimal generic extension over $V_1$, i.e., every set of ordinals in $V_2\setminus V_1$ generates $V_2$ over $V_1$.

Bauer, Broersma and Veldman [Discrete Appl. Math. 99 (2000) 317--321] constructed $(9/4-\varepsilon)$-tough graphs without a Hamiltonian path for arbitrarily small $\varepsilon>0$. For the weaker requirement of a $2$-factor, Enomoto et al. [J. Graph Theory 9 (1985) 87--95] proved that every $2$-tough graph of order at least three has a $2$-factor and that the toughness threshold $2$ is best possible.
