McKean--Vlasov Diffusions from Liouville Spectral Green Response

For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion with $0<γ<2$, the Gaussian response of a finite vector of logarithmic eigenvalues determines a conditional Green energy. We weight this energy by the current spectral density in the fixed reference space. The resulting self-consistent evolution is a porous-medium equation for the canonical spectral form. We construct its positive probability flow, prove an energy identity, and pass from the regularized response forms to the Green limit. The energy identity yields strong convergence of the Gaussian gradients and of the conditional response drifts. A superposition argument then realizes the flow as a McKean--Vlasov weak diffusion.
An asymptotic preserving scheme for kinetic equations describing bacterial traveling pulses
Canan Akkoyunlu; Jose A. Carrillo; Gissell Estrada-Rodriguez; Xinran Ruan

We consider a kinetic model for bacterial chemotaxis that describes the propagation of traveling pulses driven by a nutrient and a self-produced chemoattractant. In the diffusive regime, the model converges to a macroscopic drift-diffusion system with bounded chemotactic fluxes. We construct a fully discrete asymptotic preserving (AP) finite difference scheme based on a micro-macro decomposition of the kinetic equation. The method is stable uniformly with respect to the scaling parameter and, as this parameter tends to zero, reduces to a consistent discretization of the limiting macroscopic equations. We prove positivity and mass conservation for the limiting scheme, and use a positivity-preserving correction for the kinetic solver. Numerical simulations reproduce the experimentally observed traveling pulses at both the kinetic and the macroscopic level, validate the theoretical traveling wave speed, and illustrate the convergence of the kinetic model to its macroscopic limit.

We give a general proof of the Rényi QNEC formulated using the Araki-Masuda weighted $L_p$ norms for all $p > 2$. This generalizes the algebraic proof of the QNEC applicable at $p=2$. Our approach utilizes a weighted version of a conditional $L_p$ norm which extrapolates the quantum expansion/ant-quantity. We elucidate some properties of the corresponding weighted conditional entropy both for half-sided modular inclusions and for general von Neumann subalgebras with a common cyclic and separating vector. The $p=2$ limit computes a conditional dynamical entropy originally defined in the context of black hole dynamics.
An optimal quantum strategy for the $2$-hat game
Georgios Baziotis; Sang-Jun Park; Sang-Gyun Youn

We study the two-player hat game as a two-input, three-output non-local game. We calculate the quantum commuting value and show that it coincides with the quantum one. In particular, we show that \[ω_{\rm q}(H_2)=ω_{\mathrm{qc}}(H_2)=\frac{15+\sqrt{33}}{36}\approx 0.576238.\] We achieve the optimal quantum advantage using a shared non-maximally entangled qutrit state. To establish optimality, we exploit the game's symmetry under the dihedral group $D_8$ and apply its representation theory to substantially reduce the complexity of the underlying matrix problem. We also determine the no-signalling value $ω_{\mathrm{ns}}(H_2)=2/3$.
Schmidt games for nonautonomous Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti maps

Liverani--Saussol--Vaienti (LSV) maps form a family of piecewise differentiable dynamical systems on $[0,1]$ depending on a parameter $a>0$. These maps are expanding away from a neutral fixed point. In this paper, we study Schmidt games for nonautonomous compositions of LSV maps with arbitrary parameter sequences in a compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$. For every countable set $P\subset[0,1]$, we prove that the set of points whose orbit closure is disjoint from $P$ is absolute winning on $[0,1]$. Our proof combines a potential game argument with an interval tree constructed from successive returns.
Becker's Conjecture on Compositions of Higher Degree Diagonal Forms
Hua-Lin Huang; Yiming Liu; Huajun Lu; Yilun Tang

Becker's conjecture asserts that a rational composition of sums of $d$-th powers of size $[r,s,n]$, with $d>2$, requires $n \ge rs$. We show that this formulation fails over every characteristic-zero field in odd degree, and in every degree over a suitable finite extension of $\Q$. Over formally real fields in even degree, however, we prove that every polynomial composition satisfies $n\ge rs$.
Bounds and Constructions for Optimal Wide-Gap Frequency Hopping Sequences

In a frequency-hopping (FH) system, to reduce interference to the received signal, each user's frequency hopping sequence (FHS) shall have wide-gap property. In this paper, we update the upper bounds on the minimum gaps of optimal uniform wide-gap frequency hopping sequences (WGFHS) with parameters $(v,s,λ;e)$ where $v=ks, k\ge 3, λ=k$ and $s\ge k(k-1)+1$ is odd. We completely prove the existence of such WGFHSs for $k\le 3$.
Group cosets with all elements automorphically equivalent

Let $G$ be a finite group and let $N$ be a proper non-trivial normal subgroup of $G$. We say that $(G,N)$ is an \textit{automorphically equivalent pair} if for every element $x\in G\setminus N$, the elements in the coset $xN$ belong to the same orbit under the action of ${\rm Aut}(G)$. This generalizes the concept of a Camina pair and constitutes a particular type of equal order pair. In this note, we determine all automorphically equivalent pairs in the class of finite abelian groups.
The solution of the Bochner--Krall problem

We solve the Bochner--Krall problem posed by Krall in 1938, extending the classification beyond regular orthogonal sequences. We classify monic polynomial sequences for which multiplying each polynomial by the variable gives a linear combination of that polynomial and the polynomials of the immediately preceding and following degrees, and whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients. Orthogonality is not assumed. The general formulation allows sequences to start at any fixed degree. In every degree beyond a fixed threshold, each sequence agrees, up to an invertible affine change of variable and monic normalization, with a Hermite, Laguerre, Jacobi or Bessel family, the monomial basis, or a finite rational Darboux transform of a Laguerre or Jacobi family. In the positive-definite case, we determine the representing measures, prove their uniqueness and specify the admissible endpoint masses. No boundedness assumption on the support or asymptotic conditions on the recurrence coefficients are imposed.
Fredholm weighted composition operators on the Lipschitz space of a tree

Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the Lipschitz space of a tree. In this paper, we establish a complete characterization of the weighted composition operator $W_{ψ,φ}$ to be Fredholm on $\mathcal{L}$. Applying our characterization, we describe the connection between the Fredholmness of $W_{ψ,φ}$ and that of the composition operator $C_φ$.
The Alt-Phillips Multiple Membrane Free Boundary Problem

Motivated by diffusion--reaction processes in porous catalysts, we study an Alt--Phillips model for ordered membranes with weighted gap interactions. The model connects adhesive harmonic junctions \cite{DSS24} and forced multiple membranes \cite{SY19} through the exponent $0<γ<1$. For arbitrary positive weights, we prove optimal $C^{1,β-1}$ regularity, where $β=2/(2-γ)$, and obtain nontrivial $β$-homogeneous blowup limits through Weiss almost monotonicity. Under strict discrete concavity of the weights, we establish a gluing principle, minimality of flat single-gap cones, and $C^{1,α}$ free boundary regularity at points admitting such blowups. We also classify all one-dimensional vertically critical cones. For three membranes, we identify cone families that are non-minimizing for small $γ$ and minimizing near $γ=1$.
Isoperimetric comparison for surfaces with nonnegative curvature and uniformly convex boundary

We establish a sharp relative isoperimetric comparison for compact surfaces with nonnegative Gaussian curvature and smooth nonempty boundary whose geodesic curvature is at least 1. We prove that the normalized relative isoperimetric profile for such a surface is bounded below by that of the Euclidean unit disk, with equality holding at some area fraction in (0,1) if and only if the surface is isometric to the unit disk. The proof uses a differential comparison argument for the isoperimetric profile, based on a suitable non-constant normal variation of isoperimetric curves inspired by the model geometry.
The topology of end-periodic smoothing operators

We develop an algebra of smoothing operators adapted to the geometry of end-periodic manifolds. We extend the renormalized trace and trace defect formula of Mrowka-Ruberman-Saveliev to this algebra, and establish a Fredholm criterion and winding-number index formula for smoothing perturbations of the identity. Our main result computes the homotopy groups of the associated end-periodic smoothing group. This provides a foundation for future work on relative index theory for families of end-periodic differential operators.
Thermochemical Rossby waves in rapid rotation: from swallowtail geometry to nonlinear selection

When heat and solute both destabilise a rapidly rotating fluid, do their buoyancies add? Codensity models assume so, giving a straight onset diagonal; spherical shells show curved and kinked thresholds. We study the Busse--Simitev rotating annulus, whose normal modes obey an exact complex cubic dispersion relation. Combining the Bilharz criterion with the neutral-curve envelope yields, in the rapid-rotation limit, an explicit swallowtail wave front, in Arnold's sense, that bends the codensity diagonal into smooth and then kinked thresholds as the diffusivity ratio decreases. Its cusp edges lie inside the unstable domain and its exposed kink ends at the swallowtail singularity; these are singularities of wave-number selection, without coalescence of temporal eigenvalues, and the swallowtail diffusivity ratio has analytical small- and large-Prandtl-number limits. At a kink, broad, fast thermal and narrow, slow compositional Rossby waves become neutral together; hidden arcs mark the birth and merger of unstable wave-number bands. The same geometry enters nonlinear selection: mean-scalar feedback factors through neutral-arc normals and scalar responses, so the mean-profile coexistence margin vanishes with the kink angle as the waves merge. Complete cubic coefficients predict robust coexistence at a reference corner and a narrow bistable interval near merger. Exact finite-rotation corners and periodic-cell simulations confirm the coexisting waves and their invasion thresholds.
Accelerated Reinforcement Learning for Soft Robotics: Hours Instead of Years
Roshan S. Kaundinya; Hehui Zheng; Robert K. Katzschmann; George Haller

Reinforcement learning (RL) requires large amounts of interaction data or a reliable simulator, both hard to obtain for nonlinear soft robotic hardware. Recent work shows that a time-scale separation inherent to soft robot dynamics justifies their reduction to low-dimensional invariant manifolds, known as adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs). We demonstrate that an aSSM-reduced model, a simple polynomial ordinary differential equation learned purely from pre-collected data, can serve as an RL training environment. On a pneumatically actuated soft arm, we train a trajectory-tracking policy in 3 hours on a six-dimensional aSSM-reduced model and deploy it without fine-tuning, whereas reproducing this policy training extrapolates to 3 years of hardware interaction. Our policy tracks dynamic targets with 40% lower error than otherwise identical policies trained on a 4.8-million-parameter recurrent neural network (RNN) or a 1.7-million-parameter transformer, which take 13 and 100 hours to identify, against 5 minutes for our mathematically justified 6,924-parameter model.
Rapid Heat Removal from Chip Cores: Near-Junction Active Cooling of Power Transistors via Electron Entropy Transport and Spatial Decoupling

Chip performance is limited by a shared bottleneck: the core produces heat faster than it can be moved out. We study the hardest case, RF power GaN HEMTs, whose hotspots exceed 5 kW/cm^2, and propose a horizontal near-junction active cooling topology built on electron entropy transport. Classical on-chip thermoelectric cooling faces a contest: Peltier absorption grows linearly with current, Joule heating with its square. In a vertical pillar, its own conduction resistance locks about half the Joule heat back toward the cold end, capping net cooling. From the Onsager framework we show the origin of this asymmetry: Peltier absorption localizes at the interface where the Seebeck coefficient jumps, whereas Joule heating fills the volume. The topology exploits this: a thermoelectric thin film lies flat on a diamond substrate beside the device drain (the electron exit), so bulk Joule heat leaves vertically into the substrate. A lateral fin model gives a closed form for the recirculation factor gamma: the vertical pillar yields gamma = 1, while the horizontal film yields gamma_max = sqrt(2) L_z/L_x, about 0.03 for L_z = 10 um, L_x = 500 um. The decoupling scales the net cooling ceiling and the critical runaway current by roughly 1/gamma. At equal resistance, the same film lifts maximum cooling from 13 mW to 500 mW, and the critical current from 0.65 A to 24 A. A time-constant and linear stability analysis with temperature-sensitive parameters defines the working window and safety margins for microsecond pulse cooling. The architecture leaves the device structure untouched; the principle, absorb at an interface and extract bulk heat vertically, applies to any chip with a hot core and offers a reproducible design path for near-junction thermal management.
Geometric Rigidity of Manifolds Admitting $m$-Modified Conformal Vector Fields

We establish certain integral inequalities for $m$-modified conformal vector fields on compact Riemannian manifolds and derive corresponding triviality and rigidity results. We further obtain integrability conditions for such vector fields and establish an extended Bourguignon-Ezin identity. We then prove that a compact Riemannian manifold admitting a non-trivial closed $m$-modified conformal vector field is isometric to a round sphere under either a constant scalar curvature and positive Ricci curvature assumption or a suitable bound on the Ricci curvature involving the first nonzero eigenvalue of the Laplace operator. As a consequence, we obtain an extension of a classical sphere characterization result of Yano and Nagano to the corresponding result for a non trivial $m$-modified conformal vector field assumed closed. Finally, we consider a complete Kähler manifold admitting a closed $m$-modified conformal vector field $V$, and show that $V$ is $m$-modified Killing and around a non-zero point of $V$ the manifold splits as the product of the complex Euclidean plane $\mathbb{C}$ and a complete Kähler manifold.
Binary Belief Propagation Fixed Points: Finiteness, Rigidity, and Topological Complexity

A fixed finite binary Ising model has only finitely many admissible complex belief propagation fixed points, even at degenerate parameter values. Families of positive fixed points obtained by varying external fields can nevertheless have nontrivial topology. We study this distinction through the external-field projection. For a fixed field, we prove finiteness by bounding the pole orders of the magnetizations on a hypothetical complex solution curve. The generic degree on the support graph then bounds the total local multiplicity. A graph has a single smooth real line as its full positive response for every choice of positive couplings, base field, and strictly positive sweep direction exactly when it contains no two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. Two such subgraphs suffice to create a circular component. For a plane obtained by varying two vertex fields, connected simple bipartite cubic graphs with one uniform coupling and a universal bound on the fixed fields realize every genus. The minimum number of vertices grows logarithmically in the genus, by a matching algebraic upper bound on Betti numbers. Finally, we certify the complete field discriminant of an eighteen-vertex product model and recover its torus component's genus from the counts of distinct roots on all field cells. The three main theorems, including the logarithmic size bounds, are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
Data-Driven Precision Control of Soft Helicoid Robots
Roshan S. Kaundinya; Mark Leone; Roberto Sabella; Hugo Buurmeijer; Luis Pabon; John Irvin Alora; Marco Pavone; George Haller

A purely data-driven method grounded in the theory of adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs) was recently used to model and control nonlinear soft robotic simulators. Here, we extend the methodology to learn aSSM-reduced models from data collected from hardware soft robotic platforms. Specifically, we learn a five dimensional (5D) aSSM-reduced nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) that accurately models the dynamics of a soft-helicoid trunk robot. We then use this ODE in a model predictive control scheme to demonstrate real-time precision control across various challenging closed-loop trajectory-tracking tasks, ranging from 2D to 3D trajectories with static and dynamic constraints. We find that our methodology enhances accuracy and precision across all control tasks compared to available data-driven linear methods and model-free reinforcement learning. While we focus here on a soft-helicoid trunk robot, our methodology relies solely on hardware data and is therefore applicable to a broader class of soft robotic systems.
Derived invariance of the space of holomorphic two-forms

Let $Φ:D^b(X)\to D^b(Y)$ be a derived equivalence between smooth projective complex varieties, and let $h=c_1(L)$ for an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$. For $z\in\mathbb{C}$, transporting the cup-product action and evaluating at $e^{zh}$ gives a homomorphism of graded algebras $Θ^\bullet_{F,z}:H^\bullet(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $F$ is the cohomological transform of $Φ$. We prove that $Θ^\bullet_{F,i}$ is an isomorphism in degrees one and two. In particular, $X$ and $Y$ have the same number of holomorphic two-forms. The proof in degree two uses the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations on $X$ and on $X\times X$. We also prove derived invariance of all Hodge numbers when $K_X$ is trivial and the conjugate of a holomorphic volume form belongs to the subalgebra of $H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$ generated in degrees one and two. In even dimension, the evaluation isomorphism allows us to compare the ranks of cup product by powers of symplectic two-forms on the Hochschild diagonals. These ranks determine the Hodge numbers individually.
Integer electron-count cuts in variational second-order reduced-density-matrix theory. II. A convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations for real-space pair-density representability

Variational second-order reduced-density-matrix calculations can dissociate molecules into fractionally charged fragments; Part I largely removed this failure with integer electron-count conditions on fixed partitions. Building on the realizability theory of point processes, we place these conditions in a convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations, defined by finite occupation linear programs (LPs) on spatial partitions, for real-space pair densities at fixed one-particle density. Every level contains all representable pair densities, the levels tighten under nested refinement, and their intersection characterizes pair densities admitting a symmetric $N$-particle probability-measure extension. In a fixed orbital basis the levels give monotonically increasing lower bounds to the full configuration-interaction energy, which they need not reach, even for the Coulomb repulsion. The spin-summed real-space cuts of Part I are its two-cell members. The LP optimum is also a measure: at fixed one-particle density it equals the $L^1$ distance of the coarse-grained candidate from representability and increases under refinement to that of the candidate, with a vanishing coarse-graining error; its primal law constructs a representable approximation, and its dual a violated valid inequality, used as a cut in molecular calculations. The count conditions are not implied by the usual positivity conditions: moment data that satisfy all three-particle positivity conditions, including $T_1$ and $T_2$, give through Gaussian orbitals a smooth pair density that violates an integer count. For atoms at fractional electron number, ensemble relaxations with the integer-count condition lie closer to the exact piecewise-linear energy than the zero-variance fixed-$N$ form.
Double exponential growth for the Euler equation on the whole plane

We consider the incompressible Euler equation on the whole plane $\R^2$, without boundary and without forcing, and we construct two smooth solutions whose vorticity gradient grows fast for all large times. The first solution has finite energy, integrable vorticity and initial data in every Sobolev space. Given any function $Γ(t)$ with $Γ(t)/t\to 0$, the logarithm of its vorticity gradient is not bounded by any multiple of $Γ(t)$, and, at every sufficiently large time $t$, it is larger than any multiple of $t/\log_*t$, where $\log_*$ is the iterated logarithm. The second solution has bounded vorticity, bounded vorticity derivatives on every finite time interval, and a velocity given by the absolutely convergent Biot--Savart integral which grows at most logarithmically in space. Its vorticity gradient grows double exponentially in time for all large times. Its initial vorticity is neither integrable nor square integrable, and its initial velocity and strain are unbounded. Both constructions place infinitely many localized amplification mechanisms far apart from each other in one initial datum. The first one is based on the hyperbolic stagnation point behind a smooth traveling dipole, controlled for long times by an energy--Casimir argument. The second one is based on the hyperbolic point of the Bahouri--Chemin cross on the torus, transported to the plane by spatial dilations and by the uniqueness theory of Serfati solutions.
Uniform Hyperbolicity of Automorphism Orbit Graphs in Rank Two

We study automorphism orbit graphs of oriented conjugacy classes in the free group of rank two, with every elementary Whitehead move assigned unit cost. Collapsing signed permutations of the basis turns each orbit component into a tree of edges and triangles. We obtain this description by combining the known rank-two conjugacy-class stabilizer structure with the Bass-Serre tree of the rank-two outer automorphism group. The simplified graph and all its vertex-induced subgraphs have optimal thin-triangle constant zero for tree components and 3/4 otherwise. Every whole orbit component of the original graph has thin-triangle constant at most 2, while every component of every vertex-induced subgraph has constant at most 5/2. Both bounds are sharp in the primitive orbit and apply to the full geometric realization, including edge-interior triangle corners. The hereditary upper estimate also follows from known chordality theory; the whole-component improvement uses the geometry of adjacent permutation fibres. These results complement earlier fixed-length and minimum-length orbit classifications.
Geometry-Dependent Dimension Jumps in Planar $C^r$ Splines at Degree $2r+1$
Yi Zheng; Jiansong Deng; Xinyu Wu

We study geometric dependence of the dimensions of planar spline spaces $S_{2r+1}^r$ through families with a single moving interior vertex and determine their dimensions throughout the admissible parameter domains. For $r=1$, we extend the Wu--Deng one-parameter classification to the interior of the central quadrilateral. The dimension increases by one at exactly two isolated points, one due to a local direction-count change and the other to a global compatibility defect. For $r=2$, subdividing one triangle of the Yuan--Stillman configuration gives a twelve-triangle family with fixed local direction counts; its dimension increases by one precisely on an open line segment. For every $r\ge3$, we construct a family with $2r+12$ triangles and fixed local direction counts, proving geometric dependence at degree $2r+1$. The moving vertex lies in an open triangle, and the dimension exceeds Schumaker's lower bound by one exactly on its symmetry axis. The lower collinear vertices may have arbitrary strictly ordered heights. The low-order proofs use exact cofactor elimination. For higher orders, weighted interpolation and block elimination bound the global defect by one, and explicit extension and obstruction arguments determine the exceptional set.
Second-level termination of the PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy for two qutrits
Wei Song; Xiao-Lan Zong; Ming Yang

We prove that for arbitrary two-qutrit quantum states, the semidefinite programming lower-bound hierarchy for the PPT entanglement cost terminates at the second level. Therefore, under operations preserving positive partial transpose, its zero-error asymptotic entanglement cost can be obtained by a semidefinite program involving only three Hermitian matrix variables. The key to the proof is to shorten the feasible dual chain by one level; to this end, we combine finite certificates verified by exact rational arithmetic with analytic estimates near the boundary of the parameter domain. This result shows that a unified terminating level exists for two-qutrit systems, whereas no unified terminating level exists for all dimensions.
A Markovian SuASR epidemic framework with stochastic external factors

Epidemic waves are often shaped by uncertain external drivers, such as environmental variability or behavioral and policy changes, that can randomly amplify or dampen transmission. Capturing this randomness requires models whose dynamics evolve under time-varying, stochastic influences. In this paper, we introduce a stochastic Susceptible-Asymptomatic-Symptomatic-Removed (SuASR) framework that embeds random external factors directly into the epidemic mechanism through an extended continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). The proposed framework is flexible enough to represent epidemic dynamics both with reinfection and with infection-induced immunity, depending on the epidemiological setting under study. Unlike standard Markovian epidemic models, our formulation explicitly tracks two concurrent infectious sources (asymptomatic and symptomatic), yielding coupled infection pathways and substantially richer transient behavior. A key contribution is analytical tractability, where we derive computable expressions for the joint distribution of asymptomatic and symptomatic infection-event counts and develop tools tailored to extreme-outbreak risk, including the distribution of the maximum infectious burden. These results enable probabilistic quantification of epidemic severity beyond mean trajectories, providing direct estimates of the likelihood of rare but consequential surges. We validate the model through extensive sensitivity analysis and an application to the H1N1 influenza epidemic, illustrating how stochastic external influences reshape outbreak profiles, total infections from both sources, and the probability of extreme epidemic scenarios
Uniform Resolvent Estimates for the Dunkl Laplacian
Xiaofen Gao; Manli Song; Junyong Zhang

Let \(\Lk=-\Dk\) denote the nonnegative Dunkl Laplacian associated with a finite reflection group and a nonnegative multiplicity function \(κ\), and let $ N=d+2\gk\geq 3 $ be the corresponding homogeneous dimension. We establish uniform \(L_κ^p(\mathbb{R}^d)\)-\(L_κ^q(\mathbb{R}^d)\) resolvent estimates for \(\Lk\) whenever \[ \frac{2}{N+1} \leq \frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{q} \leq \frac{2}{N}, \quad \frac{2N}{N+3}<p<\frac{2N}{N+1}, \quad \frac{2N}{N-1}<q<\frac{2N}{N-3}, \] where the last upper bound is interpreted as \(q<\infty\) when \(N=3\). Remarkably, this admissible range coincides with the corresponding range for the Euclidean Laplacian \(-Δ\) in dimension \(N\).
Eccentricity in mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthographs of C*-algebras

We determine the eccentricity of every vertex in the orthograph of mutual strong Birkhoff-James orthogonality for arbitrary finite-dimensional C*-algebras and for the algebra K(H) of compact operators on an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space. This gives a more detailed description of the orthograph introduced by Arambašić et al. (Banach J. Math. Anal. 14 (2020), 1751-1772). As an application, we characterize scalar multiples of unitary elements among invertible elements of finite-dimensional C*-algebras in terms of eccentricity alone. We also show that M_3(C) is the only finite-dimensional C*-algebra whose orthograph has a non-trivial connected component of radius 3.

We use tools from high dimensional probability to analyze random configurations of balls in the context of Fourier decoupling and we answer a question on the structure of superlevel sets in the setting of decoupling due to Guth.
Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of root of unity quantum cluster algebras

Many important families of algebras $R$ in the areas of quantum groups, quantum topology and noncommutative algebra are root of unity quantum algebras, equipped with Frobenius centers $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R) \subseteq Z(R)$ and quantum Frobenius maps ${\mathrm{Fr}} : R_{\mathrm{class}} \stackrel{\cong}{\longrightarrow} Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$. We explicitly classify the Frobenius automorphism groups ${\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R))$ and the ozone groups ${\mathrm{Oz}}(R):= {\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z(R))$, and prove that all endomorphisms of $R$ fixing its Frobenius center $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$ are automorphisms for all algebras $R$ that come from partial root of unity quantum cluster and upper quantum cluster algebras (which have been proved to encompass a vast majority of known quantum algebras). We prove three main theorems that give the above classification results from three different standpoints. As applications, we classify the Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of all quantum function algebras of simple algebraic groups $G$ not of type $F_4$ or $E_8$ and all quantum unipotent cells at roots of unity for arbitrary symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras.
Resolvent Ellipsoid for Minty Set Inclusions
Ashkan Soleymani; Gabriele Farina; Patrick Jaillet

We study Minty set inclusion on a compact convex set $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ with a set-valued operator $A : \mathcal{X} \rightrightarrows \mathbb{R}^d$. Under the Minty promise, the goal is to compute $x \in \mathcal{X}$ and $u \in A(x)$ such that $\sup_{y \in \mathcal{X}} \langle u, x - y \rangle \le \varepsilon$. Our approach is geometric and we work in the fixed-scale constrained-resolvent oracle model, where a query at anchor $a$ is assumed to return a resolvent point $x^+$ together with the Yosida vector $g_η(a) = (a - x^+)/η$. We prove that each oracle response yields a sharp dichotomy: either the returned point provides an $\varepsilon$-SVI certificate, or the Yosida vector defines a strict separating normal for the Minty set. Thus, a single black-box resolvent query supplies either a certified candidate solution or a valid geometric cut. Combining this separation principle with the ellipsoid method, we obtain RESOLVENT-ELLIPSOID, an algorithm that computes an $\varepsilon$-SVI in $\mathcal{O}\!\left(\operatorname{poly}(d, \log(1/\varepsilon))\right)$ black-box oracle calls to the fixed-scale constrained resolvent. For monotone inclusions, our algorithm gives, to our knowledge, the first $\mathcal{O}\!\left(\mathrm{poly}(d, \log(1/\varepsilon))\right)$ black-box guarantee in the fixed-scale resolvent model.
Rational knots, quivers, and tails of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials
Elijah Berry; Rongjiang Guo; Jonathan A. Higgins; Eduardo Perez; Henry Zaslow
We use the knots-quivers correspondence to prove that the colored HOMFLY-PT polynomial of a rational knot has a tail and give an explicit formula for calculating the tail in terms of the quiver.
Transformations of Hilbert Module Reference Frames

In this paper, we provide a functorial characterization of Hilbert module classical and quantum reference frames. Using the functorial characterization, we construct a category for equivariant couplings and Hilbert module reference frames. We prove the construction of the reference frame system from the equivariant coupling data yields a functor. We also deduce a ``unitary" groupoid as frame transformations for Hilbert module reference frames of a fixed Hilbert module dynamical system. We provide some examples of these frame transformations in the case of the indistinguishable classical two state switch and in the case of Hilbert spaces.
The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
Chris Bowman; Damian de la Fuente; Nicolas Libedinsky; David Plaza

In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.
Pointed Hopf Algebras from Pale Braidings in Characteristic 2
Dirceu Bagio; Laura Natalia Orozco García

We determine Nichols algebras associated with several families of pale braidings over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$. For the rank-$4$ families under consideration, we obtain presentations by generators and relations, explicit monomial bases and dimension formulas. We also study families of arbitrary rank consisting of a two-dimensional pale block and several points, including cases with both vanishing and nonvanishing interaction parameters. Realizations as Yetter--Drinfeld modules over suitable finite abelian groups yield finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebras by bosonization.
Universal and Reciprocating Domains in Classes of Continua and Beyond
Iztok Banič; Goran Erceg; Judy Kennedy; Chris Mouron; Van Nall

We introduce and study the notions of reciprocating domains in classes of topological spaces. A reciprocating domain is a member of a class that maps onto every member which maps onto it. We provide general characterizations, showing in particular that in upward directed classes reciprocating domains coincide with universal domains. We investigate these domains in several classes of compact metrizable spaces and continua. We also construct a chainable universal domain admitting a continuous monotone surjection onto a pseudoarc although every nondegenerate subcontinuum of the domain contains an arc. In particular, a chainable reciprocating domain need not contain a pseudoarc.
Projective symmetries and differential recursions for the large-$N$ Gross--Witten--Wadia and one-dimensional QCD matrix models

We compare the fixed-charge planar Gross--Witten--Wadia (GWW) model with source-free one-dimensional QCD at large $N$ and $N_f/N$ fixed. In both models the resolvent and one-cut condition give an algebraic equation for a derivative of the free energy: a quartic for GWW and a sextic for QCD. Finite-$N$ Toeplitz determinants independently check the selected QCD branch. Signed permutations of homogeneous parameter triples realize $S_4$; the resulting action on the algebraic branches and operator labels gives a common projective description of the two models. For QCD, the sextic yields a differential recurrence linking small-charge rows two apart. The same second-order PDE gives a finite-width column recursion that reconstructs the coefficient pyramid from its GWW boundary. A distinct boundary, obtained from the first resummed coefficient, is the Narayana triangle. A formally collapsed slice counts decorated bipartite plane trees and admits an exact symmetric product formula. The many-flavor scaling reduces the sextic to the quartic and retains transverse projective data: the QCD divided-difference triple coalesces at this boundary, whereas the limiting quartic satisfies the full standard GWW third-order system. We distinguish algebraic degree, mixed differential order, and fixed-parameter ordinary differential order throughout.
Optimal adaptive finite element methods in $W^{1,p}$

We prove linear convergence and algebraic rate optimality of an adaptive finite element method for the Dirichlet Poisson problem in W1p. We assume well-posedness of the continuous problem and discrete inf-sup stability over the refinement family. We verify both hypotheses when p is sufficiently close to 2, without requiring convexity of the domain. The Galerkin equations remain unchanged, while the residual estimator and Dörfler marking use the target exponent p. Linear convergence holds for every fixed marking fraction between zero and one. For sufficiently small marking fractions and marked sets of nearly minimal cardinality, the method attains the best algebraic rates for W1p approximation together with data oscillation. The main ingredient is a Banach-space extension of Feischl's relaxed quasi-orthogonality, proved under discrete inf-sup stability.
Nonasymptotic causal structure learning in generalized linear DAGs with continuous optimization
Chang Deng; Inbeom Lee; Bryon Aragam

We study the problem of learning directed acyclic graphs from observational data in nonlinear models and provide finite-sample, nonasymptotic statistical guarantees in these models. Although widely studied, statistical guarantees for gradient-based methods in nonlinear models are missing from the literature. Under a generalized linear model for each node, we analyze a global nonsmooth objective combining an exact acyclicity constraint with a quasi-minimax concave penalty, which can be optimized via standard gradient-based solvers. We establish finite-sample guarantees under this model, including the most widely used logistic and Poisson models. Experiments corroborate structure recovery accuracy and computational performance, including both standardized data and negative controls as baselines.
Collapsing flat manifolds with totally geodesic boundary

We study volume collapse of compact connected flat manifolds with nonempty totally geodesic boundary and uniformly bounded diameter. We prove subsequential Gromov--Hausdorff convergence to compact flat orbifolds, allowing reflector loci, and describe the limit using the canonical involutions of the doubles. We distinguish the cases in which the maximal distance to the boundary tends to zero or to a positive limit, and classify all possible limits in dimension three.
Local well-posedness for viscous heat-conducting fluids with discontinuous densities

In this paper, we consider the Navier-Stokes-Fourier system in space dimension $d\geq2$. We prove local well-posedness of solutions having density only in $L^p\cap L^\infty$, for suitable $p\in\,]1,+\infty[\,$, with no further regularity requirements. In particular, our result yields existence and uniqueness of solutions in the case of discontinuous densities presenting a jump across a smooth interface. The existence proof is based on the use of the Hoff effective viscous flux and on a combination of both maximal regularity and Chemin's striated regularity arguments. Uniqueness, under the assumption of slightly more regular initial velocity fields and temperatures, relies on a Lagrangian approach, supplemented with an original bootstrap argument which shows improved time integrability properties of the solution.

Given a full rank sink recurrent cluster $\mathcal{A}$ variety, we prove that its wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of coherent sheaves on a stacky elaboration of the dual Fock-Goncharov cluster $\mathcal{X}$ variety. In particular, braid varieties for a semisimple group are mirror to the braid varieties for the Langlands dual group. Another example: for compact surfaces with no interior marked points, a least one marked point on each boundary component, and at least two marked points in total, the Fock-Goncharov moduli for SL(2) and PGL(2) are homologically mirror. The results were obtained in communion with ChatGPT Astra.
Lieb-Robinson bound for one-dimensional continuum fermions
Marius Lemm; Hailun Lu; Harman Preet Singh

The central difficulty in quantum many-body physics is that the Hilbert space dimension grows exponentially with the total degrees of freedom. A key feature to circumvent this problem is locality, which manifests dynamically through an approximate causal structure in the form of a Lieb-Robinson bound (LRB). LRBs have been proved for quantum spin systems and certain lattice boson systems, but so far never for realistic continuum systems. We present the first LRB that applies to a standard system of one-dimensional continuum fermions. It applies to initial states with controlled moments of local particle number and energy and is thus thermodynamically stable. Our result breaks the main technical barrier that has existed for using the vast locality toolbox on continuum systems.
Adjoint Kernel Sensitivity of the Rough Heston Characteristic Exponent
Carlos Escudero; Francisco J. Luguera-Parúas; Miguel Sama

Multi-factor approximations of rough volatility kernels affect the characteristic exponents used in Fourier-based derivative valuation. We derive an adjoint representation for the first-order sensitivity of the rough Heston characteristic exponent with respect to its memory kernel, with model parameters and the input variance curve held fixed. The Volterra--Riccati functional $\mathcal L_T(K,z)$ admits a local real-analytic extension, jointly in the kernel perturbation and the transform parameter. The Fréchet derivative of this extension with respect to the kernel in $L^1$ is represented by integration against a continuous sensitivity kernel $B_K(u,z)$, obtained from a backward linear Volterra equation and independent of the perturbation direction. This representation resolves the leading-order contributions of kernel perturbations across memory lags. On the structural kernel class, which contains the fractional kernel and its multi-factor approximations and has empty interior in $L^1$, the extension yields Hadamard directional differentiability and a first-order expansion with a quadratic $L^1$-remainder for all sufficiently close structural kernels, uniformly on compact subsets of the strip of transform parameters. The same sensitivity kernel yields multi-factor weight and decay-rate derivatives. Numerical experiments at multi-factor reference kernels assess the finite-resolution implementation and illustrate how the lag distribution of positive perturbations with equal $L^1$ mass affects the first-order response.
A software infrastructure proposal for mathematical research with AI agents
Mario Vago Marzal; Enric Cosme Llópez

In 2026, AI agents began to produce mathematical results. They formalize complete theorems and settle open problems faster than a research group can review the results. The difficulty is shifting to organizing that output, deciding which results to trust and understanding them as a group. Current tools address particular problems or assist individual researchers, and none of them is designed as the shared working environment of a research group. We propose the design of a self-hosted environment in which a group of people and agents does its daily mathematical work. It consists of a small open core, which each group deploys with the resources it has and adapts through extensions. The core records who did what and gives every message and result a stable address. We also outline how the formal libraries of different groups, maintained mostly by agents, can form a network. We describe Stemma, an early prototype that implements part of the proposal, and illustrate it with a synthetic example.
Spectral Stability, Fatou Basin Contraction, and Machine-Checked Multipliers in Holomorphic Extensions of Generalized Syracuse Dynamics
Volkan Dağlı; Zerrin Dağlı; Dağhan Dağlı; Emrah Yurtseven; Murat Emre Özkaya

We embed the Syracuse operator $T(n) = n/2$ (even $n$), $T(n) = (3n+1)/2$ (odd $n$) and the Collatz map $C(n)$ into $\mathbb{C}$ via entire functions of exponential type $π$: $f(z) = \frac{1}{4}(1 + 4z - (1 + 2z)\cos(πz))$ and $F(z) = \frac{1}{4}(2 + 7z - (2 + 5z)\cos(πz))$. We prove five results: (1) every integer periodic cycle $C \subset \mathbb{N}^+$ of $T$ is a strictly attracting Fatou cycle of $f$ with multiplier $μ_f(C) = 3^{N_{\mathrm{odd}}}/2^N = \prod_{n \in C\text{ odd}} \frac{3n}{3n+1} \in (0,1)$, and $μ_f(O_{1,2}) = μ_F(O_{1,4,2}) = 3/4 < 1$; (2) on the Fatou basin $B(O_{1,2})$, $g = f^{\circ 2}$ conjugates to $Φ_j(g(z)) = \frac{3}{4}Φ_j(z)$ with Koenigs Taylor jets $c_2(1) = -\frac{13}{2}π^2$ and $d_2(2) = -\frac{9}{2}π^2$; (3) the Schwarzian derivative is strictly negative on $\mathbb{Z}$ ($S(f)(n) \le 3π^2 - \frac{3}{8}π^4 \approx -6.9196 < 0$), and a repelling Julia 2-cycle $O_{\mathrm{rep}} \subset J(f)$ ($μ\approx 1.2148 > 1$) isolates $B(O_{1,2})$; (4) on $(\mathbb{Z}_2, μ_{\mathrm{Haar}})$, the 2-adic Lyapunov exponent $λ_{\mathrm{Haar}} = \frac{1}{2}\ln(3/4) \approx -0.143841 < 0$ equals $\frac{1}{2}\ln|μ_f(O_{1,2})|$; and (5) we certify 20 theorems in Lean 4 (anc/CollatzAttractor.lean, 0 sorry). These results establish local Fatou invariants and 2-adic ergodic averages for $f(z)$, leaving open whether every $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}^+$ lies in $\bigcup_{k \ge 0} f^{-k}(B(O_{1,2}))$.
Stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam equation with distributed damping and interior time delay
Ben B. J. Siriki; N'Guessan F. Alla; Adama Coulibaly

In this paper, we investigate the effect of a fixed time delay on the internal stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam clamped at one end with distributed damping. Under appropriate assumptions on the feedback weights, we first establish that the problem is well-posed using semigroup theory. Furthermore, using the multiplier method combined with a suitable Lyapunov functional, we prove the exponential stability of the system.
Polar foliations on the Cayley plane
Miguel Domínguez-Vázquez; Ricardo A. E. Mendes; Marco Radeschi
We classify polar foliations on the Cayley projective plane, completing the classification of polar foliations on compact rank one symmetric spaces.
Exponential stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam via internal feedback under distributed time delay
Ben B. J. Siriki; Droh A. Behi; N'Guessan F. Alla; Adama Coulibaly

In this paper, we investigate the internal stabilization of a closed-loop system which consists of an Euler--Bernoulli beam subjected to a structural damping mechanism with a distributed delay into the domain. Under appropriate assumptions on the weights of the delay term and internal damping, we first prove the well-posedness of the system by a semigroup approach. Then, by constructing an appropriate Lyapunov functional and utilizing the multiplier method, we establish the exponential decay of the system energy.
The sharp bound on the distance between the centers of mass of a convex body and its boundary
Sergii Myroshnychenko; Dmitry Ryabogin; Kateryna Tatarko; Vladyslav Yaskin

We prove that the distance between the centers of mass $c(K)$ and $c(\partial K)$ of a convex body $K$ and its boundary $\partial K$, respectively, does not exceed $ D_n$ times the width of $K$ in the direction of the vector joining $c(\partial K)$ and $c(K)$. The constant $D_n$ is optimal and coincides with the sharp constant in the problem of bounding the distance between the orthogonal projection of the centroid of a convex body onto a hyperplane and the centroid of its orthogonal projection onto that hyperplane.
Predictive Neuromorphic Control of a Scanning Mirror System: An Event-Centric Framework
Changrui Liu; Robin Wroblowski; Anil Alan; Shengling Shi; Rodolphe Sepulchre; Bart De Schutter

Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.
Simple algebraic groups with good reduction, the genus problem, and unramified cohomology

We obtain a number of new results on the arithmetic of linear algebraic groups over higher-dimensional fields. In particular, we resolve some key open questions over 2-dimensional global fields, such as the finiteness of the genus of spinor groups of quadratic forms of dimension $\geq 10$. We also extend various finiteness results to new classes of fields, including function fields of $p$-adic surfaces. Our arguments rely in a crucial way on new finiteness results for unramified cohomology.
Geometric Endpoints, Global Trajectories, and Teichmüller Projection for the Möbius-Invariant Willmore Flow

We study endpoints and conformal projection of the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in the round three-sphere. Under uniform nonumbilicity or an integrable weighted condition, image-measure transport yields a unique finite-time integral-varifold limit. Reduced Hopf trajectories have unique anchored finite-time profile and marked conformal endpoints at arbitrary energy. Every smooth global reduced trajectory converges smoothly modulo reparametrization to an elastic profile, with quantitative rates and finite dissipation length. We compute the differential of the conformal-class projection along reduced trajectories and prove that its maximal rank persists at every finite time when it holds initially. Near the Clifford torus, Hopf tori with the same marked conformal type can have noncollinear projected velocities, ruling out a common autonomous Teichmüller equation even after positive time recalibrations.

We study product-one invariants of finite metacyclic groups, with particular attention to metacyclic $p$-groups. For semidirect products $C_n\rtimes C_m$ such that $\operatorname{ord}_n(\ell)=m$ and $\operatorname{ord}_q(\ell)=m$ for every prime divisor $q$ of $n$, we give a short proof of the known formula for the small Davenport constant and determine the exact value of the $η$-constant. When $n=p$ is prime, we use Vosper's theorem to obtain a growth result for products of non-trivial conjugacy classes contained in $C_p$, from which we derive a block-saturation principle for product-one sequences. For split metacyclic $p$-groups, we determine the small Davenport constant in terms of the order and the exponent, and obtain bounds for the $η$-constant and the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant. The Davenport bound is also extended to finite nilpotent split metacyclic groups. Our approach relies in part on a general quotient-lifting principle for the three invariants $\mathsf d$, $η$, and $\mathsf s$. For non-cyclic metacyclic $p$-groups, this principle applies through the Frattini quotient, which is isomorphic to $C_p^2$. We further establish upper and lower bounds for the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of arbitrary metacyclic $p$-groups, and show that both bounds are best possible within this class. The lifting method also provides a short proof of a known theorem of Han and Zhang for groups $C_m\ltimes C_n$ with $m\mid n$. Finally, we determine the Olson constant of the dihedral group $D_{2p}$, for every prime $p>3$, in terms of the Olson constant of $C_p$.
Sparse Fault Detection in Linear Systems: Equivalence of GLR Tests and $\ell_1$-regularized Least Squares

This paper studies the detection of an impulsive fault of unknown time and input channel in a linear system with unknown initial state and Gaussian measurement noise. First, we show that the generalized likelihood ratio test, after the initial state is eliminated by projection onto the parity space, is the zero-solution test of a weighted lasso with an unpenalized nuisance block; the regularization parameter is the test threshold, and for unknown noise variance the same holds for the square-root lasso. Second, we show that the null distribution depends on the system only through a Gram matrix, so that the threshold is computed exactly and offline, and we compare it with closed-form bounds. Third, we characterize the fraction of a fault that survives the projection: we give it in closed form through observability Gramians, we show that it converges to a geometrically decaying profile for strictly stable systems, and that, for systems with unit-modulus modes, it grows linearly with the fault time as a fraction of the record length. Numerical studies, including a two-input, two-output example, illustrate the results.
Karhunen-Loève Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups

The Karhunen-Loève transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix with computable bounds: for the $8\times8$ Markov block of image coding at pole $0.95$ it is below 1.2 percent. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra; a moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exact for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows; the dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means.
When Strategies Do Not Determine Play: Infinite Hat-Guessing Games on Subsets of the Reals

We study infinite hat-guessing games indexed by linearly ordered sets $S\subseteq\mathbb R$, where players guess sequentially using information determined by the order. While well-ordered standing sets admit the naive, recursive definition of play, we found a surprising example showing that this approach fails for non-well-ordered ones, where local decision rules do not determine a unique global outcome. By requiring uniqueness of play, we aim to provide a natural framework for hat-guessing games on arbitrary standing sets. For the classical visibility model, it was previously known due to Glivický that at most one incorrect guess can be guaranteed when $S$ is well-ordered. We prove the same result for backwards well-ordered sets, even in the case when $S$ has no first element. In the full-visibility version of the game, Glivický proved that at most one incorrect guess can be guaranteed if the standing set has a first element. We extend this result to arbitrary nonempty standing sets.
A Talenti-type rigidity theorem and P-function constraints for the Pompeiu--Schiffer problem in every dimension

Schiffer's conjecture asserts that the ball is the only bounded domain, with boundary homeomorphic to a sphere, carrying a nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian that is constant on the boundary; for such domains it is equivalent to the Pompeiu problem. In 2026 it was disproved in the plane and in many higher dimensions by computer-assisted and analytic constructions. We study what survives. Our main result is a Talenti-type theorem valid in every dimension $N\ge2$: if the eigenfunction $u$ stays strictly below its boundary value $c>0$, then $kR^*\ge j_{N/2,1}$, where $k^2$ is the eigenvalue, $R^*$ the radius of the ball of equal volume and $j_{N/2,1}$ the first positive zero of $J_{N/2}$; equality holds only for the ball. We compare this threshold with the unconditional bound $kR^*\ge 2^{1/N}j_{N/2-1,1}$ given by the Krahn--Szegő inequality. Using Payne's P-function $P=|\nabla u|^2+λu^2$ we prove that every Schiffer domain satisfies $\max|u|>\sqrt N\,|c|$, together with pointwise and distance bounds. We correct the shape-optimization approach of an earlier work by computing the optimality condition of the associated boundary functional with an adjoint state. Using the transcendence of the zeros of Bessel functions of integer and half-integer order, we prove the infinitesimal rigidity of the ball, in every dimension, both for the Schiffer problem and for the Berenstein problem. Finally, we reconstruct numerically the convex four-dimensional counterexample of Guo and check the above statements on it.
Division ring extensions and the realization of Coxeter diagrams $I_2(n)$

For each integer $n\ge5$, we construct a hereditary artinian ring of finite representation type with Coxeter diagram $I_2(n)$. Both of its diagonal division rings are two-generated over the field $\mathbb{Q}(ζ)$, where $ζ$ is a primitive root of unity of order $n-2$. The construction is based on a chain of quantized Weyl relations and a shift automorphism. We give one-sided bases for the corresponding division ring extensions and compute the right dimension sequence of the bimodule. The resulting ring has exactly $n$ isomorphism classes of indecomposable finitely generated right modules.
A Talenti-type result for the Pompeiu-Schiffer Conjecture

Schiffer's conjecture asserts that the ball is the only bounded simply connected domain carrying a Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian that is constant on the boundary; it is equivalent to the Pompeiu problem. In August 2026 it was disproved in the plane by computer-assisted constructions. We revisit the shape-optimization approach of~\cite{Se24} in the light of these counterexamples. We first show that the vanishing of the material derivative on the boundary, assumed in~\cite{Se24}, never holds, and we compute the correct optimality condition, involving an adjoint state, for the associated functional $J_2$. We prove that every planar Schiffer domain satisfies $\max|u| > \sqrt{2}|c|.$ Our main result is a Talenti-type theorem: if $u < c$ in $Ω$ , then $kR^* \geq j_{1,1},$ where $R^*$ is the radius of the disc of equal area, and equality holds only for the disc. Finally, using Siegel's transcendence theorem, we prove the infinitesimal rigidity of the disc for the Berenstein problem.

We prove the maximal existence conjecture for pluriclosed flow on Kähler backgrounds. This leads to a priori generalizations of the Aubin-Yau and Calabi-Yau theorems, and resolves the question of connectedness of generalized Kähler structures on Calabi-Yau backgrounds.
Lift Height and the Structure of Classification Failure

We introduce a framework for measuring the depth of classification failure relative to a chosen invariant. A \emph{shadow map} records visible structure while suppressing finer information; lift packages recover this information in successive layers, and lift height measures the depth through which classification ambiguity persists. Canonical reduction removes redundant stages and yields an essential notion of lift height. For nilpotent groups, the lower central series provides a natural commutator lift tower, with lift height controlled by nilpotency class and decreasing under refinement of the shadow. The associated graded structure gives a Lie-theoretic interpretation of the successive commutator layers. The main examples show that classification depth is genuinely unbounded. Over any field of characteristic different from two, and for every positive integer, there exist nilpotent Lie algebras with the same fixed four-dimensional abelianisation whose commutator lift packages agree through the prescribed number of layers but differ at the next layer. Moreover, such separation can occur at arbitrarily large degree even when the complete underlying lower-central graded vector space is fixed. Thus neither a fixed shadow nor the dimensions, or even the underlying vector-space structure, of the lower-central graded object impose a uniform bound on the depth at which new commutator information may appear.
The Canonical Family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms and the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm for Linear Programming

A complete canonical family of uniquely normalized, row-equivalent representatives of an $m\times n$ matrix is introduced and termed the family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms (RRPEFs). This bijection transfers the strict lexicographic order to the distinct RRPEFs and induces a finite chain from the URREF to the LRREF. The resulting structure gives rise to the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm (ILCA). Lexicographic confinement and singular-transition skipping restrict the candidate domain, whereas RRPEF reuse and scalar-equivalent transition bypassing avoid redundant Gauss--Jordan reductions while retaining the corresponding basic-solution tableaux. Strict lexicographic progression prevents cycling, while the traversal proceeds independently of objective improvement under degeneracy-induced stalling. ILCA terminates when a feasible tableau satisfies the standard optimality conditions and otherwise completes the finite traversal, including for Tucker- and Cunningham-type totally degenerate configurations.
Receding horizon control with sensor-induced positive semidefinite state penalization

This paper develops and analyzes a receding horizon control (RHC) framework for the stabilization of infinite-dimensional nonautonomous continuous-time systems with an infinite-horizon control objective. The considered stage costs penalize only a finite-dimensional component of the state and are therefore positive semidefinite with respect to the full state. In the linear case, we extend the framework to output-feedback RHC by combining it with a Luenberger-type state estimator based on finitely many sensors, and establish closed-loop stability using an augmented Lyapunov functional. The abstract state-feedback results are verified for a nonlinear Schlögl parabolic equation around an unstable steady state and, in the output-feedback setting, for nonautonomous linear parabolic equations. The control and observation realizations involve finite-dimensional actuation and sensing, including localized boundary controls and spatially localized state-penalization operators. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings and illustrate the performance of the proposed RHC schemes.
A geometrical approach for obtaining exact analytical solutions for a scalar field in a one-dimensional dynamical cavity
Maxwell F. de Araújo; Odemar Julião do N. Neto; Stanley S. Coelho; Jeferson Danilo L. Silva; Alessandra N. Braga; Danilo T. Alves

The dynamical Casimir effect was first predicted by G. T. Moore in 1969, who considered a real scalar field inside a cavity with a moving mirror in ($1+1$)D, satisfying Dirichlet boundary conditions. Moore wrote the general solution for the field in terms of a function that satisfies a functional equation nowadays known as the Moore equation.In the literature, exact analytical solutions to the Moore equation form a rather small set, restricted to specific classes of laws of motion. Cole and Schieve (1995) developed a geometrical approach that yielded a general formula for the solution of the Moore equation for cavities initially at rest. In this work, we show that their method can also be employed as a powerful method for deriving exact analytical solutions, and show the applicability of this approach to deriving analytical solutions to the Moore equation.
