The results also suggest stable behavior during long-time recursive prediction and the potential applicability of the proposed framework to two-phase flow problems.
Kolmogorov Obstacle Problems: Euclidean Free Boundary Regularity under a Cone Condition
Junkee Jeon; Takwon Kim; Jehan Oh

We study obstacle problems for Kolmogorov-type operators that diffuse in one variable and transport in another. Such problems describe American options on running averages. Under a cone estimate, a strong monotonicity condition on the solution in the diffusive direction, we show that the free boundary is a graph in the diffusive direction with Hölder continuous first derivatives in the Euclidean sense, and that every free boundary point is regular. The key observation is that a Euclidean Lipschitz free boundary is flat at the intrinsic scale. For the American fixed-strike Asian option we verify the cone estimate, so that its exercise boundary has the same regularity.
Fluctuations of heat kernels and exit times on random graphs and application to the critical long-range percolation
Zherui Fan; Lu-Jing Huang; Takashi Kumagai

Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph equipped with random conductance. We give sufficient conditions for the Markov chain on $\mathcal{G}$ to exhibit large scale fluctuations in its on-diagonal heat kernel and in exit times. The conditions also imply non-tightness of the height process w.r.t. the quenched measure, while it is tight w.r.t. the annealed measure. As an application of the general theory, we prove large scale fluctuations for the simple random walk on $1$-dimensional critical long-range percolation.
Robust Bayes-like estimation of the distribution of a determinantal process

We consider the problem of estimating the distribution of a determinantal process (DP) on a measured space from the observation of $n$ independent copies of it. Our estimator is obtained by sampling from a $T$-posterior distribution associated with a suitable prior, and we establish non-asymptotic risk bounds for the Hellinger loss which hold with high probability. These bounds remain valid when the data are only independent rather than i.i.d., and when the model is misspecified, which makes the estimator robust, for instance, to the presence of a small fraction of outliers. For determinantal projection processes of rank $k$ whose kernels are associated with $k$-dimensional subspaces of a $D$-dimensional space, Haar priors on Grassmannians lead to a rate of order $\sqrt{k(D-k)\log n/n}$, and model selection extends this result to infinite-dimensional settings. For general DPs, we introduce priors based on the spectral decomposition of the kernel that combine uniform distributions on the eigenvalues with Haar measures on Stiefel manifolds. When the underlying space is finite with $N$ elements, we obtain a rate of order $N\sqrt{\log n/n}$, without any assumption on the kernel, and derive that the $2^{N}$ principal minors of the kernel can be estimated simultaneously. Finally, for translation-invariant DPs on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, we obtain rates that only depend on the smoothness of the kernel at the origin and that are adaptive with respect to it. Combined with a new lower bound on the Hellinger distance between such DPs, these rates also yield estimators of the kernel in $\mathbb{L}_2$.
The covariety of numerical semigroups with some prescribed pseudo-Frobenius numbers
William Giovanni Hernández-Yanes; José Carlos Rosales

If $S$ is a numerical semigroup, then we denote by $m(S)$, $F(S)$ and $\mathrm{PF}(S)$ its multiplicity, its Frobenius number and its set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers, respectively. Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of positive integers. In this paper, we prove that $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)=\{S\mid F(S)=\max(\mathcal P),\ \mathcal P\subseteq\mathrm{PF}(S)\}$ is a covariety. The associated tree provides algorithms to compute $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$, its elements with a prescribed type or genus, and the set of numerical semigroups $S$ satisfying $\mathrm{PF}(S)=\mathcal P$. We show that every element of $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$ has a unique minimal system of generators relative to $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$, and we call its cardinality the $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$-rank. Finally, we characterize the elements of $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$ with $\mathcal C(\mathcal P)$-rank one.
Improved Approximation and Hardness Bounds for $β$-TSP
Paul Liu; Jack Spalding-Jamieson; Da Wei Zheng

The traveling salesman problem (TSP) asks for a minimum-length Hamiltonian cycle in a complete weighted graph. Its approximability depends on the edge lengths: unrestricted instances admit no constant-factor approximation unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, metric instances admit Christofides' $3/2$-approximation, and fixed-dimensional Euclidean instances admit a PTAS. We study $β$-TSP, where the edge lengths satisfy $ \ell_{uw}\leqβ(\ell_{uv}+\ell_{vw}) \qquad \forall\,u,v,w\in V\ \text{pairwise distinct}, \quad β\in\left[\tfrac{1}{2},1\right]. $ The condition arises naturally in various settings, for example, when metric travel times are combined with positive service times at the vertices. The previous best approximation algorithm, due to Böckenhauer et al., ranges from $1$ at $β=1/2$ to $3/2$ as $β$ approaches $1$. We obtain a strictly better guarantee for every $1/2<β<1$ by combining two simple constructions whose guarantees counterbalance each other. We also improve the best known approximation hardness bound for every $1/2<β<1$.
Zak Phase, Pole--Zero Invariants and the Maslov Index of Bloch Cauchy Lines in One-Dimensional Periodic Media

The topological properties of the Bloch bands of a one-dimensional periodic medium are described either by the Berry--Zak phase or by the poles and zeros of the surface impedance. We show that both can be read from one geometric object: the line spanned by the field and its flux (the Cauchy data) at an inversion centre. For each band, this line turns as the quasi-momentum runs over the Brillouin zone. Its number of turns, the Maslov index, is fixed by the parities (even or odd) of the Bloch functions at the two band edges, and its parity is the Zak phase. In a gap, the Cauchy line of the solution decaying on one side rotates monotonically with the energy, and an interface state between two crystals is a crossing of two such lines. This gives the known criterion of at most one state per gap in terms of the same lines. Examples with a stratified medium show that the choice of inversion centre changes the interface spectrum. The last section discusses what is missing to extend the construction to higher dimension.
A 4-regular graph with 4/5 of its vertices satisfying the Šoltés property

The Wiener index $W(G)$ of a connected graph $G$ is the sum of distances between all unordered pairs of its vertices. A vertex $v$ is called a Šoltés vertex if $G-v$ is connected and $W(G-v)=W(G)$. Since the cycle $C_{11}$ is the only known graph in which every vertex is a Šoltés vertex, a natural problem is to construct other graphs with as large a proportion of such vertices as possible. We construct a $4$-regular graph with Šoltés fraction $4/5$, improving the previous value of $2/3$.
Inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals

We study inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals over a field of characteristic zero. Our main tool is a Vandermonde-type construction of graded polynomials with a uniformly bounded number of variables. Together with a reduction to finite exterior algebras, this construction yields separating polynomials that work uniformly under bounds on Grassmann envelope representations. We prove that, under these bounds, an intersection of $T$-ideals is contained in such a product only if one member is. This proves Berele's Conjecture~3 and, consequently, his Conjecture~1 \cite{Berele2012}. We also characterize inclusions between ordered products by an explicit combinatorial criterion, proving his Conjecture~2 and answering his Question~2 \cite{Berele2012}. These results characterize inclusions between arbitrary intersections of products of nonzero proper verbally prime $T$-ideals and show that every nonzero such intersection has a unique finite irredundant representation. As an application, we characterize finite quivers whose path algebras have the same polynomial identities as some, equivalently every, positive power of their arrow ideals.
Curves with absolutely irreducible Tate modules over $p$-adic fields

Over every number field, curves whose Jacobians have absolutely irreducible $\ell$-adic Tate modules exist in every positive genus and can be chosen hyperelliptic. Over $p$-adic fields, however, inertia and Frobenius can exclude entire genera. We classify the genera that occur for $\ell\ne p$ in terms of the residue characteristic and the cardinality of the residue field. For odd $p$, we also classify the genera occurring for hyperelliptic curves. These genera have relative density zero among those occurring for arbitrary curves, yielding Jacobians whose isogeny classes contain no hyperelliptic Jacobian. For odd $p$ and even residue degree, we obtain further restrictions on the genus when the curve itself is required to have potentially good reduction. Over number fields, we obtain uniform bounds from absolute irreducibility of the Tate module at two finite places of distinct residue characteristics different from $\ell$. The dimension of the abelian variety alone bounds the number of isomorphism classes in its isogeny class and the least degrees of isogenies between them.
Isomorphisms and representations of noncommutative function algebras
Marcel Scherer; Orr Shalit; Eli Shamovich; Mansi Suryawanshi

Let $V$ be a noncommutative (NC) variety in a NC operator ball. We study the dual operator algebra $H^\infty(V)$ of bounded NC functions on $V$, and the operator algebra $A(V)$ obtained as the closure of NC polynomials in $H^\infty(V)$. In the important case where the varieties are the full NC operator balls we find a striking rigidity phenomenon: if $A(B_E)$ and $A(B_F)$ are completely boundedly isomorphic then $E$ and $F$ are completely isometric. We also present a variety of examples illustrating the results and their sharpness, showing how several results from the literature fail to generalize to the setting studied here.

Let $ϕ$ be a fixed polynomial with integer coefficients, positive leading coefficient and degree $k\geq2$. We prove that the values $2ϕ(n)$, $1\leq n\leq N$, can be written as the sum of two primes, apart from at most $N^{α_k+o(1)}$ exceptional indices, where $α_k<1$. For quadratic polynomials the exponent is $1/2$, for cubic polynomials $5/8$, for quartic polynomials $3/4$, and for $k>4$ it is $1-1/(k+1)$. The proof combines a fourth-moment estimate over primes with mean-value estimates over arbitrary subsets of polynomial sequences.
Universal Decoding for Gaussian MIMO-ISI: Spherical Ensembles and Symmetric Neighborhoods

We construct a universal decoder for cyclic Gaussian multiple-input multiple-output channels with intersymbol interference and unknown channel taps and spatial noise covariance. Codewords are drawn independently and uniformly from a sphere of fixed total energy. Under stated bounds on frequency variation, the decoder attains the ensemble-average error exponent of informed maximum-likelihood decoding for fixed channels and channels with growing memory. We approximate the frequency response by a constant matrix within each frequency block. For this auxiliary channel, every matched log-likelihood is affine in a common sufficient statistic. At fixed received output, we compute the statistic density of an independent competitor. The decoder selects the candidate with the smallest statistic density, equivalently minimizing a weighted sum of residual log-determinants. The density and its support volume give an upper bound on the universal competitor probability. Affinity ensures that at least half of a suitable symmetric neighborhood of the transmitted statistic has matched likelihood no smaller than that of the transmitted word. Integrating a density lower bound over this half gives the matched competitor bound. These bounds establish equality of error exponents, which a Gaussian channel comparison transfers to the original channel. The same decoder attains the matched exponent for independent frequency blocks with prescribed energies satisfying the stated conditions. For energies proportional to block length, an additional gain condition ensures that this exponent is at least that of the total-energy spherical ensemble.
Approximation Algorithms for Right-Hand-Side Parametric Linear Programming Problems

In parametric linear optimization problems, the objective function or the feasible set depends linearly on one or several real-valued parameters. The goal is to provide an optimal solution set, i.e., a set containing an optimal solution for each non-parametric problem induced by a particular choice of parameter values. Our first approach constructs an approximation set using a greedy staircase procedure and yields an FPTAS under general sufficient conditions. We show that these conditions hold for some important classes of RHS-PLPPs. For monotone instances, in which the feasible sets are nested as the parameter varies, our algorithm yields an approximation set of minimum cardinality. Beyond monotonicity, we establish near-minimum cardinality guarantees under more general sufficient conditions. Isomorphic classification of the coordinate algebras of the two-parameter braided quantum groups $\mathrm{SL}_2$

We classify, up to isomorphism, the coordinate algebras of the two-parameter braided quantum groups SL 2 .

We introduce an extension of Khovanov and Rozansky's categorification of the HOMFLY polynomial to arbitrary oriented tangles. Unlike previous such extensions, ours is invariant under the full suite of oriented Reidemeister moves, including the "misoriented" Reidemeister IIb. For oriented links $\mathcal{L}$, our construction recovers Khovanov and Rozansky's construction while removing the preliminary step of presenting $\mathcal{L}$ as a braid closure.

For a code $RS(256, 224)\times RS(175, 173)$ in a BSC we achieve post-decoding bit error rate (BER) of $10^{-20}$ at $\approx 5.3\times 10^{-3}$ raw BER while maintaining the common requirement to detect and correct 4 out of 32 dead tracks. We resolve two common problems of miscorrections and stall patterns that arise under such a high raw BER via simplified versions of anchor decoding and binary image analysis. The highest efficiency is achieved by performing an unlimited iterative decoder, which performs decoding iterations until no changes are made. We give an empirical analysis of the average number of iterations: below the raw BER of $5\times 10^{-3}$, four half-iterations are performed on average while improving substantially over a decoder that always performs 4 half-iterations. We provide a CPU implementation achieving 100-200 megabytes/s single-core throughput on a regular laptop and a design of a potential hybrid FPGA-CPU implementation of our decoder.

This paper addresses the birational geometry of three-dimensional algebraic varieties admitting a conic bundle structure. The central focus is on tetragonal transformations -- a special class of birational maps between standard conic bundles that are not fiberwise and play a key role in the birational geometry of such varieties.

We prove that the standard map $f_k(x,y)=(x+y+k\sin2πx,\,y+k\sin2πx)$ of the two-torus satisfies $\log(2πk+4)-2^{430}\le h_m(f_k)\le\log(2πk+4)$ for every $k\ge\exp(2^{50000})$, where $h_m$ is the metric entropy with respect to area. Thus $h_m(f_k)=\log k+O(1)$, the order of growth observed numerically since Chirikov; in particular $h_m(f_k)>0$ for all large $k$ and $h_m(f_k)\to\infty$, as conjectured by Sinai. Moreover, for each fixed $c<1$ the points whose top Lyapunov exponent is below $c\log k$ fill an area $O(1/\log k)$. Positivity of $h_m(f_k)$ for all sufficiently large $k$, with a threshold that is not effective, was obtained in a recent preprint by OpenAI. We keep some of its architecture and follow it closely in about a third of the results. New here are an explicit covering argument for cancellations and a balance across scales at a fixed parameter, an inequality between mean shortfalls that replaces the compactness argument over limits of rescaled orbit geometries; together they yield the explicit constants and the entropy bound.

In this paper, we define a Drinfeld-type center for an associative crossed module and prove that it is canonically the internal category of an explicit crossed module constructed from Mac Lane's bimultiplications. The resulting center carries a canonical multiplicative lifting, which induces a natural strict braiding, establishing its correspondence to a braided crossed module. We also examine the relationship between this center and Huq's categorical center. Finally, we obtain a canonical comparison morphism with Pirashvili's center of Lie crossed modules via the (braided) Liezation functors, which preserves braidings under an injectivity condition.
On the Motzkin-Straus theorem and clique number for k-uniform hypergraphs

In this paper, we establish a Motzkin-Straus type equality for k-uniform hypergraphs under certain conditions, which extends the classical Motzkin--Straus theorem for graphs. Using this equality, we present several spectral bounds for the clique number of k-uniform hypergraphs in terms of the spectral radii of the adjacency, signless Laplacian, and Laplacian tensors. When k=2, the bounds coincide with the corresponding known results for graphs.
On the existence of automorphisms acting expansively on the space of one-parameter subgroups of connected Lie groups

For a connected Lie group $G$, we consider the action of Aut$(G)$ on Sub$_G$, the set of all closed subgroups of $G$ endowed with the Chabauty topology. We study the action of automorphisms of $G$ on Sub$^p_G$, the closure of the set of all closed one-parameter subgroups of $G$ in Sub$_G$, in terms of expansivity. We show that a nontrivial connected Lie group $G$ with dim$(G)\geq 2$ does not admit any automorphism which acts expansively on Sub$^p_G$. We also show that a certain class of subgroups of Aut$(G)$, which include all one-parameter groups of automorphisms in Aut$(G)$, do not act expansively on Sub$^p_G$. These results generalise a results of Chatterjee, Lekharu and Shah on tori and those of Prajapati and Shah on connected Lie groups of dimension greater than $1$.
A Structural Lower Bound for the Ramsey Number of the Petersen Graph

In this note, we investigate the diagonal Ramsey number of the Petersen graph, denoted by \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P})\). To the best of our knowledge, the dynamic survey \textit{Small Ramsey Numbers} (Revision \#18, 2026) records the lower bound as 19, established by Harborth and Krause. We construct a novel 2-coloring on the complete graph \(K_{20}\) that avoids any monochromatic Petersen graph. By defining the blue graph as the complement of the red graph, we utilize a specific join graph structure \(K_{9,9} \vee \overline{K_2}\). We rigorously prove its Petersen-free property, thereby improving the previously documented lower bound to \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P}) \ge 21\). Furthermore, we demonstrate the limit of this structural family by showing that the natural extension \(K_{9,9} \vee \overline{K_3}\) contains a Petersen subgraph.
Period bounds for Bergman kernel variation and the Suita defect
Fusheng Deng; Gang Huang; Kefeng Liu

The periods of holomorphic differentials give an explicit lower bound for the curvature of Bergman evaluation matrices. We prove this bound along the Green sublevels of a smooth plane domain. For scalar evaluation at the Green pole, equality at one regular level holds precisely when that sublevel is simply connected. For complete jets at the Green pole, the matrices have continuous first derivatives, including at critical levels, and their logarithmic determinant defects are integrals of nonnegative curvature densities. A further estimate bounds the accumulated period energy by the determinant defect, with a constant independent of the jet order. On a multiply connected domain, all these defects vanish up to the first critical Green value and become strictly positive above it.
A scaled TW-PINN framework for soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries equation
Seungwan Han; Jiaxi Gu; Daniel Olmos-Liceaga; Jae-Hun Jung

Accurate approximation of soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation remains challenging for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) due to localized wave structures, high-order spatial derivatives, nonlinear interactions between solitons, and difficulties in long-time prediction. In this work, we address these challenges using a scaling PINN framework to approximate KdV soliton solutions. The framework transforms the governing equation into a normalized form, approximates its solution using a PINN solver, and reconstructs the solution in the original variables through inverse scaling. We introduce scaling transformations and PINN solvers tailored to one- and two-soliton problems. For the one-soliton case, we employ a PINN solver that incorporates a traveling-wave coordinate to capture soliton propagation. For the two-soliton case, we employ a two-step training procedure for the PINN solver. The first step learns the individual soliton profiles and estimates their propagation speeds, while the second step uses the estimated speeds to construct traveling-wave coordinates in the PINN solver and approximate the full two-soliton solution, including nonlinear interactions. We also introduce soliton-informed sampling (SIS), which places additional collocation points around the soliton trajectories. Numerical results show that the scaling PINN framework accurately captures one-soliton propagation, resolves two-soliton interactions, and preserves soliton profiles during long-time extrapolation in both cases. An additional three-soliton experiment suggests the applicability of the proposed two-step training procedure to multi-soliton solutions.
PH-Symb : Sparse symbolic identification of nonlinear port-Hamiltonian systems using Kolmogorov-Arnold networks
Achraf El Messaoudi; Karim Cherifi; Yann Le Gorrec; Yongxin Wu

The paper introduces PH-Symb, a novel symbolic structure-preserving identification method, that combines Kolmogorov Arnold networks and sparse regression to build explicit port-Hamiltonian (pH) models from data. Unlike other Machine Learning or neural pH approaches, PH-Symb recovers physically interpretable and explicit-symbolic components and enforces pH structure by construction. It also introduces a new normalization method that preserves the pH structure. It allows handling both identification from input-state-output (ISO) data and input-output (IO) data, and applications show it delivers interpretable models and lower errors than neural baselines on synthetic and real-world systems.
Unique ergodicity of systems of finite order and the density finite sums theorem in arbitrary abelian groups
Ethan Ackelsberg; Asgar Jamneshan; Or Shalom

Let $Γ$ be a countable abelian group and $k\geq 1$. We establish that every minimal topological $Γ$-system of order $k$ is uniquely ergodic. This result, which was previously only known for finitely generated groups for arbitrary $k$, answers a question of Glasner, Gutman, and Ye and yields the answer to multiple questions by Candela, González-Sánchez, and Szegedy. As applications of our dynamical results, we obtain the following combinatorial theorems. Let $A\subseteq Γ$ be a set of positive upper Banach density. Then there are infinite sets $B_1,\ldots, B_k\subseteq Γ$ such that $B_1+\dots+B_k\subseteq A$. If $Γ$ satisfies a necessary divisibility assumption, then there are also $t\in Γ$ and an infinite set $B\subseteq Γ$ such that $A-t$ contains the set of all sums of $m$ pairwise distinct elements of $B$ for all $m\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$. For arbitrary $k$, these density finite sums theorems were only known in the integers previously.
Commuting Toeplitz and Little Hankel Operators on the Bidisk
Necessary and sufficient conditions are obtained for two Toeplitz operators and for a Toeplitz operator and a little Hankel operator to commute on the pluriharmonic Hardy space of the bidisk.
One complex metric and geometric adelic nefness

We prove that an arithmetic adelic line bundle on a smooth quasi-projective variety over a number field has nef geometric part if its prescribed continuous metric at one complex embedding has semipositive first Chern current. The proof constructs semiample approximations to every positive rational ample perturbation by boundary extension, multiplier ideals, and Nadel vanishing, followed by specialization and Galois descent. This gives geometric nefness of Gao--Zhang's canonical Gross--Schoen adelic line bundle.
Root sharing and $2$-adic interpolation for Legendre polynomials

Stieltjes's conjecture on Legendre polynomials asserts that no two distinct Legendre polynomials can share a nonzero root. This question is, surprisingly, connected to a number of disparate mathematical areas. From the point of view of spectral geometry, this question concerns zero-sets of spherical harmonics. A disk counterpart to the conjecture is a famous theorem of Siegel on nonexistence of nonzero common roots of Bessel functions, proved using transcendence theory. A weak version of the conjecture is implied by the dynamical Mordell--Lang conjecture. We prove, using a $2$-adic analytic approach à la Skolem, that for a root $α\neq 0$ of $P_l$ the set $\{n\in \mathbb{N}:\ P_n(α)=0\}$ has cardinality at most $2l$. In particular, this set is finite.
A Geometric Journey Through the Aharonov--Bohm Effect: Tonomura's Toroid, Pseudoscalar Phase, and Quantum Holonomy in Clifford Algebra

The magnetic Aharonov--Bohm (AB) effect is often introduced through the idealised infinite solenoid and a complex scalar phase. We give a geometric-algebra formulation based on the compact toroidal magnets shielded by a superconductor employed in the electron-holography experiments of Tonomura and collaborators. Working in the real Euclidean Clifford algebra $ \mathrm{Cl}(3,0)$, we distinguish the unit volume pseudoscalar $I$ (grade 3), coordinate angles (scalars, grade 0), tangent vectors (grade 1), and directed surface bivectors (grade 2). The magnetic field is represented by the dual bivector $\mathcal{B}= I \mathbf B$, while the electromagnetic $U(1)$ phase is represented by the central unit multivector $e^{Iα}$ generated by the pseudoscalar $I$, rather than by a spatial rotor with a bivector generator. We establish the linked toroidal geometry, formulate magnetic flux and Stokes' theorem intrinsically in geometric algebra, and derive the holonomy element $U_Γ=\exp(IqΦ_B/\hbar)$ from $U(1)$ gauge covariance, with every sign fixed explicitly. We then express superconducting fluxoid quantization in the same notation and obtain the binary electron holonomy $U_Γ= (-1)^N$ in the ideal limit where the linked magnetic flux equals $N h/(2e)$. Finally, a short conditional-state description of the quantum source and field shows how a backreaction can introduce an additional phase and reduce interference visibility. The conditional-state overlap is represented by a central scalar--pseudoscalar element; preservation of the fluxoid sector alone does not guarantee unit coherence.
A sharp weighted $L^2$ Bernstein inequality for partial derivatives on the unit ball

We determine the sharp constant in the weighted $L^2$ Bernstein inequality for coordinate derivatives on the unit ball with a Jacobi weight and the strengthened derivative factors introduced by Beberok and Xu. The constant is expressed in terms of the largest zeros of Jacobi polynomials, and all extremal polynomials are characterized explicitly. The proof uses an orthogonal polynomial decomposition that gives diagonal formulas for both the squared norm and the weighted derivative integral. We also obtain two-sided bounds for the sharp constant and determine its leading asymptotic behavior as the polynomial degree tends to infinity.
Natural potentials for TT tensors, divergence-free symmetric tensors and linearised relativistic initial data

By diffeomorphism invariance, $DN(g\_0)^*$ takes values in divergence-free symmetric $2$-tensors, and in TT tensors if moreover $DN(g\_0)$ kills conformal directions. Such operators are local potentials, which we call machines: they produce smooth compactly supported tensors with the required property and, on closed manifolds, all of them up to a finite-dimensional space when their symbol is injective. On Einstein manifolds of every dimension, the linearised Bach tensor gives the operator $P$ of an earlier paper, which factorises on TT tensors into the massless and partially massless spin-$2$ operators; we also construct machines on Bach-flat, conformally flat and Ricci-parallel metrics. Replacing the diffeomorphisms of $M$ by those of the vacuum development, we obtain potentials, with a Fredholm property, for the linearised Einstein constraint equations on arbitrary spacelike hypersurfaces of Minkowski, de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes.
The enigma of locally Toeplitz matrices. I. Discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential

Their average can fill a region of the complex plane even when the eigenvalues of the original matrices appear to follow curves. We conjecture that, when the above average has a sufficiently regular planar density, the limiting eigenvalue measure is its mother body. We prove it for a class of finite Dirichlet discrete Schrödinger operators with complex potential $V$ and a common real coefficient $α>0$ on the two adjacent diagonals. When $(\Im V)'>0$ and $V$ admits a suitable holomorphic extension, the limiting measure is supported on finitely many analytic arcs. Its logarithmic potential falls below that of the averaged measure by twice the least of four explicit actions. We obtain these actions from a four-term asymptotic expansion of the Dirichlet determinant. When $\Im V$ is not monotone, an exact transfer recursion gives a conditional extension. For a circular potential arc we verify the geometric switching condition, leaving non-resonance as the remaining hypothesis.

We prove the existence of a Riemann--Hilbert $A_\infty$-functor from the curved dg-category of $\mathscr{A}$-connections on graded vector bundles, where $\mathscr{A}$ is a higher Lie algebroid, to the curved dg-category of $Π_\infty(\mathscr{A})$-connections on graded vector bundles, where $Π_\infty(\mathscr{A})$ is the homotopy groupoid of $\mathscr{A}$. We combine this with the Riemann--Hilbert functor to define higher parallel transport functors for $\mathscr{A}$-connections. Finally, we use these functors to define the higher holonomy groups of $\mathscr{A}$-connections and endow them with the structure of augmented simplicial Lie groups.

Moreover, smallness in $H^1$ alone is insufficient to close a direct nonlinear elliptic estimate in five dimensions. We overcome these difficulties through uniform Oseen estimates and a relative-energy comparison yielding quadratic improvement of the perturbation. As a consequence, the singular set has zero one-dimensional upper Minkowski content on every compact subset of $Ω$, and hence local upper Minkowski dimension at most one.

Moreover, we extend these examples to types $B$, $C$ and $D$ in every generic degree $r\geq 2$, and to types $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$ in generic degree $2$.

Second, we exploit this characterization to formulate mixed-integer linear constraints on the discrete-time trajectories that allow for planning a trajectory whose piecewise polynomial interpolation satisfies the continuous-time STL formula. In fact, system discretization and trajectory planning are performed in such a manner that any feasible solution to these constraints gives a discrete-time trajectory that can be transformed into a continuous-time one guaranteed to satisfy the original STL formula.
