A semi-implicit exactly well-balanced relaxation scheme for the 2d shallow water system
José Ignacio Ramírez-Fuentes; Cipriano Escalante; Tomás Morales de Luna; María Luz Muñoz-Ruiz

We propose a semi-implicit, exactly well-balanced finite volume scheme for the two-dimensional shallow water equations over a non-flat bottom, aimed at the low-Froude-number regime. The method combines a Suliciu-type relaxation of the pressure with a flux splitting that separates the fast acoustic waves from the slow transport ones: the pressure subsystem is integrated implicitly and the transport subsystem explicitly, so that the time step is no longer restricted by the acoustic stability condition. Written in terms of its Riemann invariants, the pressure subsystem decouples into independent one-dimensional problems along the grid lines, each of them governed by a banded linear system whose bandwidth does not depend on the mesh. The implicit step therefore requires no non-linear solver and costs O(NxNy) operations, regardless of the acoustic Courant number. A two-dimensional exactly well-balanced reconstruction, whose limiter weights are frozen within each time step, preserves this linear structure for the second-order scheme. We prove that both the first- and the second-order schemes preserve water-at-rest equilibria exactly, and we assess them on several two-dimensional benchmarks, where they resolve fine-scale velocity structures on coarse meshes and run up to 8.5 times faster than standard explicit Riemann solvers.
Tracking of a Moving Target on a Hyperboloid and its Extension to Leader-follower Formation Controller
Ashish Shukla; Sanad Shaha; Kashyap Rajeevsarathy; Arijit Sen

This paper proposes a novel controller for a double-integrator agent to track a moving target with bounded velocity on a hyperboloid $\mathbb{H}^n$. The control law uses the intrinsic Riemannian structure of the hyperboloid, including the logarithm map, covariant derivative, and parallel transport, to make all its terms coordinate-free. Such formulation eases the implementation of the proposed tracking controller in the ambient Minkowski space without doing any additional chart computations. We use Barbalat's lemma for the hyperboloid to establish the convergence proof. Later, the proposed tracking controller is extended to a leader-follower formation control, where each agent reaches at a desired position around a moving leader in $\mathbb{H}^n$. We validate the results with numerical simulations considering two different target trajectories, geodesic and spiral, as examples.
A splitting theorem for Einstein manifolds with symmetries

We prove that every negative-Einstein manifold with cocompact symmetries splits isometrically as a Riemannian product $H \times K$ with $H$ homogeneous and $K$ compact. This confirms a conjecture due to Böhm and Lafuente. As a consequence, we obtain a new proof of the 1975 Alekseevskii conjecture.
On the convergence of Lattice Boltzmann method for advection-diffusion equation with intermediate scaling

The purpose of this article is to study the convergence of a lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) for a simple diffusion equation. The LBM is proven to be stable and consistent in some sense, so that convergence results may be obtained. The approach is similar to asymptotic analysis in the literature, although the schemes are also studied for intermediate time scalings. Usually, LBM are used in the range of acoustic regime, where $δ$t ___ $δ$x, or in diffusive scaling, with $δ$t ___ $δ$x 2 . In this work, we study any intermediate scaling $δ$t ___ $δ$x 1+r with r $\in$]0; 1]. The goal is to prove that this scaling is capable of approximating an advection-diffusion equation, provided the relaxation rate is chosen in accordance with $δ$x. Convergence results are established and match the previously known results in the diffusive regime. The second objective is to prove that several choices for the initial condition are suitable for convergence. In particular, the usual choice of equilibrium distribution at initial time guarantees that the LBM scheme yields an accurate approximation of the macroscopic quantities.

We prove the Woo-Yong conjecture: the non-Gorenstein locus of a type A Schubert variety is the union of its generically non-Gorenstein maximal singular components. More strongly, at every scheme point, local Weil divisor classes are detected at the generic points of the maximal singular components containing that point. For arbitrary finite crystallographic type, the analogous localization map is injective on the torsion subgroup of the source local class group. This determines Cartier indices of locally $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisors and gives the Woo-Yong criterion on the $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein locus. A type D family shows the necessity of this hypothesis: the ambient variety is generically Gorenstein along its singular locus but not $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein along a deeper nonempty locus. The type A proof and the counterexamples are geometric; the general torsion proof also uses bounded finite inputs with explicit certificates and reproducible reconstruction programs.
Property Gamma and McDuff Factors from Shift-Similar and Houghton-like Groups

We initiate the study of von Neumann algebras of shift-similar and Houghton-like groups, introduced by Mallery and Zaremsky as analogs of self-similar and Röver-Nekrashevych groups, respectively. Given a shift-similar group $G$ of permutations of $\mathbb{N}$, one can form the Houghton-like group $H_n(G)$, a ``mashup" of the classical Houghton group $H_n$ with $G$, which acts on $X_n$, the disjoint union of $n$ copies of $\mathbb{N}$. One main result is that when $G$ and the canonical shift map $σ$ admit a joint Følner sequence for their action on $\mathbb{N}$, then both group von Neumann algebras $L(G)$ and $L(H_n(G))$ are II$_1$ factors with property Gamma and hence $G$ and $H_n(G)$ are inner amenable. More generally, let $Γ$ be an ICC group of permutations preserving the ends of $X_n$. We prove that if the natural near action on $\mathbb{N}$ of the germs of almost permutations arising from $Γ$ along some ray is amenable, then $L(Γ)$ has property Gamma; if this group of germs is itself amenable, then $L(Γ)$ is McDuff. Then we construct a shift-similar group $G$, using property (T) groups with certain actions, such that neither $G$ nor $H_n(G)$ is inner amenable. Finally, we produce extremely broad and diverse sources of shift-similar groups satisfying the joint amenability condition. These examples come from residually finite groups and from wobbling groups of a variety of metric spaces. In particular, we completely characterize all metrics $d$ on $\mathbb{N}$ for which the wobbling group $W(\mathbb{N},d)$ is shift-similar in terms of a coarse geometric property---namely, that $σ^{-1}$ is bornologous with respect to $d$. As a consequence, this gives us necessary and sufficient conditions for when the wobbling group of any countable metric space admits a shift-similar embedding.
A Fermat--Torricelli convex-hull characterization of inner-product spaces via Birkhoff--James orthogonality
Zhiyao Fang; Junxiang Qi; Qi Liu

The classical location problem posed by Weber [Über den Standort der Industrien,Tübingen: J. C. B. Mohr, 1909] has motivated various geometric characterizations of inner-product spaces. Benítez, Fernández and Soriano [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. \textbf{354} (2002), 5027--5038] characterized real inner-product spaces through the convex-hull property of Fermat--Torricelli medians.Pakhrou [J. Funct. Anal. \textbf{285} (2023), 110078] further established a characterization using $γ$-centers and equilateral triangles. Building on these results, we show that the Fermat--Torricelli convex-hull criterion remains valid when restricted to triples satisfying a one-sided Birkhoff--James orthogonality condition.The proof combines norming functionals, radial rescaling,Alexandrov differentiability, and the area formula.No completeness, smoothness, or strict convexity assumptions are required.
Boundary singularities for the Lane-Emden equation
Weiwei Ao; Sho Katayama; Juncheng Wei

For every $n\ge3$ and $(n+1)/(n-1)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct positive solutions of $Δu+u^p=0$ in the half-space with zero Dirichlet data away from the origin, the homogeneous singular profile there, and Poisson-kernel decay at infinity, resolving a question of del Pino--Musso--Pacard. Under a weighted non-degeneracy condition, these half-space solutions serve as building blocks for positive very weak solutions in smooth bounded domains, singular along prescribed compact smooth boundary submanifolds of normal dimension $n$. We verify non-degeneracy in the initial stable interval and at and just beyond its threshold when this lies below $(n+2)/(n-2)$. For isolated boundary singularities, the construction applies throughout the strict subcritical interval outside a locally finite exceptional set.
Centres and semisimple deformations of contraction algebras

Let $A_{\rm{con}}$ be the contraction algebra of a $3$-fold flop of an irreducible curve, with genus-zero Gopakumar-Vafa invariants $n_1, \dots, n_l$. We show that $\prod_j M_j(\mathbb{C})^{n_j}$ is the only semisimple algebra to which $A_{\rm{con}}$ deforms. Hence $A_{\rm{con}}$ encodes its Gopakumar-Vafa invariants intrinsically, answering a question of Wemyss. Hua and Toda showed that this deformation exists, and Jelisiejew and Smoktunowicz proved its uniqueness in types A and D. The key step in our proof is that the centre of $A_{\rm{con}}$ has dimension $n_1 + \dots + n_l$. To prove this, we lift the contraction algebra of the universal flop to the Cartan subalgebra, where it becomes a corner of a deformed preprojective algebra. We show that the universal contraction algebra and its zeroth Hochschild homology are free over a polynomial ring, with presentations whose determinants are products of roots. Pulling these presentations back along the arc that classifies the flop gives the count, and recovers Toda's formula for $\dim A_{\rm{con}}$. We also prove Hua and Toda's flatness conjecture, and determine which Gopakumar-Vafa invariants occur in lengths 3 to 6.
Provable State Estimation with Recurrent Models
Vincent Andrieu; Pauline Bernard; Lucas Brivadis; Laurent Praly; Christian Wolf

Estimating the state of a dynamical system from observations is a crucial task in robotics and control. Despite their empirical success, recurrent models often lack formal guarantees on convergence and robustness. We bridge this gap by analyzing these architectures from the perspective of nonlinear observer theory. By framing RNNs as a time-discretization of continuous latent dynamical systems (Neural ODEs), we demonstrate that enforcing a contraction condition on the latent flow guarantees the existence of a smooth, injective map of the true physical state into the latent space. We prove that this architecture acts as a tunable observer: by increasing a single scalar gain that scales the latent vector field, the estimation error can be driven to an arbitrarily small neighborhood of zero at an exponentially fast rate. We further establish quantitative bounds on the MLP complexity required to decode this latent state, and extend our formal guarantees to the discrete-time residual RNN implementation. We validate the theory on a real mobile robotic task, where a provably contracting model outperforms a vanilla GRU with substantially more stable training. We also report that unconstrained GRUs converge to contracting dynamics on this task, suggesting that contraction is an emergent property of well-trained sequence models.
Mesoscopic eigenvalue statistics for random regular graphs: a case study

We study mesoscopic fluctuations of linear eigenvalue statistics for random $d$-regular graphs on $N$ vertices with fixed $d\ge 3$. Revisiting the approach developed by Dumitriu-Johnson-Pal-Paquette (2013) and Johnson (2015), we establish a mesoscopic central limit theorem in the bulk and identify its universal limiting variance. Our result applies to test functions with smooth compactly supported Fourier transforms and to a specific range of spectral scales $(\log N)^{-1}\llη\ll 1$. In particular, this case study allows the mesoscopic scale to tend to zero arbitrarily slowly.
Joint modelling of financial cost and carbon footprint in motor insurance claims: a BINAR(1) decision framework for circular auto parts adoption
Charles Minier; Stéphane Loisel; Renata Alcoforado

Motor insurance claims management increasingly faces a dual objective: controlling claim costs while reducing greenhouse-gas emissions associated with vehicle repair decisions. This paper proposes a bivariate, discrete-time modelling framework that links the dynamics of financial claims and repair-related carbon footprint inspired by a BINAR(1) dependence structure, allowing for temporal persistence, cross-dependence and a positive/negative correlation between the two dimensions. Using externally sourced emission factors and cost information for replacement parts, we operationalise the carbon footprint of claims under two repair pathways: new parts versus circular-economy reused parts (PIEC). We then conduct scenario analyses in which the acceptance rate of reused parts varies, and we quantify the joint implications for expected monetary outlays and CO 2 -equivalent emissions. Results show that higher PIEC acceptance can simultaneously reduce expected emissions and average claim cost, and the magnitude of the joint benefit depends on the dependence structure and persistence captured by the BINAR(1) process. The proposed framework provides a transparent, reproducible tool for insurers to evaluate repair-policy levers and to align claims operations with decarbonisation targets while retaining an explicit stochastic risk perspective.
Bounded Ratios of Best Approximations: Sharp Bounds and Spectra of Diophantine Exponents

We solve Problems 1, 2, and 3 posed by Marnat, Moshchevitin, and Schleischitz (arXiv:2505.15964). We consider totally irrational real n-by-m matrices and two conditions on their sequences of best approximations: (B) bounded successive height ratios and (C) bounded successive error ratios. Under (C), we prove that the ordinary Diophantine exponent is at most m and, when both dimensions are at least two, that the uniform exponent is at most m^2/(m+1). Combining these bounds with known results, we determine the individual spectra of both exponents under (C), with and without the additional assumption (B). When both dimensions are at least two, imposing (B) changes neither spectrum. A key ingredient is a block lemma for consecutive best approximations lying in a fixed rational subspace.
Boundary integral methods and shape reconstruction for periodic fluid--solid interfaces
Yongxin Liu; Junliang Lv; Ning Wang; Yi Wang

This paper studies direct scattering by periodic fluid--solid interfaces and interface reconstruction from multifrequency near-field data. Using Helmholtz decomposition and quasi-periodic single-layer potentials, we formulate a coupled boundary integral system with the standard stress traction, establish its equivalence to the original fluid--solid transmission problem under suitable assumptions, and construct a corresponding Nyström discretization. For near-field observations at finitely many measurement points, we establish local Fréchet differentiability of the observation map with a quadratic remainder estimate. In the smooth setting, the derivative transmission problem and its boundary integral formulation are used to compute the observation Jacobian required for interface reconstruction. The interface is reconstructed by regularized Gauss--Newton iteration in a Fourier space that is progressively enriched as the frequency increases. Numerical experiments assess direct-solver accuracy and reconstruction performance for different interfaces, material configurations, and noise levels.
Elliptic units, derived Heegner classes and the p-adic Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer quotient of CM elliptic curves of rank two

Let $E\colon y^2=x^3-Dx$ have rank two and let $p\equiv1\pmod4$ be a prime of good reduction. We study the conjecture that the $p$-adic quotient $q_p$, the leading coefficient of the cyclotomic $p$-adic $L$-function divided by the Euler factor and the $p$-adic regulator, equals the complex quotient $q_\infty=L''(E,1)/(2Ω_E\mathrm{Reg}_\infty)$, and that the latter is rational. In rank one the analogous statement is a theorem of Perrin-Riou and Rubin, because a Heegner point computes both sides; in rank two there is no such point. We show that $q_p$ is the constant of the quadratic term of the two-variable Katz measure; this is how the conjecture arises, and it computes $q_p$ modulo any power of $p$ from critical Hecke $L$-values. We then show that $q_p$ is the coordinate of two global classes: Rubin's rank-two elliptic-unit class, whose position in $E(\mathbb{Q})\otimes\mathbb{Q}_p$ is $q_p$ times an explicit vector, and the derived Heegner class over an auxiliary imaginary quadratic field $F$, for which we prove an exact identity. As consequences, whenever such a field $F$ satisfying our hypotheses exists, $q_p$ is a square in $\mathbb{Q}_p$ times the product of the Tamagawa numbers of $E$, so that the unit $q_p/A_E$ of the $p$-adic Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula is a square when Sha is finite; if moreover the derived Heegner class has non-zero formal logarithm, the conjecture of Agboola and Castella for $E/F$ holds up to a $p$-adic unit, and with a theorem of Burungale, Castella and Skinner the anticyclotomic main conjecture holds integrally; and our conjecture is equivalent to the analytic form of theirs, with the products of anticyclotomic heights read sesquilinearly, which differs by a sign from its literal formulation. The conjecture is verified modulo $p^3$ for 5520 pairs $(E,p)$ with conductors up to $3.9\cdot10^{12}$, including curves with analytic Sha of order 4 and 9.
Entropy and frame measures for self-similar measures

For $0<ρ<1$ and a set of $N\ge2$ distinct real digits $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\mathbb{R}$, let \[ μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}=\frac1N\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}\circ S_i^{-1}, \qquad S_i(x)=ρ(x+d_i). \] Write $X=\sum_{j\ge1}ρ^j d_{ω_j}$, where the symbols $ω_j$ are independent and uniform on $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$. We prove that $μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy $H(ω_1\mid X)>0$. In particular, this holds for all $ρ>1/N$, without any absolute-continuity assumption or arithmetic restriction on the digits or the contraction. At $ρ=1/N$, for commensurable digits, a frame measure exists if and only if $μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor. For $\mathscr D=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ and $ρ<1/N$, we also prove nonexistence whenever $ρ^{-m}=a/b$ for some $m\in\N$, with $a/b$ in lowest terms, $b\mid N$ and $N/b\nmid a$, extending the integer-power obstruction. The extension compares mask quotients using finite families of target pole classes in place of one target class.
Controlled Excitation for Identification of Nonlinear Systems with Saturated Outputs
Adel Malik Annabi; Jean-Baptiste Pomet; Dario Prandi; Ludovic Sacchelli

We consider nonlinear systems whose measured output is the product of an unknown matrix and a known saturation function of the unmeasured state. Generating excitation that allows the matrix to be recovered from the output is challenging when the dynamics are largely unknown. We exploit saturation to construct this excitation. Under a geometric accessibility condition, we derive explicit open-loop controls that drive the state into regions where the saturation takes prescribed values. For componentwise saturations, this condition holds generically with as few as two independent control directions. The controls require no state measurement and only partial knowledge of the dynamics, with no information on the structure of its nonlinear part. The resulting regressor is known in advance, and the unknown matrix is recovered exactly by a closed-form regression. Under stronger structural assumptions and with sufficiently many independent outputs, an output feedback tracks prescribed reference trajectories within the unsaturated region to arbitrary accuracy and permits exact state recovery. Suitably chosen references then also enable exact identification of linearly parameterized (nonlinear) dynamics. We analyze robustness to measurement noise and illustrate the method numerically in the presence of both measurement and dynamical noise.
Real-Time Nonlinear Mixed-Integer Model Predictive Control With Horizon-Tail Relaxations

Model predictive control (MPC) of nonlinear systems with discrete decisions leads to mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) whose combinatorial complexity often prevents real-time deployment. In this paper, we propose a decomposition-based MPC method that reorders and reduces computations to shorten the delay between receiving a state measurement and applying the control input. Before the measurement arrives, we solve a continuous relaxation of the MINLP at a predicted state and construct a mixed-integer quadratic program (MIQP). Once the measured state is available, we solve the MIQP that reconstructs the discrete controls and simultaneously performs one sequential quadratic programming step toward the corresponding nonlinear solution. To reduce the combinatorial complexity in the horizon length, we either fix the integer controls or relax their integrality over the prediction horizon tail, while retaining an integer-feasible first control input. We derive error bounds relating the nonlinear objective values obtained with the horizon-tail approximations to the optimal value of the original mixed-integer problem. In a data center cooling example, the proposed method reduces mean feedback computation time by 94% relative to a state-of-the-art MINLP method with a total closed-loop cost difference of less than 1%.
Recurrent and rigid multipliers on commutative Banach algebras. The Fourier algebra
María J. Beltrán-Meneu; Jorge Galindo; Enrique Jordá

We study recurrence, rigidity and uniform rigidity of multipliers on semisimple commutative Banach algebras. For a power-bounded multiplier $T$ on a Tauberian, self-adjoint algebra $\mathfrak{A}$, we show that $T$ satisfies each of these properties if and only if the multiplication operator on $C_0(Δ(\mathfrak{A}))$ induced by the Gelfand transform of $T$ does. One consequence of our analysis is that, if $Δ(\mathfrak{A})$ is $σ$-compact, then recurrence implies rigidity for such multipliers. We examine in detail the multipliers of the Fourier algebra $A(G)$. In particular, we show that recurrence of a multiplier of $A(G)$ is equivalent to recurrence of the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ when the connected components of $G$ are open. For multipliers that are not power bounded, a flexible construction based on chains of compact subgroups of a locally compact abelian group $G$ produces multipliers of $A(G)$ that are rigid but not uniformly rigid, and multipliers that are recurrent but not rigid, such that in each case the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ is uniformly rigid. Via the Fourier-Stieltjes transform, these results describe the recurrence and rigidity properties of convolution operators on $L^1(G)$.
Dynamics of subcritical threshold solutions for the three-dimensional energy-critical NLS

We extend the radial threshold classification of Duyckaerts and Merle on the lower kinetic branch to nonradial solutions of the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation in \(\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)\). At the ground state energy and with initial gradient norm strictly below that of the ground state, every solution is global and either scatters in both time directions or is a symmetry transform of the special solution \(W^-\), possibly after conjugate time reversal. The proof combines Su and Zhao's below-threshold scattering theorem with a coercivity estimate for the interaction form at threshold under a kinetic gap and a local analysis near the ground state orbit.
Enhanced Informed Dynamic BP Decoding Scheduling Strategies for 5G NR LDPC Codes
Tofar C. -Y. Chang; I-Hsiang Lee; Pin-Han Wang; Jian-Jia Weng; Yu T. Su

We present an enhanced informed dynamic scheduling (IDS) strategy to avoid propagations of unreliable messages in the residual belief-propagation (RBP) algorithm for decoding low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. To reduce the resource needed for updating the degree-one variable nodes (VNs) in an RBP-based algorithm for decoding 5G New Radio (NR) LDPC codes, we further introduce a process consisting of several simple procedures for managing the resource consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that our RBP algorithm based on the Proposed IDS strategy outperforms existing RBP-based algorithms at the early decoding iterations. By using our degree-one VN resource managing approach, the performance of both the proposed and the existing decoders is significantly improved in decoding the 5G NR codes.
On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test
Prahladh Harsha; Swastik Kopparty; Mrinal Kumar; Ramprasad Saptharishi; Madhu Sudan

We investigate the derandomized version of the classical line-point low-degree test in the high-error regime in the bivariate setting and reveal some unexpected behavior. The classical line-point low-degree test takes an $m$-variate function $f$ over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, queries it along a random line and accepts if the restriction of the function to this line is a low-degree polynomial. The high-error version of (the analysis of) this test asserts that if $f$ has at least $ε$ expected local agreement with a degree-$k$ univariate polynomial on a random line, then in fact $f$ is non-trivially close to some degree-$k$ $m$-variate polynomial even as $ε$ approaches $0$ (provided $q$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$ and $1/ε$). The derandomized version of the problem asks if the same holds when the line is not chosen uniformly over all possible lines but rather from a small set. In this paper we explore the bivariate case ($m=2$). We show, somewhat surprisingly, that there exists a function $f\colon \mathbb{F}_q^2 \to \mathbb{F}_q$ and a set of lines $\mathcal{L}$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^2$ of size nearly $q^{3/2}$ such that on every line in $\mathcal{L}$, $f$ has agreement $\approx 1/2$ on average with some univariate polynomial of degree $k=\sqrt{q}/2$ and yet $f$ is $1 - O(q^{-1/2})$ far from every polynomial of degree $O(k)$. On the positive side, we show that once the field size $q$ is at least $k^2/(ε)^{O(1)}$ such examples disappear and we can get sets of lines of size $O(q/ε^{O(1)})$ on which the low-degree test has a high-error analysis. On the way to our positive result, we show a new high-degree version of the classical two-direction Polishchuk--Spielman divisibility lemma.
Hecke Algebras for Minimal Equicontinuous Cantor Actions

In this work we extend the concept of Hecke algebras to a pair of a separable infinite profinite group and a closed core-free subgroup. Motivated by applications to minimal equicontinuous Cantor actions, which are characterized by such pairs, we characterize isometric *-algebra isomorphisms between such Hecke algebras by showing that they always arise as Koopman operators of homeomorphisms between the double coset spaces combined with the multiplication by some character. We then prove that two minimal equicontinuous Cantor actions with isometric isomorphic Hecke algebras have the same Steinitz order. We provide examples including the infinite dihedral group and the Grigorchuk group.
Positive self-similar solutions of a parabolic equation with spatially weighted absorption in a half-space

We study positive solutions of $u_t-Δu+x_1^{2α}|u|^{q-1}u=0$ in the half-space $\{x_1>0\}$, with $α>-1$ and $q>1$, vanishing on $\{x_1=0\}$ and at $t=0$ away from the origin. Let $q_c=(N+3+2α)/(N+1)$. For $1<q<q_c$ we prove that there is exactly one positive self-similar solution continuous away from the origin, and that its profile satisfies Gaussian bounds that are sharp up to multiplicative constants. For $q\ge q_c$ there is none. We also show that, after removing the Gaussian factor, the profile has an angular limit shape $Φ$ in every mode, give an integral formula for its Kummer coefficients, prove that $Φ$ is real-analytic and is the uniform limit of the rescaled profiles, that $Φ/(η_1/|η|)$ is monotone along meridians, and that $Φ$ is proportional to $η_1/|η|$ if and only if $2α+q=1$. Every self-similar solution of finite energy, or continuous away from the origin, is dominated in absolute value by the positive one, and for $(N+4+2α)/(N+2)\le q<q_c$ the only nontrivial ones are $\pm u_s$. For $α=0$ existence, uniqueness and the upper bound are due to Marcus and Véron; the lower bound with the sharp exponent and the description of $Φ$ are new also in that case. The existence and uniqueness proofs use a Brezis--Oswald type comparison principle and explicit barriers, given by explicit formulas; the analysis of $Φ$ uses Kummer functions.
Construction of DAE solver Rodas4PW and numerical test examples with Rosenbrock and W-methods in OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl

This paper compares various Rosenbrock and Rosenbrock W-methods. To achieve this, some methods implemented in the Julia package OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl are selected and benchmarked using test examples. The test examples include stiff ODE problems as well as differential-algebraic equations. In addition to the already known methods, the new W-method Rodas4PW is introduced and included in the tests.
A structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin method for variable-density incompressible flow with a partitioned time integrator
Zonghao Bai; Yinhua Xia; Yan Xu

Preserving density bounds and mass conservation, together with a conservative momentum discretization and exact incompressibility, is a central challenge in high-order simulations of variable-density incompressible flow. We develop a structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin method that couples conservative density transport with an \(H(\mathrm{div})\)-conforming mixed discretization of the momentum equation. The method uses a partitioned time integrator: density is advanced explicitly by strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta stages with a bound-preserving limiter, while momentum is updated by a linearly implicit backward differentiation formula. The transport velocities are extrapolated from previously computed mixed velocities. Because the discrete solenoidal space is linear, this extrapolation preserves elementwise zero divergence and single-valued normal traces, providing compatible transport velocities without an auxiliary reconstruction or projection. For source-free transport on triangular meshes with impermeable or periodic boundaries, we prove bounds for density cell averages and limiter control-point values under the stated spatial, quadrature, and stagewise Courant--Friedrichs--Lewy conditions. The conservative fluxes and mean-preserving limiter yield global mass conservation. Numerical experiments on triangular and structured rectangular meshes demonstrate the expected convergence rates, machine-level divergence errors, and bound preservation, including in a low-density regime with high density ratio.
The multiplier step size in classical two-block ADMM: convergence and counterexamples
Benqi Liu; Qiming Dai; Zaiwen Wen

How large can the multiplier step be in the classical two-block alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)? We keep the penalty fixed and use the usual primal updates. We consider finite-dimensional problems with closed proper convex objectives. We assume that a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker point exists and that each block subproblem attains its minimum at every step. Under these assumptions, the constraint images and the multiplier converge for a range of factors that extends beyond the golden ratio. The constraint matrices may be rank deficient. For larger steps, we construct two fixed compact polytopes and give an explicit threshold below two. The polytopes admit an infeasible periodic orbit for every factor at or above this threshold. At that threshold, ADMM can cycle even for smooth strongly convex objectives. This gives a negative answer to Glowinski's question about the full interval from zero to two. A different pair of piecewise-quadratic objectives gives geometrically growing residuals. For the general convex class, we locate the endpoint of the uniform convergence interval near 1.88688256. A convergence certificate on the unit circle gives the lower bound, while a separate periodic orbit gives the upper bound. Exact arithmetic verifies that the two bounds differ by less than 0.000000174.
José Correa; Svenja M. Griesbach; Elfarouk Harb; Felix Hommelsheim; Reda Jlibene; Vasilis Livanos; Eilon Solan

Given red and blue points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, connect every red point to every blue point and weigh each segment by its length under a fixed norm. What fraction of the total weight can always be captured by a single affine hyperplane separating the segments' endpoints? We study this question for finite point configurations in affine general position and, more generally, for pairs of probability measures. For dimension one, we show that choosing the best of three thresholds determined by the means of the two distributions captures at least one third of the total red-blue distance. We also give a matching upper bound. Embedding the line construction to higher dimensions shows that the guarantee of $1/3$ cannot be improved for arbitrary measures. Thus, we pivot to the family of measures whose atoms are in affine general position and whose non-atomic part places zero mass on all hyperplanes. Crucially, we establish that the worst-case guarantee is identical for finite configurations in affine general position and several natural classes of probability measures, thereby unifying the discrete and continuous formulations of the problem. For this family of measures and for higher dimensions, we extend our guarantee of $1/3$ for all norms. Our proofs combine the ham-sandwich theorem with a novel coupling argument and, in the planar case, an integral representation of norms. We also show that the optimal guarantee improves as the dimension grows, giving a lower bound of $1/2-\operatorname{O}\left(1/\sqrt{d}\right)$ as well as an asymptotically matching upper bound of $1/2$ for every $d$. For the Euclidean distance, we refine the lower bounds to $8/(8+5π)$ and $1/2-\operatorname{O}\left(1/d\right)$ and, for $d=2$, the upper bound to $5/11$. We also derive dimension-dependent guarantees for finite point configurations, including perfect separation of $n$ points of each color when $d\geq2n-1$.
On the optimal mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled to the Navier-Stokes equations
Lili Du; Yulan Wang; Yichen Zhang

We investigate the mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled with the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In the absence of fluid interaction, the classical Keller-Segel system admits a well-known $4π$-critical-mass dichotomy: for every suitably regular initial datum of total mass $m<4π$, the associated no-flux initial-boundary value problem admits a global bounded classical solution, whereas for $m>4π$, there exist smooth initial configurations of mass $m$ such that the associated solution blows up in finite or infinite time. For the fluid-coupled system, Winkler ({SIAM J. Math. Anal.}, 52:2041-2080, 2020) first established global generalized solvability under the condition $m<2π$ and posed an open question whether the fluid action may lower the critical blow-up mass to some value lying between $2π$ and $4π$. Based on numerical evidence, Bonilla and Gutiérrez-Santacreu ({J. Numer. Math.}, 32:175-212, 2024) later conjectured that the critical value is still $4π$. In the present work, we resolve this open problem and provide a rigorous mathematical proof to the conjecture, which indicates that the presence of the fluid does not alter the critical mass threshold, and the entire classical subcritical regime remains intact---every admissible initial datum with total mass $m<4π$ generates a unique global classical solution that is uniformly bounded in time. Our proof relies on the construction of a new quasi-energy inequality. The key underlying observation is that combining relative isoperimetric estimates with rearrangement techniques yields a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality on bounded planar domains with an explicit leading constant.
A Structured-Surrogate Double-Model Approach to Regularization Parameter Selection
Malena Español; Markus Juvonen; Samuli Siltanen; Ilaria Trombini; Chuyang Wu

Double-model methods select a regularization parameter by matching the discrepancy between two reconstructions of the same data to a prescribed target. The Structured-Surrogate Double-Model (SSDM) framework is developed around a computationally inexpensive structured surrogate of the forward operator and a spectrally explicit perturbation, with the selected parameter subsequently applied to the original inverse problem. Given a prescribed target, parameter selection requires neither prior knowledge of the noise level nor training data. For a class of Tikhonov regularization problems, the squared discrepancy is shown to attain a strict maximum at zero regularization, decay as $λ^{-2}$, and decrease strictly beyond an explicit phase-aware threshold. A complementary, data-dependent certificate is established to guarantee strict monotonicity on finite intervals, enabling unique and reliable target matching even when the global threshold is overly conservative. The discrepancy is further connected to directional roughness in image deblurring, providing a geometric interpretation of the selection principle. Experiments on synthetic images and on synthetically blurred natural photographs illustrate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical applicability of certified parameter selection.
$\mathrm{X}$-evolution flows/foliations for cluster algebras: partial Bongartz (co-)completions and acyclicity

We first generalize the notion of $\mathrm{X}$-foliation on cluster complexes to the context of cluster algebras. This is a continuous generalization of Keller's green mutation, which was previously introduced in the prequel within a categorical setting. We show that the wall-crossing structure (of possibly higher co-dimension) is encoded by $\mathrm{X}$-supports, which form a partial version of Cao-Gyoda-Yurikusa's Bongartz (co-)completions for cluster algebras. Moreover, we prove that for any cell transversed nontrivially by a fixed $\mathrm{X}$-leaf, its rank is an invariant bounded below by the rank of $\mathrm{X}$. Finally, we prove the acyclicity conjecture for $\mathrm{X}$-foliation, which also implies the compactness conjecture for any $\mathrm{X}$-foliation in finite type cases.
A Dirichlet form approach to the potential theory of $m$-subharmonic functions
Bowoo Kang; Jaechul Lee; Zhenghao Li

On a bounded open subset of $\mathbb{C}^n$, we study the Dirichlet form induced by an admissible pair $(θ,μ)$, where $μ$ is a positive Radon measure and $$θ=dd^c u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^c u_{m-1}\wedge(dd^c \lvert z\rvert^2)^{n-m}$$ for locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions $u_1,\dots,u_{m-1}$. We prove that locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions belong locally to the domains of these Dirichlet forms and are quasi-continuous with respect to the induced capacities. We establish a monotonicity property for Dirichlet forms, which motivates the introduction of $μ$-quasi-monotone convergence of $m$-subharmonic functions. The natural embeddings into these domains are continuous with respect to this convergence. These results yield new proofs of the commutativity and continuity of complex Hessian operators. Using this framework, we characterize quasi-continuity with respect to the induced capacity for an arbitrary $m$-subharmonic function in terms of its pole set having zero measure $μ$, or equivalently, zero induced capacity. On bounded strictly $m$-pseudoconvex domains, we prove that the Bedford--Taylor capacity for $m$-subharmonic functions and the capacities induced by the corresponding Dirichlet forms have the same null sets. We further characterize $m$-polar sets in terms of Dirichlet forms and stochastic processes, extending the corresponding characterization of pluripolar sets due to Fukushima and Okada to the $m$-subharmonic setting.
Erratum to: Monotonicity of Ursell functions in the Ising model
Federico Camia; Jianping Jiang; Charles M. Newman
In this note, we correct an error in the proof Theorem 1 of Comm. Math. Phys. 401 (2023), 2459-2482.
Campana points on quadrics with hyperplane boundary

Let $Q\subset\mathbf P^{d+1}_k$ be a smooth quadric of dimension $d\ge2$ over a number field, and let $H_i=Q\capΠ_i$ be hyperplane sections for $1\le i\le d$. For every integer $m\ge2$, we prove Campana strong approximation for the pair $\bigl(Q,(1-1/m)(H_1+\cdots+H_d)_{\mathrm{red}}\bigr)$.
Second-order optimality conditions for $C^{1,1}$ sparsity constrained optimization problems via disjunctive programming
Luu Thi Thu Huyen; Liguo Jiao; Nguyen Van Tuyen

In this paper, we investigate second-order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for a class of $C^{1,1}$ sparsity constrained optimization problems via a disjunctive programming approach. More precisely, by utilizing the limiting/Mordukhovich second-order subdifferential of the associated Lagrangian function, we establish new second-order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for local optimal solutions. These results are derived under mild assumptions and extend several existing results in the literature. In addition, we apply our theoretical developments to sparse multiobjective optimization problems and derive second-order optimality conditions for efficient solutions.
Spectral Characterizations, Harmonic Analysis, and Phase Transitions in 2-Nice and $k$-Nice Recurrence

We investigate the structural mechanisms governing $2$-nice and $k$-nice recurrence in measure-preserving dynamical systems. For weakly mixing systems, we establish a complete spectral characterization of two-sided $2$-nice recurrence via quadratic spectral functionals and Herglotz--Bochner duality, extending the theory to arbitrary integer polynomial configurations $\{0, p_1(n), p_2(n)\}$ with zero constant term and to actions of countable abelian groups. Using stationary Gaussian processes and Hermite mode decoupling, we construct explicit weakly mixing counterexamples separating one-sided and two-sided $2$-nice recurrence. Furthermore, we uncover a fundamental structural phase transition at $k=3$: while $k=2$ recurrence is rigidly controlled by a quadratic spectral functional whose two-sided symmetrization eliminates all higher-degree cumulants, at $k=3$ fourth-order centered correlations survive symmetrization and can drive a strict recurrence deficit even when the quadratic spectral functional remains strictly positive. Using lacunary and multi-frequency Riesz products alongside uniform Wiener lemmas, we analyze the upper Banach density obstructions of negative spectral sets, establish partial partition regularity on the spectral cone, resolve an inverse Furstenberg correspondence problem of Rodríguez Martín for countable groups via Bernoulli product extensions, and characterize spectral $2$-nice ultrafilters in the Stone--Čech compactification $β\N$.
Elastic Wave Imaging via Kirchhoff Migration: Resolution Analysis and Inclusion Identification

We consider the inverse problem of determining the location, orientation, shape, and material parameters of a small elastic inclusion embedded in a homogeneous medium from full-aperture measurements of the scattered field. Using a small-volume expansion, we derive explicit leading-order expressions for four Kirchhoff migration imaging functionals, denoted by PP, PS, SP, and SS, corresponding to the four combinations of pressure (P) and shear (S) waves used for receiver- and source-side backpropagation. The resulting point-spread functions quantitatively characterize the resolution of each mode and show that the SS mode achieves the highest spatial resolution. For an elliptic inclusion, we show that the PP mode uniquely determines the elastic moment tensor (EMT) within the leading-order asymptotic model, thereby enabling the reconstruction of the material and geometric parameters of the inclusion. For a general small scatterer, the reconstruction may instead be interpreted as an effective elliptic representation determined by its leading-order EMT. For a disk, the parameter-identification problem is underdetermined; nevertheless, explicit upper and lower bounds on its volume are derived. We further analyze the model error arising from neglected cross-mode contributions when the distance from the center of the measurement configuration is not sufficiently large relative to the elastic wavelengths. Numerical experiments support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed imaging and reconstruction methods.
Strong convergence rates for numerical approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation with additive rough noise

We establish strong convergence rates for a fully discrete method of the one-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive rough noise. Using the Cole-Hopf transformation, the equation is converted into a linear stochastic heat equation, which is discretized by a spectral Galerkin method in space and an accelerated exponential Euler method in time. A numerical approximation of the original solution is then reconstructed through a regularized inverse Cole-Hopf transformation. The analysis combines strong Sobolev error estimates with the positivity and inverse-moment bounds for the transformed solution. For additive space-time white noise, the numerical method achieves mean-square convergence rates arbitrarily close to 1/2 in space and 1/4 in time. The rates are slower when the noises are rougher.
Formalization of Filter-Method Construction for Real Numbers in Coq

This paper presents a formalization for a theory of constructing real numbers using concepts related to filters. The formalization is implemented using the Coq proof assistant and is grounded in axiomatic set theory. The theory encompasses various notions such as filters, ultrafilters, principal ultrafilters, and arithmetical ultrafilters. A special filter, namely the non-principal arithmetical ultrafilter, whose existence requires the Continuum Hypothesis to be proven, is employed to establish several non-standard number sets: *N, *Z and *Q. The set of real numbers, R, is subsequently derived by equivalently classifying a specific subset of *Q. The entire theory is thoroughly formalized, with each detail verified to ensure rigor and precision. This work contributes a new selection of foundational materials for the formalization of mathematical theories.
Maximizing Reaction via Spatial Localization: The Reaction-Flux Landscape and Maximizing Sequences
Mohammad Yasir Feroz Khan; Bo Li

We continue our study of a PDE-constrained variational model for maximizing the total reaction flux by optimizing the spatial distribution of catalytic materials, such as enzymes. The total amount of enzyme is fixed, and the substrate concentration is governed by a reaction-diffusion equation with prescribed boundary values. We consider both linear and nonlinear Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics. In previous work, we constructed a maximizing sequence, computed the first and second variations of the reaction functional, and established the nonexistence of local maximizers. Here, we conduct a more comprehensive analysis. We prove that the functional is strictly concave for linear kinetics but need not be concave or convex for nonlinear kinetics. We also show that no critical points exist. We then characterize maximizing sequences and identify all their possible limiting measures. Our analysis reveals the mechanism of reaction maximization through spatial localization: maximizing sequences concentrate enzymes near the portion of the boundary where the substrate concentration is largest. Moreover, the landscape of the functional defining the total reaction differs between the linear and nonlinear cases, a point less emphasized in applications. Consistent with existing biophysical studies, these findings motivate the development and analysis of regularized models.
Every IC-planar graph has weak-strict degeneracy at most 6
Zhen He; Yilong Li; Tao Wang; Xiaojing Yang

We prove that every IC-planar graph has weak-strict degeneracy at most $6$. Weak-strict degeneracy is the weak degeneracy of Bernshteyn and Lee plus one, so it bounds the coloring parameters controlled by weak degeneracy. In particular, every IC-planar graph is $6$-choosable, $6$-DP-colorable and $6$-paintable, which strengthens the theorem of Yang, Wang, Wang and Lih that IC-planar graphs are $6$-choosable. An IC-planar graph is a subgraph of a plane graph in which a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint inner $4$-faces, called marked faces, receive both diagonals. Our main tool is a Thomassen-type statement for such graphs: vertices of marked faces get one extra unit, except those in a prescribed independent set of boundary vertices. With no marked faces, this statement is exactly the theorem of Bernshteyn, Lee and Smith-Roberge that gives weak-strict degeneracy at most $5$ for planar graphs, so it contains both results. We prove it by a minimal-counterexample argument following Bernshteyn, Lee and Smith-Roberge. The new ingredients are a deletion rule that turns destroyed marked faces into ordinary edges, a pseudo-$2$-chord lemma for paths that use one diagonal, and a choice of orientation of the outer cycle that avoids a vertex of the independent set joined to two vertices of the prescribed boundary path.
Infinity operad pairs, higher distributivity and spectral Tambara functors

We introduce an $\infty$-categorical model of operad pairs and their associated bimonoidal categories. We study the related concepts such as cocartesian-cartesian operad pairs, algebra pairs and the Day convolution. Using the Day convolution for operad pairs, we can define distributive functors between a symmetric bimonoidal category and a cartesian closed monoidal category. As an application, we show that for a finite group $G$, the operadic distributive functors from $\mathrm{Span}(\mathsf{Fin}_G)$ to any cartesian closed monoidal category coincides with the distributive functors defined by the distributive diagram. Therefore, we show that the connective $G$-equivariant $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectra are equivalently the spectral $G$-Tambara functors.
Tom Goertzen; Abel Lacabanne; Daniel Tubbenhauer; Pedro Vaz
Using annular webs and Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients, we disprove Guralnick's absolute boundedness conjecture for first cohomology.
The Sparse-Complement Conjecture for Two Distinct Eigenvalues

For a graph $G$, let $q(G)$ be the minimum number of distinct eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix whose off-diagonal zero--nonzero pattern is $G$. We prove that $q(G)=2$ whenever the complement $H=\overline G$ of a graph of order $n\ge3$ has at most $n-3$ edges, resolving the sparse-complement conjecture of Fallat and Mojallal. If $H$ contains a cycle, the proof constructs a nontrivial orthogonal projector with the strong spectral property and rank at most $|E(F)|-|V(F)|+4$, where $F$ is the union of the cyclic components of $H$. The construction combines faithful stress-free Gram representations, a one-coordinate lift for each excess core edge, exact orthogonal-frame completion, and a Stiefel-manifold pendant-extension argument.
Yuxuan Wang; Yu Sun; Bowen Li; Kangqiang Li

We study Byzantine-robust distributed sparse softmax regression in high-dimensional settings. We propose a communication-efficient distributed algorithm that employs robust aggregation methods---coordinate-wise trimmed mean and coordinate-wise median---to defend against Byzantine attacks. Under sub-Gaussian design assumptions with sparsity constraints, we establish that the distributed estimator achieves the convergence rate of $O_{P}(K^{\frac{5}{2}}\sqrt{s\log(Kd)/N})$ when the Byzantine fraction $α\asymp 1/\sqrt{m}$, matching the centralized oracle rate. Numerical experiments on synthetic data demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method.
A Smooth Equality Reformulation of Nonlinear Exponential Cone Optimization

Exponential cone optimization has received considerable attention in the modern literature, but studies involving nonlinear objective and constraint functions are still limited. This work can be seen as one of the first steps toward understanding nonlinear exponential cone optimization (NECO) problems. Here, we ask the question "Can smooth equality constraints replace nonlinear exponential cone constraints?". From a practical point of view, even squared slack reformulations in nonlinear programming introduce difficulties. However, such reformulations can be useful for studying optimality conditions. Motivated by this observation, in this work, we use a smooth surjective parameterization of the exponential cone to reformulate NECO as an equality-constrained nonlinear program (RNLP). We then analyze Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) and second-order optimality conditions for NECO through RNLP. Although feasibility is represented exactly, the KKT conditions for RNLP do not in general guarantee those for NECO. We characterize this correspondence through multiplier restrictions that are equivalent to a second-order condition involving only slack variables. We also establish an exact curvature identity showing that RNLP reproduces the sigma term of NECO without additional assumptions. Finally, we prove the relationships between second-order necessary and sufficient conditions for the two problems. We identify when RNLP can be used to rule out local minimizers of NECO or establish strict local optimality for NECO without explicitly evaluating the sigma term.
Group Invariance of Statistical Models and Associated Statistical Manifolds

We study the group invariance of a parameterized statistical model that is closed under push-forward sample transformations given by a group action. We prove that the group action on the sample space induces an isometric action on the associated statistical manifold. Furthermore, it preserves the Fisher-Rao metric as well as the Amari-Chentsov tensor. Moreover, we establish that this isometric action is compatible with equivariant and sufficient statistics in the spirit of the Hall-Wijsman-Ghosh generalized Stein's theorem. This compatibility leads to a novel reduction of the original group-invariant model, where its Fisher information loss is explicitly quantified via conditional expectation. As an application, we apply this framework to a generalized cardioid distribution in circular data analysis, illustrating how the reduced model facilitates estimation and hypothesis testing for relative parameters.
Cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension

We define cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension over fields of characteristic zero, extending the definition for curves by Grothendieck. Our notion of cuspidal sections is defined relative to a normal crossings compactification. We prove that the closure of the resulting set is independent of the choice of a compactification. For varieties iteratively constructed from fibrations, we compare our definition to an inductive notion of cuspidal sections, and discuss connections to the section conjecture of Grothendieck.
Slim Polygons, Hyperbolicity, and a new Quasi-Isometric Invariant

We introduce the slimness function, $\mathrm{Slim}_X(n)$, of a geodesic metric space, which records the maximal slimness of its geodesic polygons as a function of the number of sides. We study the large-scale behaviour of this function and its relation to hyperbolicity, growth function, and quasi-isometries. We first establish that the slimness function is a natural quasi-isometric invariant in the hyperbolic setting. We then obtain quantitative estimates for geodesic polygons in hyperbolic spaces and bounded-valency graphs. In particular, we show that sufficiently slow growth of the slimness function forces tree-like geometry. We also prove a decomposition result for trees of hyperbolic spaces. We show that for a finitely generated hyperbolic group $G$ there are only two possibilities: either $G$ is virtually free and $\operatorname{Slim}_G$ is bounded, or $\operatorname{Slim}_G(n)\simeq\log n$. Finally, we investigate the interaction between polygonal slimness and the growth of connected bounded-valency graphs. Combining the resulting estimates with large-scale dimension theory, we obtain criteria implying that an unbounded graph has asymptotic dimension one.
Quantitative group testing with a fixed shore: sharp asymptotics and exact formulas

We study adaptive quantitative group testing with one defective item in each of two disjoint sets. When one set has fixed size, we determine the leading term of the difference between the binary bound and the largest searchable opposite set size. The result extends to fixed unions of complete bipartite graphs and to positive weighted sums of the opposite set sizes. We determine exact eventual formulas when the fixed set has six, seven or eight items. The eight-item formula has a period-three correction. We explain this correction by optimizing the sizes of shared test pieces within fixed decision-tree prefixes. For each fixed finite family of such prefixes ending in star forests, the optimal deficit is eventually a rational polynomial plus a bounded periodic function. The asymptotic proofs are analytic; the exact formulas also use integer constructions and rational exclusion certificates.
Characterization of Attenuated V-Line Transform and Direct Reconstruction from Samples

The V-line transform (V-LT), a generalized Radon transform (RT), is widely used in Compton scattering imaging (CSI). The central mathematical problem of CSI is to reconstruct a function from its V-LT. Unlike V-LT, the attenuated V-line transform (AV-LT) accounts for the medium-induced loss of intensity, and has been demonstrated to improve image quality. The present paper makes two main contributions. (1) We establish the fundamental characterizations for AV-LT including operator properties ($L^2$-boundedness, operator norm etc.), a necessary and sufficient condition for the preservation of compact support, and sharp estimation of Sobolev smoothness. These characterizations remain unexplored, and they reveal essential differences among AV-LT, RT and V-LT. (2) We develop a direct reconstruction method based on AV-LT samples that does not require solving any equation. Our sampling formula gives exact reconstruction for band-limited functions. We also provide approximate reconstruction for functions in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ with $s>2$.
Claw-free minimal factor-critical and bicritical graphs
Huaibin Zhou; Mingyang Guo; Xiumei Wang

A graph $G$ is called $k$-factor-critical if $G-S$ has a perfect matching for every subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|=k$, and is minimal if $G-e$ is not $k$-factor-critical for every edge $e$ of $G$. The cases $k=1$ and $k=2$ correspond to factor-critical and bicritical graphs, respectively. In this paper, we obtain complete structural characterizations of claw-free minimal factor-critical graphs and claw-free minimal bicritical graphs. The former is characterized by ear decompositions. For the latter, we first characterize the $3$-connected case using the theory of line graphs and then extend the characterization to the general case by a suitable $2$-sum operation.
Complete uniqueness for two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows

Alt, Caffarelli and Friedman established the existence of two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows in [Asymmetric jet flows. Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 35, 29--68, 1982]. In their formulation, the constant fluid speed $λ$ on the free boundaries and the downstream asymptotic angle $θ$ are selected as part of the solution. In this paper, we prove that the asymmetric jet is unique for a prescribed nozzle and mass flux. We first establish the strict vertical monotonicity of the stream function $u$ and introduce the partial hodograph coordinates $ξ=x$ and $η=u(x,y)$, which map every fluid domain onto the same fixed strip. Under this framework, each jet is characterized by a height function $y=h(ξ,η)$, which determines the vertical position along the streamline $u=η$ at horizontal coordinate $ξ$. By analyzing the difference between the height functions of two candidate jets on this strip, we derive an elliptic equation with Dirichlet conditions on the fixed walls and conormal conditions on the free boundaries. Combining these mixed boundary conditions with the asymptotic behaviors, we first establish the uniqueness of the free-boundary fluid speed $λ$. For the resulting common speed, a local perturbation of the height function near a nozzle endpoint, together with the maximum principle, proves that the two height functions must coincide. Inverting the partial hodograph transformation then establishes the uniqueness of the physical jet.
Hausdorff dimension of planar box-like self-affine sets with rotations
Antti Käenmäki; R. Dániel Prokaj; Károly Simon; Sascha Troscheit

We study the Hausdorff dimension of proximal planar self-affine sets whose defining maps have diagonal or anti-diagonal linear parts, with both types present. Such systems are irreducible but not strongly irreducible. Under a projective exponential separation condition, we show that the Hausdorff dimension equals the minimum of $2$ and the affinity dimension, thereby extending the dimension formula of Hochman--Rapaport to all proximal irreducible planar systems. When the affinity dimension is at most an explicit threshold determined by the Lyapunov exponents, the formula holds assuming only that there are no exact overlaps. Above the threshold, it holds under the strong open set condition. These dimension formulae are proved by approximation with finite diagonal subsystems. Assuming projective exponential separation, we also determine the pointwise dimensions of the coordinate projections of the equilibrium state. Below the threshold, the projections are not exact-dimensional: the pointwise dimension of each exists almost everywhere and takes exactly two values, each on a set of positive measure. At or above the threshold, both projections are exact-dimensional with dimension one.
Ore-degree conditions for matchings in uniform hypergraphs

Let $σ_r(\mathcal{H})$ be the minimum sum of vertex degrees over all nonedges of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ on $n$ vertices. Balogh, Palmer and Raeisi conjectured that $n>2rs$ and $σ_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ imply the existence of a matching of size $s$ in $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that, for every fixed $r\ge3$ and all sufficiently large $s$, $σ_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ forces an $s$-matching whenever $n\ge rs+\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$. A complete $r$-graph on $rs-1$ vertices together with $\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$ isolated vertices shows that the vertex bound is sharp for all sufficiently large $s$. By adding new vertices to $\mathcal{H}$, retaining all its edges, and adding every $r$-set containing at least one new vertex as an edge, we also deduce that $n\ge rs+C$ suffices under the same degree condition for every $s\ge1$, where $C$ is a finite constant depending only on $r$. For $r=3$, we provide the explicit sufficient order $n\ge\lceil(7s+11)/2\rceil$ for $s\ge6$, together with bounds for $2\le s\le5$, establishing the conjecture in this uniformity. For $s=2$, we improve the known sufficient order $2r+2$ to $2r+1$ for every $r\ge3$ and show that this order is best possible.
Cable Knot Counterexamples to the All-Knot Volume Conjecture

Let $E$ be the figure-eight knot and let $V$ be the hyperbolic volume of its exterior. We study the reduced colored Jones polynomial at $q=e^{2πi/N}$ for the $(p,w)$-cable of the connected sum of $d\ge 2$ copies of $E$, where $w\ge 2$ and $p,w$ are coprime. The normalized logarithmic growth rate converges to the JSJ volume $dV$ along colors coprime to $2w$, and its upper limit along colors sharing a divisor with $w$ is at most $V$. Thus the $(1,2)$-cable of $E\#E$ violates the full-sequence volume limit for knots. The $(1,3)$-cable of the same companion shows that convergence can fail even along all odd colors. The separation comes from the multiples of $N$ in the exact cabling sum and a uniform first-derivative estimate for the other companion colors.
Fair Selection of Generalized Nash Equilibria: A Comparability Perspective
Sophie Hall; Heinrich H. Nax; Saverio Bolognani

Generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems model self-interested agents coupled through their costs and shared constraints, and arise throughout control applications that allocate a scarce common resource. Such problems typically admit a continuum of equilibria, so any implementation must \emph{select} one. This selection is not neutral: it decides how the cost of the shared constraint is distributed among the agents, a decision often expected to be fair. The variational GNE (v-GNE), which charges all agents a uniform shadow price, is the conventional choice and is frequently advocated as fair. Through the lens of \emph{comparability} from social choice theory, we show that the GNE set itself requires no inter-agent comparability of costs, whereas the v-GNE implicitly assumes cardinal unit comparability, one of the stronger notions. We then introduce the fair GNE (f-GNE), which selects an equilibrium by explicitly optimizing a fairness metric matched to the comparability at hand, and give constructive routes to compute it for single-constraint and linear-quadratic games. An electric-vehicle charging game serves as a running example throughout this self-contained tutorial.
Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations

Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. Motivated by the principle of gradient equidistribution from the stretching approach in grid generation, which redistributes solution gradients to reduce functional complexity, we propose Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which incorporate learnable coordinate transformations to map the physical domain into a computational domain where the physical solutions become approximately affine, making them easier for neural networks to learn. We propose two constructions of the transformation: an explicit construction based on Majorants and an implicit construction based on invertable neural networks. Experimentally, the explicit construction can improve accuracy for PDEs with available explicit coordinate transformations, and the implicit construction can be combined with other advanced PINN models as an efficient plug-in module to improve performance across a range of challenging PDE benchmarks.

We show that $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$ contains an infinite family of Zariski-dense subgroups isomorphic to the fundamental group of a fixed closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, which are pairwise noncommensurable up to conjugacy.
Resolvent-Diagonal Energy of Isospectral Jacobi Matrices

We study the minimum squared resolvent diagonal among Jacobi matrices with prescribed eigenvalues. For the zeros of $P_n^{(α,β)}$, we construct a canonical realization and bound its asymptotic cost against the optimum. Its rescaled inverse converges to the Green operator of a reflection-symmetric singular Schrödinger operator with Bessel-zero spectrum. A Green-coordinate identity places this construction and all finite realizations in the same density framework. Mass-constrained spectral problems then give computable lower bounds. The bounds meet at $α=1/2$, with optimal energy $2/15$, and have first-order contact with derivative $-13/75$. We classify the constrained extremal profiles and the three endpoint geometries of the canonical density. Two polynomial families with the same limiting edge spectrum have different limiting optimal energies. For Nesterov momentum $(s-1)/(s+1)$, the optimal leading endpoint Hessian-drift gain among nonnegative-link Jacobi realizations is $\sqrt{2}$ times the original gain. An explicit isospectral flow strictly improves the standard one-sided realization for $α>-1/2$, $α\ne1/2$.
Asymptotic stability of high-index saddle dynamics
Baoming Shi; Lei Zhang; Xiangcheng Zheng; Shangqin Zhu

High-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) has been extensively adopted to compute saddle points of arbitrary index, with various applications such as constructing solution landscapes of complex systems. In this work, we prove the asymptotic stability of various HiSD methods, including the idealized, perturbed, and coupled HiSD methods, as well as their momentum-accelerated variants. The analysis is Jacobian-free and thus compensates for the linear stability analysis in the literature. The results not only provide specific characterizations for the convergence rate and the basin of attraction, but also reveal intrinsic correlations among dynamics in the coupled HiSD. Theoretical results are substantiated by numerical experiments.
The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
Lei Liu; Pedro A. S. Salomão

We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The main result of this paper is a construction of an inductive process that can replace Feynman diagrams. Combining this result with the notion of the L-functional, one can give an exposition of QED that does not suffer from infrared divergences

Constrained Nested-Logit Pricing: An Exact Reformulation and Global Optimization Method

This structure makes the number of nests, rather than products, govern the exponent in a conditional worst-case complexity bound. In synthetic experiments, the method certifies solutions for assortments of up to 500 products with few nests. Infinitely many convex polytopes with dihedral angles bounded above by $π/2+δ$

For every $δ>0$, we construct infinitely many pairwise combinatorially distinct convex three-dimensional polytopes whose dihedral angles are all less than $π/2+δ$.

Perfect wave transfer (PWT) reproduces spatial reflection at a common finite time under a fixed Hamiltonian. In the single-charge model, the first two notions coincide. Global transfer additionally requires rephasing of the compact zero mode. For regular reflection-symmetric channels, exact oscillator transfer forces an odd multiple of the optical crossing time and a strictly ordered, parity-compatible spectrum differing from the conformal ladder at only finitely many levels. This spectral condition is also sufficient when the Robin boundary data induced by the physical profile are included. Requiring Neumann conditions after the Liouville transformation instead forces conformality. We construct an explicit, regular one-defect family for every $r>1/2$. Its transfer parameters are precisely the reduced fractions $r=p/q$ with odd numerator and denominator, with shortest transfer time $pL/v_0$. At the delay $3L/v_0$, the $r=3/5$ profile has numerical contrast $K_{\max}/K_{\min}\simeq 12.913$, compared with $81$ for $r=3$. Two independent conservative discretizations show second-order convergence on fixed mode bands. Occupation- and charge-constrained error estimates quantify robustness, while an exact homogeneous-chain calculation explains the $J^{2/3}$ resolved-band scale also observed in the engineered channels. These results provide a spectral design method and finite-device benchmarks for quadratic quantum channels. An interacting microscopic realization remains open.

Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite and self-dual vertex operator algebra of CFT type, and let $G$ be a finite cyclic automorphism group of $V$. We establish a twisted Verlinde formula for cyclic groups of arbitrary finite order, expressing fusion coefficients among twisted $V$-modules in terms of the $S$-matrix in the orbifold theory. The main objective is to quantify modeling and discretization errors in terms of the nonlocal horizon, the mesh size, the Sobolev regularity of the local solution, and the compatibility of boundary data. We apply the framework to two constant-horizon nonlocal Laplacians with exterior boundary data and to heterogeneous localization models with classical Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions. The resulting estimates provide quantitative guarantees of asymptotic compatibility and improve existing error bounds under weaker regularity assumptions. Walsh analysis connects ordered Fourier convergence, summability, nonlinear approximation, and universal representation through a common character algebra. This survey examines developments from 2000-2026 against their classical foundations. Binary kernel geometry explains Hardy-space losses and summability thresholds; interval and packet methods control spectral selection; localized blocks produce correction and universal representations with distinct coefficient and exceptional-set requirements. Selected proofs and counterexamples compare these mechanisms and identify where an implication needs an additional hypothesis. The same distinctions organize digital integration, sparse measurements, Boolean spectra, and generalized Walsh bases. Quantitative thresholds, source conventions, and published theorem pointers are collected in comparative tables. The concluding problems separate source-listed questions, proposed refinements, and elementary obstructions. Supplementary derivations preserve normalization checks and finite covariance calculations while keeping the main exposition focused on the analytic mechanisms.
Critical Resonance and the Radial Branch in Maz'ya's Weighted Hessian--Gradient Inequality

We study the sharp constant $C(p,γ)$ in Maz'ya's planar weighted inequality \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|\nablaψ|^p|x|^{p(γ-1)}\, \mathrm{d} x \le C(p,γ)\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|D^2ψ|_{\mathrm{F}}^p|x|^{pγ}\, \mathrm{d} x, \] where $|\cdot|_{\mathrm{F}}$ denotes the Frobenius norm. An explicit example shows that global symmetry breaking can occur even when this second variation is nonnegative.

We establish the binary Goldbach conjecture which asserts that every even positive integer greater than four can be expressed as a sum of two odd primes. This goal is achieved by proving that the number of ordered Goldbach pairs that add up to $2n$ is an $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{n}{\ln^{2} n}\right)$ function. As an application, we provide a simpler verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture that was first established in [6,7].
Supporting Data Center Grid Integration via Co-Optimized Battery Energy Storage Sizing and Capacity Allocation

Interconnecting large data centers can be delayed by grid requirements on demand flexibility, ramping limits, and ride-through performance. This paper proposes an optimization-based framework to size a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) that accelerates data center grid integration by providing BESS capacity required to meet selected flexibility and grid-support requirements. The model co-optimizes BESS power rating and energy capacity while allocating capability across three services: (i) demand response over a specified duration, (ii) mitigation of high-magnitude, high-frequency load fluctuations through reserved active power with zero net state-of-charge change, and (iii) voltage support via reactive power capability at the point of common coupling. A case study using a real data center load profile demonstrates the proposed method and quantifies the BESS power-energy requirements and operational trade-offs needed to satisfy the multi-service constraints, providing practical guidance for interconnection planning and deployment.
A Trivalent Graph of Girth 14 and Order 372

The smallest known trivalent graph of girth 14 is constructed. The graph has 372 vertices, improving the old upper bound of 384 \cite{exoo14}. The construction uses methods that may be new to this problem.
Finite-rank Toeplitz commutators on the harmonic Bergman space

We determine the sharp condition for local superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation $(-Δ)^m u=u^{\frac{n+2m}{n-2m}}$, where $m\geq2$ is an integer and $n>2m$. For a solution in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at zero, local superharmonicity holds if and only if \(\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)>0\). The threshold is sharp. In the biharmonic case $m=2$, for every $n\geq5$, we construct smooth positive solutions of $Δ^2u=u^{\frac{n+4}{n-4}}$ in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at $0$, satisfying $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)=0$ and $\limsup_{x\to0}u(x)=+\infty$, while $-Δu$ converges to a finite negative limit along a fixed ray. The construction relies on an infinite array of concentrating bubbles arranged on concentric polygons, with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction controlling their interactions against a vanishing background.

Vector approximate message passing (VAMP) often fails to converge on ill-conditioned matrices, and its damping factor is tuned either manually or adaptively. Using the fact that VAMP iterations are the discretization of an electric circuit, we show that the denoiser and the likelihood act as nonlinear resistors, the Onsager correction is a mirror resistor and damping is a lag filter. This circuit gives a closed-form loop gain whose spectrum can predict when VAMP fails. Because a lag filter cannot isolate the oscillating modes, we add a lead capacitor whose design often results in a negative capacitance. Across a wide range of condition numbers, our proposed damping strategy achieves a higher convergence rate than adaptive damping and Anderson acceleration at a lower mean iteration cost. On ill-conditioned multipath channels, across ranks and sparsity levels, it also converges more reliably than existing damping baselines.
Power Mean, Karcher Mean, and Log-Euclidean Mean on Positive Constant Upper Triangular Matrices

Building on the general triangular-group theory, we use the central decomposition CP_n \cong \mathbb R_+ -by-UP_n to separate the scalar power mean from a unipotent mean with reweighted coefficients. Finite nilpotent functional calculus yields concise formulas on CP_2 and CP_3, where the Karcher and log-Euclidean means coincide. In every dimension, the same commutator is the leading term of their small-dispersion difference.
The splitting type of jet bundles on the projective line
