Given a vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on a smooth variety X, one can associate to it its jet bundles, or bundles of principal parts. These bundles encode the Taylor expansions of local sections of $\mathcal{E}$ and arise naturally in the study of differential operators. When $X=\mathbb{P}^1$ is the projective line, jet bundles decompose as direct sums of line bundles, making it natural to study their splitting types. The splitting type is well understood in characteristic zero, but exhibits subtler behavior in positive characteristic. Our goal is to give a complete answer in every positive characteristic, and in particular to provide a characterization of semistability for jet bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$. We also determine their extremal summands and give applications to differential operators and formulas for cohomology of line bundles on infinitesimal thickenings of the diagonal.
Polynomial complexity, random graphs, and strict ergodicity
Be'eri Greenfeld; Paul-Henry Leemann; Carlos Gustavo Moreira; Efim Zelmanov

We construct infinite words $w$ whose complexity functions are quadratically bounded, but whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, resolving a question of Cassaigne. Moreover, we construct infinite words of polynomially bounded complexity, and subshifts of quasi-linear complexity, whose discrete derivatives do not decay compared to their complexity functions, thus exhibiting a typical exponentially-growing behavior. As an application, we give the first examples of subshifts of polynomial complexity whose Rauzy graphs do not have Benjamini-Schramm limits. Finally, we realize (up to an inevitable linear error factor) every function satisfying the necessary conditions, as the complexity function of a minimal, uniquely ergodic, cube-free subshift, strengthening previous realization results in this direction, and derive consequences for the growth of simple algebras and just-infinite semigroups satisfying nontrivial laws.
Joint Approximation and the Mixed-Prime Character Group

For the integer metric defined by the square denominators of two distinct primes, we prove simultaneous approximation to zero in one prime metric and to any prescribed integer in the other. A normalized convolution argument gives a uniform central spectral bound. Random relative translations of smooth weights produce an exact positive cas cade; Fourier positivity places every normalized finer convolution below its value at zero. A far-field recursion, the growth of merged square powers, and a two-term logarithmic-form estimate give summable fac tor bounds. Consequently, for every fixed pair of distinct primes p,q, the mixed continuous character group is Z[1/(pq)]/Z: no irrational pa rameter is continuous. The mixed completion is the product of the one-prime completions. For each fixed pair this also gives a compati ble rational join and a strictly finer compatible join of the associated real TVG topologies, with the same prescribed real character group. Exact witness search terminates at every strict precision and integer target. We retain the structural, density, divisibility, sequence and finite-certificate results leading to this proof. The existence argument does not give practical witness-size or runtime bounds, and it does not assume independence or equidistribution of the two digit systems. Se lected abstract components have been checked using Lean and Mathlib; the complete analytic argument has not been formalized. The corre sponding problem for three or more primes remains separate.
Disjointness preserving operators on Köthe-Banach spaces

A well-known result of Abramovich says that if $E$, $F$ are rearrangement invariant Banach spaces on a finite atomless measure space such that $E$ has an absolutely continuous norm and $E\not\subseteq F$, then there are no nonzero disjointness preserving bounded linear operators $T \colon E\to F$. Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalize the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including a general axial condition that allows for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behavior of matter. A Poincare-Einstein Liouville Theorem and the Yamabe Invariant of Lens Spaces

Schoen conjectured that the Yamabe invariant of every lens space is achieved by the round metric. A proof of this conjecture is presented for all lens spaces, together with rigidity: equality is only achieved for the round class. The key step is to show that every $\mathbb Z_p$-invariant Yamabe-positive conformal class on $S^3$ admits a $\mathbb Z_p$-equivariant Poincaré-Einstein filling. The distance function from a fixed point of the filling then gives an invariant test function with Yamabe quotient at most $σ(S^3)$, which descends to the lens space. The proof of the main theorem was generated by AI (ChatGPT Astra, September 2026); this is mainly a learning note of the AI generated proof.

In recent years, the Schur products of linear codes have been extensively studied due to their favorable applications in cryptography. Let $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ be two narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes with designed distances $δ_{1}$ and $δ_{2}$, respectively, where $2\le δ_{1},δ_{2}\le n$. Let $\mathcal{C}_1\star\mathcal{C}_2$ be the Schur product of $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$. Furthermore, we determine the dimensions of these products and lower bounds on their minimum distance. Several linear codes with best known parameters are found.

Let $ϕ$ be an elliptic univalent self-map of the unit disc in the complex plane that is not an automorphism, with multiplier $0<|λ|<1$ at its Denjoy--Wolff point. We establish exact support recovery and show that post-screening factor re-estimation converts the weak-loading problem into a pervasive one relative to the retained dimensions, yielding sharper convergence rates under substantially weaker dimensional growth conditions and consistent factor-number determination. We illustrate the gains obtained by the response-guided factor construction with two empirical applications.

Consequently, it has been shown that do-calculus is both sound and complete in these problems. Despite these well-established results, a formal definition of what it means for the do-calculus to be complete does not exist. We propose a rigorous formalization for the completeness of the do-calculus and show that the completeness results in previous work remain valid. However, for more general problems, such as uID, the rules of do-calculus are no longer complete. This is perhaps the reason why the uID problem has remained open thus far.

We further study the set $V_g^p$ and characterize the coincidence of the holomorphic optimal domains.

We also give a purely topological-analytic proof of the theorem.
Reflections of Nichols algebras in braided monoidal categories

Let $\C$ be an essentially small abelian rigid braided monoidal category. We prove a reflection theorem for Nichols algebras in $\Ind(\C)$ and show that tuples admitting all reflections define connected semi-Cartan graphs. As applications, we prove that a finite Nichols algebra has a generating object of length at most one in $PSU(2)_k$ for odd $k\ge3$, in $SU(2)_{4m}$ for $m\ge1$, and in the representation categories of the Virasoro minimal models $\mathcal M(2,p)$ for odd $p\ge5$. In all three families, we prove that every finite pre-Nichols algebra is a Nichols algebra.
Feng Dai; Egor Kosov; Noel Murasko

For $p>2$ and an $N$-dimensional subspace $X\subset L_\infty(μ)$ satisfying \[ \|f\|_\infty\le (KN)^{1/p}\|f\|_{L_p(μ)} \quad\forall f\in X, \] we show that $m\ge C(p)KN \bigl(\varepsilon^{-p} +\varepsilon^{-2}\log_2(2N)\bigr)$ independent samples $ξ^1,\ldots,ξ^m$ with distribution $μ$ satisfy \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(ξ^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \quad\forall f\in X \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c(p)\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This gives the optimal sample-size order $N\log_2 N$ for independent random sampling with fixed $K$, $p$, and $\varepsilon$. This result follows from a more general empirical moment estimate over unit balls of $p$-convex norms.
Slice Regular Capacity and Rational Approximation
Thankarajan Prasad; Rincy Susan Raju; Enose Shine Lal

Approximation theory in the complex plane is a well established area of mathematical research, with extensive contributions documented in the literature, notably through the classical results of Weierstrass, Runge, Mergelyan, and Vitushkin. Approximation theory in quaternionic settings, particularly rational approximation on compact sets, which studies when slice regular functions can be uniformly approximated by rational functions, is one of the recent areas of interest in quaternionic rational approximation theory (See [6,13]). In this paper, we discuss Vitushkin approximation theorem in the quaternionic setting by using the quaternionic analogue of analytic capacity and also we establish Davies modified Vitushkin scheme in quaternionic setting. We also discuss quaternionic analogue of $γ_{+}$- capacity and Cauchy capacity and the remarkable results of Tolsa [35] and Younsi [45] related to these capacities in complex plane setting.
A counterexample to Manin's Conjecture for almost Fano varieties

We give an example of a smooth rational threefold over a number field with a big anticanonical divisor that does not satisfy the thin set version of Manin's Conjecture. In particular, Manin's Conjecture does not hold for rationally connected almost Fano varieties.
Generalized Edge Ideals and Regularity Offset of Graphs
Grigoriy Blekherman; Jiaheng Li; Jianuo Zhou

We introduce generalized edge ideals by assigning pairwise coprime monomials, instead of variables, to the vertices of a graph. We use the lcm-lattice to show that the multigraded Betti numbers and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the quotient by a generalized edge ideal agree with the Betti numbers and resolution regularity of the quotient by an ordinary edge ideal in a non-standard Z-grading. We define the regularity offset as a measurement of the difference between the regularities of the quotients by a generalized edge ideal and its ordinary counterpart, and prove bounds for the regularity offset. We compute the regularity offset for co-chordal graphs and paths, and derive a formula for the regularity offset of forests. We also derive a graph-theoretic criterion for when a forest's regularity offset is always zero, or equivalently, its top-level Betti number is nonzero.
On nonlocal geometric rigidity estimates in bounded uniform domains

We prove fractional geometric rigidity estimates and fractional Korn's first inequalities with general singular weights in bounded uniform domains in $\mathbb R^n.$ The classical choice of the energy well $SO(n)$ for the geometric rigidity estimate fails due to the lack of a notion of orientation for Lebesgue fields. The remedy is to choose $O(n)$ as the energy well. Due to the recently developed theory of local-to-nonlocal passage of rigidity estimates developed by the first author, both estimates reduce to the analogous local estimates on the cube, which we prove in several steps by compactness and linearization arguments.
KAM theory for quasi-periodic equilibrium of generalized Frenkel-Kontorova model in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$

We extend the KAM theory for one dimensional Frenkel-Kontorova model to multidimensional case in quasi-periodic media. By using the quasi-Newton method, we reduce the linearized operator with quasi-periodic coefficient in the Nash-Moser iteration to the composition of two diagonal operators and a near-identity operator, such that the small divisor problem can be overcome by imposing the simultaneous Diophantine condition. In contrast, we also discuss the application of Craig-Wayne-Bourgain method to the quasi-periodic equilibrium problem.
Reweighting for Transfer Classification: Exact Risk Conversion and Minimax Adaptation

A source can make a training mixture easier to learn while making its accuracy less valuable for the target. We study how the training problem a source creates and the finite-sample error of learning it jointly determine target-risk guarantees under reweighting. For binary classification, for each pair of laws and each positive target weight, we derive the sharpest target excess hinge-risk bound implied by mixture excess alone, uniformly over clipped predictors. This exact conversion curve is determined by density-weighted local votes. A two-sample oracle inequality for weighted support vector machines supplies the mixture excess, and the composition becomes explicit for Gaussian kernels. On a tilted-boundary class, we establish the all-procedure minimax classification rate $[n+s_+^2/(m^{-1}+τ^2)]^{-1}$ in the transferable strength $s_+$ and the tilt $τ$, separating source sampling uncertainty ($m^{-1}$) from relation uncertainty ($τ^2$). A target-checked Gaussian-SVM selector adapts to unknown $s_+$ and $τ$ up to a logarithmic factor for fixed dimension, and retains the target-only rate up to the same factor against arbitrary independent sources under the stated target model. On a separate smooth opposition class, the minimax risk within the family of exact Gaussian SVMs fitted to the original labels with nonnegative weights is exponentially larger than the unrestricted minimax risk whenever the target sample is at most half the source sample, despite arbitrary data-dependent weighting and tuning. The value of a source thus depends on the training problem it creates, on what accuracy there means for the target, and on whether the permitted use of the source can implement the needed correction.

We prove that every signed planar graph $\widehat G$ of negative girth at least $\ell\geq 3$ satisfies $χ_c(\widehat G)<\frac{2\ell}{\ell-2}$. As a consequence, for every integer $k\geq 1$, every planar graph $G$ of odd girth at least $4k+3$ satisfies $χ_c(G)<\frac{2k+1}{k}$ and hence admits a homomorphism to $C_{2k+1}$. Our proofs build on recent results of Jafari on circular flows. In particular, Jafari proved that every $(4k+2)$-edge-connected graph has circular flow number strictly less than $2+\frac{1}{k}$. We revisit his theorem, providing an alternative proof that emphasizes the underlying graph-theoretic ideas. We also extend the result to signed graphs and weaken the connectivity assumption by imposing a lower bound only on the size of negative cuts. The key step is a small-correction lemma associated with a distribution on spanning trees. A splitting argument first gives the required correction in an even-degree graph; doubling the edges removes the degree-parity assumption. Plane duality then gives the coloring theorem. We discuss tightness of bounds in the end.
Synchronized Optimal Transport Reconstructs Coupled Transcriptomic and Chromatin Dynamics
Jingfeng Wang; Yanxiang Zhao; Qing Nie; Zixuan Cang

Single-cell RNA and ATAC data collected across developmental stages provide time-course snapshots of transcriptional and regulatory states. Since sequencing is destructive, trajectories between these snapshots must be inferred from independently sampled cell populations. Existing approaches typically infer continuous dynamics in a single modality or integrate RNA and ATAC in a shared representation. Here we present Cross-Omics Aligned Trajectory Inference (COATI), which extends unbalanced synchronized dynamical optimal transport to time-dependent cross-modal maps for reconstructing coupled trajectories in distinct RNA and ATAC state spaces. We evaluated COATI on synthetic benchmarks and four developmental datasets using held-out-stage reconstruction and lineage analyses. COATI improved reconstruction of cell populations at held-out stages, including recovery of chromatin-state heterogeneity within cell types, and better preserved developmental lineage relationships. The unbalanced formulation allows the inference of population mass changes, which were shown to associate with DNA-replication programs at early stages and lineage-maturation programs later in development. The coupled trajectories enabled analysis of lineage-specific transcriptional and chromatin changes and their temporal relationships during development. Lineage responses inferred by COATI agreed with independent CRISPR perturbation results, and the inferred regulatory patterns were consistent with independent epigenetic data.
Plus Constructions and Canonical Induction for Green Categories

We develop canonical induction for Green categories associated with Mackey systems. We establish a change-of-rings framework in which the lower-plus and upper-plus constructions are realized by induction and coinduction of modules. The two plus adjunctions yield the mark morphism, and, when the relevant group orders are invertible in the coefficient ring, Möbius inversion gives an explicit inverse. Using the resulting linearization and tom Dieck maps, we construct a canonical induction map, give an explicit formula for it, and characterize when it is a right inverse of linearization. In the classical setting of Mackey functors, our construction and splitting criterion recover Boltje's results.
Prosenjit Bose; Bobby Miraftab; Tyler Tuttle

Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane, and let $C$ be a compact, convex subset of the plane that contains the origin in its interior. We study the problem of finding two points $p$ and $q$ of $P$ with the property that any homothet of $C$ that contains $p$ and $q$ must contain at least a constant fraction of the points of $P$. We give proofs for several cases. When $C$ is strictly convex we achieve a fraction of $1/5$, and when $C$ is a general convex region we achieve a fraction of $1/6e$. We show how the ideas of this second bound can be used to prove a lower bound for a version of the problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $C$ is a $d$-ball. We also consider a few special cases. When $C$ is a triangle we get a lower bound of $1/12$, and when we allow that triangle to be rotated by $π$ radians in addition to being scaled and translated we get a lower bound of $1/768$. In proving this last result, we improve the state of the art on the version of this problem in three dimensions, where $C$ is a parallelepiped. We also consider the algorithmic aspects of finding such a pair of points.
Beyond the Lower-Star Filtration: Alternative Filtration Methods for Persistent Homology

In the lower-star filtration (LSF), simplices are assigned filtration values according to the maximum-vertex rule, with each simplex entering the filtration when its highest-valued vertex appears. A limitation of this construction is that some higher-dimensional simplices may enter simultaneously with their boundary faces, causing certain topological features to be filled immediately upon formation and thus not appear in the resulting persistence diagram. To address this limitation, we propose three alternative filtration methods: the \(\varepsilon\)-lower-star filtration (ELSF), the \(L_p\) filtration (LpF), and the softmax filtration (SMF). {ELSF introduces a dimension-dependent delay to the maximum-vertex rule,} allowing higher-dimensional simplices to enter the filtration after their boundary faces, whereas {LpF and SMF use aggregation functions that depend on all vertex values rather} than solely on their maximum. By modifying how filtration values are assigned, these methods allow simplices to enter the filtration more progressively, so that topological features such as loops and voids may persist over longer filtration intervals rather than being filled immediately. Consequently, the resulting persistence diagrams may include persistence features that are not observed under LSF, potentially providing useful information for distinguishing data populations. Experimental results on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed filtration methods are computationally efficient and can provide greater sensitivity to structural differences in the data than LSF.
An improved isodiametric inequality for convex surfaces

Alexandrov conjectured that every closed convex surface of area $A$ and intrinsic diameter $D$ satisfies $A/D^2\leqπ/2$. Using an averaging argument over the curvature measure, we prove that every closed convex surface satisfies $A/D^2\leq2π/3$, improving the best previously known bound.
Differentiation of tepui groupoids and the holonomy groupoid of singular foliations
Alfonso Garmendia; David Miyamoto; Leonid Ryvkin

Tepui groupoids are a generalization of Lie groupoids which allow the arrow space to be singular, as is the case for holonomy groupoids of singular foliations. We construct a Lie differentiation functor for a large class of tepui groupoids. When restricted to effective and source-connected tepui groupoids, this differentiation recovers the correspondence between holonomy groupoids and their underlying singular foliations.
Reflexive polytopes can have doubly exponentially many vertices

Reflexive polytopes are lattice polytopes containing the origin in their interior such that also the dual polytope is a lattice polytope. On the basis of low-dimensional observations and of bounds known for special classes of reflexive polytopes, the second author conjectured in 2004 that the number of vertices of $d$-dimensional reflexive polytopes is bounded from above by $6^{d/2}$. In this note, we present counterexamples showing that this conjecture is false in every dimension $d \ge 8$. In fact, rather surprisingly, in sufficiently large dimensions $d$ the number of vertices (equivalently, by duality, the number of facets) can be as large as theoretically possible, namely doubly exponential in $d$. These results were found using GPT-6.1 Sol.
Multilevel kernel approximation of log-Euclidean manifold-valued functions

We study kernel approximation and multilevel residual correction for functions with values in a manifold that admits a global logarithm onto a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, such as positive definite matrices, exponential Lie groups, and Hadamard manifolds. Approximating in logarithmic coordinates keeps the approximant on the manifold and transfers Hilbert-space error estimates verbatim. To express these errors in the natural geometry of the target, we prove metric comparisons. In particular, we obtain a sharp, scale-invariant bound between the log-Euclidean and affine-invariant distances on positive definite matrices, with a constant that depends only on condition numbers. For multilevel approximation, compactly supported kernels scaled to the fill distance give algebraic convergence with sparse, uniformly well-conditioned systems. These guarantees require appropriate sample locations and approximation scales. Compact groups are treated through a principal logarithm, where a bi-invariant metric gives error bounds with constant one. Finally, the log-Euclidean and Karcher means differ by $\mathcal O(r^3)$ near the identity and by $\mathcal O(r^2)$ around a general point, where $r$ is the logarithmic data radius and the second bound is sharp.
Bryce Kerr; James Punch; Tim Trudgian

Let $S_χ(N)= \sum_{n\leq N} χ(n)$, where $χ$ is a Dirichlet character modulo a prime $p$. For integral $r\geq 2$, Burgess gave bounds of the shape $S_χ(N) \ll N^{1-1/r} p^{(r+1)/(4r^{2})} \log p$. The factor of $\log p$ was reduced by several authors. We show that it can be removed completely.
Left-Invariant Kernels of the Hodge-de Rham Operator on Three-Dimensional Lorentzian Lie Groups

We determine the kernel of the Hodge--de Rham operator on left-invariant differential forms for the seven customary families of three-dimensional Lorentzian metric Lie algebras. Every parameter stratum is treated, including zero structure constants, singular bracket matrices, and null modular directions. If $θ(X)=\mathrm{tr}\,\mathrm{ad}_X$ is the modular character, the full kernel is the direct sum of constants, the space $K=\mathrm{Ann}([\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{g}])\capθ^\perp$, its Hodge dual, and the volume forms. We give explicit real bases in all seven families and compute the exterior differential and geometric codifferential on every basis form. The non-unimodular calculation remains valid without the customary extra normalization conditions, and hence also covers metric representatives omitted by those conditions. The resulting dimensions are $2,4,6$, or $8$; the two middle-degree dimensions agree. Explicit examples distinguish the kernel of the first-order operator from the kernel of its square. All assertions concern smooth left-invariant forms, with no square-integrability condition.
Galois lines for the maximal curve with the second largest genus in characteristic two

We determine all Galois lines for the embedding of the maximal curve with the second largest genus in characteristic two into $\mathbb{P}^{3}$ induced by its Frobenius linear series. We also determine the associated Galois groups.
Sensing-Based Communication: A Non-Orthogonal Passive Reflection Framework for ISAC
Xin Xiong; Mathew Salas; Sihua Shao; Chen Chen; Mostafa Hassanalian; Rafael Fierro

While integrating uplink without disrupting the primary downlink remains a critical challenge for existing reflective communication systems, this paper proposes a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) mechanism termed Sensing-based Communication. Originating from and validated within an optical retro-reflective system, this mechanism possesses an underlying wave-agnostic architecture with the potential to be generalized across other physical modalities. It leverages incident downlink signals for parasitic modulation via passive tags. By relying solely on fundamental on-off keying (OOK) reflection, the tag unifies the reflective sensing channel and the uplink communication channel, and simultaneously achieves both sensing and duplex communication. Consequently, our approach introduces uplink capability without sacrificing the downlink data rate or consuming additional spectrum resources. At the receiver, we design a joint decoding architecture combining cross-correlation computation and successive interference cancelation (SIC) to fully exploit the degrees of freedom in broadband signals for multi-user interference suppression. We derive closed-form expressions for the interference and bit error rate (BER) assuming zero-mean Gaussian signals. Using an experimental testbed, we validate the pivotal theoretical finding, the scaling relationship of SINR with signal bandwidth and cross-correlation time--where linear regression yields a strong goodness-of-fit with $R^2 = 0.9688$. Furthermore, evaluations under noise-like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms exhibit high consistency between theoretical derivations and simulation data ($R^2 = 0.9372$, mean absolute percentage error, $\text{MAPE} = 14\%$), confirming the model's accuracy and waveform generalizability.
Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras

We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(Λ)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $Λ$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(Λ)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $Λ$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.
On the dynamics of weighted shifts on Fréchet sequence spaces over trees
Mateus Azevedo; Fernando Costa Jr.; João V. A. Pinto

In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fréchet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of Köthe spaces $λ_p(A,V)$, where $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ and $V$ is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces $\ell^p(V)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$, and $c_0(V)$.
Mingcheng Nie; Shuangyang Li; Ruoxi Chong; Giuseppe Caire; Yonghui Li

Conventional channel estimation for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) relies on the pilot interpolation without explicitly identifying the sparse delay-angle (DA) components. To exploit DA sparsity while maintaining backward compatibility with existing MIMO-OFDM systems, we propose a cross-domain channel estimation scheme for multiuser MIMO-OFDM (MU-MIMO-OFDM) systems. The scheme exploits the circular convolution structure in the DA domain to identify candidate DA pairs by correlating delay-domain observations with DA pilot responses. These pairs and the known pilots then define a time-frequency (TF) dictionary for refining the DA coefficients from TF observations through least-squares or sparsity-regularized fitting. The refined coefficients and candidate pairs reconstruct the aggregate channel across antennas and subcarriers aligning with the geometric channel model. Numerical results show approximately 10 dB and 7 dB lower normalized mean-square error than the conventional OFDM estimation schemes for integer and fractional delay and angle indices, respectively.

A Markov operator on a matrix algebra, that is, a unital completely positive map, is called positivity improving if it maps every nonzero positive element to an invertible one. This is the noncommutative counterpart of a stochastic matrix with strictly positive entries. We show that positivity improvement is self-dual and equivalent to a faithful quantum Markov--Dobrushin--Doeblin minorization. We also compare the scalar trace minorization with the optimal common-lower-bound construction of the quantum Markov--Dobrushin coefficient. We then characterize positivity improvement through the Kraus space of the map: a Markov operator is positivity improving if and only if the Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal complement of its Kraus space contains no operator of rank one. As a consequence the Kraus rank of a positivity improving Markov operator on the algebra of $d\times d$ matrices is at least $2d-1$, and an explicit Hankel-type channel shows that this bound is attained in every dimension. Although deciding positivity improvement is NP-hard in general, we obtain complete and effectively checkable classifications for qubits and qutrits, together with families of examples (Pauli, Weyl and Werner--Holevo channels) showing that all our estimates are optimal. Finally we show that, in infinite dimensions, positivity improvement no longer implies any contraction of the Markov operator.
A recursion relation for the coefficients of Swinnerton-Dyer type polynomials

We study a family of polynomials that are very closely related to the Swinnerton-Dyer polynomials. As main result, we determine a recursion relation for the coefficients of this family of polynomials. We briefly explain our own and others' interest in this family of polynomials.
Local contraction of stochastic affine recursions of $\mathbb{R}^d$
Richard Aoun; Sara Brofferio; Marc Peigné

We consider affine stochastic recursions $X^x_{n+1}=A_{n+1}X^x_n+B_{n+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $(B_n,A_n)$ are i.i.d. in $\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with strongly irreducible and proximal linear part. In the critical regime where the top Lyapunov exponent vanishes, we show that the recursion is locally contractive in every direction, yielding uniqueness, up to a positive multiplicative constant, of the $μ$-invariant non-zero Radon measure. This extends to every dimension $d\geq 2$ a result of Babillot-Bougerol-Élie (1997) in dimension one. The proof is based on the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the "joint process" $(X^x_n,X^y_n)$, using geometric and measure-theoretic properties of the diagonal affine action. A key ingredient is an abstract criterion for the total dissipativity of semigroup actions, which we apply to this process.
Proof of the Cordero-Torregrosa Conjecture for Methods with Arbitrary Rules and Its Refinement under Paired Function and Jacobian Evaluations

We study the Cordero--Torregrosa conjecture on the order that can be guaranteed when solving nonlinear systems with prescribed budgets of function and Jacobian evaluations. We consider deterministic, causal, memoryless methods whose rules may be discontinuous, nonmeasurable, or noncomputable. We give an independent proof of a scalar barrier for queries of $f$ and $f'$ by constructing a fixed entire function, a simple root, and a single sequence of initial points that simultaneously exclude every exponent greater than $2^{d-1}$, where $d$ is the maximum number of queries. An exact simulation of vector-valued responses yields the Cordero--Torregrosa inequality $p\le 2^{N_F+N_J-1}$ for function classes containing the analytic test fields. The proof holds for $N_F,N_J\ge 0$, $N_F+N_J\ge 1$, without assuming $N_J\le N_F$; in particular, it covers $N_J>N_F$. Under pairing at the end of the cycle, we obtain the sharper bound $p\le 2^{N_F-s+1}3^{s-1}$, $s=\min\{N_F,N_J\}\ge 1$, without requiring temporal precedence. The proofs use indistinguishable perturbations, kernels of constraints, and a construction that preserves responses while producing a single entire witness. These results are upper bounds on the universal local order of a cycle; they do not establish attainability for every budget.
Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
Erik Brodsky; Leonid O Chekhov; Quanyu Tang

We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.
High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction
Saksham Jain; Guillaume Braun; Masaaki Imaizumi

Reward models used for off-policy evaluation (OPE) are commonly selected using held-out data. When sample size and context dimension grow proportionally, the difference in test risk between models fitted on the full sample and on a fixed fraction of it need not vanish. Held-out evaluation can therefore consistently estimate the test risk of the model trained on the smaller sample, but because the relative ranking of candidate reward models can change after full-data refitting, held-out selection can be suboptimal. We develop an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion that estimates the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk under the target policy using only its training observations. This enables early stopping along the full-data gradient-descent trajectory without sample splitting. For neural networks with fixed depth and hidden width under Gaussian contexts, single-index rewards, context-dependent multi-index target policies, and known context-independent logging, we prove uniform consistency of our criterion over a fixed finite set of gradient-descent iterates and a near-oracle guarantee for the selected reward model. The same correction yields a doubly robust estimator that consistently estimates the true policy value without sample splitting, even when reward-model prediction error does not vanish. Experiments show decreasing risk-estimation error as dimension grows at a fixed sample-to-dimension ratio, and improved reward-model selection relative to held-out baselines. Empirically, our correction also reduces the root mean squared error of doubly robust value estimates computed from the same data used to fit and select the reward models.
Exact optimality of augmented order-of-addition designs
Stelios D. Georgiou; Haralambos Evangelaras; Stella Stylianou

We prove that, for the pairwise-ordering model with at least three components, adding any run to an order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a $D$-optimal design among all exact designs of the enlarged size, allowing replication. We also establish the corresponding result for foldover designs: adding any reversal pair to a foldover order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a $D$-optimal design within the foldover class at the enlarged size. Both augmentations also minimise the average prediction variance and a covariance-scaled information discrepancy, and maximise the minimum relative efficiency. The key step represents the scaled discrepancy through signed comparisons of triples and derives a sharp integer lower bound; classical spectral inequalities then give the exact-size optima, and signed four-component relative-order counts characterise equality. Complete reversal pairs additionally protect the estimation of pairwise-ordering effects against arbitrary reversal-invariant nuisance means. At the smallest estimable five-component foldover size, exact enumeration identifies five determinant-optimal classes with different prediction and balance properties, and a seven-component example shows that deleting a reversal pair need not be optimal even when it minimises the discrepancy. Constructions through ten components illustrate the attained run sizes.
Talanov dynamics and chirp-controlled rogue-wave formation for the vector nonlinear Schrödinger equation
G. Ortenzi; G. Roberti; M. Sommacal

We study the focusing vector nonlinear Schrödinger equation, or Manakov system, for a pair of coupled initial conditions with compactly supported, concave parabolic density profiles and phases depending quadratically on the spatial coordinate. We focus on the natural class of self-similar solutions generated by such profiles, whose dispersionless evolution we refer to as Talanov dynamics. We extend the criterion for blow-up in finite time, first established for a single field, to the Manakov case. For arbitrary initial chirps in the two fields, we provide closed-form expressions for their evolution, and an explicit expression for the time of the gradient catastrophe, if it occurs, and we classify the effect of the coupling on the catastrophe. Depending on the initial chirps, the two fields may catastrophise, or relax, as each would if decoupled. However, coupling can also force the catastrophe in fields that would otherwise relax if decoupled. For identical initial supports, and in the presence of dispersion, we numerically show that the same dispersionless criterion determines, in the semiclassical regime, whether the fully dispersive solution relaxes or develops a rogue wave in each field, whose onset time is accurately predicted by the corresponding dispersionless catastrophe time, in direct analogy with the scalar case. As chirp and amplitude are relatively easy to control experimentally, we expect these results to be relevant to experiments in nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates, extending to coupled systems observations made for the scalar equation.
Blind Noise Equalization for Large Data Matrices under General Variance Profiles
Boris Landa; Francesco Strino; Fabio Parisi; Ruiqi Li; Yuval Kluger

Low-rank approximation is a basic tool for inference from large and noisy data matrices. However, when noise variances differ across entries, a setting known as heteroskedasticity, the noise can distort the observed spectrum, producing spurious components and obscuring weak signals. To address these challenges, we develop BRINE (Blind Resolvent-based Iterative Noise Equalizer), a data-driven procedure that iteratively rescales rows and columns to equalize the average noise variance across both dimensions. Under suitable conditions, this procedure restores the Marchenko-Pastur law for the noise spectrum and can amplify signal components without prior knowledge of the signal or noise structure. A key idea underlying our approach is to equalize the diagonal entries of the data resolvent as a proxy for equalizing the unknown noise variances. At the population level, we identify a potential function that characterizes this equalization and motivates an iterative minimization procedure. We prove convergence of the iterations to the true equalizer for arbitrary positive variance profiles, with a geometric rate under mild conditions. The updates can be estimated directly from noisy data, and we establish probabilistic error bounds for the scaling factors. Simulations and experiments across diverse biological data modalities and preprocessing pipelines illustrate the effectiveness of our approach.
Multi-Model Over-the-Air Federated Learning via Transceiver Beamforming and Device Grouping
Chong Zhang; Min Dong; Ben Liang; Ali Afana; Yahia A. Eldemerdash Ahmed

This paper considers uplink communication design for training multiple independent machine learning models via wireless federated learning. To reduce communication delay, we utilize multi-antenna beamforming and propose a multi-model over-the-air (M-OTA) uplink transmission and aggregation method for simultaneous training of multiple models. Devices are formed into groups for local model training based on the model assignments per communication round and simultaneously perform OTA aggregation over a multi-access channel. Based on the M-OTA transmission and reception process, we formulate a joint optimization of transmit and receive beamforming and device grouping over $T$ communication rounds to maximize the training convergence rates of all models. We analyze the per-model optimality gap, which captures the impact of noisy aggregation and inter-model interference on the learning performance. We further show that the $T$-round joint optimization problem can be decomposed into per-round online optimization to devise solutions. Following this, we propose a device grouping strategy that explores channel correlation among devices to maximize OTA aggregation performance. Furthermore, we present a low-complexity iterative algorithm for joint transmit-receive beamforming with closed-form updates. Simulation shows that our proposed M-OTA approach substantially outperforms the conventional single-model sequential OTA approach and other commonly used beamforming schemes.
On Lipschitz Explosion in Deep Neural Networks with Normalization: Consequences for Optimization and Adversarial Robustness
Ashkan Soleymani; Reyhaneh Hosseinpourkhoshkbari; Hadi Daneshmand; Patrick Jaillet

Can a network look stable at every layer and still be exponentially unstable as a whole? The Lipschitz constant of a neural network is a basic stability quantity appearing in optimization guarantees, generalization bounds, and robustness certificates. Deep networks naturally admit two such notions, input Lipschitzness, measuring sensitivity to data perturbations, and parameter Lipschitzness, measuring sensitivity to weight perturbations. We prove that, for deep networks with normalization layers, with batch normalization as the canonical example, both Lipschitz constants can grow exponentially with depth and hence with parameter dimension, even under strong per-layer norm control such as $\|W_\ell\|_2\le 1$, and already for linear activations. Thus, a mechanism widely used to stabilize training can create severe worst-case instabilities that are invisible locally, i.e., from layerwise norm bounds alone. Parameter-Lipschitz explosion turns Lipschitz-dependent nonsmooth optimization guarantees into exponential-in-dimension bounds for deep normalized networks, while input-Lipschitz explosion makes worst-case Lipschitz-based generalization and robustness certificates vacuous. The latter also yields a concrete rank-separation mechanism for adversarial vulnerability. The theory predicts that perturbations introducing new singular directions should be amplified much more strongly than perturbations at the same noise level that remain within the input's original singular subspace. Experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 support this prediction, showing that rank-creating perturbations cause substantially sharper drops in accuracy, confidence, and margins than same-subspace perturbations.
Cantor's onion: a uniformly quasiregular map whose Julia set is a Cantor set of spheres
Alastair N. Fletcher; Gaven J. Martin

For integers $d,m\ge2$ with $1/d+1/m<1$, we construct a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{S}^3$ of degree $d^2+m^2$ whose Julia set is a Cantor set of concentric round spheres. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a uniformly quasiregular map in dimension three with infinitely many Fatou components. The map is a three-dimensional analogue of McMullen's maps $z^d+λ/z^m$, built from two Zorich-type power maps glued across a single shell by a slit construction. Its Julia set has Hausdorff dimension $2+s$, where $d^{-s}+m^{-s}=1$, and the restriction of the map to its Julia set is a skew product over the shift on two symbols and has topological entropy $\log(d^2+m^2)$. We also prove that uniformly quasiregular maps that expand uniformly near their Julia set, possibly with branching there, have no wandering domains and only finitely many periodic Fatou components, all of them attracting basins. The map constructed here belongs to this class.
Global regularity of the two-dimensional fractional Boussinesq equations with critical dissipation
Qian Li; Jiahong Wu; Xiaojing Xu; Zhuan Ye

In the present paper, our primary focus is on the Boussinesq equations with fractional velocity dissipation $Λ^αu$ and temperature diffusion $Λ^βθ$. On the critical balance line $α+β=1$, establishing global regularity for weak velocity dissipation has been obstructed by the quadratic convective-buoyancy feedback, and all available results below $α=\frac{10}{13}$ require a smallness assumption on the initial temperature. In this paper, we prove large-data global regularity across the extended regime $α>\frac{\sqrt{57}-5}{4} \approx 0.637$. This provides a step beyond the previous barrier $α=\frac{10}{13}$, unconditionally dismantling the temperature smallness assumption that has persisted in the literature for over a decade. The mathematical mechanism relies on a high-order Quadratic Normal Form transformation $H=ω-R_αθ-\Bop(θ,θ)$ tailored to eliminate non-resonant quadratic vorticity-temperature interactions. Crucially, by uncovering the exact physical scalings of the underlying multilinear commutators and maintaining sharp fractional conjugates in the $L^m$-energy framework, we ensure that the global energy closure is governed entirely by the quadratic thermal dissipation. Once an integrability threshold $m>\frac{2}α$ is attained, a fine Littlewood-Paley transport estimate drives a fractional regularity gain $H \in B_{r,\infty}^{3α-2}$, ensuring the velocity field achieves critical drift regularity $C^α$. By Silvestre-type drift regularization, this spontaneously generates positive Hölder continuity for the temperature, which in turn elevates the drift regularity strictly beyond the critical threshold, unlocking non-local Schauder estimates to prevent finite-time singularity formation.
Pruning free resolutions over a complete intersection

Given a free resolution $F_\bullet$ over a polynomial ring $R$ and a system of higher homotopies on it for a regular sequence $a_1,\dots,a_c$, we can use the Eisenbud-Shamash construction to build a free resolution over $\overline{R}=R/(a_1,\dots,a_c)$. We provide a combinatorial formula for the new system of higher homotopies on a pruned free resolution $F_{\bullet}^{\mathcal{M}}$ that corresponds to a pruning of the Eisenbud-Shamash resolution.
Multi-monopoles and monodromy around the wobbly divisor

The multi-monopole equations are a generalisation of the Seiberg--Witten equations where the spinor is coupled to an auxiliary vector bundle. The signed count of multi-monopoles on a 3-manifold can vary according to a new type of wall-crossing phenomenon. For products $S^1\times C$, where $C$ is a closed Riemann surface, we relate the wall and chamber structure to loops in the complement of the wobbly divisor of $C$. Such a loop induces a monodromy map on the multi-vortex moduli space, and the count of its fixed points is expected to agree with the count of multi-monopoles on $S^1\times C$ in the given chamber. By studying singularities of framed multi-vortex moduli spaces, we are able to understand these monodromy maps for various loops. Counting fixed points suggests that product 3-manifolds display incredibly rich wall-crossing behaviour.
A new characterization of the round sphere

We provide an elementary proof of Hersch's inequality and Cheng's theorem, both characterizing the sphere. We revisit these classical results in connection with the geodesic monotonicity of heat kernels on two-dimensional spheres, which provides a third characterization.
Projective flatness of cylindrically symmetric Finsler metrics
Newton Solórzano; Víctor León; Dik Lujerio

In this paper, we study cylindrically symmetric projectively flat Finsler metrics \(F=|\bar y|ϕ(x^0,r,s,z)\). We reformulate the conditions for projective flatness and strong convexity in terms of \(Ω=ϕ-sϕ_s-zϕ_z\), isolating the compatibility condition missing in earlier work. Using the method of characteristics, we give an integral formula for all smooth local solutions near points with \(r>0\) and \(s=z=0\). These solutions are determined by a characteristic potential up to the addition of an invariant exact one-form. In the reversible case, the equation for the potential reduces to a \((2+1)\)-dimensional wave equation on a half-space. We illustrate the reconstruction with a polynomial potential and compute the potentials of a known family of spherically symmetric metrics and their linear pullbacks. The convexity conditions also admit decreasing profiles and recover the spherical Beltrami metric as a particular case. Finally, suitable positive sums of linear pullbacks yield smooth reversible projectively flat Finsler metrics on \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) whose tangent norm at the origin is non-Riemannian. Consequently, these metrics are not linear pullbacks of spherically symmetric metrics
An Asymptotic Framework for Closed-Form Estimators from Surrogate Estimating Equations

Many statistical estimators, including maximum likelihood and method of moments estimators, are defined as roots of estimating equations. In complex models, these equations often cannot be solved explicitly; although numerical methods can provide approximate solutions, closed-form approximations can reduce computation and facilitate theoretical analysis by making an estimator's dependence on the data more transparent. In this paper, we develop a general approach to constructing such approximations and a framework for quantifying their accuracy. Our theory accommodates sequences of parameters that approach the boundary of the parameter space or diverge to infinity, and provides conditions under which a closed-form approximate estimator has the same first-order asymptotic distribution as its exact counterpart. We focus on approximations to maximum likelihood estimators, although the theory applies to general estimating equations. We apply the framework to iid models from the gamma, zeta, von Mises, and generalized Pareto families, as well as to gamma regression. Together, these examples cover scalar and vector parameters, iid and non-iid settings, and normal and nonnormal asymptotic regimes. Each example is accompanied by a simulation study, and the gamma regression example also includes a real-world data application.
Entropic Martingale Optimal Transport with Wasserstein Relaxed Marginal Constraints
Haowen Chen; Renyuan Xu; Xin Zhang

Martingale optimal transport (MOT) is a fundamental framework in robust finance, yet its stability under marginal perturbation no longer holds in high dimensions $d\geq 2$. In this paper, we introduce Wasserstein-relaxed entropic martingale optimal transport (WEMOT), which combines Wasserstein relaxation of the second marginal with entropy regularization. This formulation ensures stability under perturbations of the marginals, thereby facilitating numerical implementation. We establish strong duality and dual attainment for WEMOT, which leads to efficient Sinkhorn-type algorithms. We further prove a convergence rate of WEMOT to MOT as regularization parameters vanish, and also the quantitative stability of WEMOT with respect to marginal perturbations.
Uniform and Relative Non-Associativity on Minimal Free Resolutions

We study unital chain-map multiplications on minimal free resolutions of quotient rings. We prove that Katthän's example admits no associative multiplication over any field, without assuming graded commutativity or compatibility with an internal grading. The proof gives a relative obstruction in which associativity on a specified finite collection of triples forces failure at another triple. The argument extends to a family that includes nonmonomial ideals. We also give criteria for uniform non-associativity, where a fixed triple fails for every multiplication, by comparing either associators or their primitives under changes of multiplication. These criteria persist from monomial elimination ideals and give explicit obstructions for Avramov's example and the known eight-vertex Bier sphere over every field. As an application, we show that the edge ideal of the eight-cycle admits an injective Taylor comparison on five selected generators, while every selection of that size fails to admit a multiplicative comparison. Four generators admit a multiplicative embedding.
Extensions of operators between ordered vector spaces

We prove analogues of several classical theorems about operators between vector lattices in the context of directed Archimedean ordered vector spaces. In particular, we show that every order continuous operator between pervasive Archimedean ordered vector spaces can be extended to an order continuous operator between their Dedekind completions. Additionally, we introduce the universal completion of a directed Archimedean ordered vector space, and show that every supremum-preserving operator between directed Archimedean ordered vector spaces can be extended to an order continuous homomorphism between their universal completions. We also establish some universal properties for the relative uniform completion.
Vector Lyapunov functions for nonconvex constrained optimization

Nonconvex constrained optimization problems are commonly solved by a Newton method for necessary conditions (sequential linear/quadratic programming) or a barrier reformulation (interior-point methods). We present a vector Lyapunov analysis for Newton-type algorithms based on constraint violation and optimality of the primal solutions to a sequence of approximate optimization problems. We thus prove local stability and convergence by constructing a strict Lyapunov function for the primal solution.
Composite witness sieves, Kneser--Plancherel containers, and the exponent $5/7$ for the Erdős--Straus conjecture

For the Erdős--Straus equation $4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z$, Vaughan's unconditional bound on the exceptional set $E(N)$ has stood at $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c(\log N)^{2/3})$ since 1970. We harness composite divisor witnesses at growing depth to cross this $2/3$ barrier unconditionally. On the full exceptional set $E(N)$, we prove the unconditional bound $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c'(\log N)^{5/7}/(\log\log N)^{2/7})$, improving the exponent to $5/7$ (with an intermediate stage at $7/10$). On the structured component $E_2^{\mathrm{small}}(N;J(N))$, an algebraic and spectral container hierarchy combined with a generating-polynomial large sieve reaches the exponent $1-o(1)$: $|E_2^{\mathrm{small}}(N;J(N))|\ll_κN\exp(-(\frac{1}{40960}+o(1))\frac{\log N}{(\log\log N)(\log\log\log N)^κ})$, matching the CRT capacity scale. These results resolve the obstructions to composite-witness sieving at growing depth. First, we replace subgroup generation by Kneser's stabilizer $K(M)$, which embeds into a $2$-primary character kernel, reducing container counts from $2^{Θ(J^{4})}$ to $\exp(\mathcal{O}(J^{2}\log\log J))$. Coupling this with a generating-polynomial large sieve, Markov $1/2$-popular symmetry containers, and Pontryagin--Plancherel character containers yields the exponent $1-o(1)$ on $E_2^{\mathrm{small}}$. Second, to bypass unlocalized diffuse divisor sheets without subset enumeration, we construct a semi-composite congruence sieve $s=pq\equiv-1\pmod{12ua}$ ($p\in(Z^{9/10},Z]$, $q\le Q$ rough). Conditioning on $n\bmod M_{\mathrm{small}}$ yields CRT mutual independence while decoupling the modulus $12ua\le 12Z^{1/4}$ from $q$; a Bonferroni majorant and the Bombieri--Vinogradov theorem then yield the unconditional $5/7$ exponent on all of $E(N)$. Finally, we study bilinear dispersion on $4uavw-4u^{2}v-w=n$ and difference sets $D(K_c)$.
Long-root $\SL_2$ dual pairs in split exceptional groups: Compact types, cone geometry, and theta correspondence

The paper establishes a case of Howe duality for an exceptional theta correspondence using the ping-pong of types method. To that end, one needs to compute lifts of types of maximal compact subgroups. A brand new ingredient enters here: The graded module of the minimal representations is the coordinate ring of an affine cone whose projectivization is a Grassmannian. Via the filtered Nakayama lemma the problem of lifting types becomes a problem in algebraic geometry: compute certain linear sections of the Grassmannian.
Peter Boyvalenkov; Danila Cherkashin; Peter Dragnev; Peter Grabner

We develop a Levenshtein-type linear programming framework (for maximal $s$-codes and for minimal energy) for $(a,b)$-avoiding spherical codes, that is, codes whose inner products between distinct points avoid $(a,b)$. We introduce and investigate signed measures that are positive definite up to an appropriate degree and yield stationary auxiliary linear programming polynomials and exact quadrature formulas. We give explicit conditions for positivity of the quadrature weights and sufficient Krein-type conditions for nonnegative Gegenbauer coefficients (positive definiteness of the candidate optimal linear programming polynomials). Under these hypotheses and suitable node-location assumptions, the resulting cardinality bounds are optimal within the corresponding degree restriction and unique under natural nondegeneracy conditions. Under proper conditions on the quadrature nodes, we obtain universal lower energy bounds by utilizing Hermite interpolants as polynomial solutions of the respective linear program. Common test functions characterize optimality in the full polynomial linear programs under mild additional assumptions.
Optimal Feedback Control of the Fokker-Planck Equation for an SIRS Epidemic Model

We develop a Fokker--Planck feedback control framework for a stochastic susceptible--infected--recovered--susceptible (SIRS) epidemic model with three intervention mechanisms targeting disease transmission, loss of immunity, and recovery. The interventions are formulated as space- and time-dependent feedback controls that influence both the drift and diffusion coefficients of the underlying stochastic differential equations, allowing control of the probability distribution of epidemic states. We investigate the existence of optimal controls and derive first-order necessary optimality conditions involving a forward Fokker--Planck equation, a backward adjoint equation, and a Hamiltonian minimization condition. For numerical approximation, we combine a Chang--Cooper discretization of the diagonal drift--diffusion terms with a finite-difference treatment of cross-diffusion and a sequential quadratic Hamiltonian (SQH) algorithm for computing the optimal feedback policies. We also examine sufficient-decrease and convergence properties of the SQH iteration. Numerical experiments consider four epidemiological objectives involving cumulative infection burden, infection-threshold exceedance, terminal susceptible population, and a combination of running and terminal costs. The resulting feedback policies exhibit distinct spatial and temporal structures depending on the epidemiological objective. Monte Carlo simulations of the underlying stochastic system illustrate that the optimized interventions can substantially reduce infection growth and undesirable epidemic outcomes relative to uncontrolled dynamics. The proposed framework provides a distribution-based approach to stochastic epidemic control that integrates mathematical analysis, numerical optimization, and state-dependent intervention design.
Stability of large dynamical systems using Gershgorin Disc Theorem

Understanding the stability of large nonlinear dynamical systems is a fundamental problem in many fields, including biological, technological, and social networks. Traditional stability methods often rely on explicit eigenvalue calculations or the construction of Lyapunov functions, which become computationally difficult for large interconnected systems. In this work, we introduce a stability classifier that provides a computationally efficient way to determine the stability of complex systems without performing full spectral analysis. Our approach combines the Dynamical Jacobian Ensemble framework, which uses the network structure and the underlying dynamics to construct a Jacobian, with the Gershgorin disc theorem, which provides bounds on the eigenvalues of the system's Jacobian matrix. Using this combination, we derive an analytical classifier that predicts whether a dynamical system is asymptotically stable, unstable, or sensitively stable based on a small set of dynamical and network parameters. The analysis reveals that the stability of large dynamical systems is strongly influenced by highly connected hub nodes. This observation allows the stability condition to be simplified by focusing on the contribution of the hub-associated Gershgorin disc. Extensive numerical simulations on large ensembles of Jacobian matrices confirm that the proposed classifier accurately separates stable, unstable, and sensitively stable regimes across a wide range of dynamical parameters and network structures. The resulting framework provides a simple and scalable tool for predicting the stability of large dynamical networks while capturing the interplay between network topology and interaction dynamics.
The quaternionic reflection groups with imprimitive complexifications and the finite subgroups of GL(2,C)

We give a transparent development of the quaternionic reflection groups which have imprimitive complexifications, including a description of their reflections and the corresponding normal reflection subgroups. They are seen to be of rank one or rank two, and are obtained from minimal complex reflection groups by the addition of one quaternionic reflection and a complex scalar matrix of finite order. In the case of the rank two groups, we use our techniques to consider the broader question of what are the minimal irreducible subgroups of GL(2,C) with a given collineation group. This leads to a complete classification of the finite irreducible subgroups of GL(2,C) in terms of the minimal groups, with the groups giving rise to quaternionic reflection groups located within it.
A Gamma-Mixture Solution for Definite Noncentral Complex Gaussian Quadratic Forms
Fernando D. Almeida García; Carlos R. Nogueira da Silva; Felipe A. P. de Figueiredo; Rausley A. A. de Souza; Michel Daoud Yacoub; José Cândido Silveira Santos Filho

Finding exact solutions for the statistics of definite noncentral complex Gaussian quadratic forms (CGQFs) has long been a challenging problem. Among existing exact approaches, Raphaeli's formulation [1] remains the most computationally efficient. However, its analytical tractability is hindered by the dependence of its series coefficients on the evaluation variable, which confines their statistics to the probability density function (PDF) and cumulative distribution function (CDF). This paper overcomes this limitation by deriving novel Gamma-mixture representations for the PDF and CDF of positive- and negative-definite noncentral CGQFs. The resulting structure broadens Raphaeli's statistical framework beyond the PDF and CDF to a wider class of CGQF functionals and a substantial range of practical applications. In particular, expectations of integrable functions of definite noncentral CGQFs are expressed as weighted sums of the corresponding expectations over Gamma random variables, enabling the direct derivation of moments, transforms, and performance measures. Moreover, the proposed formulation reduces the single-point complexity from \(O\!\left(n^2K+nK^2\right)\) for Raphaeli's method to \(O\!\left(nK+K^2\right)\), where \(n\) denotes the quadratic-form dimension and \(K\) the truncation order. The proposed Gamma-mixture structure also enables closed-form approximations that, by construction, remain valid probability distributions for any truncation order. In addition, uniform PDF and CDF truncation-error bounds are derived, allowing prescribed-accuracy truncation. As a sample application, we derive the first reported exact average bit error rate expression for maximal-ratio combining receivers with an arbitrary number of branches under an arbitrary positive-definite Rician correlation structure.
Regularity of Weak Solutions near Singular Minimizing Cones for the One-Phase Free Boundary Problem

Alt and Caffarelli proved an Allard-type $ε$-regularity theorem near the flat one-homogeneous minimizer of the one-phase free boundary problem. A natural follow-up question is whether an analogous regularity result holds near singular minimizing cones. In this paper, we prove such an $ε$-regularity theorem near a strongly integrable one-phase minimizing cone with an isolated singularity. More precisely, we show that, after a suitable translation and rotation, the free boundary of any non-degenerate weak solution sufficiently close to the cone is graphical over the free boundary of a leaf of the De Silva--Jerison--Shahgholian foliation. This result is analogous to recent $ε$-regularity theorems in minimal surface theory by Edelen and by Edelen--Spolaor; our proof adapts the strategy of Edelen to the one-phase setting.
McShane's identity and the Brownian loop measure

We combine McShane's identity for a once-punctured torus with the length-spectrum identity of Wang and Xue. An exact identity in each primitive homology class yields a finite limit for the difference of two divergent length-spectrum sums over self-intersecting hyperbolic geodesics. The limit is $\frac18$ and is equivalent to McShane's identity. We also derive higher-iteration identities governed by integer divisors.
Compressed Per-Player Local Methods for Multiplayer Federated Learning: Exact Convergence via Increment Sharing
Bhavika Balani; TaeHo Yoon; Nicolas Loizou

Multiplayer Federated Learning (MpFL), introduced by Yoon et al. (2025), extends classical federated learning to settings where clients are rational players in a game with individual objectives and strategies, seeking an equilibrium. A natural baseline is Per-Player Local SGD (PEARL-SGD), where each player performs several local SGD steps before exchanging strategies through a central server. However, the original PEARL-SGD formulation does not extend cleanly to compressed communication. Directly compressing the players' strategies can prevent convergence to the equilibrium, even with deterministic gradients. To address this issue, we reformulate PEARL-SGD so that players communicate local strategy increments rather than the strategies themselves. Without compression, the two formulations are equivalent, but with compression, increment sharing preserves exact convergence, allowing us to design the communication-efficient compressed PEARL-SGD (C-PEARL-SGD). Beyond compression, we also consider variance reduction as another axis of improvement, introducing PEARL-SVRG and its compressed variant C-PEARL-SVRG. Under the original MpFL assumptions, we establish convergence guarantees for all variants through a unified parametric inequality. Numerical experiments, including distributed spectrum sensing, demonstrate the practical benefits of our methods over vanilla PEARL-SGD.
Special line bundles on tetragonal curves

One can associate a pair of vector bundles $(E, F)$ on $\mathbb{P}^1$ to every tetragonal curve: $E$ is the Tschirnhausen bundle and $F$ records numerical data of the ideal for the curve under its relative canonical embedding. In this note, we show that a Hurwitz--Brill--Noether general tetragonal curve must have balanced $E$, $F$ bundles, and provide counterexamples for the converse when $g = 8$ or $g \geq 10$.
Counting Finite Maps through Functional Digraphs and Fibers

We count solutions of composition identities for maps on finite sets, first for three identities in which both maps vary and then for commutation with a prescribed arithmetic map. For $f\circ g=f\circ g\circ g$, drawing an arrow from each element to its image reduces the enumeration to rooted trees attached to directed cycles. For $f\circ f=f\circ g\circ f$, grouping elements with the same $f$-value leads instead to a partition-based enumeration. A classical rooted-forest enumeration leads in both problems to $\mathcal T(x)$, the exponential generating function for rooted labeled trees. For $f=g\circ f\circ g$, the values on the cycles of $g$ determine all remaining values. The exponential generating function $\mathcal D$ for these ordered pairs and the ordinary generating function $\mathcal A$ for endofunctions up to relabeling satisfy $\mathcal D(x)=\mathcal A(\mathcal T(x))$. Finally, we count functions on $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ satisfying $f(ax)=af(x)$, first for prime multipliers $a$ and then for a broader class of composite multipliers. In each problem, fixing one map exposes independent choices for the other through its functional digraph or its fibers.
Non-conical classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated singularity

Several examples of one-homogeneous classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated free boundary singularity are known. Adapting the approach of Caffarelli, Hardt, and Simon for minimal surfaces, we construct non-conical classical solutions with an isolated free boundary singularity by perturbing a one-homogeneous solution $U$. Moreover, if $U$ is strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate), then any solution sufficiently close to $U$ is also strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate).
Standard Subspaces and Modular Theory -- General Theory and Applications to QFT
Ricardo Correa da Silva; Gandalf Lechner; Roberto Longo

This is a preview of an upcoming monograph on standard subspaces and modular theory. At the moment, it consists of the first chapter. This starts with a gentle introduction to the subject, and then describes the modular theory of standard subspaces, the characterization of their modular data by the KMS condition and reflection positivity, and various constructions of standard subspaces. Further topics in Chapter 1 include the connection of standard subspaces to complexifications and symplectic structures, including their polarizers, and operations with standard subspaces, namely direct sums, direct integrals, and tensor products. Many examples and classification results are included as well. This first chapter also contains a description of the free U(1)-current and some other applications to quantum field theory, such as KMS states of type I factors, the local subspaces of the free Klein--Gordon field, and the entropy operator defined by a standard subspace.
Blow-Up and Life-Span for Nonlinear Hardy-Hénon Parabolic Equations

We consider the nonlinear Hardy-Hénon parabolic equation $ u_t=Δu+|x|^l|u|^αu,$ $t>0,$ $x\in\mathbb{R}^N$ or $x\in\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}$, with $N\ge1$, $l>-\min\{2,N\}$, $α>0$, with nonnegative initial datum $u_0$. We first establish new criteria for finite-time blow-up. We then derive optimal upper bounds for the life-span $T_{\max}(λφ)$ of solutions arising from the initial datum $u_0=λφ$. These estimates establish a precise dependence of $T_{\max}(λφ)$ on both the initial profile $φ$ and the parameter $λ$ in the small and large-amplitude regimes.
Liouville transforms for ordinary differential equations with distributional coefficients

We study Liouville transforms for the differential equation $Ju'+qu=wf$ on the real interval $(a,b)$ where $J$ is a constant, invertible, skew-hermitian matrix and $q$ and $w$ are matrices whose entries are distributions of order $0$ with $q$ Hermitian and $w$ non-negative. In particular, we examine their use in the treatment of quasi-regular endpoints and their impact on the Weyl-Titchmarsh $\mathbb M$-function associated with the differential equation.
Fractional Fefferman--Stein inequalities on infinite rooted $k$-ary trees

We study weighted endpoint estimates for the centered fractional maximal operator on the infinite rooted $k$-ary tree, $T$. Our first result is a Fefferman--Stein type estimate \[ w\bigl(\{M_αf>λ\}\bigr) \lesssim_{α,s} \frac1λ\sum_{x\in T}|f(x)|M_{α,s}w(x), \qquad s>1, \] with a constant independent of the branching parameter $k$. Although the proof is inspired by the non-fractional argument of Ombrosi, Rivera-Ríos and Safe in \cite{ORRS}, the fractional normalization introduces a genuinely new scale interaction. At radius $r$, one must renormalize the function by $k^{rα}$ while keeping the dyadic cutoff at $k^r$; this leads to a new summation mechanism involving simultaneously $k^{rα}$ and $k^{r(1-α)}$. We then study sharpness and the geometry of admissible weights. We construct counterexamples showing that the estimate cannot in general be reduced to $s=1$ for any $0<α<1$. In the subcritical range $0<α<1/2$, we characterize power-type radial weights satisfying the natural fractional $A_1$ condition and prove that the failure persists after any fixed finite number of iterations of $M_α$. We also prove that $M_αw\lesssim w$ is necessary for the corresponding weighted weak type estimate but is not sufficient in the subcritical range. Finally, we identify a phase transition: for $1/2\leα<1$ no nonzero global weight can satisfy $M_αw\lesssim w$.
Jan Hückelheim; Jeffrey Larson; Matt Menickelly

We present branch-extended automatic differentiation (BEAD), a software package that provides information about inactive branches of piecewise-differentiable functions, intended for use in nonsmooth optimization algorithms. BEAD is implemented in Python, building on the popular JAX framework. For supported nonsmooth operations such as abs and max, BEAD identifies alternative branches within tolerance from the given input, and computes gradients of the resulting branches extended to the given input. Such information has been previously used for robust optimization methods, but has required error-prone and tedious manual differentiation, unlike BEAD, which is fully automated for functions written in NumPy-like JAX code. Our experiments show that our approach is as accurate as manually written derivative code, and offers more flexibility in modifying the function and choosing between branch-discovery rules. While we were originally motivated by the manifold sampling algorithm for nonsmooth composite objectives, we also integrate BEAD branch-extension gradients into a nonsmooth BFGS-SQP solver. On two small nonsmooth test problems, the resulting path-aware search resolves failures or substantially reduces the number of evaluations required by the BFGS-SQP solver.
Regularity of elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure

We study autonomous elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure of the form \[ -\operatorname{div}\big(\mathfrak a(|Du|)Du\big)=0 \quad \text{in }\ Ω\subset \mathbb R^n \] Under two-sided quantitative $(p,q)$-growth conditions on $\mathfrak a$, we prove gradient Hölder continuity with constants and exponent depending only on the dimensions, $p$ and $q$. This improves the classical theory initiated by Uhlenbeck by removing the continuity requirement on $\mathfrak a'$. The proof uses nonlinear comparison systems whose regularity follows from a scalar uniformly elliptic equation. Under weaker $(p,q)$-growth conditions on the convex function $φ(t):=\int_0^t s\mathfrak a(s)\,ds$, we obtain local $W^{1,s}$-regularity for every $s>1$, and hence Hölder continuity of solutions with every exponent less than one. An additional lower growth condition on $\mathfrak a$ yields local Lipschitz continuity, even when $\mathfrak a$ is discontinuous.
Evasive subspaces, minimal rank-metric codes and subspace designs via auxiliary fields

We extend the auxiliary-field method for scattered subspaces to evasive subspaces and subspace designs. For $1\le h\le k<hn$ and coprime $h,k+1$ with $n(k-h+1)\ge k+1$, we construct spanning $(h,k)$-evasive $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^r$ of dimension $rn(k-h+1)/(k+1)$ in every sufficiently large admissible ambient dimension, with a threshold independent of $q$. When $k<n$, this dimension is maximum. The proof combines an intersection lemma, a rank-support density inequality, scalar orbit counting, and a profile preserved by direct sums. The coding consequences include, for every fixed odd extension degree $m\ge3$ and every sufficiently large $K$, minimal rank-metric codes of optimal length $2K$ with first two generalized weights $(m+1)/2$ and $m+1$.
