This allows us to prove unique continuation properties of axially symmetric solutions to $p$-Laplace equations in higher dimensions $N\geq3$, with axially symmetric $p$-harmonic functions as a particular case. Unlike in our previous work, the analysis is based here on the regularity and quasiconformal properties of the whole stress field $|
abla u|^{p-2}
abla u$ in the plane, taking into account the more delicate regularity theory for $p>2$. This allows us to prove Liouville-type and bubble profile decomposition results for critical problems in dimensions $N\geq3$ and in the whole range $1<p<N$, under some symmetry conditions.
The Cost of Minimal Completeness: Gamma-to-Delta Aliasing in Discrete Markets

A $(d+1)$-state lattice is the smallest complete one-step approximation of a $d$-dimensional Brownian market. Its centered quadratic increments must lie in the span of the traded innovations. We study the resulting Gamma-to-Delta aliasing through the linear operator $\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)=\mathbb{E}[(ξ^\top Hξ-\operatorname{tr} H)ξ]$, $H\in\operatorname{Sym}_d$, for centered isotropic innovations $ξ$. For quadratic claims this operator is exactly the difference, scaled by $\sqrt{h}/2$, between the lattice's replicating exposure and its price-sensitivity Delta. Applying the lattice replication rule to a Brownian market adds the tracking-error variance $hT|\mathcal{A}_ξ(H)|^2/4$ relative to ordinary discrete Delta hedging. We prove that the smallest worst-case aliasing over all minimally complete lattices is $\sqrt{d-1}$, uniquely attained by the equal-probability regular simplex. For positive-semidefinite and rank-one unit-Frobenius Gamma classes, the sharp minimax value is instead $(d-1)/\sqrt{d}$, with the same unique optimizer. We also describe the corresponding orthogonal quadratic residual in nonminimal markets and the leading implementation error for smooth claims.
Logarithmic corrections for four-dimensional loop percolation

We study the one-arm probability of the discrete random-walk loop soup on $\mathbb{Z}^4$ at small positive intensity. Using the small-loop crossing and macroscopic attachment estimates of Gao, we prove that the expected capacity of the origin cluster formed by loops contained in a box grows at most as the square of the logarithm of the box radius. Consequently, there are constants $α_0,c,C,β>0$ such that, for $0<α\leα_0$, \[
 cαR^{-2}[\log(R+2)]^{βα}
 \le \mathbb{P}_α(0\leftrightarrow B_R^c)
 \le CαR^{-2}[\log(R+2)]^2. \] The interval $(0,α_0]$ is strictly subcritical. The upper bound rests on a simultaneous capacity estimate for neighborhoods of loop ranges, followed by an expansion over chains in which sufficiently small intermediate loops have been removed. A deterministic bound on the variation of the surviving scale sequences makes the expansion summable. The positive logarithmic-power lower bound is already known from work of Chang and Sapozhnikov; we give a proof using macroscopic attachments and a layer-cake argument, with constants uniform at small intensity. In particular, the one-arm exponent equals two, and the logarithm of its correction has order $\log\log R$, for every fixed intensity in this interval. We also derive polynomial tail exponent one for the cardinality and capacity of the full cluster, determine their positive moment thresholds, and give an application to random wires.
A unified approach to fluctuations of LES of time-dependent generalized patterned random matrices
Kiran Kumar; Shambhu Nath Maurya; Koushik Saha

A unified approach for studying the linear eigenvalue statistics (LES) of generalized patterned random matrices was developed in Kumar, Maurya, Saha (2026). In this paper, as a continuation, we develop a unified method for studying the time-dependent LES of generalized patterned random matrices with independent process entries such as Brownian motion and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. We prove that if the limiting moment sequence of the LES of the generalized patterned random matrix with independent standard Gaussian entries is M-determinate, then under some minimal assumption on the link function, the time-dependent LES converges to a deterministic real-valued process.
Perelman's entropy and Gromov-Hausdorff versus dynamical stability of round spheres

We study the Gromov-Hausdorff stability of round spheres under perturbations of Perelman's nu-entropy. We show that in dimension two almost maximal entropy, together with an area normalisation, implies Gromov-Hausdorff closeness to the round two-sphere. In contrast, in dimensions at least three, we construct smooth metrics on the sphere whose entropies converge to that of the round sphere, but which remain a definite Gromov-Hausdorff distance away from it. These metrics can be chosen conformal and uniformly bi-Lipschitz equivalent to the round metric, with the same volume as the round sphere. Finally, in dimension three, we contrast this Gromov-Hausdorff instability with a dynamical stability result: metrics with nu-entropy above that of the round shrinking cylinder converge exponentially fast to round metrics under the volume-normalised Ricci flow.
Concavity of Normalized Generalized Brézin--Gross--Witten Correlators and Its Applications

In this paper, we study the generalized Brézin--Gross--Witten model using its BKP integrability. By virtue of the formula for connected $n$-point functions of tau-functions of the BKP hierarchy obtained by Wang and the first-named author, we prove that the normalized generalized BGW correlators are strictly concave for fixed genus and fixed total degree. As applications, we establish the strict Schur-concavity and derive upper and lower bounds for these correlators. We also prove the strict monotonicity of normalized ordinary BGW correlators, which resolves a conjecture by Guo--Norbury--Yang--Zagier.
Robust Markov Decision Processes: An Introduction Using Convex Optimization and Game Theory

The goal of these notes is to provide a unified and rigorous introduction to robust sequential decision-making. We offer a self-contained introduction to the main results in the field. After a concise introduction to MDPs we introduce robust MDPs with general uncertainty sets, before focusing on rectangular models of uncertainty. We make a significant effort to show connections between robust MDPs and several other popular models for sequential decision-making: MDPs with uncertain rewards, Multi-Objective MDPs and Pareto optimality, MDPs with time-varying uncertain parameters, non-rectangular robust MDPs, stochastic games, distributionally robust MDPs, and risk-averse MDPs. Having all these results in one place, within a single unifying formalism, will hopefully be useful for researchers who want to start working on this topic. The exposition combines operator and fixed point approaches, convex optimization (more specifically, duality in saddle-point problems), and game-theoretic arguments. The latter identifies robust MDPs with a certain type of two-player game; this helps build useful intuition, especially when constructing counterexamples.
Polynomial-Time Differentially Private Synthetic Graph Release with Nearly-Linear Additive Error
Marek Eliáš; Gautam Kamath; Janardhan Kulkarni; George Z. Li; Jingcheng Liu; Sepideh Mahabadi; Pan Peng; Jakub Tarnawski; Hangyu Xu; Zongrui Zou

We give a polynomial-time $(\varepsilon, δ)$-edge-differentially private algorithm that releases a synthetic graph approximately preserving all cut values of a nonnegative weighted input graph $G$. Our algorithm outputs a nonnegative weighted graph $H$ such that, with probability at least $1-β$, simultaneously for all $S\subseteq V$, \[
 \left|w_G(S,V\setminus S)-w_H(S,V\setminus S)\right|
 \leq γw_G(S,V\setminus S)
 + O\left(\frac{n}{γ\varepsilon}
 \log^7 \frac{n}{δβγ\varepsilon}\right). \] For fixed $γ, \varepsilon$ and $δ= β= n^{-10}$, the additive error is $n \operatorname{polylog} n$, improving upon the previous efficient bound of $n^{13/12 + o(1)}$. Furthermore, we establish an $Ω(n/γ\varepsilon)$ lower bound for the relevant parameter regime, showing that our result is tight up to polylogarithmic factors.
 Our algorithm uses a log-det-regularized SDP to generate fractional queries for multiplicative-weights updates and certify accuracy for all cuts. The privacy analysis charges privacy loss only fractionally per mechanism call, based on the amount of mass on edge coordinates retired from subsequent iterations.
 Our synthetic graph release yields improved error bounds for several downstream tasks in private graph analysis including correlation clustering, Max-Cut, Max-$k$-Cut, constrained cut problems and hierarchical clustering. Most notably, for unweighted complete-graph correlation clustering, we achieve the optimal $\widetilde O(n)$ additive error while reducing the best previously known approximation ratio for this additive error from several thousand to $1.387$.
 We also provide a formalization of our results in Lean.
Large particle number asymptotics for point-interacting bosons in the plane

We consider $N$ bosons in two dimensions interacting via point interactions, modeled by the TMS Hamiltonian. We prove that their ground state energy has the asymptotic behavior $-e^{C N }$ for large $N$, for an explicit constant $C$ related to the sharp constant in the Ladyzhenskaya-Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. Such asymptotic behavior was predicted in the physics literature, based on a variant of the mean-field approximation.
To lift or not to lift: Operator inference for nonlinear PDEs with boundary control
Zhuoyuan Wang; Yorie Nakahira; Wael H. Ali; Saviz Mowlavi

Operator inference (OpInf) provides a nonintrusive framework for learning projection-based reduced-order models directly from data, but its standard formulations do not explicitly account for the fact that boundary actuation changes the admissible solution space of a PDE. This paper develops and evaluates a boundary-consistent, lifting-based OpInf formulation for nonlinear PDEs with time-varying inhomogeneous boundary conditions. The proposed approach decomposes the state into a known lifting component that satisfies the prescribed boundary conditions and a homogeneous component represented in a POD basis. Substituting this decomposition into the governing dynamics reveals a boundary-consistent reduced model structure in which the learned dynamics includes bilinear state-input and quadratic input-input interactions for quadratically nonlinear PDEs. The resulting operators are inferred from data, preserving the nonintrusive character of OpInf while guaranteeing boundary condition satisfaction by construction. Numerical experiments on boundary-actuated heat, Burgers, and lid-driven cavity problems show that the lifted formulation improves boundary compliance and can enhance prediction accuracy, solver stability, and computational efficiency, although these gains vary across problems and reduced model dimensions. Overall, this study establishes lifting as a principled extension of OpInf for boundary-actuated PDEs, clarifies when and how this formulation improves performance, and indicates that standard OpInf can remain an effective alternative in certain regimes.
Sobolev--Poincaré inequalities for piecewise $W^{2,p}$ functions over general polytopic meshes

We establish Sobolev--Poincaré inequalities for piecewise $W^{2,p}$ functions in two and three dimensions over families of general polytopic (including shape-regular simplicial and Cartesian) meshes, allowing for degenerate facets. The proposed inequalities feature control by either the broken Hessian or, more naturally for general fourth-order problems, the broken Laplacian. Important tools in their derivation are a Helmholtz decomposition in Banach--Sobolev spaces and Sobolev--Poincaré inequalities for piecewise $W^{1,p}$ functions; we avoid the use of any inverse inequality. We provide estimates with fairly general Lebesgue exponents. Applications to the stability analysis of nonconforming discretizations for second- and fourth-order, linear and nonlinear problems are exhibited.
David H. Wolpert; David C. Krakauer

``Emergence'' refers to the fact that different mathematical languages and theories seem to be required to describe scientific theories that operate at different spatial and temporal scales. Highly circumscribed, special cases of emergence have been investigated using many different formal tools, including coarse-graining (over space and / or time), renormalization, dimension reduction, broken symmetry, and various formulations of causality. Here we extend the mathematics of model theory to unify and extend these earlier investigations. As a preliminary application of our framework, we investigate canonical examples of emergence, including the emergence of genetics from chemistry, of psychology from neurobiology, and of different forms of collective behavior from the laws governing their constituent parts. By exploiting the power of model theory we also uncover many aspects of emergence that were previously obscured. In particular, we uncover some of the rich hierarchical structure that relates different scientific fields. For example, we show that scientific fields can be related via a collection of multiple partial orders, all defined over the same set. Vladimir Gurvich; Matjaž Krnc; Martin Milanič; Mikhail Vyalyi

At high temperatures and high on-site field strengths, it has a unique KMS state that does not have the weak Gibbs or regularity properties.

atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups, given one named hypothesis that is a theorem of that library, so that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. The resulting practical stability guarantee concerns the field, input bias, and sensitivity estimate, and is unaffected by a constant cost offset under corresponding filter initialization. In this paper, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for $RG$ to be Jordan nilpotent of index $n \geq 2$. In particular, we establish a connection between the study of Jordan nilpotency in group rings and the study of Lie nilpotency in these algebras. At larger amplitudes the whirl becomes modulated, reverses its direction, and becomes chaotic. Moreover, we prove that the suspension of a naturally expansive endomorphism is naturally expansive. Math. 2023], and also establish lower bounds for the probabilities of visiting finite sets in Euclidean lattices.

We discuss a model of a soft waveguide described by Schrödinger operator whose potential is a twisted straight channel of non-circular profile. We show that a compactly supported twist makes the operator subcritical, the property being expressed in terms of a Hardy-type inequality. On the other hand, a periodic twist raises the essential spectrum and its local slowdown may give rise to isolated eigenvalues below the essential spectrum threshold.

This paper investigates the small inertia limit of the distribution-dependent stochastic Cucker--Smale equation with the full velocity alignment source term, which serves as the mean-field equation for the stochastic Cucker--Smale model. Then we define a global position correction and a quadratic remainder, both with uniformly bounded tails. Applying the Aldous criterion, we obtain tightness of the position correction, which in turn yields tightness of the position process. Subsequently, using the averaging method on the fast time scale, the quadratic functional can be decomposed into the equilibrium average, local quadratic fluctuations, and exponential transients. Then, the Poisson--Lyapunov equation is employed to prove the convergence of the time integral. Finally, under various suitable assumptions, we obtain the weak convergence of the laws of the approximating processes to the law of the solution of the small-inertia limit equation, along with the identification of the limiting process, and also the convergence rate of strong $L^1$-convergence. The extra noise-induced drift term can be expressed as the solution of a contraction-type Fredholm equation. This paper is complementary to the deterministic particle limit work of \cite{Carrillo2021,Choi2021} .
Uniform localization and boundary corrections for two-node quiver Coulomb branches

We construct simple coherent classes and compute their normalized difference operators for the two-node quiver Coulomb branch with gauge group $GL_1\times GL_2$ and $m-1$ framing columns at the second node. The first magnetic charge is fixed at zero. For every $m\geq1$, every support $(n,-1)$ with $n\geq1$, and every integral electric twist, we prove that termwise saturation of the matter Koszul complex gives the simple intermediate extension. A graded normalization formula expresses its localization on every stratum as a finite binomial shuffle sum. The resulting operators satisfy bar symmetry, positive bubbling order, paired root-residue cancellation, and integral Laurent polynomial action. For $m=4$, we construct the derived boundary correction on $(2,-2)$, retaining the nonsemisimple odd-electric boundary object, and compute all electric twists. Finally, matter Euler divisibility proves triangular uniqueness on arbitrary fixed rank-two magnetic supports inside the actual integral Coulomb image. A pole-free counterexample shows why residue conditions alone do not give this uniqueness. Existence on general deeper mixed-sign supports remains open.
Higher Integrability, Generalized Symmetries, and Partially Topological Field Theories
Luigi Alfonsi; Leron Borsten; Mehran Jalali Farahani; Hyungrok Kim; Martin Wolf; Charles A. S. Young

We exhibit a classical link between higher Lax integrability and generalized symmetries in a non-Lorentzian higher semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory on $M\times\mathbb CP^1$. The equations of motion determine a spectrally dependent flat higher connection on $M$ whose Laurent coefficients organise an infinite hierarchy of conserved quantities. We construct a spectral family of classical $(d_M-2)$-form symmetry line defects associated with the Lax connection, establish an action-preserving deformation law, and exhibit suitable gauge-invariant probes on which the induced transformations act nontrivially.
Property F and weak integrality of braided fusion categories

We prove that a braided fusion category with property F is weakly integral, provided it admits a pivotal structure whose left categorical dimensions are positive on the intersection of its Müger center and its adjoint subcategory. In particular, the converse implication in the property F conjecture holds for modular fusion categories and pseudounitary braided fusion categories. We also show that the positivity condition holds for every pivotal braided fusion category if and only if every braided fusion category over $\mathbb C$ admits a pivotal structure.
A Variational Quantum Algorithm for Multi-Skill Project Scheduling
Raul Martinez; Miguel Sánchez-Beato; Matilde Osa; Jorge Parra; Mario Calonge

Job scheduling is an NP-hard optimization problem with clear industrial relevance. In practice, distributing work across a team is not only about meeting deadlines or improving productivity; it also affects fatigue, stress, and employee well-being. Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) provide a promising way to address these problems through QUBO formulations, although their scalability on near-term NISQ hardware is still limited by Hilbert-space growth and barren plateaus. In this work, we simulate a VQA for a realistic Multi-Skill Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (MS-RCPSP), including worker capacities, skill matrices, task priorities, deadlines, and calendar stability during rescheduling. To keep the problem within a near-term circuit size, we use a temporal batch decomposition that solves one day at a time, propagates the remaining workload, and combines it with a logarithmic binary encoding that keeps every batch at or below 30 qubits. Because the ground state of a QUBO Hamiltonian is a computational basis state, entanglement is not required to represent the solution, raising the question of whether it helps or hinders ansatz training. We address this question by comparing the linear and brick-wall entangling topologies of a hardware-efficient ansatz with an entanglement-free reference that has the same number of parameters and by training every configuration with COBYLA and with Adam using SPSA gradient estimation. For the instance and initialization studied, the entanglement-free reference produced feasible schedules under both optimizers. With COBYLA, it produced the feasible schedule closest to the required workload at a fraction of the simulation cost of the entangled topologies, indicating that entanglement did not improve the solutions found by the VQA.
Energy-Accumulate-Then-Act Backscatter Communications With Retransmission Under Imperfect Feedback Detection
Rui Xu; Yinghui Ye; Guangyue Lu; Liqin Shi; Gan Zheng

In this paper, we propose a threshold-triggered energy-accumulate-then-act backscatter communication system with retransmission under imperfect feedback detection. Under this system, harvested energy is accumulated across transmission blocks, and the backscatter device switches among different operation modes, including energy harvesting, initial transmission, and retransmission, according to its stored energy and decoded feedback. To characterize the resulting dynamics, the joint evolution of the packet-buffer and stored-energy states is modeled, based on which an embedded Markov chain is constructed to derive the steady-state energy distribution at the beginning of each update cycle. Subsequently, the average age of information (AAoI) is derived from the statistics of the inter-update interval and its correlation with the preceding packet system time, while the packet loss rate (PLR) caused by imperfect feedback detection is also obtained. Simulation results validate the analytical results and reveal that retransmission reduces PLR but may either improve or degrade AAoI, depending on packet-generation energy, data transmission rate, and feedback power. Moreover, lower feedback power shrinks the AAoI-favorable region of retransmission at low transmission rate, whereas the opposite trend emerges at higher rate.
Constrained defined-contribution pension management: A reparameterized neural network approach

This paper studies constrained defined contribution (DC) pension management under a two-factor financial market model. The pension participant is allowed to invest in cash, two nominal bonds, an inflation-linked bond, and a stock index. Moreover, they can also purchase term life insurance to manage pre-retirement death risk. Unlike traditional literature, we consider a pension member restricted to a general non-empty, closed, and convex trading constraint set that includes no short-selling, no borrowing, and portfolio-mix constraints as special cases. Such restrictions reflect common limits on pension-account trading. To solve the problem, we construct a family of unconstrained artificial markets, in which the original trading constraints are satisfied by adjusting the drift terms of the risky assets. Using a duality transformation, we derive the Lagrangian dual problem and propose a reparameterized neural network method to compute lower and upper bounds on the primal value function. We calibrate our model with U.S. data using a Kalman filter method, and find that our method produces a smaller duality gap than the benchmark methods. We also compare the constrained results with the unconstrained explicit solution and find that trading constraints substantially change wealth accumulation, portfolio strategies, and insurance demand. This highlights that unconstrained solutions may provide misleading guidance for pension management in practice.
A $2.81^n$ upper bound on the number of stable matchings

We study the maximum number ${\rm SM}(n)$ of stable matchings in an instance with $n$ men and $n$ women. Karlin, Oveis Gharan, and Weber (STOC 2018) proved the first single-exponential upper bound; their argument gives ${\rm SM}(n)\le 2^{17n}$ for sufficiently large $n$. Palmer and Pálvölgyi (FOCS 2021) improved this bound to $3.55^n+O(1)$. We prove that ${\rm SM}(n)<2.81^n$. This brings the exponential base closer to $2.28$, the base of the best known lower bound. More precisely, we bound the number of stable matchings in each instance in terms of each person's number of stable partners, where a stable partner is someone matched to that person in at least one stable matching. Our proof assigns each person a weight determined by this number and uses these weights to bound the number of stable matchings by induction.
Nonisomorphic separable Banach spaces at Lipschitz distance one

We construct nonisomorphic separable real Banach spaces whose multiplicative Lipschitz distance is one. Building on OpenAI's graph-space construction, we arrange two sequences of graph spaces into countably many blocks and form two spaces that differ by a single additional block. This block distinguishes their linear structures: one space contains a complemented copy of $\ell_1(c_0(\ell_2))$, whereas the other does not. By mapping the additional block to increasingly late positions and rearranging the remaining blocks, we obtain homeomorphisms whose Lipschitz constants and those of their inverses tend to one, while both spaces and their norms remain unchanged.
Largest-Angle Bisection and Statistical Regularization of Triangle Shapes

Largest-angle bisection (LAB) repeatedly divides a triangle by bisecting its largest angle. Although this procedure is known to preserve nondegenerate triangle shapes, less is known about the distribution of shapes across the resulting refinement tree. We show that its long-term behavior is governed by a distinction between pure and mixed branches. A branch that eventually selects only one of the two children may approach an exceptional family of shapes. By contrast, every branch that changes children infinitely often converges in shape to a right-isosceles triangle. This follows from a projective Lyapunov function that is non-increasing at every refinement and decreases strictly whenever the selected child changes. Consequently, a random branch converges to the right-isosceles shape with probability one, and the proportion of triangles near that shape tends to one across complete refinement levels. Largest-angle bisection therefore produces statistical regularization even though exceptional branches remain present.
Fluctuating Hydrodynamics of Quantum Fluids from the Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equation

Starting from the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation (NFPE), we establish the fluctuating hydrodynamics for quantum fluids. We also investigate the corresponding stochastic thermodynamics and derive the associated fluctuation theorems. We then apply this framework to both fermionic and bosonic systems. For the ideal Fermi gas, we study the electrical conduction and reveal a resistance proportional to the product of temperature and the density of states at the Fermi surface. For bosonic fluids, we analyze the relaxation time characterizing the critical slowing down phenomenon and identify three distinct scaling behaviors corresponding to the non-interacting, repulsive interaction, and attractive interaction regimes. Overall, this work provides a experimentally verifiable phenomenological description for the dynamics of quantum fluids and demonstrates the applicability of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation in characterizing such systems.
How many sorted projections determine n points in k dimensions?

Let $d_1,\dots,d_m$ be directions in $\mathbb{R}^k$, where $k\ge 2$. A multiset $X$ of $n$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ projects to the $m$ multisets of numbers $\{\{x\cdot d_j : x\in X\}\}$, or equivalently to the $m$ sorted lists of these numbers. How many directions are needed for these projections to determine every multiset of $n$ points? Two simple bounds are known in every dimension: more than $(k-1)\log_2 n$ directions are always needed, and $(k-1)n+1$ directions in general position always suffice. In the plane much more is known: Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron showed that almost every choice of $O(\log n \log\log n)$ directions suffices. Whether anything similar holds in higher dimensions was left open by Dym, Wellershoff, Tsoukanis, Levy and Balan. We observe that two lemmas of Hair and Sahai, proved for list recovery of random linear codes, answer that question, and by tightening their argument we show that in every dimension almost every choice of $(4k-2)\ln(2n)\ln(k\log_2 2n)+k+1$ directions suffices. For $k\le 10$ this beats the linear bound once $n$ is larger than about 100: for example, 144 directions suffice for multisets of 1000 points in the plane, and an exact computation lowers this to 133. Letting some of the random blocks in their argument fail removes a factor $\log k$: almost every choice of $O(k\log n\log\log n)$ directions suffices, uniformly in $k$ and $n$. We also show that $2k-1$ directions never determine three points, so that the logarithmic lower bound is not tight; that every $m$ directions in the plane fail on some pair of multisets of size $O(1.78^m)$, improving the bound $O(1.80^m)$ of Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron; and that for each $k$, $m$ and $n$, either almost every choice of $m$ directions works or almost none does.
Yufei Chang; Zhilan Wang; Shuo Wei; Jin Yan

We study balanced cycles in regular multipartite tournaments. A cycle in a $c$-partite tournament is $k$-balanced if it contains exactly $k$ vertices from each partite class. We prove that there exists an absolute integer $r_0$ such that every regular $c$-partite tournament with each partite class size of $r\ge r_0$ contains a $k$-balanced cycle for every $1\le k\le r$ when $c=3$ or $c\ge5$, and for every $2\le k\le r$ when $c=4$. In particular, our result confirms three conjectures of Volkmann and Winzen for large regular multipartite tournaments. We also confirm Yeo's conjecture on the existence of $(p,q)$-cycle factors for large regular $c$-partite tournaments $G$ with $c\ge4$, where a $(p,q)$-cycle factor is a pair of vertex-disjoint cycles of lengths $p$ and $q$ spanning $G$.
Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks with Uncertain and State-Dependent Couplings
Iva Bačić; Philipp C. Böttcher; Marc Hunkemöller; Carsten Hartmann; David Gross; Andrea Benigni; Dirk Witthaut

Phase locking in oscillator networks depends critically on the interaction strengths between coupled units. In many applications, however, these couplings are uncertain, state dependent, or time varying. We derive rigorous conditions for phase locking in Kuramoto-type networks when each coupling strength is known only within prescribed bounds. Building on a convex formulation of the nonlinear fixed-point equations, we obtain edge-wise error bounds for arbitrary feasible approximations that hold uniformly over all admissible couplings. These bounds yield sufficient conditions for the existence of phase-locked states with prescribed phase-difference limits. We illustrate the framework for AC power grids with uncertain voltage magnitudes and adaptive oscillator networks with state-dependent couplings. For the latter, the bounds can be further tightened by exploiting the state dependence of the couplings.
Planar Central Configurations of Four Equal Masses: Classification and Morse Indices

We study the planar central configurations of four equal positive masses under homogeneous interactions with force exponent $A>2$. For $2<A\le 3$, we prove that there are exactly four types of configurations up to similarity and relabeling: the square, the centered equilateral triangle, a unique nontrivial concave kite, and a unique collinear configuration. Combined with known results for $A>3$, this completes the classification for all $A>2$ and gives an affirmative answer to Problem 11 of Albouy, Cabral, and Santos. We also establish the nondegeneracy modulo rotation of these configurations and determine their Morse indices, confirming Hampton's Conjecture 2. Our proofs are based on analytic arguments and exact algebraic calculations.
A general technique for explicit quantile representations

This work proves existence of contours independent of probability level for exact quantile integrals of strictly positive real-analytic densities. Explicit constructions cover five broad distribution families and yield a finite-interval representation of Black-Scholes implied volatility using forward functions.
Beyond the Gap: What Imaginary-Time Evolution Reveals About the Edge of the Continuum

The spectral gap, the energy separating the ground state from the first excitation, governs many quantum phenomena, yet it is far harder to compute than the ground state. We propose a mathematically rigorous method for extracting the gap from imaginary-time evolution in infinite-dimensional Hamiltonians, where the first excitation typically marks the edge of a continuous spectrum. We show that a gap is not automatically detected: detection depends on how the initial state and observable couple the ground state to excitations at the bottom of the continuum. When this coupling follows a power law, the gap is recovered together with a logarithmic correction whose coefficient yields the exponent of the spectral density near the edge of the continuum, which reflects the physics of the excitations. We confirm both predictions numerically for an exactly solvable model. Our results offer a new numerical approach to many-body quantum physics, in which both the gap and the threshold exponent are obtained merely at the cost of a ground-state calculation.

The $\Ng:=2^{g}$ lifts give $\Ng$ trivial $α$-holonomy even spin structures $\Lg$.
 The remaining $2^{2g}-\Ng$ spin structures
 are not treated in this paper.
 We prove, on an open set (H) of Schottky parameters and more generally whenever the critical exponent of $Γ$ is below $\half$ (any genus $g\ge 1$) the following:
 absolute and locally uniform convergence on $Ω_0\timesΩ_0$, where $Ω_0$ is the full region of discontinuity including the point $\infty$ (treated in homogeneous coordinates);
 invariance without Eichler-type defect; skew-symmetry; a simple pole on the diagonal as the only singularity; $H^0(\Sg,\Lg)=0$; and hence identification of $S_\eps$ with the Szegő kernel of $\Lg$. At genus one the kernel is computed explicitly and the relations between lifts and theta characteristics are determined. We further prove that the diagonal coefficient defines a projective connection that differs from the Bergman projective connection by a quadratic differential

On isotropic points and contact invariants of curves

Let $(C_{f},0) \subset (\mathbb{C}^{n},0)$ be a germ of an irreducible holomorphic curve, given implicity by $f(x)=0$ if $n=2$ and by $f(x)=g(x)=0$ if $n=3$, and parametrised by $γ:(\mathbb{C},0) \rightarrow (\mathbb{C}^{n},0)$. We define the contact invariants $\operatorname{Iso}_{f}$ and $\operatorname{Iso}_γ$ for $f$ and $γ$, respectively, which count the number of isotropic points that appear after a generic deformation of the curve. We first consider the case where the curve is regular and establish a relation between those invariants and the number of vertices, inflection points and the zero-torsion points (for $n=3)$ that emerge from the deformation of the curve. Furthermore, we consider a germ of a singular curve with an isolated singularity and relate the number of isotropic points with the Milnor number of $f$
Laurent Bienvenu; Noam Greenberg; Ludovic Patey; Dan Turetsky

We study the relation between the existence of escaping (or hyperimmune) functions and weak 1-genericity using computability over ideals. We prove in particular the existence of an $\mathcal{I}$-escaping function which does not $\mathcal{I}$-compute any weakly $\mathcal{I}$-generic set whenever $\mathcal{I}$ is a countable Turing ideal closed under the existence of diagonally non-computable functions.
OSD-JSCC: Neural Joint Source-Channel Coding with One-Step Diffusion

Neural joint source-channel coding (JSCC) enables efficient image transmission over noisy channels, yet distortion-optimized approaches often produce blurry reconstructions. While diffusion priors can enhance visual fidelity, their iterative sampling incurs substantial decoding latency. To address this limitation, we propose OSD-JSCC, an SNR-adaptive JSCC framework with a single diffusion step. Specifically, OSD-JSCC transmits pretrained variational autoencoder (VAE) latents through an SNR-conditioned JSCC codec and incorporates two key designs. First, we introduce a stochastic diffusion-state interface that enables the JSCC decoder to predict a Gaussian diffusion state rather than a clean latent, while extracting image-specific semantic tokens. The sampled diffusion state preserves spatial structure and provides a good initialization for one-step refinement, whereas the semantic tokens, together with an SNR token, guide the reconstruction process. Second, we develop SNR-conditioned feature modulation and adaptive timestep selection to jointly adapt latent transmission and diffusion refinement to varying channel conditions. Furthermore, we adopt a three-stage training strategy with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to efficiently adapt the pretrained diffusion prior to the JSCC task. Extensive experiments on Kodak and CLIC2020 demonstrate that OSD-JSCC achieves superior perceptual quality and decoding efficiency. Compared with existing diffusion-based JSCC baselines, OSD-JSCC reduces LPIPS by approximately 43% on Kodak and 53% on CLIC2020, while achieving up to a 50.6$\times$ reduction in decoding latency.
Private key sieves for improved attacks on RSA

The RSA cryptosystem has been studied extensively and its insecurity in specific scenarios is well known. For instance, a sufficiently small private key allows to factorize the modulus $N$ and break the system. Attacks like this are often based on lattice reduction for finding small roots of polynomials, but high lattice dimensions can make it difficult to achieve the theoretically proved bounds in practice. In this paper, we adapt a sieve technique originally developed for deterministic integer factorization and apply it to RSA parameters. The sieve allows for an asymptotically significant reduction of the private key search space, and can be used to decrease the bounds for the polynomial roots. We also provide a square-root speed-up of the best currently known runtime bound for factoring semiprime $N=pq$ with small prime difference $q-p$.
Grigori A. Karagulyan; Linda A. Khachatryan; Khazhakanush V. Navoyan

We show that any discrete-time filtration can be embedded into a dyadic filtration, realized via a non-classical measure-preserving map. This embedding makes it possible to reduce certain problems involving vector-valued martingales to the case of Haar martingales. Some applications of this result will also be discussed.

Kramar and Kramar Fijavž proved that a commutator $Y=AB-BA$ of two complex square matrices is nilpotent whenever $Y$ commutes with an iterated commutator $δ_Y^{k}(A)$, where $δ_Y(T)=YT-TY$, and asked whether this result can be generalized to bounded operators on infinite-dimensional spaces. We show that for $k\geq 2$ such a commutator need not be quasinilpotent. On the other hand, for every $k$ it is quasinilpotent whenever it is compact, or more generally whenever it is a Riesz operator or $AY-YA$ is compact. Moreover, its Riesz projection at any non-zero isolated point of its spectrum always has infinite rank.

We develop normalized abacus combinatorics for affine type \(C\). We also give explicit product formulas for the number of Scopes classes at every level and every positive depth in affine types \(A\) and \(C\).
On Partitions with Constant-Sum Gap Sequences

We introduce and study \emph{constant-sum gap partitions}: for a fixed nonnegative integer $C$, these are partitions $λ=(λ_1,\ldots,λ_k)$ whose successive differences $d_i=λ_{i+1}-λ_i$ satisfy $d_i+d_{k-i}=C$ for all valid $i$. We derive the generating function for this family, treating partitions of odd and even length separately, and compute it explicitly for $C=0, 1,2,3,4$. We then construct explicit bijections between constant-sum gap partitions with $2m+1$, respectively $2m$, parts and partitions into odd, respectively even, parts in which parts below the largest part have bounded multiplicity, together with an exact weight relation between a partition and its image. Finally, we give a geometric characterization of constant-sum gap partitions in terms of their Ferrers diagrams: removing a prescribed, linearly growing number of cells from each row renders the diagram symmetric about its middle row, for both the odd- and even-length cases.
Macroscopic return-time spectra and Hausdorff dimension transitions

Can the complete macroscopic spectrum of return times determine the Hausdorff dimension of the corresponding set of initial points? We classify all common lower and upper macroscopic intermediate-dimension spectra of zero-density integer sets and realize every admissible spectrum on a full-dimensional family of zero-frequency orbits under logarithmic-power bounds on inverse-branch contraction. For first-return branches with stretched-exponential contraction $e^{-n^δ}$, $0<δ<1$, complete spectrum levels exhibit a sharp zero/full dimension transition at the counting endpoint $δ$. At the critical exponent, exact laws $N_y(t)\sim c_0t^δ(\log t)^β$ yield zero dimension for $β\le0$ and full dimension for $β>0$, even with the complete spectrum fixed. An explicit two-branch intermittent interval map realizes this transition through genuine first returns. Above the critical exponent, imposing an exact counting law and a complete spectrum does not reduce the dimension of an intrinsic mean-energy level in an affine return tower. For nonlinear branches, we obtain quantitative bounds and an exact conditional-pressure formula under thermodynamic regularity assumptions, verified for an explicit non-affine family.
Definably isometric cuboids over Hensel minimal fields

We show that, over a valued field $K$ with $1$-h-minimal theory $\operatorname{Th}(K)$, two Cartesian products of balls must be equal up to translation and coordinate permutation in order for there to exist a definable surjective isometry between them. For this purpose, we introduce a notion of relative dimension for cuboids in $K^n$ that is computed combinatorially and relates to the notion of dimension for definable sets in Hensel minimal theories when $K$ has infinite residue field.
A volume-conserving ALE continuous Galerkin method with residual-based Dirichlet--Neumann fluxes for nonlinear free-surface waves

We develop an arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian continuous Galerkin finite element method for two-dimensional fully nonlinear free-surface potential flow. An isoparametric finite element method computes the interior potential on the current fluid domain, while a residual-based Dirichlet--Neumann flux drives the surface evolution. The residual-based flux satisfies a global discrete balance inherited from the interior variational formulation. When combined with compatible mesh motion, surface projection, and quadrature, this balance yields conservation of the discrete fluid volume at the semi-discrete level. An optional volume-conserving sixth-order surface dissipation controls high-frequency oscillations, and the surface equations are advanced with fourth-order Runge--Kutta integration, updating the mesh and interior solution at every stage. Numerical experiments confirm the expected spatial convergence for linear free-surface waves and demonstrate reduced mesh sensitivity for nonlinear waves over flat and curved bottoms. A rotating-wavemaker example further illustrates the treatment of moving solid boundaries.
Alexandrov's theorem in the anti-Gaussian space: A Reilly-formula approach

We give an alternative proof of Alexandrov's theorem about constant weighted mean curvature hypersurfaces in the anti-Gaussian space, due to the authors and Johne-Silini independently, via a Reilly-type formula approach. Moreover, we establish a sharp Heintze-Karcher-type inequality for hypersurfaces in manifolds with a generalized substatic condition, together with its rigidity in Euclidean space with density.
Endpoint Schatten class properties of commutators on quantum Euclidean spaces
Changbao Pang; Maofa Wang; Hao Zhang

We study commutators $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$ involving fractional Laplacians on quantum Euclidean spaces associated with arbitrary real antisymmetric matrices $θ$. For $d\geq2$ and $-\frac d2<ε\neq 0<1$, we characterize critical weak Schatten class membership of $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$ for any $x$ as a tempered distribution by Sobolev spaces, with equivalent corresponding norms. We also establish precise asymptotics of singular values for $[(-Δ_θ)^{\fracε{2}},M_x]$. For this purpose, we extend the Cwikel estimates and the required asymptotics of singular values to arbitrary real antisymmetric matrices, and we also establish a systematic approximation theory of tempered distributions on quantum Euclidean spaces.
The optimal barrier parameter of the three-dimensional power cone
Rui-Jin Zhang; Wenhao Fu; Yu-Hong Dai

We determine the optimal logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barrier parameter for the three-dimensional power cone. Although several self-concordant barriers for this cone have been constructed, its optimal barrier parameter had remained unknown. For a power cone with exponent $c\in(0,1)$, we prove that the optimal parameter is $\frac{3}{1+\min\{c,1-c\}}$. Except at $c=1/2$, this value is strictly smaller than the parameter $3-2\min\{c,1-c\}$ of Chares' conjectured barrier. At $c=1/2$, the optimal parameter equals $2$, in agreement with the optimal barrier parameter of the second-order cone. The proof combines a sharp lower bound for arbitrary logarithmically homogeneous self-concordant barriers with an explicit barrier attaining the bound.
Twofold Control: Simultaneous Optimization of Initial Conditions and Control Inputs

The paper introduces a novel control notion, twofold controllability, which consists of the joint optimisation of the initial state and the distributed control input in a controlled dynamical system, with the aim of reaching a prescribed target state within a given time interval. We show that the resulting problem is well-posed, derive the corresponding optimality conditions, and provide an explicit formulation of its solution. The proposed approach ensures the reachability of any target state independently of the Kalman rank condition. We show that incorporating the additional control component enlarges the set of states reachable with a fixed control cost. At the same time, the average energy required to reach target vectors on the unit sphere decreases. Furthermore, we analyse the asymptotic behaviour as the cost of controlling the system through the initial state tends to infinity. Particular attention is paid to the case in which the controllability Gramian is singular and the classical notion of controllability does not hold. The theoretical results are illustrated by numerical examples, including ones arising from the semi-discretisation of the heat and wave equations with boundary control.
On the proof of multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for hyperplane arrangements
In this article, we use Wu's method to prove Budur's multi-variable $n/d$-conjecture for completeness.
High-Degree Restricted Cohomology for $K(3;1)^{(1)}$ in Characteristics Five and Seven

We determine the high-degree restricted first cohomology of the positive subalgebra of the rank-one contact algebra in characteristics five and seven, with parabolically induced coefficients. In degrees from twice the characteristic through four times the characteristic minus three, each characteristic has six nonzero homogeneous components, of total dimension thirteen. The constituents include Frobenius twists of the natural horizontal module, represented by Cartier cocycles. PBW duality converts the calculation into bounded-degree homology, where the coefficient action couples the natural and cubic relation coordinates. The resulting modules determine the high-degree part of the coefficient cohomology used in the Lyndon-Hochschild-Serre term $E_2^{0,1}$ for extensions of induced contact modules. In particular, extensions from the Steinberg induced modules vanish in these degrees.

abla^α\cdot)$ of order $2α\in (0,2)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, built from the Riesz fractional gradient and divergence, with bounded, measurable and uniformly elliptic complex coefficients $μ$. More precisely, we show that the domain of $L^{1/2}$ coincides with the distributional fractional Sobolev space $\mathrm{S}^{α,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and that $\|L^{1/2} u\|_{\mathrm{L}^2} \simeq \|
abla^αu\|_{\mathrm{L}^2}$, with constants that are locally uniform in $α$. As a consequence, we recover the Kato square root property for elliptic operators $-\operatorname{div}(μ
abla\cdot)$ in the limit $α	o 1$, and we obtain continuity of the square root with respect to the parameter $α$. The proof follows the second-order approach to the Kato problem. Its two new ingredients are nonlocal off-diagonal estimates of polynomial order for the resolvents of $L$, and a construction of $T(b)$-test functions that circumvents the nonlocality of $
abla^α$ by factorizing it through Riesz potentials.

We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. This gives a nonlattice-transversality alternative of the monodromy group. On the other hand, we generalize Filip's Assumptions A and B to give classes of polarized variation of Hodge structures that achieve the equality. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.

We analyze the unusual microstructure resulting from the cubic to orthorhombic phase transformation in the shape-memory alloy ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$. This seems to represent an approximate experimental realization of a deformation having a finite number of incompatible deformation gradients, which has been known to exist only as a theoretical possibility. Dooge asked whether hydrology has laws at the catchment scale. Conservation makes it a flux-connected storage network, dissipation fixes the sign of every flux and aggregation determines how the unresolved composition enters the fluxes, through effective laws over threshold distributions and a memory of the forcing. Exponential Deviations and Hölder Continuity for Moving-Law Mixed Cocycles
Zhongmin Liu; Dengdi Chen; Yan Zheng

We study mixed random-quasiperiodic cocycles whose one-step laws evolve along an ergodic environment. Under mixed-base ergodicity, bounded logarithmic growth, and stationary-value uniqueness, which we characterize by relative quasi-irreducibility, we prove exponential quenched deviations for finite-time directional growth. The Siler model describes mortality from birth to old age as the sum of a declining immaturity hazard, a constant background hazard, and an increasing senescence hazard. Its remaining life expectancy has no known closed form, and numerical evaluation alone does not reveal how the immaturity hazard enters it. We show that the remaining-lifetime distribution at age $x$ is Gompertz--Makeham with a Poisson-distributed Makeham term. Successive Makeham terms differ by the rate at which immaturity mortality declines, and the Poisson mean is the cumulative immaturity hazard remaining after age $x$. In a latent-clock construction, individuals carry a Poisson number of constant-rate clocks, and selection removes those carrying more clocks first. The life expectancy lost to immaturity mortality is close to the probability of carrying a clock times life expectancy with that hazard removed, with a closed-form error bound. Intersection Product Formulas and Integral Dependence

We prove the intersection product formulas of Gaffney and Gassler for polar multiplicities and Segre numbers over arbitrary Noetherian local rings. For equidimensional and universally catenary rings, we give a geometric refinement of the Principle of Specialization of Integral Dependence, in which the maximal dimension of the images of exceptional components mapping into the hypersurface determines a precise Segre number that strictly increases.
Inference for Realized Quadratic Covariation of $R$ and $R^2$ as a Measure of Return Asymmetry

We propose a nonparametric test of return asymmetry based on the realized quadratic covariation between a cumulative return path and its square using high-frequency data. Our null hypothesis is that the volatility path is independent of the Brownian motion driving returns. Under this null and a martingale condition, the infill limit of the statistic is conditionally Gaussian given the volatility path, with a conditional variance determined by integrated variance. Studentization by a feasible variance estimator yields an asymptotically standard normal statistic without specifying a parametric model for volatility. Simulations under Heston and Bates dynamics show near-nominal per-window size, quantify power gains from independent-window aggregation, and assess sensitivity to jump removal and volatility-dependent drift. An application to 165 U.S. stocks over 1998--2025 finds that rejections concentrate in negative asymmetry, consistent with the leverage effect.
Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields

We provide an algorithm for enumerating ordinary K3 surfaces over a fixed finite field based on Taelman's theorem. We use this algorithm to prove that there exist no K3 surfaces without rational points over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q\geq 13$. For elliptic K3 surfaces, we give a geometric proof of this non-existence without computer assistance. On the other hand, we also provide explicit pointless K3 surfaces over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q\leq 11$.
Discrete Backbone Elasticity and Curvature-Dependent Torsion Statistics in Proteins

Coarse-grained models of protein conformational dynamics use $\mathrm{C}_α$ geometry to describe the probabilities of regular helices, ordered turns and disordered conformations. To test how much of this order arises from local chain elasticity, we connect discrete Hasimoto frame transport to neighboring bending mismatch, deriving a curvature-product torsion interaction and a six-parameter generalized von Mises density. Remaining angular errors in these trajectories are associated with atomic context at shared bends, as bend-matched peptide frames adopt opposite torsion signs with distinct hydrogen-bond patterns and a proline-containing $\mathrm{HP35}$ turn remains at negative torsion. In 1989, Gyárfás conjectured that the vertex set of every $r$-edge-coloured complete graph can be partitioned into at most $r$ monochromatic paths. The case $r=2$ follows from a theorem of Gerencsér and Gyárfás, and Pokrovskiy proved the conjecture for $r=3$. Recently, Li and Wang disproved the conjecture for all sufficiently large $r$, leaving open the smallest number of colours for which it fails. We show that this number is four. For every integer $n\geq118$, we construct a four-edge-colouring of $K_n$ in which every monochromatic path partition contains at least five paths. We prove that the hydrodynamic limit of the asymmetric Brownian energy process (ABEP) is the viscous Burgers equation. We also prove the hydrodynamic limit of the dynamic ABEP which leads to a nonlinear equation for the macroscopic tail-energy potential. Both processes are related to the Brownian energy process (BEP) through invertible, non-local transformations involving discrete tail energies, which can be thought of as the microscopic equivalent of a transformation of Cole-Hopf type. Our main tool is a general micro-to-macro result showing that, under suitable conditions, such microscopic tail transformations induce corresponding transformations of the limiting density profiles. Combining this result with the fact that the hydrodynamic limit of BEP is the heat equation, we obtain the limiting profiles of ABEP and dynamic ABEP as explicit nonlinear transformations of solutions of the heat equation.
On the (in)finiteness of fixed characters in genus $3$
We construct a counterexample to the Putman--Wieland conjecture in genus $3$ and discuss some of its consequences.
R. Giménez Conejero; J. J. Nuño-Ballesteros

We consider the comparison between a Milnor fibre of a function $f$ and its section by the zero locus of a second function $s$ in a general ambient variety $\mathcal{X}$. We give a formula that generalizes those of Lê and Siersma, expressing the difference of their Euler characteristics as a sum of local contributions associated with the critical points of the restriction of $s$. We provide an algebraic formula in the case that $\mathcal{X}$ is {smooth of pure dimension outside $f^{-1}(0)$}, and show some applications and examples.

We consider the Lane-Emden problem $-Δu=|u|^{p-1}u$, $p>1$, in bounded domains of a half-cylinder $ω\times(0,+\infty)$, with Dirichlet conditions on the relative boundary and Neumann conditions on the boundary of the cylinder. We study the stability of these domains, as critical points of a related energy functional, with respect to volume-preserving deformations of the domain. We prove that, for $p$ large, the flat cylinders are stable as soon as their height exceeds a threshold growing linearly in $p$, while, for $p$ close to $1$, both stability and instability occur, with explicit thresholds depending on $m$ and on the first nontrivial Neumann eigenvalue of $ω$. These results rely on a detailed analysis of the one-dimensional profiles: we describe their asymptotic behaviour, and that of the first eigenvalue of the associated linearized operator, as $p\to1^+$ and $p\to+\infty$, we obtain expansions of the amplitude with explicit constants, and we prove global comparison results with respect to $p$, some of which are new also for positive solutions.
A weak Galerkin finite element method for the coupled Stokes-Biot problem
Rui Li; Hui Peng; Xiuli Wang

In this paper,we consider a stable numerical method for the Stokes-Biot model. We adopt the standard formulation of the Stokes equations coupled with the mixed formulation of the Biot system involving the additional total pressure variable. We construct the semi-discrete scheme on polygonal meshes by employing weak Galerkin finite element methods for spatial discretization. It is convenient to incorporate the interface conditions into the semi-discrete scheme via the edge-based degrees of freedom. Furthermore, we give a fully discrete scheme based on the backward Euler method. We establish the well-posedness of these two schemes and provide a rigorous error analysis. Finally, we present some numerical examples to verify the convergence and stability of our algorithm under a wide range of some physical parameters.

We prove that for every infinite cardinal $κ$ there is an indecomposable $A$-module $M$ with $\dim_k M=κ$. Over algebraically closed fields, this settles Simson's conjecture, also called the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture, that every representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra has indecomposable modules of arbitrarily large cardinality. To construct these modules, we extend Bongartz's representation embedding from finite-dimensional Kronecker modules without a simple injective summand to such modules of arbitrary dimension. Applying it to the indecomposable Kronecker modules of every infinite dimension constructed by Göbel and Simson yields the required $A$-modules.

We study the Cauchy problem for the parabolic Hardy--Hénon equation $\partial_tu=Δu^m+|x|^σu^p$ with slow diffusion $m>1$ and a potential which is singular at the origin, $-2<σ<0$, in dimension $N\ge3$. Nonlocal diffusion operators with a drift term naturally arise in models such as moving coordinate systems induced by climate change.

We allow the dispersal kernel to be heterogeneous and non-symmetric, and remove the standard global upper bound on the kernel (thereby covering the case of heavy-tailed dispersal kernels). To overcome the analytical difficulties brought by this more general setting, we establish a new Harnack-type inequality for non-compactly supported kernels, and apply homogenization and cut-off approximation techniques to derive two-sided bounds for the domain approximation limit of GPEs. Furthermore, under the almost periodic setting, we prove that the GPEs defined through different admissible test function spaces (e.g., \(C^1\) spaces with bounded derivatives and uniformly continuous function spaces in the viscosity sense) are completely coincident. Exact certification for conic optimization over quadratic modules: partitions of unity and recession directions

We consider linear conic problems whose cone is a product of truncated quadratic modules, the sum-of-squares (SOS) side of the moment-SOS hierarchy. We characterize their existence, relate the canonical one to the analytic center of the dual pseudo-moment cone, Christoffel-Darboux polynomials and Pell equations, and we derive closed-form rational partitions for balls and boxes. The loss incurred by the certification is the optimal value of a recession problem, equal to a support function of the masses of the dual feasible pseudomoments. We prove a Dolgopyat-type estimate for the twisted transfer operators of a class of two-dimensional partially hyperbolic endomorphisms of the torus, not necessarily skew-products. The twist satisfies a quantitative transversality condition on the cotangent dynamics of the associated three-dimensional extension which, in the skew-product case, is related to Tsujii's notions of transversality and partial captivity conditions. First, we introduce a normal form reduction at the level of the Gevrey energy, which reveals an additional cancellation in the cubic Gevrey commutator and separates it into a non-accumulating boundary correction and a quartic remainder. Second, we establish a global-in-time periodic $L_{t,x}^4$ estimate for the non-polynomial phase $k|k|^α$, valid for every real $α\ge2$. Together, these ingredients yield a refined almost conservation law and the $T^{-1}$ lower bound for the radius of spatial analyticity.

The increasing enumerations of the infinite members of the constructed space form an unbounded family under eventual domination. The Exact Memory-Rate Tradeoff for Three-User Secure Coded Caching
Han Fang; Nan Liu; Wei Kang

We determine the exact zero-error memory-rate tradeoff for secure coded caching with three users and any number $N\ge2$ of independent files. Each user recovers its requested file, while its cache and the broadcast jointly reveal no information about the complete tuple of unrequested files. For $N\ge4$, two converse inequalities establish the optimality of the known achievable points and the memory-sharing segments between them. For $N=3$, two additional bounds identify a new corner at $(M,R)=(3/2,2)$, where memory and rate are measured in file units. An explicit linear code over $\mathbb{F}_3$ attains this corner and reduces the rate by one quarter of a file relative to memory sharing between the known points. The converse links the information held by cache pairs and triples to delivery under repeated and distinct requests. Its equality conditions guide the construction: users cancel the keys to recover their requested files, while uniform masking protects the complete tuple of unrequested files.

A digraph is $k$-quasi-transitive if the endpoints of every directed path of length $k$ are adjacent. In this paper, we prove that every strong non-bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian when $k\ge7$ is odd. Moreover, combined with the known even case, for $k\ge6$, we also prove that a strong bipartite $k$-quasi-transitive digraph of diameter at least $k+2$ is Hamiltonian if and only if it has a cycle factor. The halting problem asks whether a program eventually halts, with unrestricted resources. First, it defines an exact finite-budget problem, placing the simulated program and the checker on the same unit-cost timescale, so the checker can be embedded in an adversarial program. They separate a fixed model with extendable external resources, a model family that grows with T, and a larger system built around a fixed component. We extend the method of Van Woerden \cite{woerden} to totally real and CM number fields to obtain an upper bound for the number of $\GLo-$equivalence classes of perfect forms. Moreover, by considering appropriate barycentric subdivisions of the Voronoi tessellation, we extend these estimates to the number of $\GLo$-orbits of $k$-dimensional faces of the Voronoi tessellation. As a consequence, we improve the asymptotic order of the bounds for the torsion part of $K_m(\rint)$ obtained by Soulé \cite{soule_hermitian_bounds} and Houriet \cite{Juliet_PHD}. Fields, 2025), and the three-dimensional estimate of Drewitz, Prévost and Rodriguez (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2026). Our proof adapts the entropy method of Dewan and Muirhead (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2023) to the loop-soup setting. This yields a renormalization inequality for the one-arm probability, from which we derive the upper bounds.

We consider the binomial differential equation $$ ff'-a(f'')^2=be^{2c},$$ where $a(z)$, $b(z)$, $c(z)$ are polynomials such that $b(z)\not\equiv 0$ and $c(z)$ is non-constant. In this paper, we determine all entire solutions of this equation.

Uniqueness of the hexagonal lattice's universal optimality

We build on a recent proof of the universal optimality of the planar hexagonal lattice. We extend this result to demonstrate that, up to Euclidean motion, the hexagonal lattice is the only periodic configuration with this property.
Classification of radially symmetric solutions to a Hardy-H{é}non equation with sublinear absorption and applications

Uniqueness of a non-negative radially symmetric solution with non-increasing profile to the Hardy-H{é}non elliptic equation with sublinear absorption \\ ____________ $Δ$v(x) + |x|\textsuperscript{$σ$}v(x) - v\textsuperscript{1/m}(x)=0, ______ x$\in$___\textsuperscript{N}, \\ is established in the range N$\ge$1, m>1 and $σ$$\in$(max{-2,-N},0). Consequences of this result are the uniqueness (up to scaling) of the non-negative extremal function to a Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality and the uniqueness of a non-negative radially symmetric self-similar solution with nonincreasing profile to a parabolic Hardy-H{é}non equation with quasilinear diffusion. The proof relies on ordinary differential equations techniques, which can be used thanks to the radially symmetric setting, and requires in particular a delicate analysis of the well-posedness and continuous dependence in view of the non-Lipschitz nonlinearity and the singularity of |x|\textsuperscript{$σ$} at the origin.
On generalized $k$-token graphs with distinguishable tokens and a maximum capacity of $s$ tokens per vertex
Yiting Cai; Cristina Dalfó; Blas Fernández; Miquel Àngel Fiol

Supertoken graphs \(F^s_{k\times1}(G)\), also known as generalized token graphs, model configurations of \(k\) distinguishable tokens on a graph \(G\), with at most \(s\) tokens at each vertex. We study structural and metric properties of these graphs in terms of the base graph. For regular \(G\), we characterize when \(F^s_{k\times1}(G)\) is regular. We show that bipartiteness is inherited from \(G\) and characterize it for complete base graphs. For \(s\ge2\), we characterize connectedness and show that \(t\)-vertex-connectivity of \(G\) implies \(t\)-vertex-connectivity of the supertoken graph. We obtain exact diameter formulas in several regimes, including complete graphs and stars, and derive lower bounds and a conjectured formula for odd cycles. We also determine the clique number, give bounds and equality conditions for the chromatic number, and characterize planarity for complete base graphs.
Small 5-chromatic unit-distance graphs in disks of radius 3/2, 5/4 and 23/20

We give three explicit unit-distance graphs in the plane with chromatic number 5 whose vertices lie in small disks: a graph with 773 vertices inside an open disk of radius 3/2, one with 5713 vertices inside an open disk of radius 5/4, and one with 8168 vertices inside an open disk of radius 23/20. The smallest examples previously reported for these radii have 11725, 11725 and 31171 vertices. All coordinates are exact elements of Q(sqrt3, sqrt5, sqrt11). In each case 5-chromaticity is certified by an explicit 5-colouring and a DRAT proof that no 4-colouring exists. The 773-vertex graph is vertex-critical.
Retrials in Loss Systems: Mean-Field Analysis, Erlang Bounds, and Power-of-$d$ Comparison
Daniela Cuesta; Matthieu Jonckheere; Balakrishna Prabhu; Olivier Brun

We consider a system of $N$ parallel, homogeneous servers, each with finite capacity $C$. Jobs requiring one unit of capacity arrive according to a Poisson process with total rate $Nλ$ and have exponential service times with rate $μ$. We study a decentralized random--retrial policy with $d$ attempts: upon arrival, a job is assigned to a uniformly chosen server; if the server is full, the job is reassigned to another uniformly chosen server, for at most $d$ attempts; if all $d$ attempts fail, the job is rejected. In the mean-field limit, we prove that the stationary blocking probability is characterized by the unique solution of a fixed-point equation involving the Erlang-B loss function, and we establish global convergence of the fluid model to this equilibrium. We also compare the mean-field stationary blocking probability with the analogous quantity in the power-of-$d$ model under the same parameters $(C,λ,μ)$. For the same $d$, we show, via coupling techniques, that the blocking probability under power-of-$d$ is always less than or equal to the blocking under retrial-of-$d$; but if we consider $d$ and $\tilde d$ with $\tilde d>d$, then the retrial-of-$\tilde d$ policy achieves a strictly lower blocking than the power-of-$d$ policy when $ρ=λ/μ$ is sufficiently large. Moreover we show that for some specific cases, like $C=2$, $d=2$ and $\tilde d=3$, it occurs for all $ρ>0$, not only for $ρ$ sufficiently large. We complement the analysis with simulations that estimate the load level above which retrial-of-$\tilde d$ outperforms power-of-$d$ in terms of blocking.
Homology and Topology of Partially Ordered Fields

We develop a unified homology theory for directed partial orders (DPOs) and lattice-ordered positive cones on fields of characteristic zero. With the underlying field and its operations fixed, we define order?carrying spaces independently by topological conditions, establish a bijection with DPO positive cones, and characterize lattice orders by intersections of minimal open neighborhoods. A unified comparison theorem identifies graded Ext for region ideals with sheaf cohomology and multiplicative Tor with the reduced singular homology of truncated regions, giving a topological interpretation of the existence and preservation of reduced decompositions. We obtain canonical cohomological obstructions to lattice ordering, prove that a coefficient module for positive multiplication is flat if and only if the multiplier has a positive inverse, and show that every strict extension of positive cones on the same field produces a nonzero first Tor obstruction. Finally, we place the concrete lattice recently constructed by Bao-Zhang within this framework.
From the quantum group $U_{q^{1/2}}( {\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}}_2 )$ to the Kronecker quantum cluster algebra
Junyuan Huang; Xueqing Chen; Ming Ding; Fan Xu

Let $\mathcal A_q$ be the Kronecker quantum cluster algebra with principal coefficients. We construct an explicit algebra homomorphism from the whole quantum group ${U_{q^{1/2}}}( {\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}_2}} )$ to $\mathcal A_q$, whose images together with either of the two frozen variables generate $\mathcal A_q$. As an application, we obtain algebra homomorphisms from the split $\imath$quantum groups of affine $\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}_2$ to $\mathcal A_q$. Moreover, we explicitly determine the images of the positive and negative real and imaginary root vectors of ${U_{q^{1/2}}}( {\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}_2}} )$ in terms of quantum cluster variables.
Hopf-Galois Structures on Extensions Arising from Division Points on Elliptic Curves

We provide a general construction of infinite Hopf-Galois extensions from a direct system of finite Hopf-Galois extensions. We then apply this framework to extensions generated by division points on elliptic curves. Specifically, for a number field $K$ and an elliptic curve $E/K$ of rank at least $1$ with $P\in E(K)$ of infinite order, we consider for each integer $n\geq 2$ the extension $L_n=K(Q_n)$, where $Q_n\in E(\overline{K})$ is such that $nQ_n=P$. We show that the finite-level extensions $L_n/K$ need not be Hopf-Galois, and we give sufficient conditions for them to be so. We then prove that the infinite extension $L_\infty=\bigcup_{n\geq 2}L_n$ of $K$ is potentially Hopf-Galois, meaning it becomes Hopf-Galois after a finite extension of the base field.
Law-Dependent Poisson-Refresh Randomised Feedback Control for Stochastic Systems

This paper studies a continuous-time probabilistic control problem for stochastic systems in which the feedback law assigns a probability distribution over control inputs. The control is modelled as a law-dependent Poisson-refresh process: it is held constant between refresh times and resampled at Poisson times from a feedback rule depending on the current state and state law. The closed-loop system is therefore formulated as a jump--diffusion for the joint state--control process. The objective is to design the sampling rule by comparing the realised closed-loop system with a prescribed reference description. The cost separates two local terms: a relative-entropy penalty for the instantaneous refresh kernel and a state-side drift-mismatch cost. The state-side term is evaluated at the realised control value and is motivated by a frozen-control Girsanov identity. Under global Lipschitz, moment, and uniform ellipticity assumptions, we prove well-posedness of the closed loop and a dynamic programming principle on the joint state--control law space. For linear data and admissible mean-dependent affine-Gaussian refresh rules, the full joint law need not remain Gaussian, but the first and second moments of the joint state--control process close exactly. This yields a deterministic reduced control problem on moment space, with an explicit running cost, a reduced Hamiltonian, and a verification theorem.
A Polynomial Erdős-Pósa bound for Eulerian digraphs
Esther Galby; Roohani Sharma; Bart van der Steenhoven

In [Combinatorica 1996], Reed, Robertson, Seymour and Thomas proved Younger's conjecture dating back to 1973 that states that directed cycles have the Erdős-Pósa property. Specifically, they showed that every directed graph $D$ contains either $k$ arc-disjoint cycles or a set of at most $f(k)$ arcs that intersect every directed cycle. The function $f$, depending only on $k$, is however notoriously large--in fact, not even elementary. The first improvement on this function was only very recently provided by Hatzel, Kreutzer, Milani, and Muzi [FOCS 2024] who showed that $f$ can be taken to be an exponential tower of height $8$.
 In this work, we improve this function to $O(k^4)$ in the case where the digraph is Eulerian. This also answers an open question by Wahlström [Springer Monographs in Mathematics 2018] who asked explicitly when Eulerian digraphs have a polynomial Erdős-Pósa property.
 The only other known result about Erdős-Pósa on Eulerian digraphs is a result from Seymour [Combinatorica 1996] who showed that $f(k)=k$ when the Eulerian digraph admits a linkless embedding in 3-space, and such an equality is not possible for general Eulerian digraphs. We also complement our positive result, by showing that the result of Seymour cannot be extended to give a linear bound ($O(k)$) on general Eulerian digraphs, by showing that even on Eulerian digraphs the lower bound for the Erdős-Pósa property is $Ω(k \log k)$.
Existence of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow Singularities with Bounded Mean Curvature

In every dimension $n \ge 3$, we show there exist Lagrangian mean curvature flows that develop neck pinch singularities such that the mean curvature remains uniformly bounded. This follows from a related result that, under a structural assumption on the singularity formation, the mean curvature at small scales near the singularity can be bounded by the Lagrangian angle at outer scales with suitable weights. Applying this result to a subset of the finite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed in the companion paper [arXiv:2607.03152] and the infinite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed by Tsai, Wood, and the second-named author [arXiv:2401.02228] then gives examples of both finite-time and infinite-time singularity formation with uniformly bounded mean curvature.
Certified Collision Exclusion and an Unconditional Upper Bound $Λ<0.156821$ for the de Bruijn--Newman Constant

The de Bruijn--Newman constant $Λ$ is the transition time beyond which all zeros of the heat-deformed Riemann $ξ$-function are real. We develop a computer-assisted collision-exclusion method and obtain the bound $Λ<156821/10^6=0.156821$, in the normalisation of Polymath. The proof combines the published finite-height verification and the starting inequality $Λ\leq1/5$ with a compact-interior continuation theorem, five stable prime-polynomial Gram sources, certified moving-index recovery, a balanced real-jet transfer and a uniform Euler-product barrier at infinity. The resulting closed time-band exclusion, together with uniform remote reality, forces strictness at the proposed endpoint. The finite certificate uses 664,505 structural Fourier coefficients, 44,182 closed torus boxes, 184 separator moments and 17,385 separator rectangles. We isolate a Cauchy--Schwarz obstruction intrinsic to the four-prime source family, explaining the narrow feasibility margin of the certified endpoint. We state the proof-to-certificate interface and distinguish the present unconditional logical claim from other recent, as yet unrefereed, computational bounds.
From Continuum-Kinematics-Inspired Peridynamics to Simplicial Hyperelasticity

We develop a variational and functional-analytic framework for continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamics with simultaneous nonlocal interactions among multiple points. We encode the finite-difference data of each interacting simplex in a simplicial deformation gradient. For nondegenerate simplices in three dimensions, the gradient, its cofactor, and its determinant encode the associated continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic line, area, and volume changes, respectively.
